Core Core is the shared code every mod in the series runs on. It adds nothing to a game on its own, but everything here shows up in any game with one of the mods loaded: the grimoire, the dice and the roll log, the talk window, towns, the raider who got away, the shared settings window, the sworn home, boons and favours, Backgrounds, gatherings, the tavern, beasts and familiars, and the smarter enemies. Load it after Harmony and before the other mods. Each mod's own pages explain these systems in that mod's words; the pages below list everything Core itself defines.

A counter for selling drinks, drugs and meals. Most evenings guests come by, buy from the counter and any shelf in the tavern if they like your prices, leave the silver on the counter, and stay to sit and talk. The tavern is the room the counter stands in, plus any tavern area painted next to it. The Guests button picks who may come, and guests who hate each other may come to blows. Prices are set here or from any shelf in the tavern, and the tavern can be closed for the night. Beds marked for tavern guests are rented out for the night.
What each update changed, newest first, as the grimoire shows it.

- Ask understands everyday words: "why is my vampire burning" finds Sunlight, and "how do I make a new vampire" finds the Embrace. - A word only matches whole, so "rage" no longer finds "storage". Rare words count for more than ones found on every page. - A word spelled a letter off, or without its accent, still finds its page. - The best answer opens in a box at the top with its whole part of the page. The links above the answers keep only one mod's. - Answers about the kinds your colony has come first.

- A new Why tab lists what just happened to your pawns and why: a frenzy, a roll that went wrong, a power that can't be used, a letter from these mods. The newest is on top, and each goes after a day. - The grimoire's words in each row are links. The number on the tab counts the rows you haven't seen.

- Every power, Gift, Edge, rite, ritual and spell page now starts with a card: what it does, its price, its reach and cooldown, and the dice the selected pawn rolls for it. - The same card shows when you hold the mouse on a power on the gizmo bar. - Holding the mouse on a link shows its page beside the panel, and a link inside that one opens a second. - Game words such as Willpower, Generation or Rage are underlined the first time a page uses them, with their meaning on hover. - Pages have a path back to their section at the top, Back and Forward, and a Pin link. Every health condition, state and effect a pawn can carry, as shown on its Health tab. Condition Bad What it does Bargained This spirit struck a bargain. It serves the one it made it with for a day, then goes its own way. Blood dammed Yes The blood in this vampire's veins has gone still. It can't be spent, for powers or anything else, until the dam breaks. Bloodied Covered in someone else's blood. Censer smoke Yes Blessed smoke in the lungs. The thing living in this body can't stand it. Cold iron's touch Yes Cold iron has cut this sorcerer's hold on the dead. No corpse will rise for them for a while. Fighting beside its master Fighting at its master's side, as it was trained to. It reads their moves and strikes where they leave an opening. Fugue Yes Now and then this mind simply goes away. The body wanders off, and when they come back to themselves they have no idea how they got there. Gave up Yes Beaten and out of ways to run, this one has dropped its weapon and gone down on its knees. It waits to hear what happens to it. Gripped Yes Held by a man catcher's collar, and dragging against it. Gripped by silver Yes Held by a man catcher's collar, its silver spikes burning into the flesh. Hamstrung Yes The tendons at the back of the legs are cut, so this body can only crawl. Hired ally Paid to fight and to see nothing. Hysteria Yes Every fright and every slight lands twice as hard. In a vampire the Beast is never far below the surface. In Twilight The dead is on the ghostly side of the world. The living can't see it yet, and physical harm can't reach it. Manic-depression Yes Long highs and long lows, and little in between. Neither has much to do with what is actually happening. Most wanted Its own kind's enemies want it dead more than almost anything else, and it has outlived everyone they sent. It shrugs off half of every wound and fights like little else in the night. Multiple personalities Yes More than one person lives in this body, and they take turns. Each has its own idea of what work is worth doing. Nemesis Got away from a fight with the colony once and remembers it. Whatever hurt them most, they've learned to take, and every time they escape they come back harder. Netted Yes Caught in a wire net that won't hold long. It slows the body until it's torn loose or cut away. Obsessive-compulsive Yes Everything has to be clean and in its place. A dirty room is torture, and now and then they drop everything to scrub. Paranoia Yes Everyone is watching, and everyone wants something. They are cold with people and sometimes shut themselves away until the feeling passes. Powers sealed Yes Something has cut this creature off from its own power. It can't use any of its gifts, spend its blood or heal the way it should until the seal fades. Quicklimed Yes Burned through with quicklime. Nothing can raise this body. Schizophrenia Yes Voices, things at the edge of sight, and a growing sense that none of it is safe. When it gets bad they wander off, lost in what only they can see. Sees nothing Keeps what it sees to itself. Showing itself The dead lets the living see it, pale and see-through. Ordinary weapons still pass through it. Silver net Yes Tangled in a net of silver wire and held down, and no Garou can change form inside it. It lasts until the net is ripped apart from inside, which takes real strength, or until someone cuts it away. Silver nitrate Yes Silver salts eating into the skin. They go on burning for a few seconds. Sneaking Slipped into a hostile town by night. Its people can't see this person unless they find them: one who notices something searches the spot, and a searcher who comes close may find who is there. Attacking anyone gives this person away. Spared Yes The colony let this one go after it gave up. It won't come back as a nemesis. Tie Sent by someone. Tied up Yes Tied hand and foot, so this body can only lie where it's put. It lasts until the rope is worked loose, which takes a person about half a day and something stronger a few hours, or until someone cuts it. True faith A conviction so deep it has weight. Vampires who come at this person in close combat may break and run, and the mind is harder to bend. It can't survive the taste of vampire blood. Unhealing wounds Yes Something in these wounds won't let a vampire's blood close them. They'll mend in a day, the slow way. ← Core contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Every item, weapon and piece of apparel this mod adds. Value is the base market value in silver.
Name Damage Value What it is

14 melee A priest's holy-water sprinkler, made heavy enough to break bones. The hunting orders arm their Inquisitors with them. Swung by someone with True Faith, every blow burns a vampire the way a holy symbol does. Without faith, it's only a mace.

15 melee A short spear with a hollow steel point and a blood groove running back into a glass chamber. Every wound drains a vampire's blood pool and bleeds a ghoul's vitae out with it. To anyone else it's a poor spear.

11 melee An old iron sickle with a tight curve, the kind once laid over the necks of the buried dead. It hooks the neck of the afflicted for extra damage, and does more to a corpse-risen shambler. Otherwise it's a weak sickle.
5 burst, range 12.9 A paper-wrapped bundle tied with string, used up when thrown. It bursts into white chalk, and anyone hidden by a power is coated and can be seen and shot. It hurts nobody.

15 melee A straight, plain sword of dark unpolished iron, the hammer marks still on the blade. It bites hard into spirits and the afflicted, and a hit stops a necromancer raising the dead for a while. Brittle, and worse than steel against anyone else.
5 burst, range 12.9 An olive grenade with a slotted whistle built into the top, used up when thrown. The screech stuns anyone in Lupus or Hispo and shakes every other Garou. People hear nothing.
6 , range 7.9 A pump shotgun with a scorched barrel and a flared muzzle, firing shells of burning metal. Very short range, a cone of flame, and the barrel needs time to cool.
1 burst, range 4.9 A pierced brass censer on short chains, swung at close range. Its smoke pulls a bane out of a possessed person alive, and hurts a fomor over time. It does nothing to anyone else.

6 flame, range 5.9 A spear with a tube of powder and pitch lashed behind the head. Lit, it spits flame a few steps and sets whatever it reaches on fire, and once it burns out it's still a spear. Vampires fear fire more than anything, and hunters know it.
7 melee A short wand with a lit pilot, on a hose from a pair of heavy tanks that slow whoever carries them. It sets everything in front of it alight, allies included.
8 flame, range 19.9 A stubby orange pistol with a wide barrel and one cartridge at a time. The flare sets its target alight and lights up the ground around it, and reloading is slow.

1 burst, range 25.9 A long pneumatic dart gun with a glass sedative vial in each dart. A hit puts a frenzying vampire or Garou out of its frenzy, which is also how a mixed colony stops its own. It does nothing to anyone else.
11 melee A worn digging spade, its edge sharpened and caked with dry earth. It's cheap, and any downed afflicted it hits loses its head. Otherwise it's a poor club.
11 melee A long pole with a hooked, inward-curving blade. It goes for the legs, so one of the afflicted can only crawl. That won't end one. It's a weak polearm otherwise.

10 melee A knotted hawthorn stake, its point hardened in the fire. Hawthorn is slow to work and old stories trust it over any other wood: a thrust at a vampire finds the heart and holds it far more often than plain wood does. Against anything else it's a sharpened stick.

24 melee A long, broad two-handed sword with a square, pointless tip, made for one job. It's slow and awkward, but it goes for the neck of the afflicted. Against anyone else it's clumsy, and it misses often.
14 holy water, range 12.9 A flat pewter flask with a small cross stamped on it, used up when thrown. The water burns monsters in wounds that heal the slow way. It does nothing to people.

4 holy water, range 7.9 A garden pump with a steel backpack tank, a hose and a short wand, a cross painted on the tank. A short-range spray gives monsters a weak burn over a small area, puts out fires, and does nothing to people.

15 bullet, range 15.9 A pump shotgun loaded with magnesium shells. Each blast hits a little softer than buckshot, but it often sets the target alight. Fire is the one wound a vampire can't easily shrug off.

17 stake bolt, range 12.9 A workshop nail gun rebuilt to fire wooden bolts, with a short air tank under the barrel. Short range and much faster than a stake crossbow, and a bolt through a vampire's heart can pin it. Against anything else the bolts do little.

9 caustic splash, range 12.9 A thick clay pot of quicklime sealed with waxed cloth, used up when thrown. A corpse in the splash can never be raised, and the patch eats at any afflicted that stands in it. On anyone else it's a mild burn.
10 bullet, range 12.9 A battered pump shotgun loaded with coarse rock salt. A blast stuns spirits and the afflicted. It barely hurts people.
5 burst, range 9.9 A small burlap sack slit at one corner, used up when thrown. The salt pours out in a ring a spirit won't cross for a day. It does nothing to anyone else.

9 caustic splash, range 12.9 A brown glass flask of silver salts in solution, used up when thrown. It burns a Garou on the spot and goes on burning for a few seconds. On anyone else it's a mild chemical burn.

5 burst, range 9.9 A folded net of fine bright wire with lead weights along the edge, used up when thrown. A Garou caught in one is held down and can't change form until it rips the net apart with its own strength or someone cuts it free. Anyone else is only slowed, and soon tears loose.

12 bullet, range 25.9 A short old revolver hand-loaded with silver. Each round burns a Garou like a silver blade. Silver is soft and light, so against anyone else it's a weak pistol that cost a fortune to load.
17 melee A broad silver-plated spearhead with a thick steel crossguard behind it. Made to stop a boar: a Garou that runs onto it loses its momentum and takes the burn. A plain, weak spear otherwise.
9 melee A long pole ending in a two-pronged spring collar lined with silver spikes. It grips and slows whoever it catches, and burns a Garou for as long as it holds. It hardly hurts anyone else.
17 stake bolt, range 24.9 A heavy crossbow that shoots sharpened hardwood bolts. It's slow to load. Hunters carry it for one reason: a bolt that finds a vampire's heart can pin it like a stake.
Not a garment. It marks someone who has taken another shape, and goes when the shape does.

Name What it is A witness This outsider saw something they shouldn't have. Name What it is Cautious Hates being in anyone's debt. Pays well in silver and …, but only ever owes a small …. Cold to anyone from a colony it has never talked to. Conniving Never owes a … of its own. It pays with one another member owes it, so the colony ends up holding someone else's debt. Short with anyone who stops it for a chat. Cowardly Hands out work freely, one job more than its means would allow. Its missions are the dangerous kind, aimed at its enemies, and pay a fifth more. Generous Pays well and asks little, and its good opinion fades slowly. Once a year, after two jobs, it asks for something back. Greedy Pays less silver and more … for the work it hands out. Loyal Pays a quarter more in everything as long as the colony never works against it or its friends. Never forgives a betrayal, and takes the colony leaving the home as one. Proud Pays in prestige: more …, less silver. A refused mission is an insult it remembers. Short with anyone who stops it for a chat. Vengeful Remembers every slight. Its grudges never fade by themselves, and it turns enemy sooner than most. Short with anyone who stops it for a chat. Zealous Cares only for the home's cause. Every job it gives is a fight against the home's enemies, and it pays half again for them.

Every setting in Options, Mod settings, The Rim by Night, with what it does. Setting What it does The one who came back Now and then a colonist, prisoner or slave who died in the colony's care in the last year comes back at night, and wants one thing before it can rest. How often the dead come back The chance of the one who came back, as a share of the usual. It's twice as likely on a dark moon. Days before an ignored ghost turns Spectre How long a returning dead waits before it goes bad and turns hostile. At Never, the haunting still grows, but it never attacks. Merits at making How many Merits the making menu lets a new vampire, Garou or Fera take. Each Merit past the first comes with a Flaw of its own, picked or rolled. At 1, one Merit and one Flaw, as before. Grimoire Show the grimoire button at the bottom right: a book of everything the Rim by Night mods add and how it works. One bottom-bar button While the colony has two or more kinds (say vampires and mages), only the window you used last keeps its button on the bottom bar. The list down the left side of each window opens the others. Rim by Night Overview The Overview page under Rim by Night, at the top of the list down each window's left side: all our kinds at once, their pools, what they're doing, and who needs you. Off, Rim by Night keeps only its Chronicle and Our story pages. Missions ending soon A mission or an offer with this many hours left or fewer shows under "Needs you" on the Rim by Night Overview, with a red mark. Power tiles Put a vampire's powers on one small tile per Discipline, and a werewolf's Gifts on one tile per breed, auspice and tribe. Turn it off to give every power its own full-size button, as vanilla does. Pools over the inspect pane Show a selected colonist's blood, vitae, Rage, Gnosis and Willpower just above the inspect pane, where the Kindred and Garou tabs open. It hides while a tab is open. Kindred right-click submenu Gather feeding, staking, the Embrace and the other vampire orders under one "Kindred" entry in the right-click menu. Turn it off to list them with vanilla's orders. Power timers in the inspect pane List a selected vampire's running powers and the time each has left in the bottom-left inspect pane, so you don't have to open the health tab. Effects on the Kindred tab Keep a vampire's buffs, powers that are switched on and other harmless effects off the health tab. They are listed under Active effects on the Kindred tab's Sheet page. Wounds and anything harmful stay on the health tab. Fighting motion Blurred vampires dash at their foes, Potence knocks people back, and Kindred blows show on screen. Turn it off for plain vanilla melee. Power auras A faint glow around a vampire while a buff lasts, with a trail and a mark on its blows. Gore How much blood a fight with a vampire spills, and whether cut-off hands, limbs and heads fly off and lie where they land. At 0 there are no sprays and a lost part is simply gone, as in vanilla. Hunters Hunters and investigators who come because of Masquerade breaches, and hunter raids. Nemeses Hunters and our kind who get away from a fight with the colony remember it, and come back with their next raid, harder each time. Derangements Off, no one gains a new derangement, and the ones they have don't cause episodes or make frenzy harder to resist. The world lives on When a Kindred court, a Garou sept or a hunter cell falls, its people live on: some die, some go missing, the rest look for a new home that will take them, and some may come to your colony. Homes go to war on their own, settled by a quick battle of their real members. Off, a fallen home vanishes with its people, as before. The World of Darkness reaches orbit Off, nobody from these mods comes uninvited to a colony in orbit, and visitors wait until it lands. Help you call still comes, by drop pod. On, enemies drop in by pod too, and friendly visitors come only with Royalty, leaving on its shuttle. Bloodiness of falls How many die when a home falls without a battle (a town razed, a faction wiped out). Battles take their own dead. World pace How often homes go to war. At 100%, on a usual world, a court changes hands every two or three years, about one sept falls a year, and a hunter cell or two are wiped out. First encounter, earliest The earliest day a colony without vampires, Garou or hunters meets its first one: a pale stranger, a stray cub or a hunted stranger. First encounter, latest The latest day for that first meeting. Never earlier than the earliest day. Cover names Each world gives the monster factions a random name and a word for their people, so the names don't give away what they are. Off, they go by what they are: the Sabbat Packs, Pentex, the Garou Nation. A name you gave a faction yourself stays. Monsters shrug off mortal moods A lupus Garou ignores the vanilla moods a wolf wouldn't feel, such as kibble, rotten food or a cramped room, and a vampire far from its Humanity ignores corpses and strangers' deaths. Off, they feel them like anyone. Prisoners keep their secret A prisoner looks mortal on its tabs until the colony finds out what it is. Off, the tabs show it at once. Ambitions Off, no pawn is offered new ambitions. One already taken still counts and still pays. Days between ambition offers How long after three ambitions are turned down, left unanswered or dropped before the next three come. Groups plot against their leaders A coterie, pack, cell or cabal that grows close to the ruling group's power starts plotting to take its place. Off, none starts on its own; a group your colonist leads can still move when you say. Chance to be spotted sneaking in The chance each look a town's people take spots a pawn sneaking in, against the usual. At 0% nobody is ever spotted. Prejudice between kinds How much vampires, werewolves, hunters and mages living in one colony think less (or better) of each other for what they are, by clan, tribe, Creed and Path. Family and lovers feel half of it, and it never goes past 20 either way. At 0% they don't care. Blood-feeders can become hunters and mages Sanguophages and other pawns with the blood-feeder gene stay mortals with genes, never vampires. Off, they can't be imbued or Awaken. On, they can be either and keep their genes. Proximity detectors ignore the harmless On, a proximity detector rings only for unseen creatures hostile to the colony. Friendly spirits and ghosts, and your own people hiding with a power, leave it quiet. Off, it rings for anyone unseen, as in the base game. Beast training speed How fast animals learn from a keeper of our kinds or in a kennel, against the usual. Mission pay The silver every court, sept, cell and Consilium mission pays, against the usual. Names on each wanted list How many names the Red List, the Wyrm's Hunted, Most Wanted and the Proscribed each keep. A list fills back up over time; a smaller one loses no names until they are hunted down. Show wanted marks always Every mark on the Red List, the Wyrm's Hunted, Most Wanted and the Proscribed shows on the world map wherever it is, and can be clicked and reached. What each one is still has to be learned. Hours a wanted name holds its camp When a caravan runs a wanted name down, how long it and its people hold their camp before coming out to fight. Tavern guests How many guests come to a tavern each night, against the usual. Fights between guests Guests who hate each other, like a Garou and a vampire, may come to words, blows or a killing. Off, they never do. NPC cunning How clever enemies of our kinds are. Plain fights as before this update. Smart uses fighting styles, picks its targets, runs when desperate and may give up. Ruthless is Smart, but it goes for the weakest colonist and never gives up. Allies and colonists always fight Smart. Desperate drops hiding One of ours who is badly hurt, alone or losing stops hiding what it is: obvious powers, Crinos and vulgar magic in front of mortals. A drafted colonist never does. Fighting styles Each of ours rolls a style from its clan, tribe, auspice, Creed or Path: Brawler, Controller, Stalker, Caster or Guardian. The style decides which powers come first, how close it fights and when it pulls back. Giving up A beaten enemy with no way out may kneel and drop its weapon. You decide whether to let it go, take it prisoner or finish it. The nemesis learns A nemesis caught by a hidden foe comes back with a way to see it, goes first for the colonist who beat it, and brings one or two more of its kind. Mixed fights Kinds that hate each other by lore fight each other on the colony's map as well as the colony: Garou go for vampires, hunters for every monster, Seers for mages. Visitors use their powers Traders and visitors of our kinds sway prices, read what your people are, and scry the base before a raid. Very rarely, one feeds on a colonist alone at night. A colonist with a sense power can catch them. Colonists use powers outside fights Colonists with sense powers look over each visitor, the colony's trader sways prices under the Freely habit, healers mend the resting, and night watchers warn of raids an hour early. Scouts Before some raids a scout of our kinds comes first. Catch it to question it; let it get away unseen and the raid comes knowing where to strike. Caravan ambushes A hostile group of our kinds may wait on a caravan's route, at most once a month each. Grudges Someone with a grudge against the colony acts on their own: a small raid, a curse from afar, rumours, or hired help. Hunt planning Hunters coming for the colony's monsters bring the arsenal's weapons meant for them and switch to the right one, lay traps on the way in and fall back behind them, and send one with second sight ahead to find the hidden. Truces After two lost raids, a group of our kinds may offer a truce. Cover-ups A vampire or Garou deals with a witness of its own side's breach without being told: the colony's own when their box on the tab is ticked, a court's or a raider's always. It uses the surest way it has and never kills. Allow a sworn home Off: the swear link is gone, and a home already sworn is left quietly. War chance How often the world's wars pick the sworn home, against the usual chance. Enemy acts a season How many enemies inside the home act against the colony each season. Regard fades How fast members' regard drifts back toward zero each season. Rival strikes on Backgrounds How often a rival's act strikes one of your Backgrounds, against the usual chance. All the way left turns strikes off. Every thought and mood this mod adds. Mood is the change to mood; "opinion" ones change what one pawn thinks of another. Thought Mood Lasts What it is A place I knew fell -3 8 days I knew people there. Some of them are dead now, and nobody can tell me which. Cursed by a spirit -8 5 days A spirit I bound cursed me as it went free. Nothing feels right since. Cursed with nightmares -12 3 days Every time I close my eyes the same face is waiting. I wake up with someone else's hatred on me. Depressive spell -12 3 days Nothing is worth doing. It never was. Dreamed of … -4 1 days They were in my dream last night, standing in the dark and looking at me. They didn't say anything. They didn't have to. Dreamed of … 3 1 days They were in my dream last night, sitting at the end of my bed like they used to. It felt so real I said their name out loud when I woke. Some of them sound like people I knew. Manic spell 10 3 days I can do anything tonight. Everything is wonderful and I can't sit still. An Abomination is a Garou who rose from the Embrace. It needs both this mod and The Rim by Night: Garou loaded; with either alone, none of this happens. The werewolves' side is on the Garou wiki's Abominations page.

- A vampire Embraces a Garou. Before it dies, the Garou rolls Gnosis at difficulty 6. A success is a quiet death, a failure a death in agony, and only a botch rises. That is about 10% at Gnosis 1, 6% at 3, 2% at 5 and under 1% at 7. The confirmation shows the odds. - An unwilling Garou with Willpower left, and not in Harano, spends it for a sure clean death. One that asked, or is willing, never does. - It rises a few hours later as a vampire of its sire's clan, one generation weaker. It keeps its forms, Rage, Gnosis, Gifts, tribe, breed, auspice and rank.

Humanity is replaced by Ego, the Hierarchy of Wyrm Taint. It starts at the Garou's Gnosis. - Ego never rises, and experience can't buy it, the Virtues or Willpower. - By day, Ego caps every dice pool. - Below 7 it smells of the Wyrm: Sense Wyrm finds it and the Banes treat it as a friend. - Its own ambition, the wolf's hunger, is to bring down five animals with the bite. - At 0 it is the Wyrm's. It leaves to join the Black Spiral Dancers and comes back with their raids as a nemesis. The sins on the list, worst first: breaking the Litany (10), feeding on a Garou or Kinfolk (9), hurting a friend in a frenzy (8), calling on a Bane (7), killing in a frenzy (6), killing a Garou, Kinfolk or wolf outside a fight it was attacked in (5), diablerie or torture (4), killing an innocent (3), a Bane fetish or fighting beside fomori (2), helping destroy a caern (1).

Rule What happens Dice pools Every pool is halved, never below one die. A point of Willpower gives full pools until sunrise, by the "Full pools tonight" button, or on its own when a fight starts at night Willpower Buys no automatic success One pool a turn No blood within a turn of spending Rage or Gnosis, and the other way round Healing Only with blood. No regeneration Gnosis Never refills Renown and rank Frozen at the Embrace Its blood Dead: it can't Embrace or make ghouls Silver Burns it in every form, Homid included Frenzy Anger is the wolf's frenzy, rolled on Rage. Hunger frenzy rolls Rage too Mood "Dead and cut off from Gaia", -12, for good. A new break, "walk into the dawn", sends it out to stand under the sky Its Gifts that use only Rage, or nothing, work as before. A Gift that calls on spirits reaches only Banes and tests Ego. About once a season a Bane offers a Gift of the Black Spiral Dancers, bought with experience.

- Courts: a court that learns of it, because one of its vampires saw it shift or the colony visited with it, calls a blood hunt and demands it. Hand it over, or refuse for -15 goodwill while it lives and court raids aimed at it. - Septs: a sept's Garou who sees it in a wolf's shape tells the sept: -20 goodwill while it lives, and the next raid comes for it. - Its own colony: colony Garou think 20 less of it, colony Kindred 5 less.

- A colony Garou deep in Harano, or of a fallen tribe, may ask a colony vampire for the Embrace. - A hunted Abomination may come in by night and ask for shelter. Take it in and the blood hunt and the sept's anger come with it. Turn it away and its hunters may pass through after it. Sometimes one comes to kill instead. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. A vampire keeps its skills, traits, relationships and backstory. Most of what keeps a colonist alive stops mattering, and a few new things start to.

Gone New Food and Rest needs The Vitae need: the blood pool Ageing, disease, toxic buildup, breathing, bleeding out Burns in sunlight and takes fire badly Natural healing and medical tending Heals only by spending blood Most pain Sleeps by day whether it likes it or not Losing a lung, kidney, liver or stomach Can be staked through the heart Psychic drones, soothes and other psychic effects still work on Kindred.

Blood (vitae) pays for everything: waking up each night, healing, the blood buff and most Discipline powers. - Upkeep. One point each time the vampire wakes. With an empty pool it can't wake and falls into torpor. - Hunger. Above 70% the vampire is sated. Below 40% it's hungry, and below 15% it's starving and may frenzy at the sight of a vessel. A colony vampire hunts back up to the target set on its Vitae bar, 40% unless you move it (see Feeding). - Spend rate. Generation limits how much blood a vampire can spend in a short burst. A big power is paid partly now and the rest as the limit refills.

Lower generation means closer to Caine: a bigger pool, a faster spend rate, and higher limits on Attributes and Disciplines. Generation Blood pool Per turn Highest dot 4th 50 10 9 5th 40 8 8 6th 30 6 7 7th 20 4 6 8th 15 3 5 9th 14 2 5 10th 13 1 5 11th 12 1 5 12th 11 1 5 13th 10 1 5 The 14th and 15th generations are thin-bloods: a smaller usable pool, a lower cap on Disciplines, and every blood cost but upkeep doubled. In return the sun hurts them less and they can keep food down. A 13th-generation vampire's childer are 14th. Animal blood is worth half from the 8th generation down and nothing from the 6th. The only way to lower your generation in play is diablerie.

Healing is automatic. Each vampire's heal policy (never, when safe, always) under Habits on the Kindred tab decides when it spends blood on it. - Ordinary wounds. One blood point heals 12 HP of injury, worst wounds first. - Aggravated wounds (fire, sunlight, fangs and claws, some powers): 5 points and a full daysleep heal 10 HP. They are what kills a vampire for good. - Lost limbs grow back through blood, at the aggravated cost. A vampire healing with blood shows it: red mist drawn in and small red sparks, for as long as it heals. Ghouls healing with vitae show the same.

- Blunt damage is halved. - Bullets and arrows do 70% damage. - Melee blades do full damage. - Burns of any kind, from any mod, are aggravated. - However armour, Fortitude and the rest stack, damage never drops below 40%, so nothing makes a vampire untouchable.

Sunlight deals aggravated burns every second the vampire stands under an open sky by day. Full clothing cuts the damage to about a third but never stops it. A neonate at noon has well under a minute (real time, at 1x speed). A thin-blood gets an ordinary sunburn instead, which heals like any wound. - Dawn and dusk hurt much less than noon. Eclipses and dark weather help too. - Stepping into the sun can trigger Rötschreck, a panic that sends the vampire running for shade. See Humanity and frenzy. - An alert warns you about Kindred outdoors two hours before dawn. Vampires head for a roof on their own when the sky starts to brighten.
Fire is the other thing vampires fear. Burns are aggravated, Kindred catch fire more easily, and fire nearby can trigger Rötschreck. Firefighting is off for Kindred by default.

From dawn to dusk a vampire sleeps in a bed, a coffin, or any roofed cell. - The coffin is a bed anyone can sleep in. Its lid keeps the sun off even under an open sky, and a full day in it is a good mood. - Woken by day (drafted, or by danger), a vampire gets day lethargy: slow and clumsy, more so at low Humanity, and its rolls are capped at its Humanity. - Waking time. High Humanity wakes earlier at dusk. - Eclipses. When an eclipse or a dark sky leaves the day too dim to burn, vampires wake as at night: no daysleep, no lethargy and no cap on their rolls. Dawn and dusk don't count, and hunters and raids still treat it as day. - Dug in. A vampire caught with no roof in reach digs into soft ground and sleeps there. It's a bad day's sleep for anyone but a Gangrel, and outsiders who see it dug up start talking. - Dreams. After a full daysleep a vampire sometimes dreams: of its old life, its sire, the Beast, or, for a Malkavian, of something about to happen.

- Kindred take no penalty for darkness and never get the "in darkness" thought. - They won't start outdoor work by day. Drafted orders still go through. - To keep mortals awake at the same hours, copy a vampire's schedule to them in the Schedule tab. - A mortal partner doesn't mind sleeping apart.

When a vampire would die from anything but aggravated damage, or wakes with an empty pool, it falls into torpor: down, unconscious, no upkeep. Wounds don't heal, but lost parts grow back. - How long depends on Humanity: about a day at 10, years at 1. A letter gives the expected date. - Starved into torpor, a vampire lies there until someone gives it 4 blood points (vials or another vampire's vitae). It wakes in a hunger frenzy. - Ending it early. Vitae from a vampire at least two generations lower wakes it. - Torn half apart. A vampire that goes down with about half its body gone falls into torpor as well. While torpid it regrows one lost part every three hours, as long as it has more than 2 blood. A healing policy of "never" stops this. - Choosing it. A button on the vampire puts it into torpor to sit out a bad stretch. - A torpid vampire can be carried, kept in a coffin, staked, or diablerised.

A vampire is destroyed for good when: - its head is destroyed or cut off; - its body is destroyed (burned up, eaten); - aggravated damage hits it while it's in torpor or down; - sunlight or fire takes it past the point of death; - someone completes diablerie on it. What's left depends on its true age: a young vampire leaves a corpse, an old one leaves ash.

A wooden stake through the heart paralyses a vampire. It stays awake and helpless until the stake is pulled. A stake can be wielded as a weapon, and the stake crossbow shoots them: a hit that lands in the heart pins the vampire about half the time. Right-click a downed or torpid vampire to drive one in where it lies, for certain. It takes a moment in torpor and longer while the vampire is awake and struggling. A pawn with no heart can't be staked.

- Moving as a cloud. A vampire with three or more dots in a Discipline moves in a faint cloud of that Discipline's colour when drafted or charging, faster than it walks. - Physical Disciplines show. Celerity dashes, Potence knocks foes back, and a dodge is a sidestep or a clash of blows. - Stuns hit a vampire less the lower its generation is compared with whoever stunned it. - Crawling. A vampire that loses its legs and still has blood keeps fighting from the ground instead of going down. - Gore. Blows spray blood, and a part cut off throws what butchering it would give. A Gargoyle's throws stone, and an old vampire's turns to ash. A kill with Potence 5 or Taste of Death bursts the body. Close kills, feeding frenzies and diablerie leave the vampire covered in blood. The amount of gore and the fighting motion are mod settings.

From the right-click menu a vampire can eat a meal to look human. It costs a Willpower point (free with the Eat Food Merit, or for a thin-blood). Unless it's a thin-blood, it has to throw up a couple of hours later, and it waits until no outsider is looking if it can.

Every vampire has a power to pass as alive until dawn: warm skin, breath, a pulse. It removes the corpse-like social penalty with mortals. It costs 8 blood minus the vampire's Humanity, so it's free at 8 and above. A vampire on a Path can't use it. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material.
