Each blood sorcery has several paths, learned and raised separately like Disciplines of their own, and a set of rituals.

- Primary path. The first path learned. It can reach 5 (or higher, for an elder). - Secondary paths. A second path opens once the primary reaches 2 (3 for Necromancy). No secondary path may be higher than the primary. - Cost. A new path costs 7 experience; secondary dots cost current rating × 4. Tremere in good standing with the Pyramid pay less. - Rolls. Every Thaumaturgy power rolls Willpower. Necromancy and the others roll what each power says. - Who can learn. Thaumaturgy is in-clan for the Tremere and Necromancy for the Giovanni and their kin. Others need a teacher. A non-Tremere caught using Thaumaturgy may find a Tremere hit team at the door. Koldunic Sorcery is for the Tzimisce only. Assamite sorcerers learn Awakening of the Steel, a Thaumaturgy path, in-clan.
Blood magic, made by the Tremere and guarded by them. It is learned one path at a time, alongside rituals.
The first path of Thaumaturgy, the blood's mastery of itself Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Touch 10 s Touch someone's blood and learn from it: whether they are Kindred, ghoul or mortal, and how much blood they have left. With two successes it also tells a vampire's generation, and with three whether it has ever committed diablerie. For a day the sorcerer's own rolls against them get two extra dice.

1 blood Touch 15 s Touch another vampire and make its blood surge. It burns a point of blood for each success, gets a burst of speed and strength from it, and has to fight off a frenzy that gets harder with every success.

1 blood Self 1 day Concentrate the blood until it is as strong as an elder's. The vampire counts as a lower generation for four hours or more: a deeper blood pool, more blood spent at once, and eye contact that works on stronger blood. More successes lower it further and make it last longer. Any blood beyond the normal pool thins away when it ends. Once a night.

1 blood 15 cells 10 s Pull someone's blood out of them in a stream through the air, a point for each success, from up to fifteen cells away. It feeds the vampire like drinking does, but never creates a blood bond. Nobody who sees it will mistake it for anything natural.

1 blood Touch 20 s Touch someone and boil their blood. A mortal burns inside and bleeds for each success: a few put them down, enough of them kill. A vampire loses a point of blood for each success and takes aggravated harm for each.
Fire called out of nothing, from a candle flame to a roaring blaze. Once it catches, it burns Kindred like any other fire, the caster included. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood 20 cells 10 s Light a small flame anywhere within reach. It catches what it touches. Five successes put the fire exactly where it was aimed; fewer let it land a few cells off. The caster isn't burned by it, but anything it sets alight is ordinary fire.

1 blood 20 cells 10 s Hurl a handful of fire that bursts where it lands, setting a single spot ablaze. Five successes put the fire exactly where it was aimed; fewer let it land a few cells off. The caster isn't burned by it, but anything it sets alight is ordinary fire.

1 blood 20 cells 15 s Call up a fire the size of a campfire. It burns everyone around the spot where it lands. Five successes put the fire exactly where it was aimed; fewer let it land a few cells off. The caster isn't burned by it, but anything it sets alight is ordinary fire.

1 blood 20 cells 20 s Call up a roaring bonfire that sets a wide patch of ground burning. Five successes put the fire exactly where it was aimed; fewer let it land a few cells off. The caster isn't burned by it, but anything it sets alight is ordinary fire.

1 blood 20 cells 30 s Call up an inferno. Everything near where it lands burns, friend or foe. Five successes put the fire exactly where it was aimed; fewer let it land a few cells off. The caster isn't burned by it, but anything it sets alight is ordinary fire.

Moving things by will alone: small objects first, then doors and weapons, then people and the thaumaturge itself, then heavy things hurled like missiles and blades left to guard the haven. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood 20 cells 10 s Yank someone's feet out from under them with an invisible hand. They go down for two seconds per success. A living target can resist with Willpower.
1 blood 20 cells 15 s Tear the weapon out of someone's hands. It lands at their feet. A living target can resist with Willpower.
1 blood 20 cells 20 s Seize someone with the mind and hold them where they stand, four seconds per success. A living target can resist with Willpower.
1 blood 20 cells 5 s Lift the body by will alone and float through the air to a spot in sight, over walls and anything else in the way. A failed roll spends the blood and goes nowhere.
1 blood 22 cells 10 s Rip a heavy chunk of something from the surroundings and throw it at someone as hard as a falling boulder.

1 blood 20 cells 5 s Lift a melee weapon lying on the floor and leave it hanging in the air until dawn. It guards the spot it rose from, or wherever it is sent later, and cuts at any enemy who comes near. The thaumaturge keeps as many going as its Intelligence.
1 blood 22 cells 40 s Seize every enemy within a few cells of a spot and hold them all where they stand, four seconds per success. Each living target can resist with Willpower.
Rot, warp and wither: decaying objects, twisting wood, acid on the hands, shrivelled limbs and years of age in a moment. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Touch 10 s Touch an object and it ages years in a moment: a fifth of its condition per success, and food spoils. Touch someone and it takes their weapon or something they wear. Living flesh is untouched.

1 blood 20 cells 10 s Twist and split wood with a glance: doors, furniture, walls, bows, a stake in someone's hand. A third of its condition per success. Every wooden weapon in an enemy's hands within sight warps along with it.

1 blood Touch 8 h Turn blood to acid on the hands. Every blow burns and leaves aggravated wounds, for about an hour and a half per success. Cast on a door, a wall or anything else built within reach, the acid eats straight into it, a heavy wound in the steel or wood for every success.

1 blood 12 cells 30 s Wither one of someone's arms or legs to bone and skin. They can try to shake it off; a partial escape leaves the limb weak instead of useless. On a mortal it is permanent unless the limb is replaced. A vampire can restore it with five points of blood.

1 blood Touch 40 s Touch someone and add ten years to their age for each success. They can resist only by beating the caster outright. Aged far enough past a natural lifespan, a mortal crumbles. Kindred only look withered for a night.

The Assamite sorcerers' path of the sword: reading a blade's history, a grip nothing breaks, strikes that ruin armour, parrying arrows and bullets, and a blow that strips a foe of everything unnatural. Every power needs a blade in hand. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Self 1 h Feel the history of the blade in hand until it answers like part of the arm, and learn what it really is if it is an unknown relic. Until it leaves the hand it strikes truer (more with more successes), nobody can knock it away, and the other powers of the path get an extra die through it.
1 blood Self 4 h Bind the blade to the hand for a while. Nothing can make the sorcerer let go of it, and nothing knocks it off its stride.
1 blood Self 8 h For about an hour and a half a success, blows go into metal armour and wreck it instead of the body under it. Against someone without metal armour they land at half strength.
1 blood Self 8 h For about an hour and a half a success, the blade can cut arrows and bullets out of the air. Each success is a better chance to stop each one.
1 blood Self 8 h For about an hour and a half a success, every blow meets its target as bare flesh: Fortitude and every other unnatural toughness do nothing against it.

Making things out of nothing: simple things first, then lasting ones, then things with working parts, unmaking them again, and at last animals with no will of their own. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Self 10 s Make a simple thing of one material out of nothing: a wooden stake, a club, mace, spear or knife of wood or steel, or a chunk of granite appears at the caster's feet. Its quality follows the successes. It is gone in a day.

1 blood Self 1 h Make a simple thing that stays: a wooden stake, a club, mace, spear or knife of wood or steel, or a chunk of granite, for a blood point. It is never better than poor, and nobody will buy or smelt it.

3 blood Self 2 h Make something with working parts out of nothing, for three blood: a revolver, a bolt-action rifle or a pump shotgun. It stays, but it is never better than poor, and nobody will buy or smelt it.
1 blood Touch 10 s Unmake something conjured, whoever made it. Aimed at someone, it unmakes everything conjured they carry, wear or hold.

5 blood Self 1 day For five blood, make a copy of an animal that lives here. It has no will of its own and guards the caster for three days, then fades. Its fur repeats like a pattern, if anyone looks closely.
Command of the sky over the land around: fog, rain, a gale, a storm, and lightning brought down where the caster wants it. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Self 2 h Call fog over the land for twelve hours. Aim at range is halved. More successes bring it sooner.
1 blood Self 2 h Call rain for twelve hours, or snow if it is freezing. Rain puts out fires and dulls the sun a little. More successes bring it sooner.
1 blood Self 2 h Call up a gale for twelve hours. Aim at range suffers. More successes bring it sooner.
1 blood Self 2 h Call a thunderstorm for twelve hours, or hard snow if it is freezing. Lightning falls where it will. More successes bring it sooner.
1 blood 30 cells 1 h Bring lightning down on a spot under open sky. Whoever stands there is badly burned. A second roll, Perception and Occult, aims it; a miss lands it a few cells away.

Command of lifeless things: the strength of stone, talk with objects, weapons that turn on their owners, the shape of a statue, and spirits of fire, air, earth and water. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Self 8 h Draw on the strength of the stone and metal nearby: about an hour and a half a success of much harder blows and a fifth less harm taken.

1 blood Touch 10 s Talk with the spirit of a thing about what it has seen. A corpse gives up its killer, who stays read for a week (rolls against the killer get two extra dice), and a sealed casket gives up what sleeps inside.

1 blood 20 cells 15 s Wake a thing no bigger than a person and set it moving: a statue walks and pounds with stone fists, a chair or a table scuttles about battering the caster's enemies, a blade on the floor rises and cuts. It moves for an hour a success, then settles where it stands. The caster keeps as many going as its Intelligence. Aimed at someone armed, the weapon in their hands twists free and strikes them once a success instead.
1 blood Self 10 s Take the shape of a statue until dawn, or until choosing to come back. The vampire can't move or act, enemies take it for a thing and pass it by, and blows do half their harm.

1 blood Self 12 h Call a spirit out of the element at hand until dawn: a salamander from a fire within ten cells, a sylph under open sky, a gnome from the soil underfoot, an undine from water within ten cells. More successes make it stronger and harder to master. A botched mastery turns it on the caster; a failed one lets it run wild.
Command of plants, living and dead: asking them what they have seen, quickening growth or rot, vines that seize, a shelter of branches, and trees that walk. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Touch 1 h Touch a plant and ask what it has felt pass by. One success tells whether outsiders are on the map, three name their factions, and five point to every one of them, even those who are hidden.

1 blood Touch 1 h Touch a plant and it grows a fifth of the way to harvest per success. Touch something wooden, or someone holding a wooden weapon, and the wood rots a fifth of its condition per success.

1 blood 22 cells 20 s Make the plants at a spot in sight come alive and seize every enemy within two cells, four seconds a success. A living target can fight free with Willpower. There must be plants there.

1 blood Self 1 h Among thick plants, weave a dome of branches round the caster and sleep in it. It keeps out the sun and anyone the caster doesn't let in, until it chooses to come out. Needs at least eight plants within three cells.

1 blood Touch 12 h Touch a tree and wake it. It pulls up its roots and fights for the caster for about six hours a success, then roots again wherever it stands. Every success costs another blood point, as far as the blood goes.
Command of standing water: seeing what it has seen, binding with it, turning blood to it, raising it as a wall, and drawing it out of a body. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Touch 1 h Look into still water and see who died near it: within twenty cells, back a day, a week, a month, a year or ten years by successes.
1 blood 22 cells 15 s Water rises and wraps round someone standing within five cells of it, holding them four seconds a success. A living target can fight free with Willpower.
1 blood Touch 20 s Touch someone and turn their blood to water. A vampire or ghoul loses a blood point a success. A mortal loses a fifth of its blood a success: three put it down, five kill it.

1 blood, 1 Willpower 25 cells 2 h Standing by water, raise a straight wall of it across the line to a spot in sight, three cells long a success. Nothing walks through it, and it stands until dawn. Costs a Willpower point as well as the blood.

1 blood 22 cells 30 s Pull the water out of someone in sight. Each success they can't fight off with Stamina and Fortitude is a wound no armour stops; a vampire loses blood instead while it has any. The agony may leave them unable to act for a moment.

Slow twisting of a mind, never an order: turning a choice to its worse side, loosing buried vices, cooling every tie, making a need, and tying a soul to the caster's. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood 22 cells 10 s Turn someone in sight from what they meant to do. They drop it and lash out at whoever is near with insults instead. Not in a fight. They resist with Willpower, a vampire with Self-Control.

1 blood 22 cells 1 h Meet someone's eyes and let loose a desire they keep buried: a binge, a sulk alone, a tantrum, a spree of insults. It lasts four hours, half a day, a day, two days or four by successes.
1 blood Touch 4 h Touch someone and cool every tie they have. They turn withdrawn and cold, a third less persuasive, for four hours, half a day, a day, two days or four by successes.

1 blood Touch 12 h Touch someone and leave them needing something: what only the caster's kind can give, the Kiss for a mortal or the blood of other Kindred for a vampire, or any drug the caster chooses, a habit it can then feed for a price.

1 blood 4.9 cells 12 h Talk with someone and tie their soul to the caster's for a day a success. Away from the caster they work and fight worse and get no Willpower back, and they resist the caster's mind powers with only half their will.

Blood magic for war: a scream against fear, blows that can't miss, a dance out of every strike, the strength of a warrior, and all of it shared with comrades. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Self 4 h Scream to the night and steel the heart for four hours: the fear of fire and sun comes a die harder, and minds are a point of Willpower harder to bend.
1 blood Self 8 h Let the blood guide the hand: for four hours, blows land far more often.
1 blood Self 4 h Move like the wind for four hours, out of the way of blows before they are thrown: far more blows dodged.
1 blood Self 4 h Burn the blood of war for four hours: stronger, faster and tougher. Afterwards it has to be rested off, or every hour on its feet costs a blood point for eight hours.
1 blood Touch 5 s Touch an ally and pass on one of the lower powers of Mars the caster knows, for as long as it would last.

Blood magic for machines: understanding them at a touch, burning them out, locking them to all but their owners, taking them over, and reaching any of them through the wires. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Touch 4 h Touch a machine, turret or mechanoid and understand it: what it is and what shape it is in. For four hours a success after, repairs come half again as fast.

1 blood 25 cells 15 s Surge the power through a machine, turret or mechanoid in sight. One or two successes stun it, three break it down, four also wreck half of it, and five destroy it. A mechanoid is stunned, and hurt from four successes.

1 blood Touch 10 s Lock a door so that only its own colonists can open it, for a day per point of the caster's Willpower. No prisoner breaking out, slave or guest gets through. Used on a locked door, it opens it again.
1 blood 25 cells 30 s Reach into a turret or mechanoid in sight with the mind and turn it on its own side for five seconds a success. If it is destroyed while held, the shock hits the caster.
1 blood 999 cells 1 h Send the mind through the wires to any machine on the map, seen or not, and work Burnout, Encrypt or Remote Access on it, whichever the caster knows.

Caine's own curses, spoken from the Book of Nod to a vampire: naming its bonds, ugliness, a diet of ash, pain in the light, and its stolen generations taken back. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood 12 cells 10 s Speak Zillah's verse to a vampire and hear who holds it: everyone it is blood bound to, and everyone it shares a Vinculum with. Until dawn those bonds give their holders no hold over it and it can raise a hand against them, and an outsider's thrall hidden in the colony is found out.
1 blood 12 cells 1 h Speak the crone's curse to a vampire. Until dawn it is hideous, and nobody can be talked round by it.
1 blood 12 cells 12 h Curse a vampire to eat only ashes for a week. Blood comes straight back up, but the ash is enough to wake each night, so it costs nothing to rise.
1 blood 12 cells 12 h Curse a vampire with the dark of the Angel of Death for a week. Any well-lit spot burns it, a little every few seconds.

1 blood 12 cells 1 day Speak the long verse against diablerie, nine seconds of it. For a week the vampire is back at the generation it had before it ever drank another's soul: a smaller pool, less blood a turn, lower limits.
Command over the dead and their ghosts, the art of the Giovanni. It is learned one path at a time, alongside rituals.
The necromancer's first path: seeing the dead and calling them back Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
Self 1 h See the dead who still linger here: who died on this map, how, by whose hand, and where. Each one can be found on the map from the letter.

1 blood 5.9 cells 20 s Call a ghost back to its corpse, or to a grave, for eight hours. It says how it died and who killed it. A colonist's last words reach the people it loved; an outsider may give away a hidden stash. Someone the necromancer killed, or someone the colony killed cruelly, comes back to haunt it instead.

1 blood 14.9 cells 20 s Bind a summoned shade into service: five days for every success beyond its Willpower. A bound shade can be drafted, scouts unseen, and warns of intruders it sees. A necromancer holds as many as its Necromancy rating. A failure costs Willpower.
1 blood 29.9 cells 1 h Tie one of the necromancer's shades to a spot, a night per success. Outsiders who come near may panic and flee; the colony's own people are used to it.
Touch 10 s Strike a shade as if standing among the dead. Anyone else's shade is banished for a month. One of the necromancer's own is cowed into serving a day longer per success.
Power over corpses: making them twitch, setting them to work, raising them to fight, and pulling souls out of the living. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
14.9 cells 10 s Make a corpse twitch, sit up or mutter a word. Outsiders nearby may panic and flee, and the colony's people are unsettled.

1 blood 9.9 cells 20 s Raise a corpse, and one more nearby for each success after the first, as a mindless labourer. It hauls and cleans and nothing else, and falls apart after two days per success. A necromancer keeps up to twice its Necromancy rating of raised dead at once.

1 blood 14.9 cells 30 s Raise a corpse, and one more nearby for each success after the first, to fight. They feel no pain and do nothing but fight. They never tire of it: draft them where they should stand and they stay there, as long as the necromancer lasts, until something cuts them down.

1 blood 9.9 cells 1 h Tear the soul out of a living mortal. The body lies comatose and the soul walks as the necromancer's shade, eight hours for each success beyond the victim's Willpower. If the body dies meanwhile, the soul is left behind as a free ghost that frightens everyone near it.

2 blood 9.9 cells 1 h Put one of the necromancer's shades into a fresh corpse. It gets up with the dead face and the ghost's own name and skills, and works and fights for the necromancer for three days plus a day per success, until the body gives out. A shade put back into its own corpse walks as itself again.
Looking into the land of the dead, speaking with its ghosts, touching them, and stepping into it bodily. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
Self 1 h Look through the shroud between the living and the dead. For a dozen cells around, walls no longer hide what is behind them, and the haunted places on the map are counted.
Touch 20 s Talk with the dead where they lie, without calling them up. Touch a corpse or a grave and its ghost tells how it died and who killed it, the same as a summoned one would.
1 Willpower Self 4 h Reach into the lands of the dead for four hours per success. Shades from outside the colony within ten cells can be seen and struck.

1 blood, 1 Willpower Self 8 h Step bodily into the lands of the dead for a while, about an hour and a half per success. Nobody living can see or target the necromancer, and it can step through up to four cells of wall at a time. It costs blood and Willpower both.

1 blood 29.9 cells 2 h Thicken the shroud around a spot. Other necromancers' ghosts within a dozen cells are banished for a month, and the necromancer's own shades on the map stay a day longer per success.

Sensing the ties between the living and the dead: a ghost's touch, its fetters, places near the lands of the dead, the pull of each new death, and fetters made by hand. Death Knell, the fourth dot, is always on. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
Touch 10 s Touch a person or a thing and feel what the dead have to do with it: whether a ghost is inside it or close by, and whether it anchors one.

1 blood Touch 10 s Handle a thing and learn whether it is a ghost's fetter. With three successes, whose, and knowing its anchor gives the necromancer a hold on it: that ghost resists Compel Soul with two less Willpower from then on.
Self 1 h Feel how close the lands of the dead lie here, from the deaths nearby. Where three or more died close by, the necromancer gets a die more on every roll for six hours. Once an hour.

1 blood, 1 Willpower Touch 2 h Smear blood on a thing or a person in reach and make it the fetter of a ghost of the necromancer's choosing, for a day a success. While it lasts, that ghost can always be called.

The dead body inside the vampire: a corpse's face, a corpse's numbness, the curse of life laid on another, a corpse's immunity to what kills vampires, and a day of near-life. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Self 10 s Take on the look of a corpse until dawn: pale, shrunken and stiff, slower and uglier. Standing still, nobody can tell the vampire from a dead body.
1 blood Touch 10 s Touch another vampire and force the corpse's look on it until dawn: slower, uglier and stiff. It resists with Stamina and Fortitude.
Self 4 h Take on the numbness of the dead for four hours. No pain slows the vampire, minds are a little harder to work on, and it is cold company.

1 Willpower 20 cells 1 h Curse a vampire within twenty cells with the worst of being alive until dawn: hunger, thirst, sweat and worse. Slowed by needs it no longer has, every roll it makes is two harder.

1 Willpower Self 8 h Become more corpse than vampire for about an hour and a half a success: no frenzy and no fear, a stake won't hold, and the sun burns half as hard. Whatever is waiting comes back when it ends.

6 blood Self 1 day Burn six blood to be nearly alive for a day: awake and clear-headed by day, the sun only hurting bare skin and at half, and the Beast quieter. Afterwards it is six nights before frenzy stops coming easily.

The rot that takes all flesh but a vampire's, turned on anything: corpses to dust, the stiffness of death, withered limbs, a plague of the undead, and vampire flesh to ash. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Touch 10 s Drip blood on a human corpse in reach and it crumbles to a heap of dust. No body, no evidence.
1 Willpower 25 cells 15 s Stiffen the muscles of someone within twenty-five cells as if they were dead: held four seconds a success. A living target can fight free with Willpower.

1 Willpower Touch 30 s Touch an arm, a leg, an eye, an ear, the tongue or the face, and wither it: two aggravated wounds, and the part is useless until they heal. A withered eye is blind, a withered tongue mute, a withered face ugly. A mortal never heals them.

1 Willpower 20 cells 12 h Infect a vampire within twenty cells with the plague of the undead, unless it fights it off with Stamina and Fortitude. For up to a week it is weak and slow, rising costs an extra blood, and blood often won't stay down. Drinking from it passes the plague on.

1 blood, 1 Willpower Touch 30 s Drip grave-cursed blood on a vampire in reach and its flesh crumbles to ash: an aggravated wound a success, against its Stamina and Fortitude. Costs a blood point and a Willpower point.

The Lamia's art of the four humours held still in the undead body: nightmares whispered in, a poisoned bite, humours on the skin, a corpse's dead blood drunk, and a breath of despair. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

Touch 12 h Whisper someone's name in their ear and let a breath of bile in with it. Unless they fight it off with Willpower, nightmares and mutterings plague them for days equal to the necromancer's Manipulation: poor sleep, slower work and a die less on every roll.
1 blood Self 40 s Coat the teeth with black bile mixed with blood. The next bite within the hour does twice its harm.

2 blood Touch 20 s Sweat one of the four humours and touch someone with it. Phlegm makes them sluggish, blood makes their wounds bleed twice as fast, yellow bile leaves them no Willpower to call on, black bile wounds them as deep as the necromancer's Stamina. Stamina resists. Costs two blood.

Touch 1 h Drink the dead blood of a corpse one to three days cold. For four hours the body takes blows like dead flesh, a third less harm, and the necromancer can talk with the dead as Lifeless Tongues does. Drinking it shows how close to death everyone within fifteen cells is, and whether they are Kindred, ghoul or mortal. The corpse is left dry.

1 blood, 1 Willpower 10 cells 12 h Breathe out a cloud of despair at a spot close by, two cells across a success. Anyone in it whose will fails against it breaks down, a mortal into a catatonic stupor, a vampire into a day of torpor. Even those who hold are shaken for four hours. Costs a blood and a Willpower point.

The Nagaraja's command of entropy: reading the marks of death, an aura that ruins things, feeding on the dead, death breathed into the living, and a cry heard on both sides of the grave. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

15 cells 10 s Read the marks death has left on someone: what ails and curses them, and with more successes what is likeliest to kill them and how soon. Someone friendly bleeding out within the day can be held back from death for a blood point: the bleeding stops for two hours a success. For a day after, the necromancer's own rolls against them get two extra dice.
1 blood Touch 10 s Let the cold of entropy out onto a thing in reach. It gives out: broken down and nine tenths destroyed. Machines rust, wood rots, plasteel goes brittle.

1 Willpower Touch 1 day Feed on the dead. Aimed at a ghost in reach, drink it dry, as good as blood, and it is gone. Aimed at the necromancer itself, draw a blood point from each death close by in the last day, up to four. Once a night.
1 blood Touch 20 s Breathe the mist of death into someone in reach: an aggravated wound, and until dawn people who don't know death shy away from them.

1 Willpower Self 1 h Scream into both worlds at once, over everyone within a cell per dot of Necromancy. To harm, every foe there takes an aggravated wound a success, and each after the first costs a blood point. To aid, every friend's rolls come easier for a turn a success.
The Tzimisce kolduns' sorcery of the living land, worked through four Ways: earth, wind, water and fire. Only Tzimisce can learn it, and its one ritual is Binding of the Watcher, worked anywhere.
The koldun's command of soil and stone: earth that grips and swallows, skin of stone, the ground's healing, and quakes. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood 20 cells 10 s The soil under someone within twenty cells climbs their legs and holds them, four seconds a success. It only works on someone standing on bare earth. A living target can fight free with Willpower.
1 blood Self 4 h Draw the earth's toughness into the body for four hours. The skin turns to cracked stone, and blows do a third less harm.
1 blood 20 cells 20 s The ground opens under someone on bare earth within twenty cells and swallows them to the waist. They are held three seconds a success and crushed every two.

1 blood 20 cells 1 h The earth takes someone on bare ground into itself, the koldun too, holds them, and closes a wound a success. An aggravated wound takes two successes. Every wound after the first costs another blood point.

1 blood, 1 Willpower 30 cells 12 h Strike the ground and send a quake out from a spot in sight, a cell and a half wider a success. Everyone in it takes a heavy blow, friend or foe, and buildings shake apart; wooden ones three times as fast. Costs a Willpower point too.
The koldun's command of the air: words carried on the wind, freezing and drowsy winds, flight on the gale, and storms. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood 999 cells 10 s Send a word on the wind to anyone on the map, seen or not. The koldun's own people take heart from it; anyone else is unnerved. A prisoner's resistance wears down a little, and a foe in a fight falters for a moment.

1 blood Self 20 s Call a freezing wind round the koldun. While it stands still, every enemy within ten cells moves at half speed, fumbles with its hands and is bitten by the cold every few seconds. Moving stills the wind.
1 blood Self 1 h Send a drowsy wind over every enemy within fifteen cells. Each that fails a Stamina and Plants roll moves and works at half pace for four hours; one that botches falls asleep.
1 blood Self 10 s Become a blur on the wind and fly to any spot under open sky on the map. It can't be done indoors or under a roof.

1 blood, 1 Willpower Self 1 day Call a thunderstorm: it arrives in six hours, an hour sooner a success, and rages four hours a success. While it lasts the koldun can bring lightning down on a foe for a Willpower point. Costs a Willpower point to call.
The koldun's command of water: illusions on its surface, sleep under it, gliding over it, servants raised from it, and whirlpools. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood 25 cells 1.44 h Raise an illusion on a water surface in sight: a decoy, a wall or a turret that draws fire. Anyone who touches it may see through it.
1 blood Self 1 h Sink into water and sleep under it, safe from the sun, as Earth Meld does into soil. It takes two successes.
1 blood Self 10 s From the water's edge, glide out across the water like a ghost to a spot up to twenty-five cells away. Deep water is no obstacle.

1 blood, 1 Willpower Self 12 h Drip blood into water within ten cells and raise undines from it to fight until dawn: one for each blood point spent, up to the successes. Away from water they wear away; in it they mend. Costs a Willpower point too.

1 blood, 1 Willpower 30 cells 12 h Open a whirlpool on water in sight, a cell across a success. Everyone in it is held for up to four hours, until a Strength roll frees them, and anyone who breathes drowns slowly. Costs a Willpower point too.

The koldun's command of fire and molten rock. The first dot takes the fear off fire, a little more with every dot. Then come flames out of the air, walls and floods of magma, and blasts of dry heat. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood 22 cells 15 s The air round someone in sight turns searing and they burst into flame: an aggravated burn a success, and they catch fire.

1 blood Self 1 h The ground splits round the koldun and molten rock wells up in a ring three cells out, for six seconds a success. Anyone who walks into it burns badly, while the koldun inside the ring is safe.
1 blood 22 cells 30 s Breathe a blast of dry heat over someone in sight. It parches them like the desert, a heavy wound, and a vampire loses five blood besides.

1 blood, 1 Willpower 30 cells 12 h Lava bursts from the ground at a spot in sight and spreads two cells round, for nine seconds a success, then cools. Anything in it burns. Costs a Willpower point too.

The Lasombra's study of the darkness beyond shadow. It has no paths, only rituals, each rated up to the lower of Obtenebration and Occult, and each leaves a mark on the caster that never fades. Worked anywhere, on Wits + Occult. Only Lasombra can learn it.

Rituals are longer castings: minutes to hours of work, often with ingredients and a blood cost. - Learning. Rituals are learned by study. The first dot of a sorcery comes with one level 1 ritual. After that a vampire studies them from a teacher who knows them, or from a grimoire or lore text. Study takes a night for level 1 and about a season of nights for level 5. - Level. A vampire can only learn rituals up to its sorcery rating. - Casting. Use the Rituals button on the vampire's gizmo bar. Rituals of level 3 and up need a ritual circle (Misc tab), or an ossuary altar for Necromancy. The roll is Intelligence + Occult against the ritual's level + 3. - Ghouls. A ghoul with a dot of a sorcery path gets a level 1 ritual and a dot of Occult, buys Occult in its Ghoul tab and studies rituals like a vampire, from a vampire or a ghoul who knows them. It pays blood costs from its vitae. A clan's own rites need a domitor of that clan, and a ghoul never learns a ritual that needs Kindred blood: the Ferryman's Recall, Communicate with Kindred Sire, the Gargoyle Rite, Light Within Shadow, Comforting Darkness and Claiming the Dark. A Rafastio revenant casts Thaumaturgy rituals through its family's Path of Blood.

- Stacking. Different wards on one door all burn, each its own kind. The same ward cast again on a door refreshes it and doesn't burn twice. - Seeing them. Each ward draws its own ring in its own colour, one inside the other, and the mouse over a warded cell names them all ("Warded: ghouls, Lupines"). - Removing them. Select a building with the colony's ward and press Scrub the ward. A colonist on cleaning work washes it off. Wards someone else cast stay. - Rebuilt doors. A ward belongs to the building it was cast on. Tear the door down and build another, and the new door is bare.

Four Thaumaturgy rituals ward the ground instead of a door: Warding Circle versus Ghouls (level 2), versus Lupines (3, with Garou loaded), versus Kindred (4) and versus Spirits (5, spirits, ghosts and demons, even in Twilight). Each takes a blood vial for the mortal blood. - Placing it. Pick the ritual and a ring follows the mouse. Click to set the centre, and a strip opens under the ring. The caster walks to the centre to cast. - Size. Scroll, or press Smaller and Larger, for a radius of 2 to 8 cells. Each cell past 2 costs a blood point and adds 1 to the difficulty. Past 9 the difficulty stays at 9 and the cast needs one more success for each point over. - Length. Until dawn, or a year and a day if the caster spends the whole night casting. - Who burns. Every floor cell in the ring burns the warded kind from outside the caster's faction, the same burn as a torpor crypt's floor. The caster's own people walk through.
Sigils drawn in blood around the caster keep the sun out of everywhere within seven cells, roof or no roof, for as long as the caster stays inside.
For the next day the caster wakes clear-headed by day: no daytime sluggishness, and Humanity doesn't cap any roll.
For the next day, the first stake driven at the caster's heart splinters and fails.
Reach the caster's sire across any distance. A sire out in the world sends a few blood vials by drop pod, more with more successes.
Curse a mortal with a coin passed from hand to hand. For a day, everyone who meets them dislikes them.
Knot a cord in the caster's blood and a mortal can't speak of what they saw. They stop counting as a witness, and won't become one again for a season.
Read a vampire's blood: its clan and generation, its sire and further back a generation per success, and every blood bond it carries.
The caster's melee weapon burns as it strikes: each of the next blows, one per success, adds a burn that is aggravated to Kindred. It lasts four hours.
Mark a door or other building with the caster's blood. Any ghoul from outside the colony that stands on or in it is burned.
Seal a point of blood into a small gold bead. Any vampire who crushes it later drinks the point back.
Someone turns translucent and hard to notice for the night. Mortals see what they do from only half as far.
The caster purifies its blood in a chalice. For a day, nobody who drinks from it takes a step toward a blood bond.

Pour a ring of mortal blood round the spot the caster stands on. Any ghoul from outside the colony that stands inside burns. The caster picks the size, from 2 to 8 cells, and whether it lasts until dawn or, cast over a whole night, a year and a day.
Carve a stake whose tip breaks off in a vampire it wounds and works its way to the heart over a few hours. The stake crumbles once it has struck.
For a day, Presence and Passion used on the caster turn back on whoever used them.
For four hours per success, the caster can step through up to four cells of wall or anything else solid.
Shape a small servant from the caster's blood. It hauls and cleans for a day per success, then runs back into a puddle.
For a day the caster's skin burns to the touch. Anyone who strikes it in melee is burned.
Mark a door or other building with the caster's blood and silver dust. Any werewolf from outside the colony that stands on or in it is burned.

A night of blood sorcery that binds a ghoul a second time, to the spot where it stands. The ghoul must already be fully blood bound to a colony vampire. From then on it guards that spot: it goes for any enemy that comes near, looks harder for anyone hidden there, and goes back to it when it has nothing to do. Its skin turns to grey stone. Away from its post it is unhappy, and everywhere its mind is easier to bend. The binding is for good.

Four other Tremere on the map have to put their blood in the cup with the caster's. Whoever drinks is bound for an hour per success to the clan and its goals, and is hard to break. It counts as no drink from any of them.
A red thread runs from the target to everyone it shares a blood bond with, one bond per success. At five successes the caster also sees who is bound to whom.

Pour a ring of mortal blood round the spot the caster stands on. Any werewolf from outside the colony that stands inside burns. The caster picks the size, from 2 to 8 cells, and whether it lasts until dawn or, cast over a whole night, a year and a day.
Mark a door or other building with the caster's blood. Any vampire from outside the colony that stands on or in it is burned.

The caster's heart turns to stone for a day per success. No stake can pierce it and Presence can't move it, but the caster has almost no Conscience left to resist sin with, and no warmth to charm anyone.
Hold an enchanted token to someone and their secrets come out: a thrall serving an outside vampire, or a hunter in disguise.
Animate a stake and send it at someone the caster can point to. It flies straight for the heart, and pins a vampire it hits.

Pour a ring of mortal blood round the spot the caster stands on. Any vampire from outside the colony that stands inside burns. The caster picks the size, from 2 to 8 cells, and whether it lasts until dawn or, cast over a whole night, a year and a day.

The caster binds an object to itself with blood and a long night's work. After a season it settles: it adds two dice to the caster's Thaumaturgy and can hold a few points of blood. It is useless to anyone else, and if it is ever destroyed the caster loses a point of Willpower for good.
The caster and someone of its own faction, or a prisoner, sign in blood. A prisoner who signs joins the colony. Whoever leaves the faction it was signed in, or strikes the other signer, dies.
In a few moments the caster steps out of the world and appears beside the colonist it likes best, on any of the colony's maps. Worked anywhere, no circle needed.

A night of butchery and blood magic that remakes a helpless Gangrel, Nosferatu or Tzimisce as a Gargoyle, with the vitae of a vampire of one of the other two clans close by. It keeps its generation, gains wings, loses its passions and is wholly bound to the caster. Only the Tremere teach it.

A Dur-An-Ki potion of Kindred blood that lets an Assamite lower its Generation despite the Tremere curse. Converts of other clans on the Path of Blood may brew and drink it too. The drinker rolls Willpower at 9 to keep it down, then again each hour until it has fifteen successes. Each failed roll tears at it for lethal damage.

Pour a ring of mortal blood round the spot the caster stands on. Any spirit, ghost or demon from outside the colony that stands inside burns, even unseen in Twilight. The caster picks the size, from 2 to 8 cells, and whether it lasts until dawn or, cast over a whole night, a year and a day.
A mortal starts hearing the whispers of the dead. For hours they can't concentrate and can't shake the dread.
A Black Mass in the Giovanni manner, dedicating its subject to the Endless Night. The subject has two more dice on Necromancy rolls for a day per success.
A mortal sees visions of their own death. For the next few days, terror seizes them now and then and sends them wandering.
Take a hand from a corpse and make it into a candle. Lit, it keeps every sleeping outsider within a dozen cells asleep for hours, for burglary or quiet feeding.
Find what anchors a ghost to this world. While its fetter lasts the ghost can always be called; destroy it and the ghost fades in time.
For a day, a mortal goes cold and grey and smells of the grave. They move slowly, and anyone who sees them would swear they were dead.

The caster reaches into the lands of the dead and pulls something back. Usually a ledger of the dead or a hand of glory; once in a long while an artifact of necromancy. Each extra success improves the odds.

Brings a dead Ghoul back across the river and Embraces it at the ritual's climax, long after the Embrace would normally fail. How long the corpse can have lain depends on the caster's Generation: twelve hours at the 13th, a day at the 12th, up to two weeks at the 6th.

A night of blood sorcery that binds a ghoul a second time, to the spot where it stands. The ghoul must already be fully blood bound to a colony vampire. From then on it guards that spot: it goes for any enemy that comes near, looks harder for anyone hidden there, and goes back to it when it has nothing to do. Its skin turns to grey stone. Away from its post it is unhappy, and everywhere its mind is easier to bend. The binding is for good.

The caster stares into a ball of shadow until its eyes change. A second roll, Perception + Occult at 8: on a success, Sight improves for good and the eyes turn to black pits. A failure can be tried again. A botch hurts the eyes for good. Unlike the book's Merit, the change is always on.

The darkness closes the caster's wounds, for a point of Willpower and a roll of Stamina + Occult at 8. Each success spends a point of blood, whatever the Generation's limit, and heals as two points' worth. The dark then takes twice that blood from everything the caster drinks, and the ritual can't be worked until it's paid. The blood stays nearly black ever after. A botch burns the caster.

The caster cuts itself open and draws the shadows in, a roll of Manipulation + Occult at 8. On a success its skin darkens and it hits harder and moves faster, for as long as it likes. Each day the change costs a point of blood per dot of Obtenebration, or it ends. The sun does triple damage, and the caster is uglier for it. Work the ritual again to let the shadows go. A botch costs a point of blood for each 1 rolled.
A ball of shadow shows the caster every enemy on the map, wherever it hides, and clears the fog around it. For a day after, Sight is reduced by what the caster stared at.

The caster asks the Abyss one question and falls into a sleep nothing can break. A nightly roll of Intelligence + Occult at 9 adds up to the question's rating, and a night with no success stretches the wait to a week between rolls. The answer is true and complete. Each communion leaves the caster stranger to others for good.
Under the hood the mod keeps a Vampire: The Masquerade character sheet for every Kindred. You never roll dice yourself. You see the results in messages and in the roll log (Kindred tab).

A roll is a handful of ten-sided dice, usually an Attribute plus an Ability. Each die at or above the difficulty (often 6) is a success. Each 1 cancels a success. No successes and at least one 1 is a botch, which is worse than a plain failure. Dice decide Discipline powers and resisting them, frenzy, sins, rituals, hunting trips and witnesses noticing things. Ordinary shooting and melee stay on RimWorld's own rules.

Nine Attributes, rated 1 to 5 (higher for low generations). They're worked out from the pawn as it is right now, so they follow whatever happens to it. Attribute Comes from Strength Melee, manipulation, body size, Tough, Brawler Dexterity Shooting, Melee, moving, manipulation, Nimble, Jogger Stamina Health, Tough, Wimp Charisma Social, Kind, Abrasive Manipulation Social, talking, Psychopath, Greedy Appearance Beauty Perception Sight, hearing, Shooting Intelligence Intellectual, consciousness, Too Smart, Slow Learner Wits Consciousness, Social, Intellectual, Nerves Dots bought with experience (Attributes menu in the Kindred tab) sit on top of that. Each dot above 2, bought or not, also gives a vampire stats for good. Older blood gets 5% more from each dot for every generation below the 13th, except Stamina. Hover an Attribute in the Kindred tab to see this vampire's numbers. Attribute Each dot above 2 Strength +8% melee damage, +5 kg carrying capacity Dexterity +2 levels of Melee for hitting and dodging Stamina 5% less damage taken Charisma +4% social impact Manipulation +4% negotiation ability Perception +1 level of Shooting for accuracy Intelligence +4% research speed Wits 4% less time spent aiming Appearance Nothing; it only rolls

Abilities are read from RimWorld skills: skill level ÷ 4, up to 5. Firearms is Shooting, Medicine is Medicine, the social Abilities are Social, and so on. Two are the mod's own and are raised with experience: Stealth and Occult.

Virtue Used for Path version Conscience Sin rolls Conviction Self-Control Resisting frenzy Instinct Courage Resisting Rötschreck Courage Rolled at the Embrace from traits: kind pawns get more Conscience, iron-willed ones more Self-Control, tough ones more Courage.

Willpower starts equal to Courage. - Spending it: one automatic success on a roll, a moment of control in a frenzy, a day free of a derangement or clan compulsion, and the cost of some powers. - Getting it back: a full, safe daysleep, and a good-mood day. - Policy. Each vampire spends Willpower by itself according to its policy: never, to resist frenzy (the default), or freely.

Most vampires get one Merit or Flaw at the Embrace (or pick one in the making menu). They can't be bought later. A Flaw that repeats the clan's weakness is never rolled. Merit What it is Efficient Digestion Gets more out of blood than most: half again as much from every feeding. Light Sleeper Wakes by day at once and clear-headed: no daytime sluggishness, and Humanity doesn't cap any roll. Early Riser Always up first: rises at dusk as if its Humanity were perfect. Blush of Health Still has the colour of the living. However low its Humanity falls, it never looks like a corpse. Calm Heart Slow to anger. Two more dice to resist frenzy. Eat Food Can sit down to a meal like a mortal without forcing it down. It still has to come back up later. Acute Sense One sense is unusually sharp. A little better at shooting and spotting. Ambidextrous Uses either hand as well as the other. Hits a little more often in melee. Bruiser Looks like trouble. Better at getting prisoners and mortals to do as they're told. Catlike Balance Sure on its feet. Dodges a little more often. Friendly Face Has the kind of face people trust. Slightly better with people. Enchanting Voice A voice people want to keep listening to. Daredevil Takes wild chances and gets away with them. Hits harder and dodges more, though a rough fight hurts more too. Huge Size Very large. Tougher and stronger, and easy to spot. Coldly Logical Weighs things without feeling. Harder to shake. Common Sense Knows a bad idea when it hears one. Concentration Isn't distracted when it matters. Aims a little faster and works a little steadier. Introspection Understands its own mind better than most. Time Sense Always knows the hour, to the minute. Useful Knowledge Knows something worth knowing, and learns faster for it. Code of Honor A personal code that holds up under pressure. Eidetic Memory Remembers everything it sees and hears. Learns a fifth faster and forgets skills at half the speed. Precocious Learns fast. Natural Leader People follow it. Harmless Nobody thinks it worth worrying about. Former Ghoul Served a vampire before the Embrace and knows the world it joined. Bullyboy Known as muscle, and used to it. Scholar of Others Has studied a kind of creature that isn't Kindred. Deceptive Aura Its aura is bright and healthy, like a mortal's. Healing Touch Its bite closes without a trace, and its hands are gentle. Inoffensive to Animals Animals don't mind it. Medium Hears the dead when they speak. Magic Resistance Magic slides off it, friendly or not. Lucky Things go its way more often than they should. Oracular Ability Sees signs in everything. Spirit Mentor A ghostly teacher looks out for it. True Love Someone mortal loves it, and that holds it together. Nine Lives Keeps surviving what should kill it. Thousand Meter Killer A sniper of the Assassin's Club. Shoots more accurately at long range. Dynamic Personality Mortals are drawn to it like groupies to a rock star. Drug Resistance Years of vices have built a tolerance. Addictive Blood Its blood is the perfect drug. Setite Initiate Joined the Followers of Set from another clan, with the cult's contacts behind it. Hive-Minded Its Animalism reaches insects too. Skald Remembers oral histories word for word. Lesser Mark of the Beast Keeps some say over how the Beast marks it. Totemic Change Its animal shapes are flexible, and all of them fit it well. Cannibal Human meat brings it joy, for what that's worth. Mortuario Died and came back through the Ferryman's Recall. Two more dice on Necromancy rolls. Sanguine Incongruity Doesn't carry the Giovanni's painful Kiss. Court Favorite Knows how to tip a Court of Blood. Eyes of Shadow Meeting its eyes is like staring into the Abyss. Bigger Boys Came Knows whose name to drop when someone leans on it. Call of the Sea At home with the tides. A little steadier. Controllable Night Sight Sees through the deepest shadow. Aura of Command Born to give orders. King or Queen of Shadow Draws strength from what it still feels for the kine. Long-Term Planning Every action is part of a plan. Instrument of God Believes the Lord works through it, and acts like it. Distracting Aura Its aura is close to unreadable. Prophetic Dreams Remembers its day dreams, and some come true. Cold Read Learns more than it should from a first meeting. Foul Blood Its blood is so vile that even drinking it is a struggle. Lizard Limbs Can shed a limb to escape and grow it back. Long Fingers Long, graceful fingers, good at fine work. Monstrous Maw A huge mouth of sharp teeth. Piscine Comfortable in water, even sewage. Slimy Secretes a slippery ooze. Hard to hold. Tunnel Rat Knows every way under the ground. Sleep Unseen Keeps Obfuscate up while it sleeps. Tough Hide Skin like a rhino's. False Reflection Its Obfuscate fools cameras too. Patagia Leathery flaps let it glide. Rugged Bad Looks Hideous, but might pass for human in the right light. Antitoxin Blood Immune to most drugs and poisons. Brahmin A priest or teacher among the Ravnos. Kshatriya A warrior or ruler among the Ravnos. Legerdemain Quick hands and card tricks. Mute Devotion The beasts it has spoken with stay loyal. Vaishya A trader by birth. Critters Animals want to be its friend. Heart of Needles Too jaded by its own illusions to be moved. Indelible Tattoos and piercings stay after the Embrace. Impressive Restraint Hunger barely moves it near mortals. Master of the Masquerade Remembers to breathe, blink and fidget. Slowed Degeneration Humanity comes hard to lose. Embraced without the Cup The elders' blood had no hold on it. Keys to the Library A chantry librarian with the run of its lore. Outside Haven Trusted to sleep outside the chantry. Quartermaster Runs a chantry's stores. Bioluminescence Can make its flesh glow. Pain Tolerance Shuts off its nerves. Dracon's Temperament A whirlwind of moods that keeps it on its feet. Promethean Clay Its flesh changes almost before it asks. Connoisseur Reads character in a vessel's blood. Personal Masquerade Has other vampires believing it has a clan. Unbondable No blood bond will ever take hold of it. Consanguineous Resistance No one of its own Giovanni blood can bind it. Flaw What it is Prey Exclusion Refuses to feed on one kind of person, picked at the Embrace. A frenzy doesn't care. Deep Sleeper Sleeps like the dead it is. Woken by day, it stays slow and heavy a step longer than others. Short Fuse Easily angered. Frenzy is two harder to resist. Thin Blood Weak blood that goes nowhere. Every point spent on powers or healing costs two, the blood bonds no one who drinks it, and an Embrace takes only one time in five. Slow Healing Wounds close grudgingly. Healing with blood costs twice as much. Smell of the Grave Smells of damp earth, always. People keep their distance. Infertile Vitae Something went wrong at the Embrace. Anyone it tries to Embrace simply dies. Its blood works for everything else. Hard of Hearing Doesn't hear well. Bad Sight Sees poorly, near or far. Disfigured A disfigurement that nobody forgets. Dulled Bite Weak fangs. Feeding tears at the vessel more than it should, and the bite does less in a fight. Infectious Bite Bites fester. The vampire's own wounds and its vessels are harder to keep clean. One Eye Has only one working eye. Open Wound A wound that never closes, leaking blood. Addiction Needs a drug it can only get through its vessels' blood. On edge most of the time. Deformity A misshapen body that slows it and turns heads. Glowing Eyes Eyes that shine in the dark, for anyone to see. Lame A bad leg. Walks slowly and fights badly on its feet. Lazy Does as little as it can get away with. Monstrous Plainly not human. Permanent Fangs The fangs never go back in. Permanent Wound Rises each night with the same wound, and carries it all night. Disease Carrier Carries sickness in its blood, and the people around it pay for it. Deaf Can't hear anything. Mute Can't speak. Flesh of the Corpse Dead flesh that stays dead. It takes damage like any corpse and looks like one. Blind Can't see. Impatient Hates waiting. Nightmares Bad dreams every day. It wakes tired of itself. Shy Hates being looked at. Soft-Hearted Can't stand to see suffering. Speech Impediment Trouble getting words out. Lunacy The moon pulls at its mind. Phobia Terrified of one thing, and never far from it in thought. Territorial Can't stand strangers in its space. Thirst for Innocence Innocent blood calls to it. On edge around the blameless. Vengeful Can't let a wrong go. Weak-Willed Gives in easily. Guilt-Wracked Everything it has done weighs on it. Laughingstock Nobody takes it seriously, or ever will. Cold Breeze A chill follows it from room to room. Touch of Frost Plants wilt and frost forms where it touches. Repulsed by Garlic The smell turns its stomach. Harder to keep its nerve. Beacon of the Unholy Everyone devout can tell what it is. Deathsight Sees rot and death in everything. Eerie Presence Mortals feel something wrong about it. Lord of the Flies Flies follow it everywhere. Haunted A ghost won't leave it alone. Repelled by Crosses Holy symbols hurt to look at. Grip of the Damned Its embrace is cold and terrible. Nobody wants it near. Dark Fate It knows it will end badly, and soon. Light-Sensitive Even a lamp hurts. It sees poorly and burns easily. Outcast Rejected by its caste, and worse with people for it. Broken Antitribu An Assamite who still bears the Tremere curse and has pledged to the Sabbat anyway. Multiple Curses Carries a second Assamite curse. Obvious Predator The rage shows, and mortals fear it on sight. Scales Set marked it with a patch of scales. Venomous Bite Venom glands in the mouth. Its bite in a fight is deadlier, and feeding is dangerous for mortals. Forked Tongue A forked, flickering tongue, hard to hide. Heartless Its heart lies somewhere else, out of its hands. Aura of the Typhon Something coils in its essence that draws Lupines. Member of the Pack Only one kind of beast will listen to it. Rat in a Cage Being penned in brings on real panic. Inbred Generations of cousins marrying left their mark. Shadow Walker Half in the Shadowlands. It struggles to touch the living world. Uncontrollable Night Sight Sees into shadow, but any light is close to blinding. Insubordinate Does the opposite of what it's told, on principle. Unproven Has yet to prove itself worthy of the name. Paper Trail Asylum or prison records that won't go away. Stigmata Phantom wounds that seep blood. Infectious Madness passes in its bite. Overstimulated Notices everything, and is easily distracted. Dead Inside Feels nothing but pain and numbness. Stench Stinks so badly even Nosferatu keep away. Anosmia Has no smell or taste left. Parasitic Infestation Crawling with ticks and leeches. Bestial Closer to the animals than to people. Enemy Brood Another brood of Nosferatu hunts it from one sanctuary to the next. Putrescent Slowly rotting and fragile. Contagious Full of noxious spores that sicken mortals near it. Incoherent Can't speak so anyone understands. Chandala Of the lowest jati, and treated that way. Flawed Reality Its illusions always have a tell. Oathbreaker Broke its word, and other Ravnos know. Lost Svadharma Failed its destiny, and it won't come again. Tortured Artist Nothing it makes is ever good enough. Private Life Keeps a whole second life, and the secret wears on it. Arcane Curse A magical curse, from its studies or someone else's. Cloistered Has seen little outside the chantry. Betrayer's Mark Loyal, but branded with the antitribu mark. Bound to the Clan Fully blood bound to Clan Tremere. Unblinking Its eyes never close. Ancestral Soil Dependence Sleeps badly without soil from a homeland it has never seen. Faceless Wakes with a new face every night. Privacy Obsession Can barely make itself cross a threshold uninvited. Consumption Something inside is eating it. Uncommon Vitae Preference Its taste is rare even for a Ventrue. Fangless Never grew fangs. Ignorance Its sire left it knowing nothing. Mage Blood Blood so tied to magic that it can learn no Discipline but blood sorcery: Thaumaturgy, Necromancy, Koldunic Sorcery or Abyss Mysticism. Thaumaturgically Inept Magic won't work for it. It can never learn Thaumaturgy. Bulimia Blood makes it sick, and it needs blood.

Every vampire belongs to the clan of its sire. The clan decides three in-clan Disciplines (cheaper to learn), a weakness, and a calling: one thing the clan is good for in a colony. Weaknesses are full strength by default. The "soften clan weaknesses" setting gives each a milder form.
The thirteen clans and the Caitiff

Clan Disciplines Sect In short Brujah Celerity, Potence, Presence Camarilla Rebels and firebrands, quick to anger and quicker to act. They argue for every cause and fight for most of them. Gangrel Animalism, Fortitude, Protean Camarilla Loners and wanderers, closer to the Beast than other Kindred. Animals accept them, and each frenzy leaves its mark. Nosferatu Animalism, Obfuscate, Potence Camarilla Twisted into monsters by the Embrace. They live hidden, trade in secrets and hear everything first. Toreador Auspex, Celerity, Presence Camarilla Artists and patrons who chase beauty, sometimes to the point of losing themselves in it. Ventrue Dominate, Fortitude, Presence Camarilla Rulers by habit and by right, or so they say. Each can feed on only one kind of mortal. Assamite Celerity, Obfuscate, Quietus Independent Assassins from the mountain fortress of Alamut, bound by an old curse that makes other Kindred's blood burn them. Followers of Set Obfuscate, Presence, Serpentis Independent Priests of a dark god who deal in vice and secrets. The sun hates them more than most, and bright light dazzles them. Lasombra Dominate, Obtenebration, Potence Sabbat Proud masters of shadow who cast no reflection. Born to lead, or so they tell everyone. Malkavian Auspex, Dementation, Obfuscate Camarilla Every one of them is mad, and some see more clearly for it. Their warnings make sense afterwards, mostly. Ravnos Animalism, Chimerstry, Fortitude Independent Wanderers, tricksters and illusionists, each in the grip of one vice they can rarely refuse. Tzimisce Animalism, Auspex, Vicissitude Sabbat Old lords of the eastern mountains and masters of flesh. They must sleep near earth from home or lose themselves night by night. Tremere Auspex, Dominate, Thaumaturgy Camarilla Wizards who stole immortality and made blood magic of it. They answer to a strict pyramid of elders and bond to them more easily than other Kindred. Giovanni Dominate, Necromancy, Potence Independent A Venetian family of merchants and necromancers who Embrace their own relatives. Their bite brings agony instead of pleasure. Caitiff None in-clan Any Vampires with no clan. Their blood carries no clan's gifts and no clan's curse, and no clan will claim them.

Clan Weakness Calling Assamite Other Kindred's blood burns them instead of feeding them, and they can't commit diablerie Contracts. Assassination missions only they can take, paid in silver and boons Brujah Frenzy is harder to resist, and Willpower can't stop it Firebrand. Wins mortals round and recruits prisoners faster Followers of Set Sunlight hurts more, and bright light costs a die on every roll and slows work Tempter. Drugs given to outsiders make them strings, quickly Gangrel Each frenzy leaves an animal feature: fur, eyes, claws, ears, skittishness. Some become permanent Wanderer. A caravan with a Gangrel feeds its Kindred from game Giovanni Their bite hurts: no Kiss, a scream that wakes sleepers, twice the blood loss Family business. Better trade prices, and they can sell corpses Lasombra No reflection. Mortals near mirrors or still water may notice Kingmaker. Whoever they back at court rises faster Malkavian One derangement that can never be cured Insight. Cryptic warnings before some threats arrive. Sometimes wrong Nosferatu Hideous. Any outsider who sees one undisguised is a witness Secrets. Hears court news first and can sell secrets for boons Ravnos A vice (theft, deceit or cruelty) they act on when the chance comes, unless they pass a roll Swindler. Once per trade visit, one much better deal. Sometimes caught Toreador Excellent art can leave them standing entranced Patron. Their art earns standing at court and at Elysium Tremere Blood bonds take hold of them one step faster The Pyramid. A yearly tithe; in return, rituals and cheaper Thaumaturgy Tzimisce Must sleep near earth from home, or every pool halves night after night Fleshcrafter. Better surgery Ventrue Can drink from only one kind of mortal (men, the old, soldiers, prisoners and so on) Rule. Holds more strings on mortals, and they're found out less Caitiff No weakness, but no clan: every Discipline costs a bit more, and sect Kindred scorn them None Compulsions (Toreador, Ravnos, Malkavian) never fire while the vampire is drafted, fighting or fleeing, and come at most every few days.

A Tzimisce (Old Clan Tzimisce too) needs earth from home nearby when they sleep. Home is the map they were Embraced on. If they arrived already a vampire, it's the map they were on when the game first checked them. 1. On that map, build a crafting spot and add the make sack of earth bill. It takes only work, no materials. 2. Put the sack in the room where the Tzimisce sleeps (it has to be indoors), or have them carry it in their inventory. The check happens after each full daysleep. Each day spent without the soil adds a step of far from home soil, up to four: every dice pool halves again and work gets worse. One daysleep beside the soil clears it. "Soften clan weaknesses" in the settings stops it at the first step. Each sack remembers where it was dug, and its inspect pane names the place. A sack from any other map doesn't count. The Urn of the Old Country, a Tzimisce relic, counts as native soil anywhere on the map it's on.

Each clan has an inspiration of its own, three times as likely as a vanilla one for its members: Clan Inspiration Effect Assamite The hunter's patience Sneakier hunting, faster melee Brujah Righteous fury Melee hits harder and faster Followers of Set The tempter's tongue Social impact up, drugs sell for more Gangrel Call of the wild Faster movement, better taming and training Giovanni The family business Better trade prices Lasombra The shadows' favour Faster, more accurate shooting Malkavian Strange clarity Research much faster Nosferatu Ear to the walls Better negotiation and prices Ravnos Wanderer's luck Faster movement, carries more Toreador Rapture of beauty Social impact and beauty up Tremere Hunger for knowledge Learns and reads much faster Tzimisce The flesh obeys Better surgery and tending Ventrue Born to rule Better negotiation and arrests

Kindred bring old grudges into the colony: a small opinion modifier between two vampires. Everyone likes their own clan a little. Tzimisce and Tremere hate each other most. Brujah and Ventrue, Gangrel and Ravnos, and Toreador and Nosferatu don't get along. Most clans are a little wary of the Tremere, Setites, Ravnos, Giovanni and Caitiff. A blood bond or the sire-childe tie easily outweighs any of this.

Rare lines with their own Disciplines and weaknesses. They turn up among NPCs, sleepers and raiders, and you can pick them in the making menu. Clan Disciplines Sect In short Samedi Fortitude, Obfuscate, Thanatosis None Walking corpses from the Caribbean who work as killers for hire. Their flesh rots and sloughs and grows back, and they smell like it. Harbingers of Skulls Auspex, Fortitude, Necromancy Sabbat Shrunken, grinning corpses who say they were dead for five hundred years. All of them are elders, all of them are Sabbat, and they know the dead better than the Giovanni do. Nagaraja Auspex, Dominate, Necromancy None Flesh-eating necromancers, nearly hunted out of existence. They have jagged teeth in place of fangs, need flesh as well as blood, and tear it with every feeding. True Brujah Potence, Presence, Temporis None Cold, patient scholars who say they are the real heirs of Brujah, robbed by Troile. They feel less with every year, and time itself bends for them. Salubri Auspex, Fortitude, Obeah None Healers with a third eye, hunted since the Tremere drank their founder. Only a handful are left, seeking Golconda, and taking blood from the unwilling costs them dearly. Daughters of Cacophony Fortitude, Melpominee, Presence None Singers, nearly all of them women, who hear music every moment of the night. Their songs can lift a crowd, drive a listener mad or speak in an ear miles away. The music in their heads makes them a little deaf to everything else. Baali Daimoinon, Obfuscate, Presence None Infernalists who believe the world is doomed and work to hurry it along. Every other Kindred wants them destroyed. They can't bear holy things, and True Faith hurts them twice over. Gargoyles Flight, Fortitude, Potence, Visceratika Camarilla Grey, winged things made by the Tremere out of other Kindred to be guards and slaves. Many have broken free and joined the Camarilla. None can pass for human, and their minds were made to obey. Blood Brothers Fortitude, Potence, Sanguinus Sabbat Sabbat shock troops made by sorcery out of kidnapped mortals, stripped of their selves and given matching faces. A circle of them shares one mind and one pain. They can't make childer: an Embrace only kills. Line Weakness Baali Holy symbols and True Faith hurt them twice as much. Every clan hates them Blood Brothers Can't Embrace (the mortal dies). They share each other's pain Daughters of Cacophony Music always in their ears: worse hearing and sight Gargoyles Hideous and weak-willed against mind control. Made by a Tremere rite Harbingers of Skulls Corpse-like and hideous Kiasyd Iron (steel) weapons burn them and can send them into frenzy Nagaraja Need flesh as well as blood: their feeding tears wounds, and they weaken without it Salubri Feeding on an unwilling vessel costs Willpower Samedi Rotting and hideous True Brujah Conscience rolls are harder, and Virtues and Humanity cost double experience

These lines are gone from the world. You'll only meet them as sleepers in ancient caskets and in torpor crypts, but they join and Embrace like anyone else. Clan Disciplines Sect In short Tremere antitribu Auspex, Dominate, Thaumaturgy Sabbat Tremere who went over to the Sabbat and were marked as traitors. One night every one of them burned. Only those asleep somewhere far away might be left. Ahrimanes Animalism, Presence, Spiritus None Gangrel women remade by a shaman's working into something that speaks with spirits. Their blood is dead: it makes no childer, no ghouls and no bonds. The line vanished in the 1990s. Anda Animalism, Fortitude, Protean None Mongol warriors of the Gangrel blood who rode with the hordes and guarded their tribes. They can't stay put: a few days sleeping in one place and they begin to fail. None have been seen since the fall of the Khans. Cappadocians Auspex, Fortitude, Necromancy None The clan of death-scholars that the Giovanni swallowed whole in the fifteenth century. Pale as corpses, and paler with age. A few may still lie asleep somewhere the Giovanni never found. Lamia Fortitude, Necromancy, Potence None The Cappadocians' guardians, women devoted to the Dark Mother, who died defending their masters from the Giovanni. Their bite carries a plague. Noiad Animalism, Auspex, Protean None Gangrel shamans of the far north who read the will of the gods in the northern lights and guarded their tribe jealously. They can't feed on animals at all. Telyavelic Tremere Auspex, Presence, Thaumaturgy None Tremere who went to pagan Lithuania, were taken for gods of the dead and came to believe it. Christian faith frightens them as it did their flock. The clan says they were wiped out in the sixteenth century. Lhiannan Animalism, Ogham, Presence None Pagan witches of the British forests, each carrying a shard of an old forest spirit. They are bound to their own woods and grow uneasy away from them, and mortals feel there is something wrong about them. The Inquisition burned the last of them, or so it is said.

The Children of Osiris aren't a clan. A sleeper of any clan but the Followers of Set may be one: it keeps its clan, and gains Bardo as an in-clan Discipline. Disciplines are the powers of the blood. Each has dots from 1 to 7. Every dot unlocks a power on the vampire's gizmo bar, and some Disciplines also give an always-on bonus that grows with dots.

- Dots. A new vampire places three dots among its clan's Disciplines. More come from experience (see Character sheet). - The cap. Most vampires stop at 5. Dots 6 and 7 are the elder powers, open only to the 7th generation and lower (6 at the 7th, 7 at the 6th). - In-clan or not. In-clan Disciplines cost less. Learning one from outside the clan needs a teacher, and that means tasting the teacher's blood (a blood bond step). Celerity, Fortitude and Potence can be self-taught at a higher price. Caitiff pay the same middling price for everything. - Cost. Most powers cost blood, some Willpower, some nothing. The physical Disciplines' surges spend blood within the vampire's per-turn limit. - Rolls. Many powers roll dice, usually an Attribute plus an Ability. Mental powers are contests against the target's Willpower or a Virtue. Results show in the roll log. - The Masquerade. Every power is either quiet, subtle, or overt. Subtle and overt powers used in front of outsiders can make witnesses. See The Masquerade and hunters. - Forms. Shapeshifting powers (Protean, Vicissitude, Obtenebration and others) put the vampire's gear away while it's changed. - Body-leaving. Possession, Subsume the Spirit and Psychic Projection leave the vampire's body asleep while its mind is elsewhere. Protect the body.
