Self 1 h A song that makes everyone near feel what the singer wants. Friends are moved for a day; each success sends a fifth of the foes in earshot running.
24.9 cells 30 s Sing someone into madness. If the song beats their will, they gain a derangement for a night, and a night more for each extra success. It leaves when the song wears off.
1 blood Self 2 h The siren's song for a whole crowd: every enemy within earshot has to fight off the madness. A blood point covers five listeners, and one more for every five after.

1 blood 12 cells 10 s A song, even a lullaby, that splits skin and cracks bone in one listener up to twelve cells away. Each success is an aggravated wound no armour stops. Stamina + Artistic against the target's Stamina and Fortitude.
1 blood 12 cells 1 h Leave a Shattering Crescendo hanging over a spot for up to five days. The colony walks through it untouched; the first enemy to step in hears it all at once.

The Kiasyd's fae-like powers: lies laid bare, hidden purposes seen, memories drawn out of objects, sigils that leave a mind lost, and riddles that hold it fast. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
4.9 cells 1 h Talk to someone and hear the lie in what they say. A thrall of an outside vampire, or a Sabbat plant, is found out. For a day the vampire's own rolls against them get two extra dice.

24.9 cells 20 s Look at someone with eyes that see magic other than the dead's. A hunter's purpose shows plainly, and so does True Faith. For a day the vampire's own rolls against them get two extra dice.

Touch 10 s Handle a thing and soak up what was done with it, as the Spirit's Touch does. A corpse gives up its killer, who stays read for a week (rolls against the killer get two extra dice), and a sealed casket gives up what sleeps inside.
Touch 1 h Draw a sigil on someone that leaves them lost and slow-witted: four hours, a night, a week, a month or a year, by successes. An enemy wanders off, not knowing where it is going.
4.9 cells 4 h Whisper a riddle that takes over someone's mind. They stand and think about it, four hours for each success, and only harm breaks them out of it.

24.9 cells 1 h Take everything someone knows. They stand empty, and the Kiasyd has their two best skills at their level, for four hours to a season by successes. Perception and Social against their Willpower.

24.9 cells 1 day Take skill for good: a level per net success moves from the target's best skill to the Kiasyd, never past the target's own level. Anyone who resists is out of this Kiasyd's reach for good. Perception and Social against their Willpower.

The Salubri gift of healing: reading the body by touch, easing pain, closing wounds, a ring no enemy may cross, and minds set right again. It opens a third eye in the forehead. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Touch 5 s A touch reads the body: what it is, then with more successes its wounds, its blood and its diseases. The hands stay surer at tending for four hours after, and with two successes the body fights off disease a quarter faster for a day. For a day the healer's own rolls against them get two extra dice.
1 blood Touch 10 s A touch takes a friend's pain away for a while. A mortal who isn't a friend can be put to sleep, if the vampire's will beats theirs. Kindred are beyond it.
Touch 5 s Lay hands on wounds and they close, as the third eye opens. Each blood point heals a good cut; aggravated wounds take twice the blood. Up to three points a touch, on the living or the dead.

2 Willpower Self 5.76 h For a few minutes, an unseen ring three steps wide surrounds the vampire. An enemy who steps into it is thrown back and stunned, unless its will beats the vampire's by a long way. Guns still reach in.
2 blood 2.9 cells 1 h A long, quiet talk that lifts one derangement from someone. It can't touch a Malkavian's own madness, which is in the blood.

24.9 cells 1 day Draw a willing vampire's soul into the third eye and mend it. They sleep a day and wake with a point of Humanity back, up to their Conscience plus Self-Control. It costs the Salubri a dot of Willpower for good.
1 Willpower Touch 1 h A touch and a moment's concentration close every wound, aggravated ones too. Lost limbs stay lost. Works on the Salubri as well.
Hiding in plain sight, the art of the Nosferatu and the Malkavians Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

Self 1 s Fade from notice, the way the Nosferatu and the Malkavians have for centuries. At Obfuscate 1 it only holds while standing still out of bright light; from Obfuscate 2 it holds on the move, anywhere. Attacking breaks it, and it can't start while an enemy is watching. Use again to step out.
Self 1 s Wear an ordinary mortal face: no corpse-like look, and a Nosferatu passes for human. Or wear one particular person's face and build, after a good look at them. Use again to drop it.

Self 30 s Vanish in the middle of a fight, in plain sight. Enemies within six cells are dazed for a moment, their minds unsure of what they just saw. Mortals within fifteen cells who saw it may forget the vampire was ever there, and are no longer witnesses: Charisma and Social, and the successes have to beat each one's Willpower.
Self 30 s Spread the cloak over everyone close by: the vampire and its people within three cells all fade from sight together.
1 blood Touch 4 h A touch, and an enemy drops out of everyone's notice, their own side included. For four hours they are unseen and wander about lost. Wits and Social against their Willpower.
Command of shadow, the Lasombra's gift: shadows that shield, darkness that blinds, tentacles from the abyss, and at last a body made of night. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Self 40 s Make the shadows cling and writhe around the vampire for four hours. Bullets and arrows do 40% less damage, and blows find less to hit.
1 blood 24.9 cells 30 s Call up the darkness of the Abyss over a spot, four cells across each way. Nobody sees through it or shoots well inside it. Only fire still burns in it.

1 blood 24.9 cells 1 h Raise tentacles of shadow at a spot. Every enemy within three cells is held fast, unable to act, and squeezed every two seconds for ten seconds. Each squeeze a victim may tear loose with Strength and Potence against the vampire's Obtenebration.

2 blood Self 4 h Become a thing of shadow for four hours: tentacles of darkness that strike with a cold touch, harder to hurt, and so terrible to see that enemies within eight cells who fail to hold their nerve run. Charisma and Social against each enemy's Willpower.

1 blood Self 40 s Become living shadow for four hours. Nothing physical can touch it and it slips under any door, but it can't strike a blow or work, and sunlight and fire burn it half again as hard. Other powers still work.
15 cells 10 s Step into one shadow, through the Abyss, and out of another up to fifteen cells away. Walls don't matter; the place stepped into has to be dark.

1 blood Self 1 h The vampire's shadow peels off the floor and fights beside it, four hours per success and never past dawn. It hits and is hurt at half strength, except by fire and fangs. If it is destroyed, the vampire loses half its Willpower and must face down Rötschreck. Willpower at 8.

The Lhiannan's blood magic, worked through runes drawn in vitae: woods that fight for them, war spirits in the skin, curses, the blessings of moon and sun, and the life of the earth drunk dry. Weaker away from home. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Self 4 h Bleed onto the plants underfoot and wake them. For a few minutes, enemies among the plants nearby are tangled and slowed, and lashed the first time they're caught. Up to three blood points: the more, the wider the grove.

1 blood Self 4 h Paint war runes in blood across the skin and let the spirits of battle in. For four hours pain matters less with each success, frenzy is easier to hold back, and the next melee blow lands much harder.
3 blood 24.9 cells 1 h Write someone's name in blood on the skin and let them see it. For a day a mortal is sick and weak. A vampire's blood won't answer it for anything but keeping it going.
3 blood Touch 1 h Trace the sun's sign on a vampire's skin, the caster's own or a friend's. Until dawn, sunlight and fire do half their harm to it.

1 blood Touch 1 h Trace the moon's sign on a vampire's skin. Until dawn it has the gift of the moon's phase: deft at the new moon, quick-witted at the crescent, sharp-eyed at the half, charming at the gibbous, strong at the full. It also makes frenzy a little harder to resist.

1 blood 4.9 cells 1 day Drain the life out of fertile ground. Until dawn every roll gets two extra dice for each success, as many successes as the soil is rich allows. The ground around turns to sand and every plant on it dies.

3 blood Self 5 days Bleed for the spirit-shard until it gives up the name of a great beast, and call it. A thrumbo comes to the map and fights at the Lhiannan's side for three days, then goes back to the wild. Intelligence + Occult at 9.

Strength far past a living body's. Blows hit harder, loads weigh less, and doors give way. *Always on:* Strength past anything living, the kind that tears doors off their hinges. Blows land harder and loads weigh less. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Self 8 h Burn blood into the muscles and hit with the strength of the Blood: melee blows land much harder for four hours. From Potence 3 they stagger, from 4 they stun, and at 5 they hit twice as hard again.
1 blood Touch 5 s Grip a wall, a door or a machine and tear it apart like wet cardboard.
1 blood 21 cells 10 s Strike the ground, and the blow bursts up out of the earth under someone up to 21 cells away. It hits like a Surge punch and stuns for a moment.
The Blood's pull on every heart nearby Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

Self 1 s Let the vampire's Presence fill the room. Everyone nearby is drawn to it: better opinions, a stronger social impact and slightly better trade prices while it lasts. At a party, every guest enjoys the evening more. A mortal who hurts the vampire must win against its Presence once, or lower their weapon and trail after it for a few seconds. Use it again to let the pull fade.

24.9 cells 15 s Let the Beast into the face: fangs out, eyes gone animal. A target who loses their nerve runs in terror for a short while, and one who is badly beaten drops their weapon. Charisma and Social against the target's Willpower.

24.9 cells 4 h Become, for one person, the most wonderful thing they have ever seen. If it works they stop fighting and trail after the vampire for a few minutes, and think far better of it for days. A faction leader or trader won over this way brings their people round to the colony too. Appearance and Social against the target's Willpower.

1 blood 500 cells 4 h Call one person, and they will come. Anyone on the map heads for the vampire, wherever they are. Cast on the vampire itself, it reaches anyone the colony has met elsewhere: they walk in from the edge of the map, come to the vampire, then go about their business, or attack if they are an enemy. The colony's own come at once; anyone else has to fail to resist. Charisma and Social against the target's Willpower.

1 Willpower Self 12 h Spend Willpower and wear the full majesty of the Blood. Enemies within nine cells who fail to resist can't bring themselves to strike and back away in fear, and friends there feel braver for hours. Charisma and Social against each enemy's Willpower.
24.9 cells 10 s One look, and the target freezes in terror until someone hurts them: ten seconds per net success. Manipulation and Social against their Willpower.
1 blood Self 1 day Let the Blood settle on everyone of the colony within ten cells. For a night they feel on the same side: no social fights, and a better mood.
The body as clay for the Beast: eyes that see in the dark, claws, sinking into the earth, the shapes of wolf and bat, and mist. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
Self 1 s Let the eyes glow red like the Beast's. At night the vampire hits, dodges and aims better. Up close the glow is hard to explain. Use again to let them fade.
1 blood Self 40 s Let the fingers grow into the claws of the Beast for four hours: a heavy armour-piercing melee attack whose wounds are aggravated, even to other vampires.

1 blood Self 1 h Sink into the earth and sleep in it, as the Gangrel do. Safe from the sun and out of reach until dusk or until told to rise. Only on soil, not rock, floors or water. Anyone can dig the vampire out.
1 blood Self 10 s Become a great wolf for half a day: fast and deadly with its jaws, but unable to work or use weapons. Clothes and gear come back with the vampire's own shape.
1 blood Self 10 s Become a huge bat for half a day: very fast and hard to hit, with a weak bite. Clothes and gear come back with the vampire's own shape.
1 blood Self 40 s Dissolve into mist for four hours. Blows and bullets pass through, and the mist seeps under any door. It can't fight or work, and fire and sunlight still burn it.
3 blood Self 4 h For four hours the skin turns to flexible stone: blows, blades, bullets and blasts do half damage. Fire and the sun hurt as much as ever.

3 blood Self 1 h Swell into a hulking half-beast until dawn: twice as fast, with claws and jaws whose wounds are aggravated, hitting harder and harder to hurt. It can't work or use weapons, frenzy is 2 harder to resist, and Willpower won't help.
The assassin's art, the Assamite's gift: silence, poisoned blood, burst veins and caustic spittle. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Self 4 h Swallow all sound within six cells of the vampire for a few minutes. The first blow on anyone inside who isn't already fighting does double damage and leaves them reeling for two seconds.

1 blood 8 cells 40 s Turn blood into a weakening poison on the hand or blade. The next melee hit within four hours leaves the target slow, clumsy and short of breath for a day, and so does drinking from the vampire meanwhile. Aimed at someone within eight cells instead, the vampire spits the poison straight at them.
1 blood 3 cells 40 s Lay Scorpion's Touch on the ground as a hidden ward. The first enemy to step on it within five days takes the poison, weak, slow and short of breath for a day.

2 blood Self 40 s Turn blood into a narcotic on the hand or blade. The next melee hit within four hours rolls the vizier's Willpower against the target's Stamina + Fortitude. Each net success lasts longer, from moments to a year, and while it lasts the vizier's mind powers are 2 easier on that target.

1 Willpower 30 cells 30 s Burst the blood vessels of someone this vampire has struck in melee within the last day, from as far as it can see them: one pulse of internal damage a second for each success. Stamina and Quietus against the victim's Stamina plus 3.

1 Willpower 30 cells 30 s Harrow the mind of someone this vampire has struck in melee within the last day, from as far as it can see them. Manipulation + Intellectual against their Willpower: each success strips a point of Willpower, for a day.
1 blood Self 40 s Coat a blade in blood turned to aggravated venom for four hours. Every cutting or stabbing hit adds half its damage again as venom.

1 blood Self 40 s Smear blood across the eyes and over a blade for four hours. The sorcerer's version of the venom: it only works on spirits and the demon-touched, and every cutting or stabbing hit on them adds half its damage again.

1 blood Self 40 s Coat a blade in vitae for four hours. Every cutting or stabbing hit strips a point of Willpower for a day, and a target stripped bare is charmed by the vizier for a while, as good as bound. The book's blow does no damage, but here the cut still lands.
1 blood Touch 1 h Work blood venom into a knife's steel so it keeps it. The knife becomes a Quietus blade: anyone who wields it, mortal or not, adds Baal's Caress's venom to their next five hits.

1 blood 10 cells 5 s Spit a gout of the Assamites' poisoned blood at someone within ten cells. It eats flesh like acid and keeps burning for a few seconds after it lands, and its wounds are aggravated.
1 blood 10 cells 5 s Spit the Assamites' poisoned blood at a spirit or a demon-touched target within ten cells. It works on nothing else.

2 blood 10 cells 5 s Breathe a fine red mist at someone within ten cells. Four dice against their Willpower: each success strips a point of Willpower for a day, and any success counts as a drink of the vizier's blood. A target stripped bare is charmed by the vizier for a while.

1 Willpower 24.9 cells 20 s Wring guilt out of someone in sight until it runs from their skin as blood: a point of a vampire's pool per net success, or a mortal's blood as if fed on. Manipulation and Social against their Willpower.
2 blood Self 4 h Coat the blade in venomous blood for four hours: every melee hit with it is aggravated and does half again as much, and each one eats a little of the weapon away.

The Blood Brothers' shared flesh: blood spent to heal a brother anywhere, limbs passed between bodies, one mind across the circle, its generation pooled, and at last one great merged horror. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood 500 cells 2 s Spend a point of blood to heal a brother anywhere on the map, as if it had spent its own.
1 blood 9.9 cells 10 s Lend a brother arms, eyes and legs out of this body. For four hours the brother is handier, harder to hit and sharper-eyed, and this one is as much less.

1 blood Self 4 h Every brother on the map spends a point of blood and the circle becomes one mind for a while. They see what each sees and aim better for it, and a mind power against any of them meets the strongest will among them.
1 blood Self 2 h Borrow strength of blood from the circle: for four hours, a generation lower for every other brother on the map, never past the fourth.

3 blood Self 4 h Brothers within four cells melt into this one, three blood points each, and become a single mound of flesh: far stronger and tougher for each one in it, and impossible to stake. They come back apart after a while, or when it dies.
The serpent's gifts of the Followers of Set: a paralysing gaze, a forked tongue that drinks, scales, the cobra's shape, and a heart cut out and hidden. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

12 cells 15 s Catch someone's eyes and hold them. They can't move for as long as the vampire keeps staring, up to a minute; any other order breaks the gaze. Mortals can't resist. Another vampire rolls its Willpower against the vampire's Appearance and Social.
Self 1 s Let out a long forked tongue that strikes in melee and drinks half a point of blood from every wound. Use again to draw it back in.
1 blood, 1 Willpower Self 4 h Grow scales and venomous fangs for four hours: much better armour, a poisoned bite and a little more dodge, at the cost of a horrible face.
1 blood Self 10 s Become a huge black cobra for half a day: quick, hard to hit, with a venomous bite, but unable to work or use weapons. Clothes and gear come back with the vampire's own shape.

Self 1 h Cut out the vampire's own heart and set it down to be hidden. While the heart is away, no stake can paralyse the vampire and its frenzies are two steps easier to resist, but destroying the heart destroys the vampire. With the heart in hand or at its feet, use again to put it back. Another vampire's heart can be taken by surgery.
1 blood Self 4 h For four hours the fangs carry the cobra's venom. A bitten mortal is down within the hour and dies a while later unless treated; a bitten vampire burns.

3 blood Self 4 h Take the shape of one of Set's beast-headed children for four hours: much stronger, much tougher, two points of Willpower more than the vampire usually has, and so frightful that enemies within eight cells who fail to hold their nerve run. Charisma and Social against each enemy's Willpower.

The Ahrimanes' bond with the spirit world: things made to work better, animal spirits called into flesh, an animal's gift for a moment, spirits devoured for strength of will, and a cat-like hunting shape. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does
1 blood Self 1.92 h Wake the spirit of the weapon in hand so it works the way it was meant to. Better aim and surer blows, more with each success, for a while.

1 blood Self 1 h Call the spirit of an animal that lives here into a body of flesh. It guards the caster for an hour, two hours, four hours, a day or a week by successes, and fades when hurt badly enough.
1 blood Self 8 h Take one animal's gift for about an hour and a half a success: the bear's strength, the stag's speed, the falcon's eye, the cougar's nerve or the serpent's venom.
Self 1 day Seize a spirit, tear it apart and swallow it. Each success is a point of Willpower back.
2 blood Self 1 h Grow lean and hunched, with slitted eyes and claws whose wounds are aggravated. Much stronger and quicker, and monstrous to look at, for four hours for each point of Willpower.

The True Brujah's hold on time: a perfect sense of it, minds caught in a loop, a foe slowed to a crawl, fire frozen still, and moments stretched for the vampire alone. *Always on:* A perfect sense of time, to the second. This vampire is never caught out by the dawn: it heads for shelter an hour before. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood 24.9 cells 1.92 h Catch someone's mind in a loop of the last quiet moments it lived through. They stand and relive them, four hours for each success, until something hurts them. It won't take hold of someone already coming for the vampire.
1 blood 24.9 cells 15 s Slow someone's time almost to a stop. They move and strike at half speed, a third with three successes, a quarter with five, for a few seconds a success.

2 blood 14.9 cells 20 s Stop time around a spot. Enemies there stand frozen for four seconds a success, fires freeze and die out, and food keeps a day longer for each success. The more successes, the wider the circle.
2 blood Self 8 h Run time faster through the vampire alone. Everything it does goes much faster, for four hours a success.

2 blood Touch 1 h Touch someone and move time. An enemy grows 1, 5, 10, 50 or 100 years older by successes, and dies within a day if that is past their span. A friend grows that much younger instead, never below adulthood, and the vampire takes a wound per success. Manipulation + Occult at 7.
3 blood, 1 Willpower Self 1 h Step outside time: everyone else within thirty cells stands frozen for four seconds per success. Time takes its due afterwards, as aggravated wounds. Wits + Occult at 7.

The Samedi's art of dead flesh: folds of skin that hide things, a rotting touch, a body that crumbles to ash and back, limbs shrivelled at a touch. At 7 the ash of Ashes to Ashes can drift. *Always on:* Dead flesh that does what it is told. Folds of skin open like pouches, so the vampire carries more when hauling. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Touch 10 s A touch that rots. Hair falls out, teeth loosen and the skin grows mould. Rot damage and a little of the victim's looks, which a vampire gets back night by night and a mortal never does. A plant just withers.

2 blood Self 10 s Collapse into a heap of sticky white ash. Neither the sun nor fire can touch it, and the vampire rises at the next dusk or when told to. Scatter the heap and the vampire comes back torn.

1 Willpower Touch 30 s Touch an arm or a leg and shrivel it. It takes three successes; fewer only bruise. A mortal's limb stays useless unless it is replaced. A vampire's fills out again after a night.
2 blood Touch 20 s A touch that makes flesh slough off the bone. Rot damage for every success, and with enough of them the victim loses looks, then speed, then strength, until the wounds heal.
1 blood Touch 1 h A touch that leaves a Withering lying in wait. Three to six days later one of the victim's limbs shrivels.

The warrior Salubri's Discipline: the healer's touch turned to judging how close to death a foe is, then pain, a halo of red armour and a blow that can't miss. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Touch 5 s A touch reads the body: what it is, then with more successes its wounds, its blood and its diseases. The hands stay surer at tending for four hours after, and with two successes the body fights off disease a quarter faster for a day. For a day the healer's own rolls against them get two extra dice.
1 blood Touch 10 s A touch takes a friend's pain away for a while. A mortal who isn't a friend can be put to sleep, if the vampire's will beats theirs. Kindred are beyond it.
Touch 15 s A touch that feels like hot iron and leaves no mark. It spends up to three blood points; each wears a prisoner's resistance down. Anyone else just hurts for a while.
1 blood Self 1 h A shining red halo wraps the vampire like armour. Each success adds a layer, up to five, for about an hour and a half a success.
2 blood Self 2.88 h The third eye opens, icy blue, and guides the next blow. Within a few minutes, the vampire's next three melee attacks land and do double damage.
1 blood Touch 40 s A touch that hurts and keeps on hurting: four hours of strong pain and a deep cut. A vampire hurt this way tests against frenzy. Willpower at 8.

The Tzimisce art of flesh and bone: a face of clay, bodies reshaped on the table, the zulo war-form, and at last a body of living blood. At 6 the vampire's blood turns to acid. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

1 blood Self 1 h Reshape the vampire's own face and body like clay: more beautiful, less beautiful, thinner, heavier or hulking, or the exact face and build of someone else. A failed roll wastes the blood; a botch tears the flesh. Intelligence and Medicine.

1 blood Touch 1 h Reshape another body's flesh, if they are helpless, a prisoner, or one of the colony's own: sculpt them lovelier or uglier, change their build, harden their skin into a hide, smooth away old scars, seal their mouth shut, or grow them into living furniture: a chair, armchair, table, lamp or sculpture. Cast on living furniture, installed or packed up, it shapes the person back. Intelligence and Medicine.

1 blood Touch 1 h Reshape bone, in the vampire's own body or a helpless one: draw out spurs to fight with, brace the skeleton against crushing blows, or bend it into a crippling deformity. A ghoul can be remade as a szlachta, a war ghoul of bone blades and armoured hide, for good. An animal can be given bone plates, war jaws, keen senses or the war beast's frame, the Bratovitch way. Intelligence and Medicine.

2 blood Touch 1 h Work a corpse's flesh into something useful: a suit of fleshcrafted armour, or clothes and furniture of human leather. Intelligence and Crafting. The corpse is used up even if the work fails.

2 blood Self 40 s Unfold into the zulo, a towering war-form of claws and bone spikes, for four hours: nearly twice the melee damage, much harder to hurt, faster, and so hideous that enemies within eight cells who fail to hold their nerve run. It can't work or use weapons. Charisma and Social against each enemy's Willpower.

Self 40 s Melt into a pool of the vampire's own vitae for four hours. Blows and bullets splash through it, and it seeps under any door. It can't fight or work, and fire and sunlight still burn it. While in it, the vampire can melt a hand, an eye or a whole limb into blood: 3 for an arm or leg with everything on it. When it pulls itself back together, missing parts grow back for what they're worth, 2 blood at least, while the blood lasts. Costs no blood to take.
3 blood Self 1 h Spin a shell of hardened blood where the vampire stands, on any ground. The sun can't get in, and it takes a great deal of breaking. The vampire comes out at dusk or when told to.

The Gargoyles' kinship with stone: skin that takes the colour of the walls, a sense of everyone inside a building, sleeping in rock, a hide like granite, and passing through stone itself. *Always on:* Kinship with stone. From the fourth dot the skin itself turns to something like granite. Dot Power Cost Reach Cooldown What it does

Self 1 s The skin takes on the colour and grain of whatever is behind it. The Gargoyle is hidden as by Obfuscate, moving or still, until it attacks. It can't start with an enemy watching. Use again to show itself.
1 Willpower Self 1 h Feel through the stone for everyone nearby until dawn. Hidden Kindred within twelve cells are found as if by Auspex one dot below the Gargoyle's Visceratika.

2 blood Self 10 s Sink into the rock or a stone wall alongside, out of the sun, until the next dusk or until told to come out. The vampire shows against the stone as a figure in a gargoyle's grey skin, and it can be struck, but it takes a lot to break.
1 blood 6 cells 5 s Melt into a wall of rock or stone and come out on the other side, up to six cells away.

Some powers need dots in two Disciplines at once. Press Combination Powers beside Recent rolls, at the foot of the vampire's Disciplines page, to see what it can buy, what is one dot away and what it knows. Once bought, a power stays for good and goes on its own tile on the bar, or simply works if it's an always-on one. Power Needs XP What it does Armor of the Abyss Obtenebration 3, Fortitude 3 18 Shadow closes around the body and hardens, without weighing it down. Baal's Sight Auspex 2, Quietus 4 18 The sorcerer's eyes stay open to what walks without a body. The sorcerer caste's own: it sharpens sight for good. Bagman's Shelter Obtenebration 2, Fortitude 3 15 Shadow thickens around the sleeper. For a day sunlight does half its damage. Beneath Contempt Obfuscate 2, Presence 3 15 Nobody thinks the vampire worth noticing, for as long as it takes to walk away. Bestial Presence Animalism 3, Obfuscate 3 18 Something huge broods behind the vampire. Every outsider nearby feels it. Birth the Vozhd Animalism 6, Vicissitude 6 36 Twenty blood remakes one of the colony's own into a war-beast for good. Bliss Dominate 2, Presence 3 15 Fall into a trance before beauty and come back steadied, with the world a little easier to bear. Blood Sight Auspex 2, Path of Blood 1 9 Taste what a pawn's blood is, and whose. Blood Thorns Protean 2, Potence 2 12 Spit a hardened spine of blood at someone within eight cells. The wound is aggravated. Body Armory Protean 3, Vicissitude 3 18 Grow blades out of bone and flesh. Burning Wrath Celerity 3, Potence 3 18 Bare hands burn with Rage for the fight, and what they tear doesn't mend the easy way. Carriage Horses Animalism 2, Fortitude 3 15 Three of the vampire's wounds pass to a colony animal, which takes them instead. Chain of Slavery Auspex 2, Dominate 2 12 Follow someone's blood bonds to whoever holds them. Chaining the Beast Animalism 3, Dominate 1 16 Always on: mental powers can reach a vampire in frenzy or Rotschreck. Claw Immunity Animalism 2, Fortitude 4 18 The hide turns teeth and claws for the rest of the scene. Cloak the Beast Animalism 5, Obfuscate 3 24 Always on: aura reading finds nothing to read. Command from Afar Auspex 4, Presence 4 24 A word in the mind of anyone of the colony's, anywhere on the map, keeps them steady. Command the Wary Beast Animalism 2, Presence 3 15 One look, and the hostile animals around the target break and run. Creepy Clown Coat Dementation 1, Obfuscate 3 12 Wear whatever the target fears the most, and watch them go. Days of Passions Past Dementation 3, Auspex 2 15 Read an aura for what it has been feeling, not only what it feels. Denial of Aphrodite's Kiss Dominate 3, Presence 3 18 Always on: the first three dots of Presence fail against it from any vampire of higher Generation. Devil's Mark Presence 1, Vicissitude 2 9 Mark a colonist's skin with Presence, so that all who see them are swayed. Divine Aura Auspex 2, Presence 3 15 Until dawn, whoever tries to read this vampire's aura may fall entranced. Do As I Say, Not As I Say Dominate 1, Dementation 4 15 A muddled order sends the target wandering off with no idea what it is doing. Doubletalk Auspex 2, Celerity 1, Obfuscate 1 12 Always on: speaks a second meaning under the first, which makes every negotiation go better. Draught of the Soul Auspex 4, Quietus 5 27 At diablerie, three Willpower and a Willpower roll drink down what the victim knew, for a quarter of its experience on top of the usual. Ears of the Bat Auspex 1, Vicissitude 1 6 Great ears for a while. Hearing is everything, and strangers are put off. Empower Minion Dominate 3, Potence 3 18 Lend Potence to a thrall of the colony. Esprit de Corps Potence 4, Presence 4 24 Everyone of the vampire's own nearby stands firmer against fear and breaks far less easily. Eventide Strength Chimerstry 3, Fortitude 1 12 Always on: illusions last three times as long. Eyes of Alamut Auspex 4, Quietus 3 21 Read the aura of anyone on the map, in sight or not. Eyes of Blades Auspex 2, Celerity 3 15 For a few moments every blow can be seen and turned aside. Eyes of a Thousand Shades Auspex 1, Necromancy (any path) 3 12 Ghosts crowd close around the necromancer for an hour. Necromancy rolls gain two dice. Fear of the Dark Presence 2, Obtenebration 2 12 Shadows move at the edge of sight, and the target and those around them run. Flaying Touch Potence 2, Vicissitude 2 12 A touch strips the skin away. Aggravated, at arm's length. Flesh Wound Fortitude 2, Obfuscate 3 15 Injuries stop showing, and the vampire goes on as if they had never landed. Forbidden Zone Obfuscate 5, Potence 3 24 Mark out a place. For hours, outsiders who enter are slowed by dread. Forced March Celerity 2, Fortitude 2 12 Cover ground for hours at a pace nothing mortal could hold, for a fraction of Celerity's price. Haunted Place Presence 2, Obfuscate 5 21 Five blood soaked into the ground leaves a place wrong for fifteen days. Outsiders hate every moment there. Haunting Seduction Dementation 2, Presence 1 9 Whisper something, and the victim sees the vampire everywhere and can think of nothing else. Heart's Desire Auspex 4, Chimerstry 2 18 Show someone what they want the most, and they will stand and stare. Honeyed Words Auspex 2, Presence 1 9 Hear what a listener wants and say it, and everyone is easier to talk round for the rest of the scene. I Know Auspex 2, Obfuscate 2 12 A look that says the vampire knows. The target loses its nerve for the fight. Ignore Me Dominate 4, Obfuscate 2 18 The target loses all interest in the vampire and in the fight. Impeccable Manners Auspex 2, Presence 1 9 Never a wrong word: talk and trade go easier for a while. King of the Beasts Fortitude 2, Animalism 4 18 Animals called with Beckoning arrive tougher than they left. Always on. Leaps and Bounds Celerity 2, Potence 2 12 Clear walls and gaps in one bound, up to twelve cells. Malkav's Pavlovian Response Dementation 2, Dominate 2 12 Plant a feeling in a word. For a day, the target's nerves are never quite steady. Mind Strike Dominate 2, Potence 2 12 Meet someone's gaze and hit them from the inside. Mover and Shaker Auspex 2, Presence 3 15 Always on: the vampire knows everybody, and everybody thinks it's a friend. Power Animal Animalism 3, Potence 1 12 Lend Potence to a colony animal. Pulse of Undeath Auspex 1, Potence 1 6 Size up a stranger: how much Celerity, Potence and Fortitude they carry. Reluctant Performance Artist Dominate 3, Presence 3 18 A mortal stops whatever it was doing and stands there, helpless, for all to see. Every big step here can't be undone. The game asks you to confirm each one the first time.

Right-click a mortal with a vampire selected and choose Embrace. The target must be an adult humanlike who is downed, restrained, willing, or freshly dead. 1. The sire drains the mortal to death and gains the blood. 2. The sire spends a point to pass on the curse. 3. A few hours later the childe rises: one generation weaker than its sire, of the sire's clan (or line), and hungry. - The childe starts one step into a blood bond with its sire. - Mortals who loved the new vampire react: grief for some, envy or approval for others. - Under Camarilla law an Embrace needs permission. An unsanctioned childe is a problem at court. - Some lines can't Embrace at all, and thin-bloods rarely manage it.

A devoted mortal or a ghoul may ask to be ghouled or Embraced, after a Kiss, a rescue, a bad illness or the first signs of old age. A devoted pawn bleeding out asks on the spot. A letter gives you four answers: grant it, make them a ghoul instead, promise it for later, or refuse.

Drinking a vampire's blood on three different nights binds the drinker to it. Step Effect 1 Likes the regnant more. The regnant's mental powers work better on them 2 Likes them a lot more and won't start fights with them 3 Full bond. Can't attack the regnant without fighting the bond, won't leave or betray, is happiest near them. Only one full bond at a time - A drink counts once a night. - Bonds fade slowly without new drinks. A full bond fades only after a long separation. - Bonding someone unwilling is a sin. Tremere bond one step faster. - The Sabbat's Vaulderie breaks bonds and replaces them with the Vinculum (see Sects and courts).

Give a mortal or an animal a point of vitae (right-click, Give vitae) and it becomes a ghoul. - A ghoul stays mortal: it eats, sleeps and walks in the sun, so it can work by day. - It stops ageing while fed, moves faster, fights off disease better and heals from the vitae. - It needs another drink every fifteen days or so. After that comes a week of withdrawal, and then the years it skipped catch up with it. - It can learn Disciplines slowly, up to a cap set by its domitor's generation: one dot for the 8th to 13th, two for the 7th, three for the 6th, four for the 5th and five for the 4th. - It has the blood buff, paid from its own small vitae reserve. - Its Attributes count for something: each dot above 2 gives part of what a vampire's dot gives. Older blood gives more, so an old retainer of a 4th-generation domitor hits harder than a 10th-generation vampire. - It rises in rank with time served, counted in 15-day months from the day it was ghouled: Rank After What it gets Ghoul 2 points of vitae, 30% of a vampire's Attribute stats Retainer 1 month 3 points of vitae, 50% of the stats, Disciplines 15% cheaper Old retainer 4 months 4 points of vitae, 70% of the stats, Disciplines 30% cheaper, one dot past the cap - It has its own Ghoul tab. Its habits there say when it spends vitae on wounds: never, only on serious ones (downed, bleeding hard or badly hurt; the default) or always. Another habit has a colony vampire top it up whenever it runs out of vitae, not only before withdrawal. - A ghoul with a dot of a sorcery path learns rituals as a vampire does, paid from its vitae. See Blood Sorcery. - Ghouls can deal with the courts on their own, a colony with only ghouls left too: they see the courts marked on the world map and open a court from a caravan in its town. See Sects and Courts. - Ghouls fed mostly by one clan pick up a lesser form of that clan's weakness. - Most ghouls end up blood bound to their domitor.

An animal ghoul has a few extras on its Ghoul tab and gizmo bar. - Command, while its domitor is on the map and awake: it takes right-click orders like a drafted colonist (go here, attack that) and holds its ground between them. - Habits, all on at first: stalking (closing on prey from more than 5 cells it slips out of sight, and its first strike hits harder), guarding (it goes for any enemy within 8 cells of its domitor), retreat when hurt (below 30% health it runs), and blood rage (below half health, 15 seconds of speed, harder bites and less pain, once an hour). - Kennel masters: Animalism makes taming and training easier, more so at 3 and 5 dots. - Trained for: hunting (stalks, and bites land more often), guarding (watches 12 cells) or, for a bird that flies, scouting. A Gangrel kennel beast comes with one; any animal ghoul can change it. - Familiar: an animal ghoul fully blood bound to its domitor is its familiar. The domitor's Kindred tab shows what it's doing and how it feels, and the domitor knows when it's hurt, wherever it is. Borrow blood costs the domitor a blood point and lends the familiar one of its Disciplines until dawn: Potence, Celerity and Fortitude at the domitor's dots, others at the familiar's rank plus one. Disciplines taken by diablerie count; sorcery doesn't. The lent Discipline can't be raised until dawn. - A colony Tzimisce's Bonecraft works on any animal too, ghoul or not.

Tame animals can learn more than guard and attack. The extra roles show on the vanilla Training tab, are taught by a handler over several lessons, and fade the same way when nobody keeps them up. Each needs guard (obedience) first. Role Who can learn it What it does Guard post body size 0.4 or more Holds a spot you pick with its Guard post button (or right-click, Guard this spot), and goes for any enemy within 8 cells of it Watch any Raises the alarm when it sees an enemy, day or night, and wakes everyone asleep. Once an hour Sniff out an animal with a nose Barks at anyone within 12 cells who hides what they are. A pawn hidden by a power shows for an hour; a guest or prisoner in disguise is known for good Track after sniff out Follows a trail you pick with its Track button: a fled prisoner, quarry marked for hunting, an enemy unseen. It stays close and sniffs them out Scouting a bird that really flies Circles a spot, shadows someone, or flies out over the land and comes back with what it saw Messenger a flier, or body size 0.3 or more Tends one of your town contacts, or asks an allied town for a trade caravan on the comms console's terms (15 goodwill, once every four days) Hunt a predator Once a day brings back one or two small animals from round here, about half of them still alive Fight beside after attack Defends its master without an order, and fights better at their side for an hour Spirit scout a familiar only Looks across to the spirit side for three hours, once a day, and comes back with what waits there Selected, a trained animal shows a line to its guard post or to the one it's tracking. The kennel (Misc tab) takes up to six of your animals: they learn half as fast again and forget at half the rate. Name a kennel master on it, and that colonist trains the kennel's animals before any other handling work. An animal ghoul learns twice as fast and forgets at half the rate. A Gangrel kennel beast's role is learned on the Training tab too. Feral Whispers on one of your own animals can tell it a role it was never taught, and it does it for six hours as if trained. A messenger tending a ghoul or a bond carries a vial of Kindred vitae, and an addict's drug for a Setite string; a Dominated mortal still needs the vampire in person.

Any tame bird that can really fly (Odyssey's, a duck, a goose, or a mod's) can learn Scouting once it knows guard, not a chicken or a quail, which only flutter. A bird that learned it before keeps it. A trained bird has three orders: - Scout a spot: it flies to a cell and stays, clearing the fog it can see round it. - Shadow someone: it keeps near a pawn wherever they go on the map. - Fly out over the land: a world tile up to 10 tiles away. It's gone an hour a tile each way and two hours there, then comes back with a letter on what it saw. Call back ends an order. A hungry bird gives up and won't fly out.

Families bred on vampire blood for so long that the ghouling is born into them. A revenant makes its own vitae, needs no domitor, and knows its family's Disciplines. Now and then a family offers the colony one of its young, in a letter you accept or refuse: - Through a friendly court you know: its member owes you a minor boon (or standing, silver or nothing, as you pick) for taking the revenant in. - Through a Sabbat pack you know, at war with you or not: the Sabbat and that pack think 8 better of you. A Camarilla colony loses 4 Camarilla standing for it. - With no court known, the family asks on its own. Family Disciplines What they are Bratovitch Animalism, Fortitude, Vicissitude Rural kennel-keepers who breed hounds and worse, and track for Sabbat packs. They lose their tempers fast and badly. Ducheski Auspex, Dominate, Path of Blood A dwindling line that left the Tzimisce for the Tremere. Gifted with machines, and too inbred to be easy company. Grimaldi Celerity, Dominate, Fortitude Wealthy go-betweens for the Sabbat in mortal society. Every adult Grimaldi is blood bound to the sect's bishops. Obertus Auspex, Obfuscate, Vicissitude Reclusive scholars of the strange, bred for intellect. Most of them can't rest until everything is just so. Oprichniki Animalism, Obfuscate, Vicissitude Descended from a tsar's butchers, now henchmen to the Russian Tzimisce. The dead of an old massacre follow every one of them. Zantosa Auspex, Presence, Vicissitude Faded aristocrats who live for the next sensation. Whatever pleases a Zantosa once, it wants again. D'Habi Daimoinon, Obfuscate, Presence Warrior-priests of a Baali lord who betrayed him, then spent centuries as the slaves of what was left of his line. Their spirits never recovered, and they give way to a strong will. Enrathi Dominate, Obfuscate, Potence Slavers and kidnappers for anyone who pays, Kindred and mortal alike. Nothing they do bothers them, and it shows. Kairouan Brotherhood Auspex, Celerity, Obfuscate The Assamites' only revenants, spies and scholars bred by the sorcerers from captured Tzimisce stock. The breeding left their bodies slow to mend. Rafastio Animalism, Auspex, Path of Blood A proud matriarchal line of witches who sell their magic to whoever suits them. Their Disciplines fade with the moon, and the Embrace has never taken on one of them. Rossellini Dominate, Fortitude, Sepulchre Path Necromancers kept as vassals by the Giovanni, who call them little brothers. They see death and decay in everything, and sit badly in company. Servants of Anushin-Rawan Auspex, Obfuscate, Presence Polished attendants raised on a Ventrue elder's island, and mistaken by most Kindred for ghouls. Generations of breeding have made them pliable to Ventrue commands.

Diablerie is drinking another vampire's soul, the worst crime among Kindred. 1. The victim must be helpless: in torpor, staked, downed or restrained. 2. Right-click it and choose Diablerie. The diablerist drains its blood, then rolls Strength to tear out what's left. It takes time and can be interrupted, which leaves the victim in torpor and furious. 3. The victim meets Final Death and leaves ash. Rewards. If the victim's generation was lower, the diablerist's drops by one (by two if the gap was three or more). Experience, a chance at a dot in one of the victim's Disciplines, and a huge rush. Costs. - A point of Humanity at once, then a sin roll at the lowest level. - The rush is addictive. A failed Self-Control roll leaves the diablerist craving more. - Black veins in the aura for years. Anyone with Aura Perception sees them, and the Camarilla calls a blood hunt on a known diablerist. The Harpies of a Camarilla court notice the stain half the time at each visit, and a Camarilla guest with Auspex 2 or more may read it on a colonist within 12 cells: a scandal, 25 off both standings and a blood hunt. Sabbat and Anarch courts never report it. - If the victim's will was stronger, part of it may stay inside: a derangement, or worse. - Assamites can't do it. A low-generation vampire in your colony is a prize. Enemy Kindred will try to carry off a torpid elder.

Every vampire has a family tree, open from the Kindred tab. It runs one generation per box from Caine, through the clan's founder, down to the vampire, with its broodmates beside it and its childer below. Ancestors nobody knows yet stay as grey "unknown" boxes. Trees outlive their members.

A vampire whose sire is out in the world will hear from it now and then. A sire can be proud, possessive, indifferent, hunted or long gone. Calls are letters, sometimes a night visit: a demand (a task, a vessel, vitae, the childe's return for a season) or a gift (teaching, a boon, an item, an introduction at court). A hunted sire may turn up at your door.

Now and then a casket in a vanilla ancient danger holds a Kindred instead of a soldier: old, strong, and often from a bloodline that's gone from the world. Opening it wakes them confused. Most still have some blood in them; the rest wake starving and go into a hunger frenzy first. You can talk to them once they're calm, and what happens next depends on a roll and on what you say. Some join, some teach and leave, some leave owing you a boon, and some decide your colony belongs to them. Every wound your colonists give one counts against you: a sleeper you beat badly won't join, teach or owe you anything, and is far more likely to turn on you. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. What can happen to a colony with Kindred in it, grouped by the setting that switches it off (Mod settings, World and events). Switching a group off stops new events of that kind; anything already under way plays out. Most only come to a colony that has Kindred.

Setting: Hunters. Driven by the Masquerade breach score, see The Masquerade and hunters. Event What happens Travellers Visitors who are really hunters or investigators. Investigators ask around about what was seen, and once they have a name they pack up to pass it on. Stop them before they leave the map The hunters have a name An investigator got away. A group of hunters comes within a few days, straight for the vampire they named Hunters in daylight From the Exposed breach level: an armed band arrives while the sun is up, with fire and stakes The hunting order At Shattered: the Inquisition's heirs, in force and by day

Setting: Sect politics. A sect sends its enforcers when your standing with it falls low or it has called a blood hunt on your Kindred. The Sabbat also comes for a Lasombra antitribu sheltering with you. Event What happens Archons The Camarilla's enforcers Sabbat pack A war pack. Its shovelheads, freshly Embraced cannon fodder, are sent straight in while the pack waits in the dark Anarch gang The Anarchs, come to settle a score The enemy within A colonist turns out to be an outside vampire's thrall, slipping off to feed it every few nights Sabbat infiltrator A newcomer who is a Sabbat court's plant, and calls a pack when the time comes Anarch unrest A colony vampire stirs up the Anarchs against the domain's Prince. Hear them out or put it down Assamite assassin Someone paid for one of your Kindred's death. One assassin comes alone and waits for the right moment Setite corruption A colonist picks up a habit somewhere and won't say where Tremere hit team Thaumaturgy used outside the clan where Camarilla eyes saw it. The Tremere come to take it back Blood hounds A Camarilla court's Kindred come for a vampire you shelter under blood hunt. See Sects and courts

Setting: Kindred attacks. Event What happens Rogue Kindred A band of vampires with no court to answer to. They often wait out of sight for someone alone Raid with a vampire A night raid with one vampire hidden among the raiders, for a colony with no Kindred yet An elder comes A vampire of great age with a retinue of ghouls. Wounds barely slow it; fire and the sun still work. One that gets away comes back Haunting Someone killed cruelly here comes back as a ghost and frightens everyone near until it fades or is banished An Anathema calls One of the Red List within 12 tiles comes by night with its retinue. A stranger to the colony passes through unless harmed or touched by a power; one that has fought the colony stalks it

Setting: Kindred visitors. Event What happens Someone at the door A Kindred asking for shelter: a fugitive with a blood hunt on them, an abandoned fledgling, a survivor of a fallen court, a hunted sire, or a pale stranger for a colony with no Kindred yet. Auspex can read what they hide A Path's mentor A follower of a Path offers to teach a vampire who has fallen far enough. The offer waits five days in the Quests tab Occult trader A caravan with unidentified relics, lore texts, stakes, holy symbols and blood vials. Only colonies with Kindred see it Ghoul dealers The black market: blood vials, blood wine, vials of Kindred vitae, and vessels hooked on the Kiss Anonymous benefactor Unsigned gifts arrive by drop pod. Later the sender names a price A revenant offered A revenant family offers one of its young through a court or a Sabbat pack you know, for a boon or Sabbat standing
Always on, with their own settings

Event Setting What happens A sire's demand Sire calls A sire out in the world writes now and then, as its temperament takes it: a demand for vitae, a gift, a letter of teaching, an introduction to a court. A possessive sire refused too often comes in person to take its childe home The wight returns Wights come back A vampire lost to the Beast who escaped comes back in the dark, hungrier The world in the background Background world Courts change while you play: coteries rising and falling, plots and showdowns, rival schemes, blood hunts, cities going over to another sect

These arrive as letters from the courts. See Sects and courts. - A letter from court. A court learns of your Kindred and tells you where it meets. - Invited to Elysium. A court expects your acknowledged Kindred on a given night. - A debt called in. A creditor wants its boon repaid before a deadline. - Inquiry. The Sheriff wants the vampire who caused too much breach. - A blood hunt. A court invites any Kindred to destroy someone, as a mission. - The archon arrives. An inspection, after you petition to become a domain. - The Pyramid's tithe. Once a year, for each Tremere.

A Malkavian colony gets warned of some threats before they arrive, through the clan's insight or a dream (and now and then a false alarm). Kindred earn experience (XP) into a pool and spend it on the Kindred tab. A little comes in every night on its own. Most of it comes from doing things. What it costs to spend is on the character sheet. Everything below is scaled by the experience slider in the mod settings, and nothing is earned in torpor. A gain of 0.1 or more floats over the vampire as "+0.5 XP: a speech", and the XP line in the tab's heading says how much it has been earning a night lately. Each Discipline's buy button says how many nights the next dot is at that rate.

Source XP A night 0.3 A careful feeding 0.1 Holding back a frenzy 0.5 An enemy beaten 0.05 to 2, by how dangerous it was. A vampire counts double, an elder four times, a hunter with True Faith half again. Sending an enemy vampire into torpor counts. At most 3 a night A court mission done 1, 2, 4 or 6 by the size of its reward, to every colony vampire who was there Presented at a new court 1, once per court An ambition met 3, 5 or 7 A Path deed 0.1, at most two a night A first time 1, or 0.5 for a power's first use on an enemy A lesson 0.3, one a night Facing the flame 0.1 a success, at most 0.3 a night Holding the floor 0.5 to 1.5 A secret from a captive 0.5 each Reading a treatise 0.3 an hour, for ten hours A clean hunting trip 0.3 Reading lore texts, a sire's lessons, diablerie See Relics and lore and Embrace, bonds and ghouls

Each colony vampire works toward one goal at a time. At its first dusk, a letter offers three it could take, drawn from its clan, its Path and its age, and at least one from the clan or Path where one fits. The Growth page and the Quests tab show the goal and how far along it is. Only what happens after it is taken counts. A met ambition pays at the next dusk, and a new letter comes the night after. There is no deadline and no failure. Drop one, or turn all three down, and another letter comes in five days. Each morality pays for a few acts that suit it, the way it punishes sins. A Humanity vampire who tends the sick or a Path of Night vampire who spreads fear earns 0.1 XP each time, up to two a night. A deed another morality would reward pays nothing. Morality Deeds that pay Humanity Tended a patient; Won a prisoner over; Held back the Beast Path of Blood Committed diablerie; Given a vampire Final Death Path of the Bones Watched someone die; Read a corpse with the Spirit's Touch Path of Caine Finished a lore text; Learned a ritual Path of Cathari Drunk a high from a vessel's blood; Charmed a mortal Path of the Feral Heart Brought down an animal with the bite; Slept in the earth Path of Honorable Accord Repaid a boon; Finished a court mission Path of Lilith Questioned a captive with pain; Fed without care Path of Metamorphosis Grown in a Discipline; Taken another shape Path of Night Sent a mortal running in fear Path of Paradox Given a vampire Final Death Path of Power and the Inner Voice Bent a mind with Dominate; Given a servant an order Path of Typhon Left a mortal craving the Kiss Path of Entelechy Held back the Beast; Finished a lore text Path of Ecstasy Drunk a high from a vessel's blood; Charmed a mortal; Left a mortal craving the Kiss Path of the Warrior Given a vampire Final Death; Grown in a Discipline; Held back the Beast

The first time a vampire does something, it learns from it and gains 1 XP: each ritual it casts, its first childe, its first blood bond, the first hunter it kills, the first sunrise it lives through outdoors, the first frenzy it rides, its first waking from torpor, the first Kindred blood it drinks and the first relic it identifies. Every power pays 0.5 the first time it is used on an enemy or wins a contest.

A vampire learns a Discipline from another colony vampire who has more dots in it. Press Take lessons on the student's Growth page and pick a Discipline and a teacher. The student studies at a table in the same room as the teacher, two hours a night under the Research work type, so Research has to be turned on in its Work tab. The teacher carries on with its own work. - Each lesson pays 0.3 XP into the usual pool. - A new Discipline from outside the clan takes three lessons before its first dot can be bought. The first lesson starts with a point of the teacher's blood, which counts as a drink toward a blood bond. - Drinking another vampire's blood no longer teaches its Disciplines. Lore texts, sleepers and a court's teachers still do. - With Any Discipline self-taught on (Learning settings), any Discipline the vampire could take lessons in can be bought without them, at the self-taught price. With Diablerie opens the victim's Disciplines on, a diablerie opens every Discipline the victim had the same way. The rules are the same for every way a Discipline is learned: no dots past the generation's limit, Koldunic Sorcery only for the Tzimisce, Sanguinus only for the Blood Brothers, Melpominee no higher than the vampire's Artistic, and Assamite sorcerers pay half again for other blood magic. A non-Gargoyle who reaches Visceratika 4 turns grey and stony. Ghouls take lessons from their domitor the same way and earn 0.6 ghoul XP a lesson. A ghoul can't learn Protean, Thaumaturgy or a Discipline only one clan has, unless its domitor's clan is that clan.

A colony vampire with three or more dots in a Discipline gets Write a treatise on its Growth page. It writes at a table under Research, eight hours a dot, and can stop and come back to it. The treatise is a book named for its writer. Its quality comes from the writer's Intellectual skill. A vampire who has the Discipline at fewer dots than the writer earns 0.3 XP an hour from reading it, for ten hours, once per treatise. It doesn't unlock the Discipline. Anyone else reads it as an ordinary book. Treatises also turn up in the world, written at 3 to 5 dots.

Right-click a lit torch or campfire and pick Face the flame, under Kindred. The vampire sits close and tests itself against its fear every hour with a Courage roll, against 5 for a torch and 6 for a campfire. Each success pays 0.1 XP, up to 0.3 a night. A failure ends it and the vampire backs off. A botch is a Rötschreck right beside the fire. It can't be done by day or when the vampire is hungry enough to frenzy.

A vampire may make a speech once per gathering: at an Elysium, rant or esbat the colony hosts (Hold the floor on the vampire), or once per caravan visit to a court (a button in the court window). The roll is Charisma + Social against 7. A success pays 0.5 XP, a quarter more for each success past the first up to 1.5, and a point of standing with the court (two on three successes). A failure does nothing. A botch is a scandal at that court.

Set a captive Kindred, ghoul or Society hunter to Question in its prisoner tab. A colony vampire warden questions it once a night: Manipulation + Social against the captive's Willpower. The warden uses the best method it has. Dominate 2 makes it two easier, though not on a captive of a lower generation. Presence 3 makes it one easier. Without either it uses pain, also one easier, which hurts the captive and is a sin at Humanity 4. Each success pays 0.5 XP and gives up a secret. A neonate or ghoul has one secret, an ancilla or hunter two, an elder three, and a letter says when the captive has nothing left. Captive What it may give up Kindred A torpor crypt; a court's weakness or a rival's scheme; a ritual it knows; its sire, on the lineage tree Ghoul Its domitor, on the lineage tree; a court Hunter The next hunter raid put back; the way into a hideout holding a stolen heart (three more days); the cell for a mission You can also question a captive yourself. Select a vampire, right-click the captive and pick Question .... The talk window opens with three questions: where it comes from, what it knows, and what it is. "What do you know?" draws on the same secrets as the warden. It shares the warden's limit too, so a vampire who got a secret out of a captive by hand doesn't get another that night. The window has no pain: a threat (Strength + Social at 7) hurts the captive's mood and makes it harder to recruit, but leaves no wounds. Dominate 2 or Presence adds its own button, rolled against the captive's Willpower. See Talking to people for how the window works.

After a hunting trip, one time in four a letter asks what to do instead of the usual message: - A local vampire claims the herd: owe it a trivial boon and feed, fight it (a win is 1 XP and its blood), or go hungry. - A hunter takes notice: kill him, slip away, or let him follow. - A mortal who liked the Kiss asks to come along, craving it. - A stranger offers a rumour for a blood vial. A clean hunt with no letter pays 0.3 XP. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. A hungry vampire finds blood by itself, the way a colonist finds food. You can also right-click a vessel and pick "Feed". This page covers where the blood comes from and what it costs. A colony vampire has a Vitae bar on its command bar. It shows the pool in blood points, and the mark on it is the feeding target: the vampire goes hunting when its blood drops below the mark and keeps feeding until it is back there. It starts at 40% of the pool. Drag it up before a raid to have blood for powers, or down when vessels are scarce. It can't go below the starving line (15%), and a starving vampire feeds whatever the mark says.

Source Blood Notes Willing colonists Up to 3 points Leaves mild blood loss that clears in about a day. The vessel gets the Kiss, a short pleasant daze Prisoners Up to 3 points Feeding on someone who hasn't agreed is a sin at Humanity 8 Sleeping or downed pawns Up to 3 points Only a Masquerade risk if an outsider sees Animals About half per point, scaled by size Worth less from the 8th generation down, nothing from the 6th Blood vials 1 point each Drawn at a medical bed. They keep four days, so store them in a freezer Hemogen packs (Biotech) 1 point each Drunk as a thin vial: a little mood lost. They never spoil, so the AI takes vials first Other Kindred Full value Each drink is a step toward a blood bond, and it can get a vampire hooked Fresh corpses Little Costs Humanity Draining the last of a vessel's blood kills it. Careful feedings close their own wound. Frenzied feeding and bites in a fight leave fang marks, which outsiders and hunters can read. Each point taken also closes ordinary wounds for free, more for better blood, and the pool still gets the whole drink. Aggravated wounds still need blood spent on them. When "Feed" can't be picked, the right-click menu still shows it, greyed, with the reason: no blood left, one more sip could kill, Prey Exclusion, a hateful mortal awake, or a vessel that won't hold still. Children are never fed on, ghouled or Embraced.

A sleeping vessel may wake when the fangs go in. Each time, the feeder rolls Dexterity plus its Obfuscate dots against 6 (it goes in the roll log). A drunk vessel makes it easier, and a greedy feeding or a drain harder. Mortals who crave the Kiss, ghouls and the feeder's own thralls don't mind and get no roll. Result What happens Success It sleeps through and remembers nothing Failure It wakes, but the Kiss holds it until the feeding ends. It remembers, as if fed on awake, and an outsider is a witness. Dominate 3's forgetting still works Botch It wakes screaming. The feeding stops, it witnessed the bite, and everyone asleep nearby wakes too Anyone awake who sees the feeding is still a witness. Tavern guests asleep in rented beds are the usual sleepers.

- Drawing blood is a bill at a medical bed. The donor loses some blood, the colony gets a vial. - Grades. A vial remembers its donor. Good looks, a sanguine temper, Tough and good mood raise the grade; ugliness, gloom, drug interest, bad health or bad mood lower it. Fine blood lifts the drinker's mood a little and thin blood dampens it. The points are the same. - What it carries. A vial keeps its donor's drug high and disease. See below. - Blood wine. A brewery bill turns five fine vials into five bottles. Wine keeps for 30 days and lifts the mood more. The AI drinks vials only, so give wine by order. - Kindred prisoners are fed vials by wardens when the colony has them. - Patients. A hungry vampire in bed, a colonist or a guest, is brought a blood vial or a hemogen pack by a doctor. A prisoner is too, unless it's set to be executed, released or questioned. Kindred vitae is never brought, since it bonds. - Offer your wrist. A colonist who craves the Kiss or is devoted can right-click a vampire in bed and let it drink. A starving vampire drinks too deep, as it would anywhere. - Visitors. Traders, visitors and caravans arrive with at least three quarters of their blood. A vampire that isn't the colony's, and isn't hostile, heals only when out of a fight and never below the hunger line, so it doesn't spend itself into a frenzy among its own people.

A sanguophage can be Embraced, and so can anyone else with the hemogenic gene. The vampire keeps its genes and its hemogen powers, but it has one blood pool: the vitae. The hemogen bar is gone. - Costs. 20 hemogen is a blood point, and every power costs at least one. Coagulate, Piercing spine and Longjump cost 1 point. Resurrect, which vanilla gives to no gene but a mod might, costs 5. Like a Discipline, a cost above the generation's per-turn limit is paid over a few turns. - Stronger in Kindred hands. Piercing spine hits 12% harder for each dot of Potence, Longjump reaches a fifth further for each dot of Celerity, and Coagulate tends better with Medicine. - One button. The hemogen powers share a single Hemogen tile on the bar, like a Discipline's. - Feeding. Bloodfeed is gone from the bar. A vampire feeds through the Kindred menu, under the usual rules. - No drain. Hemogenic and hemogen drain lose nothing; the nightly upkeep is the only cost. - Deathrest. No need and no coma. A vampire assigned a deathrest casket sleeps the day in it, and at dusk every building that ran most of the day gives its bonus, as after a deathrest. The machines burn their hemogen packs every day. A hemopump adds a point to the pool and a hemogen amplifier adds a quarter to every feeding. - Trading blood. A vampire drinks hemogen packs as thin vials. A hemogenic mortal drinks blood vials for 20 hemogen each, the same as a pack. When hungry it takes vials before packs, since vials spoil. Turning off its hemogen packs turns off vials too. - Ghouls keep hemogen and borrowed vitae apart.

"Keep as vessel" is a prisoner interaction mode. Wardens bring food and nothing else: no recruiting, no release. Hungry vampires pick from the pen by whoever has the least blood loss, so the pen rotates by itself. Prisoners kept this way get a "kept as cattle" thought unless they've come to like the Kindred. A long-held vessel can come round and be recruited later.

- Drugs. If the vessel is high, the vampire gets a share of the same high. It's the only way Kindred feel drugs. They never get tolerance or addiction from it. - Disease. A sick vessel leaves the vampire carrying "tainted blood" for a few days. It shows in the health tab and has no symptoms, but each mortal fed on in that time may catch the disease.

Fresh blood keeps the vessel's feeling for half a day, and that strengthens a Discipline. A new feeling replaces the old one. A middling mood gives nothing, and vials carry none. The vessel Resonance What it gives Hurt in the last hour, or in an aggressive break Choleric Celerity and Potence a dot higher Mood under 30% Melancholic Fortitude a dot higher Asleep Phlegmatic A die more on Auspex and Dominate Mood over 70% Sanguine A die more on Presence and blood sorcery An animal Animal Animalism a dot higher and a die more on its powers The extra dot strengthens the Discipline's lasting effect, but never gives a power the vampire doesn't have.

Your mortal colonists know what their neighbours are. Each one has a regard for Kindred: Regard Mood near Kindred What it means Devoted Good Volunteers as a vessel, may ask to be ghouled or Embraced Fascinated Slightly good Counts as a willing vessel Uneasy Slightly bad The usual start Fearful Bad Worse opinion of Kindred Hateful Very bad Won't be fed on awake, and may try to kill a vampire Regard goes up with the Kiss, being saved by a vampire and long quiet stretches. It goes down with unwilling feeding, a friend killed by a vampire, or seeing a frenzy. Traits push the starting roll: psychopaths lean fascinated, kind pawns lean fearful. A hateful mortal's mental break can turn into "slay the monster": it goes after a vampire, ideally one asleep by day, with fire or a stake. A warning thought shows well before this, so you have time to exile, imprison, bond or win them over. A blood bond or ghouling sets regard to devoted and keeps it there.

A mortal fed on often may come to crave it and become a blood doll. While fed regularly they get a small mood bonus and offer themselves first. Without the Kiss they go into withdrawal for a while, and the craving fades after about a quadrum. A doll wants feeding more often than is safe, so set a blood-loss limit.

Every vampire has fangs as a melee attack. A bite on a standing enemy is unlikely; on a downed, staked or held one it's the first choice. Each bite that lands drinks a point, up to three per target per fight. Bites do aggravated damage to other Kindred. Frenzied vampires bite first. Each point drunk this way makes the vampire blooded for a minute: +5 melee hit and blows 5% faster for each point, stacking up to the vampire's blood per turn (one for most, more for low generations). Riding the Wave doubles both the stacks and the cap.

Drinking another vampire's blood is a rush. Each time, the drinker rolls Self-Control. A failed roll moves it toward needing more: a craving, then a habit, then a break where it goes looking for Kindred blood. It fades with time away from it.

- A caravan with any mortal or ghoul in it travels by day as usual. The Kindred ride covered. - An all-Kindred caravan travels by night and rests through the day. - A Gangrel in a caravan feeds its Kindred from game, so they need no blood that day.

A caravan with a Kindred can pick Hunt at any settlement that isn't hostile, once a night. A known court's town has no Hunt button: its herd belongs to the court's Kindred. Choose careful (less blood, low risk) or greedy (fills the pool, real risk). The roll uses Wits and Streetwise, plus the vampire's best of Obfuscate, Presence, Dominate and Animalism. Result What happens Good Fed, nobody the wiser Poor Fed a little Failed One of: a witness, a dead vessel (a sin), or lost goodwill Botched Two of those, and a hunter comes looking later Hunting the same settlement again in a season gets harder. Hunting in the city of a court you haven't met yet is poaching. On empty land a caravan can hunt animals safely for a little blood. Now and then a hunt ends in a letter with a choice instead: a local vampire who claims the herd, a hunter who noticed, a mortal who wants to come along, a stranger with news. 1. Subscribe to Harmony and to The Rim by Night: Kindred on the Steam Workshop. Without Steam, download Harmony's release and put the Kindred folder from the mod's GitHub repository in RimWorld's Mods folder. 2. In the mod list, load Harmony first, then The Rim by Night: Kindred. The mod can go into a save that's already running. Nothing changes until someone becomes Kindred or a vampire shows up from outside.

There are three ways to get one. Start with one. Pick one of the mod's scenarios when you make a new colony: Scenario What it is Lone neonate Your sire made you, taught you almost nothing and left you on a transport bound for the rim. You woke in the hold with a crate of stolen blood and nobody to answer to. Now you have a planet to hide on, and the sun comes up in a few hours.Note: one fledgling vampire with no one to feed on. A hard start. Camarilla coterie A prince far away wants a foothold on this world and sent three young Kindred to make one. Two mortal retainers came along to keep the lights on by day and the coterie fed by night. Make a domain the Camarilla can be proud of, and keep the Masquerade while you do it. Sabbat pack Three Kindred of the Sword of Caine, sent to take this world from the Camarilla, with two mortals who know better than to ask questions. The pack has already shared the Vaulderie, and the Camarilla counts you as its enemy. Anarch gang Three Kindred who walked out on their prince and kept walking, all the way to a new world, with two mortal friends who came along for the ride. Nobody here tells you what to do. Independent clan crew Two Kindred of one of the Independent clans, sent out by their elders on clan business, with three mortals to do the work by day. The clan already has a haven on this world, and it is expecting you. The stowaway The three of you wake to sirens and tearing metal and barely make the escape pods. One of you was never really asleep. They boarded the ship hidden in a cryptosleep casket, and the others are about to find out what they are. Wandering revenant Your family has served the Kindred for longer than anyone remembers, and the blood in your veins is your own. You left them with a pack animal, a purse and whatever your blood can do, to sell it to whichever court pays best. Note: one revenant ghoul and no vampires. You pick the family when the game starts. The three nearest courts are known, and they hire ghouls for errands while your caravan travels near them, even with no home behind you. Dark Ages fief Your lord granted you this stretch of wild land and told you not to come back until it paid. You rode out with two retainers who drink your blood and two serfs who don't know what you are yet. Nobody out here has heard of the Camarilla. There's only your word, your sword and the dark.Note: one vampire, two ghoul retainers bound to them and two mortal serfs. They walk in with medieval arms and the old crafts; research is as normal. Fallen knight You died on campaign, in the mud outside a town whose name you never learned, and woke three nights later with a thirst. Whoever Embraced you rode on with the army. Only your squire came back to look for you, and you've already given them your blood to keep them close.Note: one vampire in plate and one ghoul squire, with a warhorse. A hard start. Each colonist in these scenarios starts with one random weapon in hand, picked from the scenario's own list. Some scenarios add a steel helmet, a robe or both. Stowaway keeps Crashlanded's gear. You can also add the "starting Kindred" part to any scenario in the vanilla scenario editor. It sets how many starting colonists are Kindred, their generation range, and whether the others know. Be Embraced. A vampire who comes to the colony can make a colonist into one of its childer. See Embrace, bonds and ghouls. Dev mode. Turn on dev mode, open the debug actions menu, and under "The Rim by Night: Kindred" use Make vampire on a colonist. It rolls a clan and everything else for you. Open making menu lets you pick instead.

Every starting Kindred without a sire in the colony gets a window when the game begins. The game pauses while it's open. Choice What it decides Clan Disciplines, weakness and calling. See Clans Generation Blood pool size and how strong the vampire can become. 10th to 13th by default Sect Defaults to the clan's. The first Kindred's sect becomes the colony's Age Neonate (1 to 40 years undead) by default. Ancillae (50 to 150) and elders (200 to 300) start with more dots and experience. Every start comes with a sire who wants things Discipline dots Three dots among the clan's Disciplines Merit and Flaw One of each, either, or neither. See Character sheet "Roll for me" fills in anything you leave blank. Closing the window does the same.

- The Kindred tab on any vampire, next to Health and Needs: blood, experience, Humanity, Virtues, Habits, Attributes, Disciplines and rituals, over four pages. - The Kindred main tab on the bottom bar: the Masquerade, your sect, the courts, boons and the chronicle. - The Vitae bar in the Needs tab. It replaces Food and Rest. - The gizmo bar: a tile per Discipline with its powers, and buttons for rituals and the rest. - The Kindred right-click submenu: feeding, the Embrace, ghouls, stakes and diablerie. - Alerts on the right: dawn coming, starving vampires, frenzy risk, witnesses, the Masquerade. Every tab, button and menu option is explained on Menus and buttons.

1. Roof. Make sure every vampire can reach a roofed spot before dawn. Better still, build a coffin (Furniture tab) and assign it like a bed. 2. Schedule. Vampires sleep 06:00 to 18:00 on their own. Copy a vampire's schedule in the Schedule tab to move mortals who work with them onto the same hours. 3. Blood. Plan where blood will come from. Willing colonists, prisoners kept as vessels and blood vials from a medical bed all work. Read Feeding. 4. Healing. Set each vampire's heal policy under Habits on the Kindred tab: never, when safe, or always. Only blood heals them; doctors can't. 5. Fire. Keep vampires away from fire. Firefighting is off for them by default, and you should leave it that way. 6. Witnesses. Visitors and traders are outsiders. Don't feed, frenzy or use loud powers in front of them. See The Masquerade and hunters. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material.
