The words Kindred use, as the mod uses them. Word Meaning Kindred Vampires, in their own word Kine Mortals The Embrace Making a new vampire: draining a mortal to death and giving back a little of the sire's blood Sire, childe The vampire who Embraced another, and the one Embraced Vitae Vampire blood, and the blood in a vampire's pool Blood pool The vitae a vampire holds. Generation sets its size Generation Steps removed from Caine, the first vampire. Lower is stronger Thin-blood A vampire of the 14th generation or higher, close to mortal The Kiss A vampire's bite while feeding, which mortals find pleasant Vessel Someone a vampire feeds on The Beast The predator in every vampire, which frenzy lets loose Frenzy The Beast taking over, from hunger or anger Rötschreck The red fear: panic at fire or sunlight Torpor A deathlike sleep, from starvation, grave wounds or by choice Final Death Being destroyed for good Humanity The human conscience a vampire keeps. See Humanity and the Paths Path of Enlightenment A morality that isn't human, in place of Humanity Golconda A rare peace with the Beast Wight A vampire whose Humanity is gone. Only the Beast is left Discipline A power of the blood, rated in dots Blood sorcery Thaumaturgy, Necromancy and Koldunic Sorcery, learned as paths and rituals Ghoul A mortal or animal fed vampire blood, stronger and ageless while the blood lasts Domitor The vampire who keeps a ghoul Revenant A ghoul by birth, from a family bred to it Blood bond The tie formed by drinking a vampire's blood on three separate nights. Regnant is the vampire, thrall the drinker Diablerie Drinking another vampire's soul. Can lower the drinker's generation Clan, bloodline A vampire's lineage, with its Disciplines and weakness. Bloodlines are smaller lines Caitiff A vampire with no clan Antitribu A clan's members who went over to the Sabbat Sect A faction of Kindred: the Camarilla, the Sabbat, the Anarchs, or the Independents Court A sect's gathering in a settlement, under a Prince or its equal Prince The ruler of a Camarilla court or domain Elysium A court's neutral ground, where Kindred meet in peace Domain A territory a Prince rules. Your colony can become one Boon A favour owed between Kindred: trivial, minor, major or life Blood hunt A court's order that a vampire be destroyed by anyone Archon An enforcer of the Camarilla The Masquerade Hiding what vampires are from the mortal world Breach Something outsiders saw that they shouldn't have Coterie A group of Kindred who stand together: your colony's vampires, or one of the factions inside a court (see Coteries) Vaulderie The Sabbat rite that binds a pack with mixed blood ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Every vampire has a Beast inside it. Humanity measures how well the vampire holds it back, and a frenzy is the Beast getting loose.
A rating from 0 to 10, shown in the Kindred tab. Most vampires start around 7.

Doing something worse than your Humanity allows is a sin. The vampire rolls Conscience at difficulty 8. Fail, and it loses a point of Humanity. Botch, and it also gains a derangement. A vampire only tests for sins at or below its current rating, so the lower it falls, the less it feels. Every sin and its rating, for Humanity and for each Path, is on Humanity and the Paths. Killing raiders in an open fight is never a sin. At most one test per level per day, so one bad night can't strip five points.

Effect How Waking Higher Humanity wakes earlier at dusk Daytime Every roll by day is capped at Humanity, and low Humanity makes a vampire slower by day Torpor Lower Humanity means longer torpor Mortals Below 5, social penalties with mortals. Below 3, corpse-like unless it looks alive Animals Below 4, animals shy away more 0 Wassail. The vampire is lost to the Beast for good and turns on the colony Raising Humanity costs current rating × 2 experience, and only after a quadrum with no Humanity lost.

A vampire lost at Humanity 0 becomes hostile on the spot. Destroy it, or stake it and keep it. The At Humanity 0 setting softens this for your own vampires. A long frenzy: the Beast rides it for three to six hours, then lets go at Humanity 1. Rehab in a cell: it still turns, but if you down it and hold it prisoner it rolls Conscience against 8 once a week, with a die more for each dot of Obeah a colony vampire on the map has. A success brings it back at Humanity 1 and it joins the colony. If it escapes the map, it stays out there: the breach score creeps up while it's loose, and now and then it comes back at night with animals it has ghouled, stronger each time. A court you know may offer a mission to hunt it down.

Paths are moralities that aren't human. Each has its own list of sins and often its own Virtues: Conviction in place of Conscience, Instinct in place of Self-Control. Morality What it is Humanity The human conscience the vampire brought with it from life, worn down a little by every sin. Path of Blood A code of the blood: other Kindred are to be converted or destroyed, and killing mortals for food is beneath a true follower. Path of the Bones Death is the one subject worth studying. Its followers fear nothing about it, waste no chance to watch it, and never stand in its way. Path of Caine Vampires are the children of Caine and should live as what they are: apart from mortals, masters of the Beast, never denying their own hunger. Path of Cathari Followers indulge every appetite, let the Beast run with them, and kill only when passion takes them. Path of the Feral Heart The vampire is a predator and should live like one: hunting with its own body, feeding when hungry, killing cleanly and never for sport. Path of Honorable Accord A knightly code of duty, loyalty and keeping one's word. Its followers stand their ground and never kill without reason. Path of Lilith Followers believe pain teaches, hunger most of all. They go hungry on purpose, fear nothing of death, and see every killing as a lesson cut short. Path of Metamorphosis The vampire is one stage in a longer change. Followers feed without delay, study the Beast by riding it, and care nothing for what others need. Path of Night Kindred are damned to be horrors whose work is to frighten. Followers kill sparingly, rely on no one and bow to no one. Path of Paradox Kindred have slipped out of the great cycle and must send others back into it. Followers kill only for need and guard their own bloodline. Path of Power and the Inner Voice Power is the only thing worth having. Followers own their acts, reward the useful, help no one for free and never accept defeat. Path of Typhon Every vice is a tool for raising a sleeping god. Followers corrupt others, help their own and show no one any mercy. Path of Entelechy A Brujah's stoic discipline, older than Carthage. The Beast is an enemy to be mastered by reason, the mind and body are there to be perfected, and mortals are not to be used for more than a meal. Path of Ecstasy Pleasure taken past every mortal limit tears a hole in the world's lies. Followers of this Setite Path spread rapture, break taboos and treat holding back as the one real sin. Path of the Warrior Set is a god of war and storms, and his chosen are weapons. Followers of this Setite Path train and hurt themselves until the Beast fears them, and every kill is a prayer. Hierarchy of Wyrm Taint What is left of a Garou's self after the Embrace, and the Wyrm takes a little more of it with every sin. When it is gone, so is the Abomination. Each Path's Virtues and full list of sins are on Humanity and the Paths. Taking up a Path. A vampire must first fall to Humanity 3 or lower. A follower of a Path that suits its clan may then come to the colony at night and offer to teach. After a season of study there's a Willpower test. Failing costs a point and the test comes again in a few days, or a season after a botch. Living on a Path. Path followers unsettle mortals (social impact down) and can't use Look Alive. Sabbat Kindred approve. Instinct. A vampire on a Path with Instinct rolls it when a frenzy threatens. If the provocation is below its Instinct, no frenzy comes. Otherwise it may ride the wave: no pain, harder melee hits, guns dropped, still under your control.

Golconda is a lasting peace with the Beast. A vampire who has kept its Humanity can work toward it over a long time, and can lose it again easily. 1. Hear of it. From a lore text, rumours heard at a court or a sleeper who remembers. Until then the option doesn't show. 2. Be eligible. On Humanity, at 7 or more, Conscience 4 or more, no diablerie stain. 3. Find a mentor. The court that told you, or the first court you know, puts the mission on offer. Asking costs a little standing. 4. Make amends. Tending people and taking captives alive count, and so does a season without losing Humanity. The vampire needs 10 plus one for every Humanity point it ever lost. You never see the count, only a thought that hints at it. 5. The Suspire. A button at night. The vampire lies in a trance for about six hours, then rolls Conscience, Self-Control and Courage. All three must succeed. Failing the Suspire costs a point of Humanity and closes Golconda for good. Reaching it: frenzy and Rötschreck never take hold (unless starving, or Rötschreck while on fire), waking costs a fifth as much blood, no daytime dice cap, and a standing good mood. Falling below Humanity 7 or Conscience 4 loses it forever.

A frenzy is a mental state. There are three kinds: Kind What sets it off What happens Rage A heavy hit, insults, a fight, any hit while badly hurt, a lover downed nearby Attacks the source, then anything close. Melee only, ignores pain Hunger A vessel nearby while starving, the first taste while hungry Brings down the nearest vessel and drinks past the safe limit Rötschreck Fire within a few cells, being burned, the sun, True Faith Runs for the nearest dark, safe spot, attacking anything in the way - The roll. Self-Control for rage and hunger, Courage for Rötschreck, against a difficulty set by what provoked it. Three successes resist it; one or two buy a moment before another roll. - Willpower. A point buys a short window of control. Each vampire's Willpower policy (under Habits on the Kindred tab) decides when it's spent by itself: never, against frenzy, or freely. - Afterwards. Anything killed in frenzy can be a sin. Gangrel may gain an animal feature. Outsiders who saw it are witnesses. - Clans. Brujah frenzy more easily and can't spend Willpower against it. An alert shows when a vampire is at risk.

Lasting madness, gained from a botched sin roll and some powers. Malkavians always have one that never goes away. Each causes an episode every so often. A Willpower point holds one off for a day. Where everything is on screen, and what each tab, button and menu option does. Almost every line in the mod's windows has a tooltip; hover over it for the details.

Select a vampire and open the Kindred tab next to Health and Needs. The heading gives the vampire's clan, age and generation, its sire or sect, its blood and its experience. Unknown outsiders show as plain "Kindred" until you learn more about them. Once the Masquerade is no longer intact, a red line under the blood gives the breach score on every page. The pages are down the left side. A gold number beside a page counts what you can do there now: free Discipline dots to spend, or Ambitions waiting to be picked. Click a heading's name to fold the section under it; the page remembers that until you quit the game. Along the bottom: Button What it opens Lineage The family tree: sire, childer and everyone above them back to Caine. See The lineage window Recent rolls The roll log. See The roll log Combination powers On the Disciplines page: every combination power and what it needs Choose clan and Disciplines The making menu, for a starting vampire you haven't set up yet. See Getting started Click a Discipline, morality, merit or derangement to read its page in the grimoire, and the ? at the end of a heading opens the guide on that subject. Page What's on it Sheet Clan rank, morality, Virtues, Willpower, Merits and Flaws, derangements, active effects Attributes The nine Attributes Disciplines Blood powers, Disciplines, combination powers, paths not open yet Occult The Occult rating, rituals and lore books The Wolf An Abomination's wolf half: Rage, Gnosis, Gifts and rites Growth The Ambition, lessons and treatises. Your own vampires only Court The seat it holds at a court, and its familiar Backgrounds Allies, Contacts, Herd, Resources and the rest. See The sworn court Conduct Habits, how it fights, how it covers up, and Enter torpor. Your own vampires only

Section What's there Clan rank Its rank in the clan's own politics Morality Humanity or the vampire's Path, with its rating and the Virtues: Conscience or Conviction, Self-Control or Instinct, and Courage. Willpower sits under them. Hover the next dot for its cost and click it to buy Abomination Only on an Abomination: what the wolf half costs it Merits and Flaws Picked or rolled at the Embrace Feeding limits A Ventrue's one kind of prey, or the kind a Prey Exclusion flaw won't touch. A Ravnos's vice Derangements Lasting madness. See Humanity and frenzy Active effects Buffs and switched-on powers, kept off the health tab (setting "Effects on the Kindred tab")

The nine Attributes in three columns, Physical, Social and Mental, as on the printed sheet. They come from the pawn's skills, health and traits, and experience raises them a dot at a time on top of that: hover the next dot for its cost and click it to buy. Each tooltip lists the vampire's own powers that roll it. See Character sheet.

Every Discipline the vampire has, and the ones it could learn, with its dots. A new vampire's free starting dots show in gold under the heading. Each Discipline shows its powers as icons: - Hover a power to see what it does and which dot unlocks it. - Click a learned power to take it off the gizmo bar, and click again to put it back. Hidden powers still work and still autocast. - A Discipline at its limit says why: the generation's dot cap, or (for a sorcery path) the dots another path needs first. Out-of-clan Disciplines cost more, and most need three lessons before the first dot. The Blood powers row holds the powers every vampire has (blood buff, Steel the Will, Look Alive).

The Occult rating, then every ritual the vampire knows. Click a ritual to see its sorcery, level, difficulty, casting time, blood cost, ingredients, and whether it needs a circle and a target. Study a ritual starts learning one from a teacher in the colony; the progress shows here, in hours, and the work happens at a ritual circle or ossuary altar under Research. Lore books lists the lore books on the colony's maps: those the vampire would still learn from first (started ones with a bar), then the ones it has read, then the ones it can't learn from yet, greyed with the reason. Hover a book for what it teaches; click it to find it.

The vampire's Ambition and how far along it is, with a Drop button. See ambitions. Under Study: Button What it does Take lessons Picks a Discipline and a teacher among the colony's vampires. See lessons Write a treatise At three dots or more, writes a book other vampires learn from. See treatises Lessons and treatises are Research work at a table, and their progress shows here. If the vampire isn't assigned to Research, a red line says so and nothing moves.
The seat the vampire holds at the court the colony is sworn to, and its familiar, if it has one: how far away the animal is and which Discipline it has lent.

Habits are four choices per vampire. Habit Choices Blood healing Never. When safe: waits until nobody has hit the vampire or been hit by it for a few seconds, and stops before it gets hungry. Always: heals in the middle of a fight, keeping a couple of points back Willpower Never spend. To resist frenzy, the default: saved for holding the Beast back. Spend freely: also buys a sure success on important rolls Feeding Vials and vessels: blood vials and prisoners kept as vessels only. Also animals and the willing: adds the colony's animals, colonists who crave the Kiss and colonists devoted to the Kindred. Anyone Powers Only when ordered. In a fight: Disciplines against enemies nearby, but only when the vampire is set to attack or has just been hurt. Whenever useful: also outside fights In a fight picks the vampire's fighting style. The Masquerade has the cover-up switch, each witness on the map with the surest way to deal with them, and the colony's breach score with how much of it this vampire caused. Too much and the Sheriff opens an inquiry. Under Orders, Enter torpor sinks the vampire into torpor on purpose. No blood is used while it sleeps, and wounds heal when it wakes. How long depends on Humanity.

On every living mortal. It shows what the person is to the Kindred: Line What it means Regard for the Kindred A bar from hateful to devoted. See Feeding Blood bonds One dot for each night they drank from a vampire. The third is a full bond. Click to select the regnant Thrall They're under the hold of a vampire from outside the colony The Kiss They've felt the Kiss and want it again, and how badly Faith True Faith, as dots

On every ghoul, in place of the Mortal tab. Its Disciplines show five dots like a vampire's; the dots past the ghoul's cap are faint. With the setting for the ghoul's full sheet on, its pages (Sheet, Attributes, Disciplines and Conduct) are icons down the left side; hover one for its name. Line What it means Ghoul of… The domitor, and its clan. A revenant names its family instead Vitae Borrowed blood. A point of it closes a wound, and a drink from the domitor tops it up Next drink needed Days until withdrawal starts, or a warning that it already has. Revenants make their own vitae A ghoul for… Years of service. The blood holds back ageing Experience and Disciplines A ghoul learns only what its domitor's blood carries. Blood of a lower generation lets it go higher The clan's curse A share of the domitor's clan weakness, from drinking too much of that blood Blood bonds As on the Mortal tab

A vampire's buttons, besides vanilla's. Button What it does Discipline tiles One tile per Discipline, its powers as small icons in two rows. Click an icon to cast, right-click it to read the power in the grimoire, and click the tile's name for the Discipline's page. A tick marks a power that is switched on, and a green bar fills over an icon while it cools down (hover for how long). Turn the setting "Power tiles" off for vanilla's one-button-per-power layout A relic's tile Powers lent by a relic get a tile of their own, named for the relic Rituals Work a known ritual. The vampire fetches the ingredients first, and from level 3 it has to stand in a ritual circle (or an ossuary altar for Necromancy) Undergo the Suspire The last test on the road to Golconda. Only at night, and only once. See Humanity and frenzy Swindle a trader Ravnos only. Far better prices for two hours, with a chance of being caught. Every three days at most Resume own shape Ends a shapeshift Return to the body For a vampire riding someone else's body, and on the sleeping body it left Astral journey Psychic Projection's mind, looking in on far places Rise, Drift On a vampire sunk into the earth (Earth Meld and its cousins) Step through Incorporeal Passage, through a wall Restore… Brings back a limb shrivelled by Thaumaturgy, for blood Draw from the hilt The Sword of Dracula's stored blood Dispel On an illusion, to make it go Feed false news On a colonist caught reporting to a court Unleash On a drafted colonist, beside Fire at will. It goes after the nearest enemy anywhere on the map and fights as an enemy of its kind would: powers first, closing in unseen, pulling back to heal when badly hurt. Anyone with a gun backs away from melee fighters and looks for cover. A pawn scared by a power stays on the map and goes back to the fight when the panic ends. Your orders come first, and once one is done it goes back to the hunt. Undrafting ends it. While it's on, a Pick target button chooses the enemy it goes after. Once that enemy is down or gone it picks the nearest one again, and clicking the button clears the target early. A power aimed out of range or out of sight walks the pawn closer, then casts. Power menus. Some powers ask what to do once they've been paid for: which Attribute the blood buff raises, which order Dominate gives, what Fleshcraft makes. The menu stays open until you pick something. When the vampire casts by itself, it picks at random among the options that don't need you to click on the map. Unleashed by day. An unleashed vampire caught by daylight stays where it is and only uses its powers. Drafted orders. A job you give a drafted vampire (feeding, a ritual, a power with a walk to it) carries on after you undraft it. Power timers. With the setting on, the bottom-left inspect pane lists the vampire's running powers and the time each has left.

Select a vampire and right-click someone or something. The mod's orders sit under one Kindred entry (turn the setting "Kindred right-click submenu" off to list them with vanilla's). Option On What it does Feed on… A mortal, animal or vampire who holds still A careful feeding. On Kindred, each night's drink is a step of the blood bond Drain… dry A mortal Takes every drop. The Kindred button on the bottom bar. Six pages. While the colony has two or more kinds from the Rim by Night mods, only the window used last keeps its button, and a list down the left side of each window names every one with its pages, so a click opens any page of any of them; the Core setting One bottom-bar button turns that off. Anything you open from one of these pages (a court, Ask on the Boons page, Call it in, the Red List, an office pick) opens inside the same window, with a path at the top such as "Boons › Teacher: Dominate › Who it is for": each step in it is a link back, < Back goes up one step and the page's name in the left list goes back to the page. The window widens while something wider than the page is open. Page What's on it Overview The Masquerade score. Your sect and your standing with each sect (-100 to 100), permissions to Embrace, anyone blood hunted. Buttons to declare for a sect, leave it or defect. Once you're a domain, its offices and the gathering you can host. A Sabbat colony's pack offices and the Vaulderie. Read the Red List opens the Red List window Courts Every court you know of: court or clan haven, the settlement it meets in, its Prince and its opinion of you. Click one to find it on the world map; Open the court opens its window: in person while your Kindred are there, else by letter Boons: ledger One list of the favours owed to your coterie and the favours you owe, owed to you first, with the totals each way on top. Each row says who, their seat, where they are now and why the boon is owed. Call it in lets you pick a favour from the debtor, up to the boon's size. Anything it can't do is greyed, with the reason Boons: ask the courts What the courts you know can do for you now. A list down the left picks the price (trivial, minor, major, life). Its services sit under headers that fold open and shut: Secrets, Teaching, Blood and the Embrace, The Masquerade, Force and The Prince's favour. Each row names the vampire who would do it: a Tremere teaches the rituals it knows, an ancilla or elder teaches a Discipline it has, the Prince grants permits and pardons, the Sheriff deals with hunters. A row says when it comes free from your own Prince or when a boon you hold pays for it. Ask... opens a window with a row for each vampire who can do it and a button for each way to pay: Free from your own Prince, Settle a boon that vampire owes you, Pay with a boon... someone else owes you if it is the price or bigger (no change comes back), or On credit. A way you can't use is greyed; hover it for the reason. Hover a row for what it does Strings Mortals in other settlements who work for you, and who holds each. Each can be pulled once a week The world's news and the colony's own story are on the Chronicle and Our story pages under Rim by Night, at the top of the list down the window's left side. Each page holds the lines of every mod you have loaded; click a mod on its left for only that mod's lines, or a name under it for one colonist or home. Kindred write Embraces, torpor, diablerie and offices won there, and the courts' news tells of plots and showdowns, cities changing hands and blood hunts.

Opened from the Courts page. With a vampire of yours at the court, walking its town or in a caravan on its tile, it is in person. Otherwise it is a letter: you can take missions, buy services and cast rituals for the court, and everything else needs your Kindred there. It has three pages, four at a Camarilla or Anarch court, which always has more than one coterie. The boons you are owed and owe are on the Kindred tab. Page Section What you can do Court Standing The court's opinion of you, and your sect standing. Hover for exactly what raises and lowers it Court Who holds court The Prince and the other seats, highest first, each with its coterie Coteries The cards A card for each coterie: temperament, how it stands with the Prince's, members, power in ten cells, and "Plotting" on the plotters. Click one to pick it Coteries The picked coterie What it wants and pays, its members (leader marked), its missions with Take, your record with it, and during a plot the odds and Back the Prince, Back the plotters, Stay out Court Your Kindred here Present yourself (each vampire, before missions; walking into the town does it for you). Rank and missions done. Claim the clan's seat when your opinion is high enough Court Elysium Attend Elysium on the nights it's held. Each acknowledged guest raises the opinion Missions Offers Offers with their reward and standing, and which coterie offers each. Take one; it becomes a quest Missions Under way Your missions for this court or ending here. A caravan there hands over a vessel, a sealed casket or a runaway childe, stands guard at Elysium, or does a coterie's errand The buttons along the bottom: Listen for rumours (once a night: Golconda, another court, or where an old one sleeps). Offer a favour (once a season: a gift, a ritual, a Discipline taught). Sell a secret (Nosferatu). Give your art (Toreador).

A tree with one box per generation, from Caine down to the selected vampire's childer. Each box names the vampire, its clan and generation, and whether it walks the night, lies in torpor, was destroyed or was devoured. Unknown ancestors are grey. Click a vampire who is on the map to jump to it. See Embrace, bonds and ghouls.

The last 50 rolls the colony's Kindred made: who, what for, the dice and difficulty, and how it came out. Runs of the same roll are folded into one line ("3 of 5 passed"). Under each line a grey line says what the pool was made of and what set the difficulty ("Manipulation 3 + Social 2 + aura read 2, difficulty 7 (Mara's Willpower)"). Click a line to jump to the vampire. Colony rolls and big events also show in vanilla's Log tab. Dice pools. Hover a power on a vampire's Discipline tile to see the roll it makes: each part with its dice, the total and the difficulty. Before the power is aimed, a difficulty set by the target reads as a rule ("against the target's Willpower"). While a mental power is aimed, the odds under the cursor list the same parts. A power's grimoire page has the formula in a box at the top ("Manipulation + Social", then the difficulty).

Some events ask you to decide. Letter Choices Asks for the blood Grant it, make them a ghoul instead, promise it for later, or refuse (right-clicking the letter away refuses). A promise not kept within a year turns them against you. Each pawn has one letter open at a time, and a dying wish comes at most once a day A sire's demand Pay what the sire asks, or refuse. Refusing too often brings the sire in person The Pyramid's tithe Tremere only: pay silver or blood, or refuse Inquiry The Sheriff wants a vampire who caused too much breach: hand them over, lie for them, owe a boon, or refuse Dissent in the domain Give the Anarchs a say, or put it down The sleeper Talk to the old thing from the casket, let it go, or fight A debt called in Do what the creditor asks before the deadline, or refuse and take the scandal Some offers go to the Quests tab instead, where you accept them or let them run out: someone at the door (two days), a follower of a Path offering to teach (five days), an empty domain to claim (ten days) and survivors of a fallen home asking to join (two days).

Most menus open a list beside the window you clicked in, or above the gizmo. A long list has filters down the left with a count beside each, and Can pick only hides what can't be had yet. Click a row to read about it on the right, then press Choose, double-click it, or press Enter. A greyed row says under it what's missing. A list with nothing to read takes the row on one click.

The book button in the bottom-right corner, beside vanilla's play settings, opens the grimoire: a panel on the right edge that leaves the game running. It covers the alerts and letters while it's open, and its X closes it. It holds every clan, Discipline, power, ritual, merit, item and creature the mod adds, made from the game's own data, with this guide in the Kindred chapter. The setting "Grimoire", under The Rim by Night: Core in the mod settings, hides it. - Selected shows what to do about whoever or whatever you have selected, and links to read more. It changes as you select something else. A vampire or Garou hiding among your prisoners shows nothing of what it is. - Ask looks through every chapter. A question works ("how do I heal"): each answer shows the sentence it found, and clicking one opens that part of the page. - Browse lists every chapter, with a "what to do" section at the top of each mod's. - Gold, underlined words open their own page. Back returns to the page before. - The info button beside a page's title opens the game's own card, with every stat. - From the game: click a row on the Kindred tab, right-click a power's icon, or press the ? beside a tab heading. - The book opens where you left it until you restart the game.

Alert What it means Frenzy risk These Kindred are hungry or have no Willpower left, and the Beast is close to the surface. A provocation is more likely to set off a frenzy. Feed them, and let their mood recover to win back Willpower. Ghoul needs vitae These ghouls are close to withdrawal, or already in it. Without another drink they suffer, and a week into withdrawal the blood's gifts are gone and the years it held back catch up with them. A domitor with blood to spare gives a drink on its own once the night comes. If it can't, select a vampire and right-click the ghoul to give a drink of vitae. Kindred in torpor These Kindred lie in the deathlike sleep of torpor. Most wake on their own after some days, sooner with high Humanity. One that starved into torpor stays down until it holds enough blood: carry it blood vials or give it vitae. Keep them under a roof and away from enemies. Kindred outside near dawn The sun will be up within two hours, and these vampires are under open sky. Get them under a roof before it rises, or they will burn. Kindred starving These Kindred are nearly out of vitae. When the next night's blood comes due they fall into torpor if they can't pay it, and before then the sight of a vessel may hand them over to the Beast in a hunger frenzy. Feed them, or give them blood vials. Outsiders present Mortals from outside the colony are here, and they don't know what your Kindred are. Anything they see could break the Masquerade: feeding, obvious powers, frenzy, a wound that closes too fast. Keep it out of their sight until they leave. The Masquerade alert (Masquerade: …) shows from Suspected on, red from Exposed. It is Core's cover alert now, which also lists the Veil, a cell's exposure or a mage's Disbelief when those mods are loaded.

Everything the mod adds that you can hold, build, wield or meet, apart from the relics and lore texts, which have their own page.

A sealed vial of human blood, drawn at a medical bed. A vampire can drink it, though it satisfies less than blood taken fresh. A vial keeps something of its donor: how good the blood is, and any drug or sickness in it. It spoils within days unless frozen.
Fine blood, aged and sealed in a bottle the way a vintner keeps wine. A vampire drinks it for the pleasure as much as the vitae, and it keeps for a month without a freezer.
A stoppered vial of vampire blood from the ghoul trade. Nobody will say whose it was. A vampire who drinks it takes no bond from a stranger, but Kindred blood is easy to get a taste for.
A small gold bead with a point of vampire blood sealed inside by Thaumaturgy. A vampire who crushes it drinks the blood back.
A dead hand made into a candle by a Necromancy ritual. Light it and every outsider asleep nearby stays asleep for hours.
A shrivelled heart that still beats, very slowly, outside its body. Its vampire can't be staked while it is away, and meets Final Death if it is destroyed.
A figure that looks real from any distance. It isn't there.
A stretch of wall that looks solid enough to stop anything. Nobody can see through it, but anyone who touches it may find their hand goes in.
Gilt, velvet, candlelight and fresh flowers, laid over whatever is really there. The room looks and smells like a palace, and feels like one to anyone who doesn't touch the walls.
A gun emplacement that draws every eye and every shot. It never fires.
A sack of earth dug from this place. To a Tzimisce Embraced here it is home, and it has to be close by when they sleep.
A small lacquered box, sealed with wax and a Prince's mark. Whatever is inside is none of your business.
A place that a vampire has made wrong.
Something old, wrapped in rotten cloth, that feels wrong to hold. Nobody here knows what it is. It can be examined at a ritual circle or ossuary altar, or picked up and used blind, which is a risk.
A carved symbol of faith, small enough to carry. In most hands it's only a keepsake. Carried by someone of strong True Faith, it burns the Kindred they strike with wounds that heal like fire.
An object bound to one sorcerer by Thaumaturgy. Worn by its maker once it has settled, it strengthens their blood magic and holds a little of their blood. To anyone else it's a trinket.

The stake is a vampire hunter's tool first: driven through the heart of a downed vampire it holds the body rigid (see Being Kindred). The rest are hunters' weapons, and two of them use fire, which hurts Kindred worst of all. Weapon Damage What it is

10 melee A sharpened length of wood. Driven through a vampire's heart, it holds the body rigid until someone pulls it out.It can be used as a weapon. Against the living it's a poor knife. A thrust that finds a vampire's heart sometimes stays there.
9 melee A stake carved under a Thaumaturgy ritual. Wound a vampire with it and the tip breaks off and works its way to the heart over a few hours. The rest of the stake crumbles.

The coffin and the ritual circle are built from the Furniture and Misc tabs. Most of the rest appear when a power or ritual makes them: a vampire sunk into the earth, an illusion, a wall of water, living furniture made with Fleshcraft.

Build a tavern counter (Furniture tab) to open a tavern. Guests come after dark, buy from the counter and from any shelf in the tavern, and rent beds marked for them. Prices, guests and feeding on them are on the tavern's own page. Name What it is
A patch of freshly turned soil. Something is lying under it.
A heap of sticky white ash, damp to the touch. It stirs now and then.
A grey figure with a gargoyle's skin, standing half sunk into the rock.
A hard white shell of dried blood and fluids, the size of a person. Something inside it shifts now and then.
A faint shimmer in the air, and a sound just too quiet to hear. Enemies who step into it hear it all at once.
A place made holy by long meditation. Those who know the discipline of Bardo find their minds clear and their Beasts quiet here.
A long box with a lid that shuts tight. A vampire sleeping inside is safe from the sun even without a roof overhead. Anyone can sleep in one.
An old coffin, its lid fixed down long ago. Something lies inside. Whatever it is has waited a long time and may not take kindly to being woken.

A chair grown out of a living person. Their skin is the upholstery and their ribs are the frame, and it's warm to sit in.They're still in there. They don't age or need food. A vampire with Fleshcraft can shape them back into a person. If it's broken apart, they fall out downed; destroyed any other way, they die.

A dining chair grown out of a living person, folded at the waist with the back held straight.They're still in there. They don't age or need food. A vampire with Fleshcraft can shape them back into a person. If it's broken apart, they fall out downed; destroyed any other way, they die.

A table grown out of a living person, on all fours with the back spread flat and wide. People eat off it.They're still in there. They don't age or need food. A vampire with Fleshcraft can shape them back into a person. If it's broken apart, they fall out downed; destroyed any other way, they die.

A lamp grown out of a living person, drawn up tall and thin. A dim red light shows through the stretched skin, and it never needs fuel or power.They're still in there. They don't age or need food. A vampire with Fleshcraft can shape them back into a person. If it's broken apart, they fall out downed; destroyed any other way, they die.

A living person worked into a twisting knot of limbs and faces, made to be looked at. Kindred call it art.They're still in there. They don't age or need food. A vampire with Fleshcraft can shape them back into a person. If it's broken apart, they fall out downed; destroyed any other way, they die.
A circle of stone, wood or metal inlaid with silver and marked with occult signs. Blood magic of the third level and above is worked standing inside it, and rituals are taught here.
A low platform of stone, wood or metal laid with old bones in careful patterns. Necromancy rituals of the third level and above are worked standing on it, and necromancers teach their rituals here.
A dome of branches, leaves and vines grown tight together. A stranger can't find a way in. Something sits inside it.

Something lies still just under the surface. From some angles it looks like a sleeper.

The Masquerade is the one rule every vampire shares: mortals must not learn that Kindred exist. Your colonists already know. Everyone else is an outsider.

Every power is quiet, subtle or overt. Overt acts include feeding in view, frenzy, burning in the sun, healing a wound in front of someone, rising from torpor, an undisguised Nosferatu, and a drained corpse with fang marks. Subtle acts include small powers, shop talk between Kindred, and being dug out of the ground at dawn.

- When something overt happens, every outsider who can see it becomes a witness. Subtle acts only count if the outsider passes a Perception roll. - Colonists, ghouls and bonded thralls never count. Prisoners count only if you let them go. - Hostile raiders who see something overt may panic and run, but they're still witnesses. - Visitors and traders get nervous and may leave early. - An outsider sees 20 cells, half that in the dark. Out of doors the weather cuts it as it cuts a shot: fog halves it, rain and snow take a fifth. A stormy night is a good night to feed.

A witness stops counting if, before they leave the map, they: - die or are captured; - have the memory taken (Dominate 3); - are bound or discredited (a full blood bond, some rituals); - are Embraced or ghouled; - are talked out of it. To talk a witness out of it, select any colonist, right-click the witness and pick Talk ... out of what they saw. You get two tries a day: Way Roll What happens Explain it away Manipulation + Social at 7 On a success they believe it was nothing Bribe 40 silver They always take it. Seven in ten keep quiet; the rest talk anyway, and you aren't told Threaten Strength + Social at 7 On a success they swear to keep quiet. On a failure they run, and a witness who runs off the map counts Dominate Manipulation + Social against their Willpower Needs the Forgetful Mind (Dominate 3). On a success they forget A witness who leaves alive adds to the breach score.

One number from 0 to 100, in the Kindred main tab. It fades slowly while nothing new happens. Level Score What the world does Intact 0-19 Nothing Rumours 20-39 Visitors are warier. Your sect sends a warning Suspected 40-59 Hunters start looking. No traders at night. Camarilla standing drops Exposed 60-79 Hunter raids by day with fire and stakes. The Camarilla wants it fixed, or calls a blood hunt Shattered 80-100 The hunting order: organised daylight assaults with True Faith and fire You can turn the whole system off, or scale how fast breaches count and fade, in the mod settings.

Wandering hunters look like any traveller. They pass through, trade, rest, and are friendly until they see a vampire at work or spot fang marks. Then they turn hostile, or slip away and come back with friends. They carry stakes and fire, and some have True Faith. They show up more often once the Masquerade is suspected. Hunter raids come by day from Exposed. The hunting order comes when the Masquerade is shattered. A dead hunter may leave a notebook naming the breach that brought them. Hunters finish what they start. A fallen vampire gets a stake, then sun, fire or the head. By day they go straight for where the Kindred sleep. A heart kept outside its body (Serpentis 5) is crushed, or half the time pocketed: the hunter runs for the map edge, and if he gets away the Society keeps the heart at a hideout on the world map for six days, then burns it. Send a caravan before then. Hunters who escape come back with the next raid. A Society plant may also join the colony, waiting to stake a vampire in its daysleep. Hunters carry the weapons vampires fear: Weapon Who carries it What it does Wooden stake Hunters (spares), rogue thugs A weak melee weapon. A heart hit can pin a vampire Stake crossbow Hunters, mendicant soldiers Slow to reload. Its bolts pin like a stake Fire lance Firebrands Short-range flame that sets the target alight, then a spear Incendiary shotgun mendicant soldiers A shotgun whose blasts often start a fire Aspergillum mendicant Inquisitors A mace. With True Faith, every blow burns a vampire All of them can be crafted. In a world held to a lower tech level (by a mod like Rimedieval or World Tech Level), raiders only carry weapons from that era or earlier.

Some mortals have True Faith, a holy conviction that burns vampires. A vampire touched by it recoils, and it can trigger Rötschreck. At Faith 3 or more, a holy symbol carried into melee, or an aspergillum in hand, burns any vampire it strikes. Your own mortal colonists can gain it through their deeds against Kindred. Vitae, a blood bond or the Embrace takes it away.

Hostile vampires cast their combat powers, heal with blood, and stop to feed on your downed. They come only at night. They wait out of sight at the edge of the map until someone is alone outdoors, then strike, and they leave before dawn. Badly hurt, they run. From the 8th generation down they heal where they stand instead of falling back. They fight at their age. A neonate has Melee and Shooting of at least 6, an ancilla 11 and an elder 15, with a dot (ancilla) or two (elder) more on each Physical Attribute. Discipline dots grow with age and generation: a 6th-generation elder has 25, most of them in Disciplines it can fight with. A vampire you make in the making menu at the same generation and age starts on the same budget. Threat What it is Rogue bands Kindred raiders who carry off the downed, torpid elders included Archons Camarilla enforcers, sent after a blood hunt or very low standing Sabbat packs With shovelheads: freshly Embraced, mindless thugs Anarch gangs Anarch enforcers An elder An old vampire and its ghouls. If it gets away, it holds a grudge and comes back Assassins An Assamite sent for one of your Kindred

A hunter or an enemy vampire (not a shovelhead) who gets away from a fight with the colony can come back as its nemesis. It remembers the colonist who beat it, takes a new name and a scar, and learns to stand up to what hurt it most: fire, bullets, blades or blows. Five days later or more, it comes back with its side's next raid, a little harder for each escape. Putting it down pays the vampire who did it as much experience as a first time, and cheers the colony. Elders with a grudge and wights keep their own returns. The setting "Nemeses", in the Core settings, turns it off.

Watch your colonists too. A mortal may be an outside vampire's thrall, a Setite's corrupted plant, or a Sabbat infiltrator who joined to call a pack. They leak secrets, steal, or tell hunters where your haven is.

Now and then, at night, someone asks to be let in: a vampire fleeing a blood hunt, an abandoned fledgling, a runaway ghoul, a survivor of a fallen court, or your own sire. They come as an offer in the Quests tab, open for two days: accept it to let them in, or let it run out to turn them away. A fugitive from a blood hunt still comes as a letter, because you can also hand them to a court. The offer may not say everything, and Auspex can read what they hide.

Ghoul dealers sometimes visit a colony with Kindred. They sell vials of Kindred vitae, blood vials and willing vessels already hooked on the Kiss, and buy blood. Every vampire holds to a morality: Humanity, or one of the Paths of Enlightenment. Its rating, from 10 down to 0, sets how long torpor lasts and the most dice a vampire can roll by day. Each morality has its own list of sins. A sin counts when its rating is at or below the vampire's current rating: then it rolls a Virtue, and a failed roll costs a point. The further a vampire falls, the fewer sins still trouble it. How it all works is on Humanity and frenzy. On a Path, Conviction can take the place of Conscience and Instinct the place of Self-Control. Conviction is rolled after a sin against the Path. Instinct is rolled when something provokes a frenzy, and lets the vampire ride it with some control (see riding the wave). To take up a Path a vampire has to fall to Humanity 3 or lower first. A follower of a suitable Path may then come to the colony at night and offer to teach. A Path primer does the same job, and there is no button for it: the vampire reads the primer through like any lore book (see lore texts), and finishing it starts the study. Either way, after a season of study comes the test. In the tables, "8" means a vampire at 8 or higher feels that sin. One that has fallen to 7 or lower no longer does.

The human conscience the vampire brought with it from life, worn down a little by every sin. *Virtues:* Conscience, Self-Control, Courage. Death is the one subject worth studying. Its followers fear nothing about it, waste no chance to watch it, and never stand in its way. *Virtues:* Conviction, Self-Control, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Giovanni. Rating Sin 10 Fled in terror from fire or sunlight 8 Killed someone who meant no harm 7 Gone hungry when it could have fed 6 Lost control to a frenzy 5 Taken someone captive instead of killing them 2 Tended someone else's wounds

Vampires are the children of Caine and should live as what they are: apart from mortals, masters of the Beast, never denying their own hunger. *Virtues:* Conviction, Instinct, Courage. Rating Sin 6 Lost control to a frenzy 5 Fled in terror from fire or sunlight 1 Gone hungry when it could have fed

Followers indulge every appetite, let the Beast run with them, and kill only when passion takes them. *Virtues:* Conviction, Instinct, Courage. Rating Sin 10 Held back a frenzy 7 Lost control to a frenzy 5 Killed someone in a frenzy 2 Killed someone who meant no harm

The vampire is a predator and should live like one: hunting with its own body, feeding when hungry, killing cleanly and never for sport. *Virtues:* Conviction, Instinct, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Gangrel. Rating Sin 10 Killed with a weapon instead of its own body 8 Stood in the sun 7 Killed someone who was already down 7 Executed a prisoner 6 Gone hungry when it could have fed 4 Killed someone who meant no harm 3 Held back a frenzy

A knightly code of duty, loyalty and keeping one's word. Its followers stand their ground and never kill without reason. *Virtues:* Conscience, Self-Control, Courage. Rating Sin 3 Fled in terror from fire or sunlight 2 Killed someone who meant no harm 2 Killed someone who was already down

Followers believe pain teaches, hunger most of all. They go hungry on purpose, fear nothing of death, and see every killing as a lesson cut short. *Virtues:* Conviction, Instinct, Courage. Rating Sin 10 Fed before the hunger had grown strong 5 Fled in terror from fire or sunlight 4 Killed someone who meant no harm 4 Killed someone who was already down 4 Executed a prisoner 4 Killed someone in a frenzy 4 Killed a vessel by drinking it dry

The vampire is one stage in a longer change. Followers feed without delay, study the Beast by riding it, and care nothing for what others need. *Virtues:* Conviction, Instinct, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Tzimisce. Rating Sin 10 Gone hungry when it could have fed 6 Taken someone captive instead of killing them 5 Lost control to a frenzy 1 Tended someone else's wounds

Kindred are damned to be horrors whose work is to frighten. Followers kill sparingly, rely on no one and bow to no one. *Virtues:* Conviction, Instinct, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Lasombra. Kindred have slipped out of the great cycle and must send others back into it. Followers kill only for need and guard their own bloodline. *Virtues:* Conviction, Self-Control, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Ravnos. Path of Power and the Inner Voice

Power is the only thing worth having. Followers own their acts, reward the useful, help no one for free and never accept defeat. *Virtues:* Conviction, Instinct, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Lasombra, Ventrue. Every vice is a tool for raising a sleeping god. Followers corrupt others, help their own and show no one any mercy. *Virtues:* Conviction, Self-Control, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Followers of Set. Rating Sin 3 Destroyed a vampire of its own clan 2 Tended someone else's wounds

A Brujah's stoic discipline, older than Carthage. The Beast is an enemy to be mastered by reason, the mind and body are there to be perfected, and mortals are not to be used for more than a meal. *Virtues:* Conviction, Self-Control, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Brujah. Pleasure taken past every mortal limit tears a hole in the world's lies. Followers of this Setite Path spread rapture, break taboos and treat holding back as the one real sin. *Virtues:* Conscience, Self-Control, Courage. *Most often followed by:* Followers of Set. Kindred The Rim by Night: Kindred brings Vampire: The Masquerade, 20th Anniversary Edition, to RimWorld. Your colonists can be Embraced, drink blood, burn in the sun, sleep through the day and fight to keep what's left of their humanity. Around them is a hidden world of clans, sects, courts and hunters. This wiki covers everything in the mod: how being Kindred works, every clan, Discipline, power, ritual, Path, item and relic, each tab and menu, the events, and the settings. > In development. Balance will change and bugs are likely. Keep a backup of any save you add > the mod to.

1. Getting started: install, your first vampire, your first night. 2. Being Kindred: what changes about a colonist once they're undead. 3. Feeding: keep it open the first time someone gets hungry. 4. Menus and buttons: what everything on screen does.

Every alert this mod can show on the right of the screen. Alert What it means Kindred starving These Kindred are nearly out of vitae. When the next night's blood comes due they fall into torpor if they can't pay it, and before then the sight of a vessel may hand them over to the Beast in a hunger frenzy. Feed them, or give them blood vials. Frenzy risk These Kindred are hungry or have no Willpower left, and the Beast is close to the surface. A provocation is more likely to set off a frenzy. Feed them, and let their mood recover to win back Willpower. Masquerade: … Too many people have seen what your Kindred are, and the Masquerade is cracking. Traders stay away at night, hunters take an interest, and it gets worse from here. Keep feeding and powers out of sight of outsiders, and deal with the witnesses who got away. Kindred outside near dawn The sun will be up within two hours, and these vampires are under open sky. Get them under a roof before it rises, or they will burn. Kindred in torpor These Kindred lie in the deathlike sleep of torpor. Most wake on their own after some days, sooner with high Humanity. One that starved into torpor stays down until it holds … blood: carry it blood vials or give it vitae. Keep them under a roof and away from enemies. Ghoul needs vitae These ghouls are close to withdrawal, or already in it. Without another drink they suffer, and a week into withdrawal the blood's gifts are gone and the years it held back catch up with them. A domitor with blood to spare gives a drink on its own once the night comes. If it can't, select a vampire and right-click the ghoul to give a drink of vitae. Outsiders present Mortals from outside the colony are here, and they don't know what your Kindred are. Anything they see could break the Masquerade: feeding, obvious powers, frenzy, a wound that closes too fast. Keep it out of their sight until they leave. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Private Life Yes Keeps a whole second life, and the secret wears on it. Promethean Clay Its flesh changes almost before it asks. Prophetic Dreams Remembers its day dreams, and some come true. Pyramid Seal One more die on occult rolls. Pyramid Seal One more die on occult rolls, two more on rituals, and no easier to bond than anyone else. Quartermaster Runs a chantry's stores. Questioned This prisoner has been made to talk. Severity counts the secrets given up so far. Quietus blade Wielding a knife treated with blood venom. Rat in a Cage Yes Being penned in brings on real panic. Razor's shield The blade moves faster than the eye, ready to cut missiles out of the air. Read by a healer A healer's touch has found exactly what is wrong in this body, and the body fights it better for being known. Regard for Kindred How this person feels about sharing a roof with the dead. Reinforced bones The skeleton has been thickened and braced. Crushing blows do much less. Relic shock Yes Handled something old and strange without knowing what it was. The head is still ringing. Repelled by Crosses Yes Holy symbols hurt to look at. Ridden A vampire's mind is in this body, steering it. When it leaves, the body goes back to what it was. Riding the wave Yes The Beast is loose, but this vampire is steering it. Rot Yes Flesh gone soft and putrid at a touch. Roused by day Woken in the haven by its animals' warning, and keeping watch until the danger passes or sleep wins. Rowan Ring A ring that becomes a stake. A lucky thrust can stake a vampire. Rugged Bad Looks Hideous, but might pass for human in the right light. Schizophrenia Yes Voices, things at the edge of sight, and a growing sense that none of it is safe. When it gets bad they wander off, lost in what only they can see. Serpent's gaze Yes Held by a vampire's stare like a bird before a snake. Can't move or look away while the gaze lasts. Setite Initiate Joined the Followers of Set from another clan, with the cult's contacts behind it. Shade A ghost called back from the dead. Shadow play Shadows cling to this vampire and twist around it. Shots lose themselves in the dark and blows find less to hit. Shadow twin A vampire's shadow, loose and fighting on its own. Shrivelled Yes Shrivelled to skin and bone by Thanatosis. Dead flesh fills out again in a night. Shroud of Absence A pocket of nothing closes around everyone of the vampire's own within three cells. Shy Yes Hates being looked at. Sign of Thoth The banishing sign is made. The next power aimed at this mind is blunted. Silence of death No sound carries within six cells of this vampire. Splinter working inward Yes The enchanted tip of a stake broke off in the wound and is working its way toward the heart. When it gets there, the vampire is staked. Spooked Yes Felt something cold near a haunted place. Staked Yes A wooden stake through the heart. The body lies as still as a corpse, but the mind is awake and knows it. Stalking Closing on its prey, low and unseen. Its first strike lands harder. Attacking ends it. Statue shape The vampire has the shape of a statue. Stolen mind Someone else's knowledge and skill, held for a while. Stony skin Armor of Terra has left its mark: the face is grey and hard as rock. Storm-caller This koldun's storm is gathering or raging, and its lightning answers to it. Strike at the true flesh Every blow meets its target as bare flesh, past every unnatural defence. Sun rash Yes Setite blood under the skin: in sunlight it breaks out in a raw, painful rash. Sun sigil The sun's sign drawn in blood. Sunlight and fire do half their harm. War cry Battle-hardened for a while: the fear of fire and sun comes harder, and minds are harder to bend. War jaws The jaw has been lengthened and packed with hooked teeth of bone that tear deep. Every event the storyteller can send, what it means and what to do about it. Most can be switched off or made rarer one by one in the mod settings. Event Kind From day Again after What happens A blood vial order Event A court's courier waits some days for blood vials of a set grade from your storage. A trivial boon for ordinary blood, minor for fine. If it leaves without them, the court thinks less of you. A chosen vessel Event A court's vampire wants to drink once from one particular colonist, within the safe line, for a minor boon. Refuse and it may come anyway some night and feed if it finds them alone. A contract from Alamut Event Alamut offers the clan's vampire a contract, as a mission. A duel Event A court's vampire challenges one of yours to a duel at the colony, to the first one down. A win raises your standing at that court; refusing costs a little. A family errand Event The Giovanni family asks the clan's vampire for a human corpse from storage. A fleshcraft client Event A vampire who heard of your Tzimisce comes to be reshaped. Your fleshcrafter right-clicks it once to do the work; it pays with a minor boon or something else you'd rather have. A Sabbat client pays silver. A gathering to host: Barons' summit Event 30 days The letter that offers you an Anarch barons' summit to host, once that tier opens. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Blood Bath Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Sabbat Blood Bath to host, once that tier opens. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Brujah rant Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Brujah rant to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Conclave Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Conclave to host, once that tier opens. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Gangrel convocation Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Gangrel convocation to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Inner Circle's envoys Event 30 days The letter that offers you a visit from the Inner Circle's envoys to host, once that tier opens. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Lasombra court of judgment Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Lasombra court of judgment to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Movement rant Event 30 days The letter that offers you an Anarch Movement rant to host, once that tier opens. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Palla Grande Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Palla Grande to host, once that tier opens. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Primogen gathering Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Primogen gathering to host, once that gathering tier opens. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Toreador salon Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Toreador salon to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Ventrue oath-taking Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Ventrue oath-taking to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: war party Event 30 days The letter that offers you a Sabbat war party to host, once that tier opens. At most once a year. A Giovanni buyer Event A Giovanni courier waits some days for human corpses from your storage and pays well over their worth. A kennel order Event When a colony vampire is Gangrel or knows Animalism, a court member orders a guard-trained animal from your kennel, sometimes a ghoul. It waits some days and takes the first fitting animal at home, then offers a minor boon (major for a ghoul). A lair wanted Event A Tzimisce asks for a dark room to shape into a lair for a season. Anyone who looks in may see too much. It leaves a piece of living furniture behind and owes a minor boon. A Path's mentor Event A follower of a Path of Enlightenment comes for a colony vampire fallen to Humanity 3 or lower and offers to teach it. The study takes a season and ends with a deed a mortal would call an atrocity. A patron's errand Event A Lasombra patron sends the clan's vampire on an errand, as a mission. A request to be taught Event A court vampire asks a colony vampire who has mastered a Discipline to teach it: 3, 6 or 10 lessons, one a night, for a trivial, minor or major boon. Teaching Thaumaturgy outside clan Tremere costs Camarilla standing. A revenant offered Event 30 days A revenant family, through a court that sponsors it, asks you to take in one of its young. A revenant makes its own vitae and knows its family's Disciplines. A Sabbat family's offer pays in Sabbat standing. A scholar asks to read Event A scholar of a court asks to read in the colony's library for 2 to 5 nights. It needs a dark bed and feeds like any guest, then owes a boon sized by the library. A greedy one may try to slip a rare book out on the last night. A temple for the cult Event A few Setite cultists come to worship for two days around the finest piece of art indoors, the colony's temple. A trade of secrets Event A Nosferatu brood offers a trade of secrets: tell what you know of one court (it may hear and think less of you) and learn where the nearest court you didn't know about is. A vessel order Event A court's courier waits some days for a living vessel of one kind from your herd. Tick Herd on a prisoner or slave who fits and it takes them, owing a minor boon. If it leaves without one, the court thinks less of you. A vizier's studies Event An Assamite vizier comes to study. It is content if your lore makes a library. A voivode's guest Event A Tzimisce voivode's guest comes to see your fleshcraft: living furniture, flesh armour worn, or a vampire with Vicissitude. A warren wanted Event A Nosferatu asks for a dark room dug under a mountain for a season. While it stays, news from every court reaches you at once. It owes a boon when it leaves. An oath of fealty Event A Ventrue elder asks the clan's vampire to swear fealty. Sworn, the colony owes the elder a trivial boon and the elder owes it a minor one for its protection. Anarch gang Big threat 6 days An Anarch gang raids when your standing with the Anarchs is very low or they hunt the colony. Anarch unrest Event In a Camarilla colony, a vampire who resents the Prince starts stirring the others up. You answer in the letter. At most once a season. Anathema Big threat 20 days One of the Red List's Anathema passes near the colony with its retinue. One that has fought you before comes stalking; any other just walks through, unless you harm it or use a power on it. Anonymous benefactor Event 30 days The first gift from an anonymous benefactor. More follow over time. Rare, at most twice a game. Archons Big threat 6 days Camarilla archons raid when your standing with the Camarilla is very low, and much more often while it hunts the colony. Assamite assassin Threat Someone has paid the Assamites to kill one of your vampires. One assassin comes alone by night and waits for the right moment. Likelier when a colony vampire has a named rival or a blood hunt called on them. Backing a Brujah cause Event A Brujah elder asks the clan's vampire for silver for a cause, from storage. Pays in clan regard. Blood for the chantry Event The chantry asks the clan's vampire for blood vials from storage. Blood hounds Threat 6 days The nearest Camarilla court's hounds come asking after a vampire under blood hunt that you shelter. Hand them over for a boon and standing, let them search, or turn them away. Carrying the Gangrel's news Event A Gangrel elder asks the clan's vampire to carry news to a far court, as a mission. Caught by the dawn Event 60 days A court's vampire on foot, burned and hungry, an hour or two before sunrise. Get it indoors in the dark before dawn and it owes you a life boon; leave it and it dies in sight of the colony. Commission a masterwork Event A Toreador wants art, or a Ventrue a weapon, of excellent quality or better from your storage while it waits. Excellent earns a trivial boon, masterwork a minor one, legendary a major one. Court craftsman Event A court's Tzimisce or Gangrel comes by night to do a service you bought on the Boons page: fleshcraft on a colonist, or a kennel beast handed over. Never sent by the storyteller. Elder vampire Big threat One elder vampire and its ghouls, worth a whole raid. Wounds that would put a younger vampire in torpor barely slow it, though fire and the sun still work. An elder that got away last time comes back first, rested and with more ghouls. Feed from your herd Event A vampire who lost its herd asks to feed on the colony's vessels for a few nights, for a trivial boon (a minor one for five nights). Needs a prisoner or enough colonists. Foster a childe Event A sire asks you to take its new childe for a season. Any of your vampires can give it a lesson once a night; 4, 8 or 12 lessons earn a trivial, minor or major boon. Ghoul dealer caravan Visitors 8 days Ghoul dealers come to trade in blood and people. Dealing with them gets talked about, and now and then hunters follow. Giovanni extortion Event With a tavern or club to squeeze, a Giovanni wants silver each season to keep the dead quiet. Pay from storage, or refuse: the restless dead come within days, but the Prince you tell owes you a minor boon. Haunting Event 20 days Someone killed cruelly on the map comes back as a ghost and haunts where they died for ten days, frightening everyone near, your own people included, until it fades or a necromancer banishes it. Rare, and only where Kindred live. Hosting a seer Event A Malkavian seer stays as a guest. On arrival it names any hunter's plant or outside vampire's thrall among your colonists. Hunter infiltrator Event A stranger asks to join and the letter reads like any joiner's. It is a Society hunter who learns the colony for a few days, then goes for a vampire asleep by day with a stake. From the Suspected breach level. Hunter raid Big threat A daylight raid on a colony whose Masquerade has failed: small hunter bands at Exposed, the hunting order in force at Shattered. They go straight for any vampire they've been told about and don't give up while the sun is up. Takes the place of a normal raid. Hunting a renegade Event The chantry asks the clan's vampire to hunt down a Tremere renegade, as a mission. Judging a Ventrue dispute Event A Ventrue elder asks the clan's vampire to judge a dispute at a far court, as a mission. Keep a torpid elder Event A court asks you to keep one of its elders in a coffin through a season of torpor. Its enemies may come for it once. Woken and gone at the end, it owes a major boon. Keeping the family's ghost Event A Giovanni asks you to keep a ghost the family wants guarded for a while. Pays when the guests leave content. Lend a ghoul Event A court asks to borrow one of your skilled ghouls for a season. It leaves at once and walks back in when the time is up, and the court owes a minor boon. Neutral ground Event Two feuding vampires of two courts ask to settle their quarrel in your best hall tonight. If both leave unharmed before dawn, each owes a trivial boon. Notes for the chantry Event The chantry asks the clan's vampire for a treatise from storage. Occult trader caravan Visitors 10 days A trade caravan carrying the occult trader's stock: lore, relics, blood and sorcery supplies. Only to colonies with Kindred, about a quarter as often as ordinary caravans. Occultists Event Mortal occultists ask your sorcerer to work a ritual for them, at a cost in blood. They pay in silver, sometimes in an artifact, and one may stay on wanting the blood. Turned away, they may talk. Raid with a vampire Big threat 6 days An ordinary night raid with one vampire hidden among the raiders, for a colony with no Kindred yet. It slips away before dawn; down it first and you can capture it, recruit it or ask it for the Embrace. Rogue Kindred Big threat Hostile Kindred and their mortals raid by night. They carry off the downed, torpid elders included, rather than kill them. Only for colonies with Kindred; takes a raid's place. Sabbat infiltrator Event A stranger asks to join, already planted by the nearest Sabbat court. The letter reads like any joiner's; what they really are shows over time. Sabbat pack Big threat 6 days A Sabbat war pack raids when your standing with the Sabbat is very low or it hunts the colony. It sends its shovelheads, freshly Embraced and starving, in first, then waits to see what's left. A Grimaldi colonist may answer the Sabbat's call and turn on you. Setite corruption Event A mortal colonist has been meeting someone in the dark and comes back with a psychite habit, as a Setite plant. The habit shows; who fed it doesn't. Sheltering a brood Event A Nosferatu brood asks to shelter at the colony for a season. The guests need dark beds; it pays when they all leave content. Someone at the door Event A guest at the door at night, asking to be let in. A colony with no Kindred yet gets a fledgling or a survivor instead, and the letter doesn't say what they are; this is the usual way a colony meets its first vampire. Auspex can see what the guest hides. Sponsoring an artist Event A Toreador patron places a mortal artist with you as a colonist. Alive, still here and in a good mood after a season, it pays. Staked for the sun Event 60 days At night, a staked vampire left at the map's edge for the sun to find. Pull the stake and shelter it, and it owes you a life boon. Surgery for a vampire Event A maimed vampire asks your doctor or Tzimisce to make it whole. The healer right-clicks it once; the part grows back and it owes a minor boon. Take in a ghoul Event A vampire going into torpor asks you to keep its one to three ghouls fed on vitae for a season. They work as colonists meanwhile. All alive at the end pays a minor boon, some alive a trivial one. The enemy within Event An outside vampire slips in at night, feeds on a sleeping colonist and makes them its thrall. No letter. You find out the way your people would, unless someone awake sees a stranger bent over a sleeper. The Regent's inspection Event A Tremere Regent inspects the colony. It is content if you have a ritual circle and a research bench to show. The Scourge Big threat 30 days The nearest court's Scourge comes to destroy a colony vampire of the 14th generation or higher, whatever your standing. Naming a Scourge of your own, in a domain of your own, ends these visits. The Tremere want their share Event The Tremere want a share of a great library. With a Tremere in good standing, the Pyramid orders copies for a trivial boon. With none, a chantry asks to read. A colony outside the Camarilla that refuses gets a raid for the books. The wight returns Big threat A wight that got away comes back at night, alone or with animals it has ghouled, and goes for the easiest blood first. At most once a season. Thin-bloods Big threat A band of thin-bloods and their mortals. Only sent as the quarry of a Scourge's mission. Travellers Visitors Hunters or investigators arrive dressed as ordinary visitors. Investigators ask around about what people have seen, and once they have a name they leave to pass it on. Rare while the Masquerade holds, common once it's suspected. Travellers passing Visitors Hunters crossing the map on their way somewhere else, at any breach level. They want nothing from the colony, but they attack if they see a vampire. Tremere hit team Threat The Tremere send a small team for a colony vampire who knows Thaumaturgy and isn't one of theirs. Comes when one is found out, and now and then after. Tremere raid for the books Big threat The chantry you refused sends Tremere and their ghouls for your library. Each raider who gets away on its feet carries off a rare book, up to three. Only after a colony outside the Camarilla refuses to share its books. Under a blood hunt Event 30 days A vampire its own court has called a blood hunt on asks for one day's shelter. Hiding it is a crime against that court, and its hounds may follow; hide it for the day and send it on, and it owes you a life boon. Welcoming a kumpania Event A Ravnos kumpania passes through to trade, as a friendly caravan. Welcoming it raises the clan's regard. Willing cattle Event A few mortals who know what lives in your colony ask for its protection and offer to be fed on. Take them in and they join, devoted to the Kindred. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Every item, weapon and piece of apparel this mod adds. Value is the base market value in silver.
Name Damage Value What it is
15 ivory arrow, range 25.9 1800 A bow of rowan and ash backed with carved ivory. Its arrows wound vampires the way fire does, and the wounds heal as slowly. The ivory is old and cracks with use.

10 melee 8 A sharpened length of wood. Driven through a vampire's heart, it holds the body rigid until someone pulls it out.It can be used as a weapon. Against the living it's a poor knife. A thrust that finds a vampire's heart sometimes stays there.
1500 Black velvet gloves that grow steel claws when their wearer wants a fight, ghoul or mortal or Kindred. Claws are hard to explain to anyone watching.

900 A pair of spectacles with one lens cracked in a starburst. The world through it looks a little wrong, and its wearer sees patterns others miss. A Malkavian who wears it gets only true warnings of coming danger.

120 A shell of hardened flesh and bone plates, grown together from a corpse by Vicissitude. It turns blades and blows well. It is also unmistakably made of a person, and any mortal who sees it worn knows something is very wrong.

2500 A small bronze oil lamp whose flame never needs feeding. Its light is the sun's. Kindred within a few strides burn and may flee in terror, and any who stay in its light for long, even from further off, fall into the sleep that comes before dawn. Mortals in it feel steadier. Hunters prize it above anything. A vampire who carries it burns too.

1800 A gold ring made for a Malkavian elder who wanted, now and then, to think straight. While it is worn, no derangement can surface. Taking it off lets them all back in at once and worse than before, and the wearer can think of nothing but getting it back.

900 A Tremere-ground lens in a silver rim, made long ago to find Nosferatu hiding in plain sight. For a blood point and a hard look through it, the wearer sees through Obfuscate and Chimerstry as only the oldest Auspex can, and may glimpse other hidden things, the dead among them. Some of what it shows is not meant to be seen.
50 An object bound to one sorcerer by Thaumaturgy. Worn by its maker once it has settled, it strengthens their blood magic and holds a little of their blood. To anyone else it's a trinket.

900 A heavy silver ring engraved with lines from an argument nobody won. It steadies whoever wears it a little. A Brujah who wears it can call on Willpower to hold back frenzy, as the clan's blood usually won't allow.

2000 A banded granite amulet hung at the belt, holding the memories of everyone who wore it before. A new wearer gains a share of their skills, and a vampire a share of their occult lore. Not all of those memories were human, and the strangest can crack a mind.

1000 A gold signet ring cut with the mark of the Tremere Pyramid. Anyone who wears it has an easier time with occult matters. A Tremere who wears it works rituals with two more dice and doesn't bond as easily as the clan usually does.

800 A plain ring of rowan wood. In a fight it lengthens into a stake on its wearer's finger, and a lucky thrust can find a vampire's heart. Nobody searching for weapons gives it a second look. It is only wood, and it wears out.
900 A single black scale the size of a palm, hung from a cord at the waist. Its wearer moves with a snake's quickness. A Follower of Set who wears it is no longer troubled by bright light.

3500 A golden serpent with lapis eyes, worn at the belt. It once sat on Osiris's crown. Its bearer can see the dead without Necromancy, and by burning the body of a mortal sacrifice can open a way into the Egyptian lands of the dead. The dead notice in return: once a season something may follow the bearer home.

2500 A priest's robe, stained and heavy, with a blessing and a curse on it. It lends its wearer the Sepulchre Path's first four powers, but only if they know no Necromancy of their own. Anyone the wearer loves who comes close enough to touch is doomed to waste away.

900 A worn coin from no country anyone can name, kept in a pouch at the belt. Once a day it turns a vampire's failed roll into another try. A Ravnos who carries it finds the clan's vice a little easier to resist.
900 An iron key, black with age, hung at the belt, said to open every door under the old cities. Its bearer digs and tunnels better. A Nosferatu who carries it spends one less blood on Obfuscate.
1100 The pelt of an enormous grey wolf, worn as a cloak. It is warm and turns blows like good leather armour. A Gangrel who wears it takes the shape of the wolf without spending blood.
