The tips the game shows the first times you meet something. Tip What it is Clans and Disciplines Every vampire carries the blood of a clan.The clan gives three in-clan Disciplines, the powers of the blood, and a weakness every member shares. The Kindred tab lists both. Disciplines are raised with experience on the Kindred tab. In-clan ones cost less, and the rest need a taste of a teacher's blood first. A selected vampire's powers sit on one button per Discipline, and most of them spend blood or Willpower.Caitiff are Kindred with no clan. Other vampires look down on them. Diablerie Diablerie is drinking another vampire's soul. The Camarilla counts it among the worst crimes a vampire can commit.The diablerist drains a helpless vampire past its blood and takes its heart. If it succeeds, its own generation may drop, by more against older blood, and it may take a dot of a Discipline. It also loses Humanity, and black veins mark its aura for years where the right powers can see them. A soul stronger than the diablerist's may not go quietly. Dice and Willpower The blood answers to the dice.A roll throws one ten-sided die per dot in the traits it uses, such as Strength plus Brawl, and every die that meets the difficulty is a success. More successes mean a stronger result. A roll with no successes and at least one 1 is a botch, and something goes wrong.Willpower buys a sure success, and it is also how a vampire holds off frenzy. Habits, on the Kindred tab, sets when it may be spent. The roll log, opened from the Kindred tab, shows recent rolls. Feeding The Beast is hungry, and an empty vampire falls into torpor.Select a vampire, right-click a person or animal and pick Feed under Kindred. Mortal donors can also give blood vials with the draw blood operation at a medical bed, and a vampire drinks those like a meal. A prisoner set to "keep as vessel" is fed on whenever someone is hungry. Habits, on the Kindred tab, sets whom a vampire may feed on without being told.Taking too much from a mortal can kill them, and feeding where outsiders can see breaks the Masquerade. Frenzy Hunger, fire, pain and insult can wake the Beast.A vampire in frenzy attacks or feeds on whoever is near, and one in Rötschreck flees fire and sunlight. Fed vampires with Willpower left resist far better. Habits, on the Kindred tab, sets when a vampire spends Willpower; keep it on "to resist frenzy" unless you need it for rolls. Ghouls A mortal who drinks vitae becomes a ghoul.Ghouls stop ageing, heal with the blood they carry and can learn a little of their domitor's Disciplines. They need another drink about every fifteen days or they go into withdrawal. Every drink also pulls them closer to a blood bond with the vampire who gave it. Humanity Every sin lets the Beast gain a little ground.Humanity runs from 10 down to 0. When a vampire does something its morality counts as a sin, it rolls Conscience, and a failed roll costs a point of Humanity. Which acts count depends on the rating: at high Humanity even small cruelties count, while at low Humanity only killing still does.Low Humanity means longer torpor and fewer dice by day. At 0 the Beast takes over for good. Some Kindred follow a Path of Enlightenment in its place, with its own list of sins. Hunters Some mortals know what walks among them, and they hunt it.Hunters follow breaches of the Masquerade. Some arrive as ordinary visitors and ask questions before they show their stakes. A few have True Faith, which the Damned recoil from. They like to attack by day, when your vampires sleep, so mortals and ghouls must hold the line until dark. Sects and courts The Kindred split into sects, and every court belongs to one.The Camarilla keeps the Masquerade under its Princes. The Sabbat, the Sword of Caine, wants the Camarilla torn down. The Anarchs refuse the elders' rule, and the Independent clans keep their own counsel. Your colony's standing with each decides which courts welcome you and which send enforcers. The Kindred button at the bottom of the screen shows your sect, your standing and the courts you know.Courts deal in boons, favours owed and paid back. A boon owed is a debt, and it will be called in. Sunlight and daysleep The sun burns the Damned, and its wounds are slow to heal.Vampires sleep through the day. Under a roof they are safe; under open sky they burn. Give them a coffin or a bed in a roofed room, and bring them in before dawn. Kindred start on a night schedule; copy it to mortal colonists in the Schedule tab to keep them awake at the same hours. The blood bond Drink a vampire's blood on three different nights and you will love them.Each drink is one step of the bond, and only one a night counts. At the third step the thrall is fully bound: it adores its regnant and struggles to raise a hand against it. A bond fades only after a long time without another drink.Mortals, ghouls and Kindred can all be bound. Feeding a ghoul binds it a little more each time. The Embrace and generation A vampire makes another by draining a mortal and giving back a little of its own blood.The childe rises some hours later, of its sire's clan and one generation further from Caine. Generation decides how much blood a vampire holds, how much it can spend at once and how high its traits can go. Each step further makes the blood thinner. The Embrace also costs the sire blood.There is no undoing it. The Kindred The dead walk among your colonists now.A vampire doesn't eat or rest. It lives on vitae, the blood in its pool, and pays some of it every night. Blood also heals its wounds and powers its Disciplines.The Kindred tab on a vampire shows its clan, generation, Disciplines, Humanity and Willpower, and is where experience is spent. The Masquerade The world must never learn that the Kindred exist.When an outsider sees feeding, an obvious power or a vampire that won't die, the colony's breach score goes up. The Kindred button at the bottom of the screen shows it. A high score keeps traders away at night and brings hunters and angry courts. It falls slowly while nothing new is seen.Your own colonists know what lives among them. Visitors, traders and caravans don't. Torpor Torpor is the deathlike sleep of the Damned.A vampire in torpor lies still for days, longer the lower its Humanity. One that starved into torpor wakes only when someone gives it blood: carry a blood vial to it or give it vitae. Keep it under a roof and out of reach of enemies, since a stake or the sun can still end it for good. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Relics are rare items with power in them. Named artifacts exist once per world. Each clan also has a relic that works better for its own members. A relic's effect is on whoever wears it, wields it, or keeps it in their haven.

Every named artifact has a keeper from the start of the game: a court's Prince, a mortal settlement, or nobody. Now and then one is stolen or traded away, and the court's chronicle says so. - Courts. A Prince sells one from the collection kept there, for a major boon. Attack the court's city and the collection is somewhere in its house. - Mortal settlements. An artifact kept there lies somewhere in the settlement's map, unidentified. - Torpor crypts. World sites where an old vampire sleeps in a sealed stone vault, with a relic beside it. One door opens on a gallery of bone-filled niches, and the tomb is at its far end, where the elder's ghouls sleep in coffins on either side of it. The tomb is sometimes warded against Kindred. The ward is written into the floor, so taking the floor up breaks it. Lore texts, court gossip and missions reveal crypts. - Missions at court, elder raiders, gifts for big boons, and the anonymous benefactor. - The occult trader. A caravan that only visits colonies with Kindred, selling lore texts and the odd relic, sometimes an artifact nobody keeps. Only an artifact nobody keeps turns up by chance. One that a raider, trader or visitor carries off your map goes back into the world: to the nearest settlement of that pawn's faction, or loose.
Relics are found unidentified. Learn what one is by examining it at the ritual circle, by using Auspex's The Spirit's Touch on it, or by risking it and using it blind.

A charred scroll in a lead case, said to be the work of the founder of the Cappadocians and to hint at a rite for becoming something more than Kindred. It is written in old Chaldean and makes no sense to anyone short of mastery in blood sorcery or Necromancy. A vampire who can work through it learns a Necromancy ritual and much about the occult. Many who have read it were never quite right after.

Clay tablets of laws that legend ties to the First City. Very hard to read, and worth it: a vampire who masters them gains a great deal of experience and can take up the Path of Caine with no mentor, once it has fallen far enough from Humanity.

A shell of hardened flesh and bone plates, grown together from a corpse by Vicissitude. It turns blades and blows well. It is also unmistakably made of a person, and any mortal who sees it worn knows something is very wrong.
A knife with a dark sheen to the steel, treated with Assamite blood venom. Its next few hits carry aggravated venom whoever holds it. When the venom is spent it is an ordinary knife.

A bronze short sword older than writing, said to have been forged by a demon for a vampire of the First City. Every cut it makes drinks: the victim bleeds out faster and a vampire who wields it is fed. The Beast likes it too. A Kindred wielder has to fight off frenzy each time it drinks.

A curved plate of engraved brass made to sit over a vampire's heart under the ribs. No ordinary stake gets through it. Stakes made by ritual still find a way. It is heavy and the body never forgets it is there.

A Tremere-ground lens in a silver rim, made long ago to find Nosferatu hiding in plain sight. For a blood point and a hard look through it, the wearer sees through Obfuscate and Chimerstry as only the oldest Auspex can, and may glimpse other hidden things, the dead among them. Some of what it shows is not meant to be seen.

A stoppered vial of something that smells of crushed grass and iron. A vampire who drinks it turns mortal over the next few hours and stays so for a day: the sun can't burn it and it needs no sleep, but it has no Disciplines at all and a killing blow kills it for good. Only one dose was ever known.

A pair of yellowed bone dice spotted with old blood. Carried by a vampire, they turn its failures into successes, and every win turns one of the forty-two spots red. With every spot red they stop winning, until someone's throat is cut and the dice are washed in the blood.

A heart in a jar of green glass, still beating after centuries. Set down in the room where its owner sleeps, it brings them luck: every roll they make is a little easier. Nobody likes sharing a room with it.

A plain ring of rowan wood. In a fight it lengthens into a stake on its wearer's finger, and a lucky thrust can find a vampire's heart. Nobody searching for weapons gives it a second look. It is only wood, and it wears out.

A small bronze oil lamp whose flame never needs feeding. Its light is the sun's. Kindred within a few strides burn and may flee in terror, and any who stay in its light for long, even from further off, fall into the sleep that comes before dawn. Mortals in it feel steadier. Hunters prize it above anything. A vampire who carries it burns too.

A heavy silver ring engraved with lines from an argument nobody won. It steadies whoever wears it a little. A Brujah who wears it can call on Willpower to hold back frenzy, as the clan's blood usually won't allow.
A single black scale the size of a palm, hung from a cord at the waist. Its wearer moves with a snake's quickness. A Follower of Set who wears it is no longer troubled by bright light.
The pelt of an enormous grey wolf, worn as a cloak. It is warm and turns blows like good leather armour. A Gangrel who wears it takes the shape of the wolf without spending blood.

A thick, old account book of the Giovanni, every page a debt owed by someone living or dead. Kept in a Giovanni's haven, it makes the dead more willing to listen: one more die on Necromancy powers for a Giovanni on the same map.
A tall mirror in a black frame that shows nothing at all, not even the room. Nobody likes it in the house. A Lasombra on the same map spends one less blood on Obtenebration.

A pair of spectacles with one lens cracked in a starburst. The world through it looks a little wrong, and its wearer sees patterns others miss. A Malkavian who wears it gets only true warnings of coming danger.
An iron key, black with age, hung at the belt, said to open every door under the old cities. Its bearer digs and tunnels better. A Nosferatu who carries it spends one less blood on Obfuscate.

A worn coin from no country anyone can name, kept in a pouch at the belt. Once a day it turns a vampire's failed roll into another try. A Ravnos who carries it finds the clan's vice a little easier to resist.

A painting its Toreador maker never finished, and the most beautiful thing many people will ever see. A Toreador on the same map can look at it without being entranced. It restores Willpower each night and keeps the clan's fascination with other works away.

A gold signet ring cut with the mark of the Tremere Pyramid. Anyone who wears it has an easier time with occult matters. A Tremere who wears it works rituals with two more dice and doesn't bond as easily as the clan usually does.
A clay urn of earth sealed with wax, the soil of a place long gone. On a map with it, a Tzimisce rests as if on native soil, and the earth inside never runs out.
A short gilded sceptre topped with a Ventrue crest. It hits like a club and lends its holder an air of command. In a Ventrue's hand, every contested mental power gets a die more.

A living eye, wet and watchful, said to have belonged to a Ravnos of terrible age. Set into an empty socket it sees better than any eye, shows a vampire host visions of what is coming, and lends the powers to bend sight and flesh. It also changes whoever carries it, a little at a time, and never for the better.

A sealed stone coffin carved with figures nobody can name, believed to hold a vampire of the second or third generation. It has never been opened and can't be. Keeping it raises the colony in the eyes of its sect, and draws rogues who want it for themselves.
A plain clay jar that the Giovanni say was made to hold their founder's blood and soul. Whoever holds it has leverage over the family, which the sect values and the family does not forgive.

A golden serpent with lapis eyes, worn at the belt. It once sat on Osiris's crown. Its bearer can see the dead without Necromancy, and by burning the body of a mortal sacrifice can open a way into the Egyptian lands of the dead. The dead notice in return: once a season something may follow the bearer home.

A smooth old skull in a silver cage, said to be what remains of the Salubri founder after his killers were done. Thaumaturgy worked in the same room is stronger. Nobody who keeps it sleeps well for long.

A small wax tablet with verses scratched into it. Washed in blood and thrown, it latches on and spreads: after a few seconds the wax burns, worse every moment, and once it covers someone they can't move, and a mortal can't breathe. It comes off only if it cools by itself. One use.
A bow of rowan and ash backed with carved ivory. Its arrows wound vampires the way fire does, and the wounds heal as slowly. The ivory is old and cracks with use.

An ornate broadsword etched with eastern letters and older signs, made to kill a demon. Its wounds are aggravated to anyone, and it drinks every cut it makes: the blade darkens from silver to red, and the blood stays fresh inside until a vampire wielder draws it out through the hilt. Those who think it belongs to them never stop looking for it.
A curved Turkish blade, sister to the Sword of Dracula. Each cut drinks from its victim straight into a vampire wielder's veins. Its owners want it back as much as the other.
A massive thigh bone, polished by handling, said to come from a Tzimisce elder of the fourth generation. Its blows wound vampires as fire does. The Tzimisce would like it back.

A two-handed bone saw, rusted brown, once owned by a Gangrel killer. Its teeth have never dulled. It tears through anything, and the stories say whoever carries it can't be shot, cut or burned. That isn't quite true, but bullets, blades and fire do only half the harm they should.

A gold ring made for a Malkavian elder who wanted, now and then, to think straight. While it is worn, no derangement can surface. Taking it off lets them all back in at once and worse than before, and the wearer can think of nothing but getting it back.

A mummified hand, still supple, said to have belonged to a mighty Brujah. Grafted onto a wrist in place of the hand that was there, it is stronger than any hand should be, hits harder, and brings some of its owner's nerve with it. There are stories that it can raise the dead, which nobody believes.

A pearl-handled razor made by a Malkavian who couldn't bear the touch of his prey. A vampire carrying it feeds from a thin cut at arm's length: quicker, with no Kiss, and it looks like an ordinary wound. It finds its way to the purest blood, people who have never had a lover, before anyone else's. As a weapon it is small, and its cuts are aggravated.
Black velvet gloves that grow steel claws when their wearer wants a fight, ghoul or mortal or Kindred. Claws are hard to explain to anyone watching.

A banded granite amulet hung at the belt, holding the memories of everyone who wore it before. A new wearer gains a share of their skills, and a vampire a share of their occult lore. Not all of those memories were human, and the strangest can crack a mind.

A vast old tapestry of tangled threads that seem to move when nobody looks straight at them. Soaked in ten points of a vampire's blood and watched for a whole night, it shows scenes of the Kindred past, present and future: who the strangers nearby really are, courts nobody has mentioned, the places where elders sleep. What it shows can break a mind. The Tremere want it badly.

A priest's robe, stained and heavy, with a blessing and a curse on it. It lends its wearer the Sepulchre Path's first four powers, but only if they know no Necromancy of their own. Anyone the wearer loves who comes close enough to touch is doomed to waste away.

A plain horse whip with a small barb at the tip, made by a Tzimisce sorcerer for those who rule. In the hand of a vampire on the Path of Power and the Inner Voice, every stroke makes the one it cuts feel small and helpless: those who can't stand up to it fall to their knees, and a few never get all of their will back. In anyone else's hand it is just a whip.

A black Roman funeral jar dug up in Venice, cold to the touch. Once a season someone can reach the dead through it. With a body laid beside it and a vampire's blood poured in, it calls that soul back into the flesh; otherwise the dead answer questions about where old things sleep or where courts meet. Sometimes one of the dead follows the question back.
A huge book locked with iron, its pages in a cipher about the dead. Kept in a haven, it gives up a Necromancy ritual written out plain once a season. The Giovanni send people to take it back.

Long nails of a metal nobody can name. Driven into a vampire's heart, by surgery or by hand, one stakes like wood and drains the staked of Willpower at every dawn, as nightmares that never stop fill the sleep. The spirit tied to them doesn't like being disturbed.
A bowl of dark carved wood, stained from the inside. Everyone who shares a Vaulderie poured into it comes away bound to the others as tightly as the Vinculum goes.
A black chalice with no maker's mark. Packs who share the Vaulderie from it hold together like family, for better or worse.

Lore texts are vanilla books. A Kindred reader gains experience, and when it finishes a text it may learn a ritual, hear of Golconda, or recognise a relic. They go in bookcases. Each book remembers who has finished it and how far everyone else got. A book gives nothing, experience included, to a reader who has finished it or can't learn from it yet: a ritual above the reader's sorcery, a Path primer for a vampire already on a Path, studying one, or above Humanity 3, a treatise in a Discipline the reader lacks or already knows as well. Vampires study the books that still teach them something as Research work, two hours a sitting, from the floor or a bookcase, and put them back after. The Occult page of the Kindred tab lists every lore book on the colony's maps and what that vampire has made of each. Text What it is
Fragment of the Book of Nod

Loose pages copied and recopied from the Book of Nod, the Kindred's oldest scripture. Vampires read them for what they say about Caine, the first generations and the end of nights. A Kindred reader gains experience, may hear of Golconda, and now and then recognises a relic from its pages.

Clay and parchment copies of the oldest known passages of the Book of Nod, found in a buried city. Hard going even for a learned vampire, and some of it should not be read too closely. It hints at where old things lie.

A vampire's notes on one Discipline: what it learned, what went wrong, what it would tell a younger Kindred. A reader who already has the Discipline, at fewer dots than the writer had, learns from it. To anyone else it is a strange book.

A Tremere working book with one ritual of Thaumaturgy written out in full: the words, the signs and what has to be bled. A sorcerer who reads it and is strong enough in the art learns the ritual. Better copies hold harder rituals.

A Giovanni ledger that mixes the family's accounts with one Necromancy ritual written out in full. A necromancer strong enough in the art learns the ritual by reading it. Better copies hold harder rituals.

A short book that sets out one Path of Enlightenment: its beliefs, its hierarchy of sins and what its followers must give up. A vampire who has fallen far enough from Humanity can take it in place of a mentor and begin a season of study.
One clan's history as its own members tell it, flattering where it can be. Any vampire learns from it, and a vampire of that clan learns twice as much.

A hunter's notebook: sightings, mistakes and what worked against the things they hunted. A Kindred reader learns what hunters look for. A mortal reader may come away believing, and belief is how True Faith starts. One taken from a hunter who came here may say which breach of the Masquerade led them to the colony.

Records of a hunting order: names, sightings and suspected havens. Reading what the hunters know about this colony shows where the colony has been careless and lowers the breach of the Masquerade a little.

A charred scroll in a lead case, said to be the work of the founder of the Cappadocians and to hint at a rite for becoming something more than Kindred. It is written in old Chaldean and makes no sense to anyone short of mastery in blood sorcery or Necromancy. A vampire who can work through it learns a Necromancy ritual and much about the occult. Many who have read it were never quite right after.

Clay tablets of laws that legend ties to the First City. Very hard to read, and worth it: a vampire who masters them gains a great deal of experience and can take up the Path of Caine with no mentor, once it has fallen far enough from Humanity.

A koldun's book, part prayer and part instruction, on drawing power out of earth, wind, water and fire. A Tzimisce who reads it through can learn the Ways without a teacher. To anyone else it is strange poetry.

A traveller's journal said to be copied from Saulot's own, from his years in the East. Between the roads and the cities are notes on healing and on the third eye's two paths, the Warrior's and the Healer's. A Salubri, or anyone who has learned their arts, can learn from it.

Verses by a Lasombra of the old Spanish courts, about the dark that answers when called. Under the poems is a working guide to it. A reader who already commands the Abyss learns more of Obtenebration.
A Ravnos family's history, every page a story and half of them lies. Read closely, the lies are lessons in Chimerstry, for a reader who already has it.

Out in the world, Kindred live hidden inside ordinary settlements and answer to sects. Your colony has a sect (set by its first vampire) and a standing with each one, shown in the Kindred main tab.

Sect What it is Camarilla The largest sect of Kindred, ruled by elders and princes. It keeps the Masquerade and the Traditions, and punishes those who break them. Sabbat The Sword of Caine. Packs of Kindred who reject their elders and their own lost humanity, bound to each other by shared blood and at war with the Camarilla. Anarchs Kindred who threw out their princes. They keep the Masquerade and little else, run free states under barons, and trade favours without anyone keeping score from on high. Independents Clans that answer to no sect: the Assamites, the Followers of Set, the Giovanni and the Ravnos. Each keeps its own haven and minds its own business. Sect Likes Hates Camarilla Keeping the Masquerade, sanctioned Embraces, paid debts Breaches, diablerie, unsanctioned childer, Thaumaturgy outside the Tremere Sabbat Strength, Paths, the Vaulderie, diablerie of elders Camarilla ties, weakness, Humanity Anarchs Autonomy, helping each other Being told what to do Independents Business Depends on the clan You can change sides. Defecting angers the sect you leave, and it may hunt the whole coterie for a season.

Tradition In the game Masquerade The breach score. See The Masquerade and hunters Domain Present yourself when you visit a court Progeny An Embrace needs permission Accounting A sire answers for its childe's mistakes Hospitality Harming a guest costs standing Destruction Killing another Kindred needs the Prince's say-so Breaking one only costs you if someone finds out.

A court is a group of Kindred hiding in a settlement. The mortals there don't know. A world has a few of them, and you only see one on the map once you've learned about it: from an envoy, a captured vampire, a sleeper, a lore text, or gossip about a court near you. Your vampires also learn of a court by meeting one of its members, or by a court you know vouching for it. Courts change while you play, and the Chronicle in the Kindred overview reports it. A Prince falls only to a plot inside the court (see Coteries). A city can fall to a Sabbat siege or an Anarch revolt, and the Camarilla can take it back. A siege always comes from a court of another faction: courts in the same faction are allies and never fight each other. A court only attacks one it can match, and a court no rival can reach may face its own Anarchs instead. While the world has fewer courts than it started with, Kindred from elsewhere found a new one about once a year. With Garou loaded, werewolf septs raid courts near them, and with Imbued, hunter cells hunt them. Visiting. Send a caravan to the court's town. Once it stands on the tile it gets two buttons beside vanilla's Trade: Court opens the court's window in person, and Enter town walks the caravan into the town as guests. Every vampire in it is presented on arrival. The first time your Kindred walk a known court's streets, a letter names the Prince, says where Elysium is and opens the court. A caravan with no Kindred gets in too, but only as visitors to an ordinary town. A court vampire who sees a Garou of yours change shape or use a Gift there turns the whole city on you. While your Kindred are there, in the town or in a caravan on its tile, the court's window (also on the Courts page of the Kindred tab, whose row says At court) opens in person: Elysium, rumours, gifts, teaching and hand-overs. The court's first letter tells you all this too. A hostile town. A town at war with you takes no guests, but any caravan standing on it gets Sneak in beside vanilla's Attack, at night only. No vampire is needed, and neither a blood hunt nor a shunned sect keeps you out. The caravan walks into the town unseen: the town's people and guns can't go for anyone they haven't found. Every few seconds, a townsman with a clear view of one of yours (12 cells in light, 6 in the dark) notices something 12% of the time, 2% less for each dot of Obfuscate (never below 1.5%). From Obfuscate 3, Cloak the Gathering, the best-hidden vampire's dots cover the whole party. Once something is noticed, the town searches round that spot for about an hour and looks twice as hard. A searcher who comes within 3 cells may find who is there, half the time, 7% less for each dot. Whoever is found can be seen and fought. Attacking anyone gives the attacker away. In a court's town, once inside, press At court beside the court on the Courts page. The court house. Every court house keeps a guest crypt of three to five coffins that nobody in town sleeps in. While your Kindred walk the town they're yours, so a vampire caught by the dawn goes down into one instead of running home. None are lent by a sect that shuns you, or to a party with a blood-hunted vampire. The town's mortals go about their day: they eat, sleep in their own beds and walk the streets. After dusk most of the court's Kindred keep round the hall, and a few, different ones each night, are out in the town instead; at dawn they go back to their havens. A Camarilla Elysium is the grandest: columns down both walls, the Prince's chair on a silver dais, armchairs facing a gold runner, a salon with a long set table, and a sculpture garden in the courtyard. Talking. In a court's town you can talk to anyone of the court's faction. In any other friendly town, anyone will tell you the news and whether they've seen a missing colonist. See Talking to people. Attacking. A court's city is streets and houses around the court's hall in the middle, built in its sect's style: Elysium's gallery and cells, the Sabbat's chapel and fight pit, the Anarchs' rant hall and garage. Every vampire of the court has a coffin by rank. Its Kindred defend it, with a guard of three to six ghoul retainers in old-world gear.

A court's Kindred are real people, and they outlive its fall. Some die, some go missing, and the rest move to a court of their sect, their own faction first, or found a new one when three or more have nowhere to go. The same happens when the court's town is razed, by you or by another mod. - The Masquerade. Each court has a rating, shown in words on its inspect pane once you know the court: Secure, Frayed, Cracking, Breaking. Crowds of Kindred, feuds and your own breaches nearby wear it down; time and a Sheriff and Keeper in their seats mend it. A court with a worse Masquerade is attacked more often. - Sieges. When a war is about to break a court you know, it is under siege for a few days first, and a quest lets you go and help. Who dies on the map is dead in the world. - Letters. A court you know falling gets a letter: who did it, if anyone knows, a few of the dead by name, who is missing. Taking a court's town yourself says so. Rumors fill in the rest later, and the missing turn up again weeks or seasons on. - Refugees. Survivors who like the colony and are within reach may ask to join, as an offer in the Quests tab open for two days. - Your rank moves to the court most of the survivors went to, one step lower. - An empty domain. When a court near you falls and you have a Kindred in good standing with its sect, an offer in the Quests tab gives you the city, with your eldest Kindred of that sect as Prince. It stays open for ten days. - Ties. Your vampires take a mood hit when their sire's or childer's court falls. Core's settings, under The world of darkness, have a switch for all of this (off: a fallen home's people just vanish), a bloodiness slider for falls with no battle, and a world pace slider.

Rank belongs to one vampire at one court. Rank How What it gives Unpresented Nothing. Feeding there is poaching Acknowledged Present yourself Missions, feeding rights, hospitality Established Several missions, no open scandal Teachers, bigger boons Officer A seat and a mission for the Prince The office's bonus, a say in blood hunts Primogen Eldest of your clan there, high standing The right to Embrace Prince Recognition, or deposing the one there Rule over that court Each step past Established names a rival who will scheme against you.

Taken from the court window, never forced on you. They use vanilla quests: silence a witness, carry a sealed item, deliver a vessel, hunt a diablerist, guard Elysium, recover a relic, clear a rogue lair, bring a childe home, find a Golconda mentor, destroy a wight. They pay in boons, rank, standing and teachers, rarely silver, and experience for every colony vampire who saw it through. Assamites get contracts no one else can take. With Werewolf or Hunter loaded, a court asks for help against the other kinds you know: - Turn back a Garou pack (with a sept you know). A pack from that sept comes to your colony at night. Drive their leader off the map or down. If the leader dies, the sept's goodwill falls. - Guard a sept's caern (while that sept isn't at war with you). Keep a caravan with two fighters in the sept's town for five days. The days only count while they're there. Then the attack comes, and the best fighter's roll decides it: held is a major boon, and some fighters come back cut. - Break the hunter cell names a cell you know, and the warrant is served if the cell falls. A caravan with no home behind it still gets work: a court offers missions to any colony caravan within 20 tiles that has a vampire or a ghoul in it, leaving out the ones that need a home (raids sent your way, prisoners to hold, a breach to keep quiet). Rewards that would come by drop pod go into the caravan instead. A court keeps up to three offers, each open for ten days, and goes on posting them while you're away. You see them only from a home on the ground or a caravan near the court. A court that has received one of your Kindred always has at least two, and a caravan arriving at any court finds at least two waiting. Ghouls at court. A caravan with only ghouls in it can visit a court and take its missions. The court hires a ghoul without receiving it, so it needs no rank and earns none, and it won't take an Assamite contract, the Golconda errand or a judgement. Its boon comes one size smaller (a trivial one stays trivial), and it earns experience like a vampire. Boons it wins can buy a ghoul a ritual, the first dot of a Discipline drunk from a court vampire, or a drink of vitae at the court. Three missions are investigations: silence a witness, find who is feeding in the domain, bring a runaway childe home. The quest names two to four settlements nearby. A caravan with a colony vampire picks Investigate at one, once a night: Perception + Investigation against 7, two dice more with Auspex 2. Two leads reveal where the quarry is. A botch warns it, and the deadline comes three days sooner. A runaway childe can be captured, or right-clicked and talked round with Charisma + Social, then handed over at the court. The nearest court you know and stand well with also sends requests through the storyteller, like any vanilla quest: - Host a conclave. Three or four of its Kindred meet at your colony from after dark until an hour before dawn. The Sabbat or hunters come for them halfway through. Keep them all alive. - Shelter a refugee. One vampire for one night, with its enemies close behind. - Lend a ghoul. The court names one of your ghouls and borrows it for five days. - Bring goods. Blood vials, blood wine, gold or medicine, by caravan to the court's town. Each pays silver and a few vials of blood, with 10 goodwill and 10 court standing. One let lapse costs half that.

A Camarilla or Anarch court is split into coteries: the Prince's own, made of the Prince and the officers, and up to three rivals, each led by its eldest and never fewer than two. A rival left with one member takes in a plain member from a bigger coterie, or breaks up. A Sabbat pack or an Independent haven is one coterie, and nobody there plots. A court from an older save gets its coteries the first time it's checked. They show on the court window's Coteries page, which is hidden when a court has only one. Temperament. Each coterie takes its temperament from its leader, and it changes when a new leader takes over. It decides what the coterie asks for and what it pays. Temperament Wants Pays, on top of the boon Its missions Tyrant Control of rivals' herds, ghouls and havens Silver Raid a rival's herd, seize a rival's ghoul, storm a rival's haven, collect tribute Scholar Texts, relics, rituals A lore text Steal a text from a Keeper, recover a relic from a ruin, escort a scholar, bring back a ritual Trickster The court shaken up Any of the others Ruin a rival's Elysium, spread a rumour, free a rival's prisoner, swap a sealed item Traditionalist The Traditions kept Standing, sometimes leave to Embrace Destroy an unsanctioned childe, bring a breaker to court, clean up a breach, judge a dispute Schemer Boons and secrets A boon a size bigger Plant forged evidence, steal a boon, gather a secret, broker a deal Zealot War on the enemy sect and hunters A weapon Raid an enemy sect's site, hunt a hunter cell, burn a ghoul farm, send fighters to a sect war Each coterie keeps up to two offers on top of the court's own, and the court still has at most three at a time. The missions play out three ways: - A site a few days out (herd, haven, ruin, prisoner, enemy site, ghoul farm): clear it. - A quarry that comes through your lands within a few nights (ghoul, courier, childe, breaker, hunters): bring it down. The ghoul and the breaker have to end up as your prisoners. - An errand at a court: take a caravan there with the vampire who took it and press Do the errand under Missions, Under way. It's one roll, shown in the mission's tooltip, and a failed roll fails the mission. Some need more: bringing back a ritual needs Thaumaturgy or Necromancy, gathering a secret Auspex or Obfuscate, judging a dispute a Primogen seat, ruining an Elysium the gathering itself, and sending fighters three colonists in the caravan who can fight (some come back hurt). Power. Each coterie's power runs from 0 to 20, drawn as ten cells. The Prince's starts at 10 to 14, a rival at 4 to 10. A mission done for a coterie adds 1, or 2 for a major one. A mission aimed at a coterie takes 1 away, and so does each member it loses. Every few days one coterie may gain or lose a point on its own. A vacant seat is likeliest to go to a member of the strongest coterie. Do five missions for a coterie and it clears one scandal against your Kindred there each season. Working against the Prince. An offer that hurts another coterie says which one under its name, in orange when it's the Prince's own. A mission aimed at the Prince's coterie rolls to see if you were found out: Manipulation + Social against 6, a die easier with Obfuscate. If you're caught, the court thinks 5 to 10 less of you and the vampire gets a scandal. Plots. When a rival stays within 3 power of the Prince's coterie for 30 days, it starts to plot. A Kindred of yours with rank there gets a letter; otherwise the news reaches the Chronicle later. The showdown comes 20 to 40 days on. Until then each side offers one deciding mission, which counts 2 power for its side at the showdown and puts you on that side. You can also pick a side on the Coteries page: Back the Prince, Back the plotters or Stay out. At the showdown each side's chance is its share of the two scores. The losers' leader is destroyed or flees, and each of its members is destroyed, flees, or goes over to the winners. After a showdown, win or lose, that court has no new plot for a year, so it changes Prince once a year at most. Your side What happens Backed the winners The new Prince honours the old one's boons to you and raises the biggest a size. Your ranked Kindred there go up a step, to Primogen at most. A drop pod brings the spoils of the losers' havens, by their temperament: lore from Scholars, silver and a weapon from Tyrants and Zealots, a boon from Schemers, blood vials from Traditionalists, any of it from Tricksters. One time in three a loser who fled comes too, staked and in torpor, as your prisoner Backed the losers The old Prince's boons stay if the Prince fled and are lost if the Prince was destroyed. The winners answer by temperament. A Tyrant names your busiest vampire and sends enforcers after them. A Scholar shuts its teachers, rituals and lore texts to you for a year. A Trickster forgives you for a minor boon. A Traditionalist puts your Kindred back to acknowledged. A Schemer wants a minor boon and gives each of your Kindred there a scandal. A Zealot costs you 10 to 20 standing Stayed out The old Prince's boons shrink a size (a trivial one stays trivial), and are lost if the old Prince was destroyed The plot section on the Coteries page shows both scores and the plotters' chance. Hover it for the rule.

Each coterie has a regard for the colony, from -10 to 10, drawn as a thin bar under its power: warm at 4 or more, hostile at -4 or less, cool in between. It drifts a step back toward 0 each season. A hostile coterie offers you no work. Regard Change A mission done for it +1 Backing it in a plot it wins +2 A mission done against it -2 Backing the other side in its plot -2 Each of its members the court knows you harmed -3 Each season one of your vampires sits in a coterie it plots against -1 Leaving it -2, and 1 of its power The detail pane lists each step with a tick or a cross for each thing it needs, and the button under it. - Join. A vampire Established at the court or higher, five missions done for the coterie by anyone in the colony, and its regard at 0 or more. Each vampire is in one coterie per court at most. While one of yours is in it, a mission done for it adds 1 more power, and each of your members there counts the power it gave. A rival can still offer work aimed at your coterie: the offer says so in orange, and taking it gives your vampire there a scandal. - Take the lead. Once the power your missions gave it since joining is half its power or more. With two of yours in it, the one who gave more (then the one who joined first) leads. You pick its temperament once, for good. A coterie you lead offers you no work, and it keeps you as leader until your vampire dies, leaves the court's ranks or leaves the coterie. - Move against the Prince. As leader, within 3 power of the Prince's coterie, after the year's wait, at a court of your sect (an Anarch colony can take a Camarilla court, which becomes Anarch). The plot starts at once and the showdown comes 20 to 40 days later. In a plot your vampires stand with their own coteries, and the Back buttons are hidden. One on the losing side leaves its coterie. Win as plotters and your leader becomes Prince: your other Kindred in the coterie take the seats the losers held, every member there owes the new Prince a trivial boon, and the court page gets a Your domain section. - Tribute: 100 silver and 25 for each member, by drop pod each season. - The Prince's word: your own vampires get leave to Embrace, a pardon and a blood hunt lifted there for nothing. - Call a blood hunt on any member. It is just when the member's coterie is hostile to you or it is on your grudge list. Otherwise your sect thinks 5 less of you. Rivals plot against your coterie as against any Prince. Lose a showdown and your vampires there go back to acknowledged, leave their coteries, and the court shuts its doors to you for a year: no missions, services or joining.

A court only knows the colony took or destroyed one of its vampires if someone who knew the victim saw it and lived to tell. That means the court's own people, its other Kindred, the victim's kin and friends, and its ghouls. Strangers, traders and other factions only saw a fight. A witness has to be awake and within 20 cells with a clear line of sight. They show on the witness alert, and the court hears once one of them leaves the map: kill them, take them too, or keep them as prisoners and the secret holds. A prisoner who is let go or escapes tells their court who held them. So does a captive you release. The court learns you Cost Took one of its vampires 5 court standing, 15 for the Prince Destroyed one 10 court standing; the Prince 30, and 30 with its sect too A vampire the colony holds, awake or in torpor, fades from its court whether the court knows or not. The court only knows it's gone. - At once its coterie loses 1 power, and 1 more every 10 days, 3 at most. The Chronicle says it vanished. - After 15 days it loses its office, which passes on as if it had been destroyed. - After a year (60 days) the court strikes it off. If it ever comes back, it rejoins as a plain member. The court window marks your captives "(your prisoner)" in the members list.

Select a colonist and right-click someone to talk to them: a prisoner (Question ...), a witness (see Witnesses), or someone in a court's, sept's or hunter cell's town (Talk to ...). Your colonist walks over and the talk window opens. Pick what to ask about, then how to put it. Each way shows its roll under the button. Way Roll Kindly Charisma + Social at 6 Firmly Manipulation + Social at 6 Threaten Strength + Social at 7. It hurts their mood Bribe 40 silver, always answers. One of the court's own costs double and its leader triple Dominate Manipulation + Social against their Willpower, from Dominate 2. Never on a vampire of lower generation Presence Charisma + Social against their Willpower, for a vampire with Presence but too little Dominate Owe a boon At a court, to one of its Kindred: the colony owes them a minor boon instead of paying silver Each roll is a point harder against anything supernatural. Nobody lies, so a poor roll just gets nothing. In a town, each person answers one question, then wants three days before the next (a setting). You can ask: - Small talk. The weather, the neighbours, whatever is on their mind; a vampire mostly gossips about the court. It costs nothing, always gets an answer, and can go on all night. - What's the news? Word of the world's courts, septs and cells, or the court's own gossip. - Where is... Pick a place from what they could know of: another court you don't know yet (Kindred speaking to Kindred), or a torpor crypt (a court's own Kindred, and most of them don't know of one). The question only shows up when there's somewhere to ask about. - Have you seen... A colonist someone took. The settlement holding them goes on the map. - What troubles you? The court has work: a new offer on its missions. A court's own vampires answer more, and a good roll (two successes or more) tells more: - Who are you? Their clan, generation and sire; a good roll adds their office and coterie. - Who do you owe? The boons between them and the colony; a good roll adds an old debt at court. - What is the court planning? The plot against the Prince and when it comes to a head; a good roll adds its odds. - Who is out of favour? The weakest coterie out of power and its leader. - Any scandals? The Harpies' gossip. A good roll gets a real secret about one of the court, which you can keep for a minor boon or report to the Prince. - Where does one feed here? How wary the herd is after your hunts; a good roll gets fresh ground, and the town forgets your last hunt there. - What else hunts the night? The nearest sept, hunter cell or other home of a kind you've already met, marked on the map. Half their answers end with a word in their clan's manner: a Brujah's rant, a Malkavian's riddle, a Nosferatu's price. A threat costs the town 3 goodwill whatever the roll. Using Dominate or Presence on one of the court's own in its town breaks Elysium if the court notices, which it does four times in ten. Your standing there falls by 10 and the court thinks less of the colony. A vampire talking in a sept's or a cell's town passes for an ordinary visitor. Asking kindly and bribing are safe. A threat gives it away one time in five, a Discipline about one in three, a failed roll one in ten and a botch one in two. Found out, the town turns on the colony.

Kindred trade favours. The boon ledger in the Kindred main tab shows who owes whom and how much: trivial, minor, major or life. A bigger boon pays for a smaller price, but smaller boons never add up to a bigger one. Size Earned by Buys at court Trivial An errand (a vessel, a sealed casket), six blood vials, a low ritual cast for the court, a hungry guest sent home fed, a Nosferatu secret, three corpses for the Giovanni Word of another court, a night's feeding for one vampire Minor Standing guard at Elysium, scouting a rogue band, a day's shelter for a court's vampire, an occult item or lore text, a level 3 ritual, a Toreador masterwork, handing over a fugitive, teaching a Discipline you have at 3 or 4 dots Permission to Embrace, where an elder lies in torpor, the Embrace for a ghoul, where an enemy hides, the way to a Golconda mentor Major Hunting a diablerist, a contract, destroying a wight, releasing a captured vampire, an artifact or clan relic, a level 4 or 5 ritual, teaching a Discipline you have at 5 dots Where an artifact is kept, a teacher, a scandal buried, witnesses silenced, a step up in rank, the hunters' files lost, an elder destroyed, the court's fighters, an artifact Life Getting a court's vampire through a hunters' raid alive (sanctuary), destroying one of the Red List, one of the three life boons below A blood hunt lifted, a pardon for diablerie Every boon in the ledger says why it is owed and at which court. Paying for a service, you pick which boon to spend. Any vampire can spend a boon the colony earned. Credit is harder: a trivial or minor service needs an Acknowledged vampire at that court, a major one Established, a life boon an Officer, and no court gives credit while the colony owes a boon anywhere. The Prince's artifact is picked from the collection that court actually keeps, so a court with none can't sell one. Some of what a court sells is just what it knows. For a minor boon it tells you where an elder lies in torpor, and the crypt shows on the world map; every crypt keeps an artifact or a clan relic. Other minor and major boons buy more. You can ask where a named artifact is kept: another court or a mortal town, which then shows on the map. You can ask where an enemy hides: a debtor who fled turns up at a court you know, so you can call its boon in, and if no debtor is missing, a Camarilla court shows you where one of the Red List is right now. Or a vampire of high Humanity who hasn't heard of Golconda can be told of it, which puts the mentor's errand on that court's missions. Where an artifact is kept costs a major boon, since there is only one of each. A ghoul can ask a court's vampire for the Embrace. Each vampire who could be its sire has a row under Court help (not a Blood Brother, a thin-blood or one in torpor). The minor boon only buys a hearing. The vampire sets the ghoul a hard errand from the court's missions, worth a major boon, and when it's done, comes to your colony by night once the ghoul is home and Embraces it. The childe has its sire's clan and sect, one generation below it, and keeps what it learned as a ghoul. A ghoul's boons survive the Embrace. A court takes one favour a season (a gift, a ritual or teaching), through Offer a favour in the court window. A boon is owed by one vampire, not by its court. If it is destroyed the boon is gone; if it flees or moves, the boon goes with it. The ledger lists each boon's size, debtor, seat, where it is now and why it is owed, and a debtor nobody can find shows a "?". - Court help, on the Boons page of the Kindred tab, lists what each court you know can do for you now, by who would do it: the Prince for leave to Embrace, a pardon, a lifted hunt or an artifact; the Seneschal for a step up or feeding rights; the Sheriff or a Hound for the hunters or fighters; the Harpy for a scandal; the Keeper for a lore text; a sorcerer for a ritual it knows; an ancilla or elder with the dots for a Discipline (neonates don't teach). A list down its left side picks the price, trivial to life, and the services fold by category. Ask... on a row lists every way to pay for it. A boon owed by the one who does it is called in; otherwise you can hand over a boon someone else owes you, as long as it is the price or bigger. No change comes back: a major boon spent on a minor service is gone. - Fleshcraft and kennels: a Tzimisce at the court reshapes a colonist (beautified, hardened flesh, bone spurs or reinforced bones, minor), regrows every lost part and smooths every scar (major), makes a human ghoul a szlachta (minor), or gives any colony animal, modded ones too, bone plates, war jaws, keen senses or the war beast's frame (minor). A Gangrel sells a kennel beast (minor): a husky, labrador, wolf, warg, cat, lynx, cougar, panther or grizzly, and with Odyssey a crow, vulture or macaw, fully trained and full of vitae but bound to nobody. You pick what it was trained for: hunting, guarding or, for a bird, scouting (see Embrace, bonds and ghouls). The craftsman comes to the colony by night, walks to the one it came for and does the work there. If it has to leave with the work undone, and nobody here hurt it, its court owes you the price back. - Credit is owed to the vampire who gave the service, and ends if that vampire is destroyed. - Call it in from the Kindred tab once you know where the debtor is. You pick one thing up to the boon's size: blood, a vessel, a word at its court, an introduction to another court, finding someone you lost track of, shelter from a blood hunt, a ghoul for a season, an errand run for you, a vote in a coming showdown, the debtor and its ghouls in a fight (more ghouls the older it is, four with a seat), or the debtor for good. Each clan has a favour of its own on top: Brujah rabble, a Gangrel guide, a Malkavian prophecy, a Nosferatu secret, Toreador art, a Tremere ritual, Ventrue money, Lasombra shadows round a caravan, Tzimisce fleshcraft, an Assamite contract, a Setite vice, a Giovanni ghost's tale, a Ravnos decoy, Salubri healing, a song from a Daughter of Cacophony, a Kiasyd lore text, a Gargoyle guard. New ways to earn one: carry a downed friendly vampire to safety (minor) or wake one from torpor with colony blood (major), keep quiet about a visitor you saw break the Masquerade (or report it to its Prince for 5 standing), or buy a trivial favour from a member with 6 blood vials or 200 silver from a caravan, once a season per court. A boon offered this way comes as a letter where you pick the boon, standing at its court (3, 6, 10 or 15 by size), silver (50, 150, 400 or 1000), or nothing. When a court calls in what the colony owes, it asks for a task of the same size: a vessel, a scouting run, a diablerist destroyed, or a far stronger lair for a life boon. A refused debt is a scandal. A refused life boon brings a blood hunt.

Three rare events, about once a year each, come only to a colony with Kindred that knows a court: - Caught by the dawn. A court's vampire runs in an hour or two before sunrise, burned and starving. Let it in and get it under a roof before the sun is up, or it burns in sight of the colony. Housed through the day it owes a major boon; if hunters follow it (one time in four) and you beat them off, a life boon. A bed or coffin in a room with no open roof also raises your standing with its court by 3. - Staked for the sun. At night you find a court's vampire at the edge of the map with a stake in its heart, tied out for the sun. Rescue it, pull the stake with the remove stake operation, and when it leaves it owes a life boon. Whoever staked it learns who spoiled it: hunters or werewolves raid within one or two seasons, and a rival court thinks 10 less of the colony. - Under a blood hunt. A Camarilla vampire hunted by its own court asks for one day's roof. Half the time the court's blood hounds come that same night. Taking it in costs no standing unless the hounds find it or you turn them away. Hide it through the day and send it on, and it owes a life boon. Hand it to the hounds, or take it prisoner and carry it to its court by caravan (the Hand back button on the town), and it owes nothing, but the court owes a minor boon and you gain 10 standing with the court and the Camarilla. Killing it gains 5. Anyone under blood hunt is disowned by its faction when you take it prisoner, and hurting or taking it costs no goodwill.

Kindred of the courts you know ask for what the colony has. At most one library visit and one mentoring stay a season, never both at once. A guest needs a coffin, or a bed in a room with no open roof, and feeds on the colony's blood. - The library. Lore books make the colony a draw: a rare text (sorcery, a Path, a hard read, one that shows a crypt or teaches a Discipline) counts 3, any other lore book 1, your own treatises 1 each up to 10, each title once. At 10 points it is a known library, at 30 a great one, at 60 the largest outside Ceoris. A scholar of the Tremere, Giovanni, Tzimisce, Assamites, Setites, Nosferatu or Toreador asks to read for 2 to 5 nights and owes a trivial, minor or major boon by the tier. On the last night a scheming or tricky one may try to take a rare book (one time in four, one in twenty for others, half that with a colonist in the room). Caught, it owes a major boon and its court loses 10 standing; not caught, the book is gone. - The Tremere want their share. At a great library the Pyramid writes. With a Tremere of the colony in good standing it orders copies of 2 to 4 rare books: any colonist on research work copies them at a table, four hours a book, for a trivial boon or its worth; refusing is a refused tithe. With no Tremere, a chantry of your sect asks to read for a minor boon. A colony outside the Camarilla near a Camarilla chantry gets that offer once, and a refusal brings a Tremere raid in points; each raider who gets away takes a rare book, up to three. - Mentoring. A colony vampire at its generation's cap in a Discipline (5 dots, or the most its generation allows) can be asked to teach it: 3, 6 or 10 lessons for a trivial, minor or major boon, one a night, the student staying twice that many nights. Right-click the student with the teacher selected to give tonight's lesson. Fewer lessons pay less; none at all costs the court 5 standing. All of them done, the student leaves with a new dot. Teaching Thaumaturgy outside the Tremere costs 15 Camarilla standing; Obfuscate, Dominate, Vicissitude or a sorcery taught outside the teacher's clan costs it a point of its clan's regard.

Courts also ask the colony for smaller things, one letter every ten days or so, each with its own setting: - Keep a sleeping elder. An elder of the 8th generation or older sleeps a season of torpor in the colony; carry it to a coffin and keep it safe for a major boon. Half the time its enemies hear where it lies and come once. - Feed from your herd. A vampire who lost its herd feeds on the colony's vessels for 3 nights (trivial boon) or 5 (minor). The colony needs a prisoner or four colonists. - Foster a childe. A new childe stays a whole season and brings a vial of blood for each night, so it costs the colony a dark bed and little else. Any colony vampire right-clicks it to give a lesson, once a night. 4 lessons is a trivial boon from the sire, 8 a minor one and 12 a major one; none costs standing. One time in three the childe asks to stay as a colonist. - A blood order. A courier waits 5 days for 4 to 8 vials of ordinary or fine blood in storage: a trivial or minor boon, and 3 standing lost if it leaves empty-handed. - A masterwork. A Ventrue wants a weapon and a Toreador a piece of art, of excellent quality or better, from storage within 10 days: trivial, minor or major by quality. - Neutral ground. Two vampires of different courts meet in the colony's best hall for a night. If both leave unharmed, each owes a trivial boon. - Make one whole. A vampire missing a part asks a colonist with Medicine 8 (or Vicissitude 2) to restore it: right-click it with the healer selected, for a minor boon. - A fleshcraft client. A vampire wants one of the shapes Fleshcraft makes (beauty, hardened flesh, bone spurs, reinforced bones) from a colony vampire with Vicissitude 2. Right-click it with the fleshcrafter selected. It offers a minor boon, or standing, silver or nothing as you choose. A Sabbat pack at peace with you can send one too; it pays silver, the price of a major boon. - A kennel order. A colony vampire who is Gangrel or knows Animalism can be asked for a beast of one of the kennels' kinds, taught guard, within 7 days. The first one at home goes with the courier for a minor boon. One order in three wants a ghoul too, for a major boon. - Lend a ghoul. A court borrows a ghoul with a skill at 8 or more for a season; it is away the whole time and walks back in for a minor boon. - Take in ghouls. A vampire going into torpor leaves one to three ghouls with the colony for a season. They work as colonists, and your vampires keep them fed. All alive when they go home is a minor boon, some a trivial one. More favours, in the same group: - A vessel order. A courier waits 5 days for a living vessel of one kind (men, women, the old, soldiers, scholars, artists, tribals). Tick Herd on a prisoner or slave who fits and the courier takes them, for a minor boon. - A Giovanni buyer. The family's courier waits for two to four human corpses in storage and pays twice what they're worth. No Giovanni of your own needed. - A warren wanted. A Nosferatu wants a room dug under overhead mountain, and a dark bed, for a season. While it stays, news from every court reaches you at once. A minor boon when it leaves. - A lair wanted. A Tzimisce shapes a lair in a dark room for a season. Anyone who looks in may see too much. It owes a minor boon and leaves a fleshcrafted armchair behind, someone inside.

The court window gets a Trade page, after Missions, when the blood price has moved, you hold one of the court's Kindred, or one of its couriers is waiting. Its tab counts the captives and orders. - Blood market. Vials, Kindred vitae and hemogen share one price. A hunter raid, a blood hunt, the Scourge, a new breach level and a month with no sales push it up; selling vials to traders brings it down. Each cause wears off over a season. Traders, your tavern and your club all use it, and the page lists why it moved. - Vessels. A court city's traders buy and sell prisoners and slaves, as slavers do. The page says what yours are worth. - Captives. A court's vampire you hold as a prisoner, or in torpor at home. Ransom sends it home for silver by its generation and 10 goodwill, though the court now knows you held it. Sell to a rival... pays half again more; the buyer takes it in, and its own court hears who sold it a third of the time. - Orders. The couriers waiting at your colony and how many days they'll wait.

A few more requests, each with its own setting: - Giovanni extortion. With a tavern counter, a Giovanni wants 300 silver a season. Pay from storage, or refuse: the restless dead come within days, and the Giovanni's Prince owes you a minor boon for telling. - Occultists. Mortal cultists ask a vampire of yours who knows a ritual to work one. It costs 2 blood and pays 150 to 400 silver, now and then an artifact, and one of them may stay on, devoted. Turned away, they may talk. - A duel. A court's Kindred challenges one of your vampires by name. It comes for a night and they fight until one goes down: a win is 8 standing at its court, refusing costs 3. - A chosen vessel. A Kindred wants to drink once from one colonist, within the safe line, for a minor boon. Refused, half the time it comes anyway and feeds when that colonist is asleep or alone. - Willing cattle. One to three mortals who know what you are ask to join, devoted to the Kindred.

Each vampire of the thirteen clans has a rank in its clan, shown on the Kindred tab's Sheet page under its name. The rank comes from what its Disciplines, paths and rituals would cost in Experience: a Discipline at N dots is worth 10 plus 5 for each dot past the first times the dot before it (x7 out of clan), a ritual twice its level. Rank Disciplines worth Also needs Unknown less than 50 Known 50 Respected 100 the 10th generation or lower A voice of the clan 150 the 8th generation or lower Every rank also needs the clan's regard at 0 or more. Regard runs from -10 to 10: a request done raises it by 1 to 3, refused or left to run out costs 1, failed costs 2 to 4. At -5 the clan's vampires won't answer when the colony calls in their boons. Known vampires get one clan request a season at most. Done, the most senior vampire of the clan at a court you know owes a boon; with none known, the clan pays silver and a point more regard. Clan Rank Request Brujah 1 Back a cause with 300 to 600 silver (minor) Gangrel 1 Carry news to the farthest court you know, a court mission (minor) Tremere 1 Send three blood vials, or a treatise written at the colony (trivial) Tremere 2 A Regent inspects for two nights and wants a ritual circle and a research bench (minor) Tremere 3 Hunt a renegade, a court mission; a captured renegade pays a size more (major) Ventrue 1 Swear fealty: you owe the elder a trivial boon, it owes you a minor one Ventrue 2 Judge a dispute, a court mission (minor) Nosferatu 1 Trade secrets: tell on a court you know, learn of the nearest one you don't (trivial) Nosferatu 2 Shelter a brood of three for a season (major) Malkavian 1 No request: the calling's warnings come more often and are wrong less often Malkavian 2 Host a seer for three nights, who names any plant or enemy thrall among you (trivial) Lasombra 1 A patron's errand, a court mission (minor) Tzimisce 2 A voivode's guest wants to see fleshcraft: living furniture, flesh armour or a Vicissitude vampire (minor) Assamite 1 A contract, a court mission (minor) Assamite 2 A vizier studies the colony's books for five nights; it needs a library (minor) Followers of Set 1 Four mortal cultists worship two days at your finest indoor art (minor) Giovanni 1 Send a human corpse from storage (trivial) Giovanni 2 Keep a Giovanni and the family's ghost for a season (minor) Ravnos 1 Welcome a kumpania: a trade caravan and the clan's regard Toreador 2 Sponsor an artist, who joins for a season and must end it alive and in a good mood (minor) Caitiff and the smaller bloodlines have no clan politics.

A colony in good standing with its sect can host the sect's gatherings. The sect writes when a tier opens, and the sect section of the Kindred main tab has an "Ask to host a gathering" link for the highest tier open now (greyed with the reason when none is). Each tier is hosted once a year at most, and one gathering at a time. Sect Standing 40 Standing 60 (a court title) Standing 80 (a title, a host of the 8th generation or lower) Camarilla Primogen gathering, 2 nights Conclave, 3 nights, an Archon's seat The Inner Circle's envoys, 3 nights Sabbat War party, 2 nights Blood Bath, 3 nights, a Bishop's seat Palla Grande, last days of fall, an Archbishop's seat Anarchs Barons' summit, 2 nights Movement rant, 3 nights, a Baron's seat; double rewards at 80 none A court title means an Officer, Primogen or Prince seat at any court. The preparation window lists what the colony needs before it can send word: the title, a hall impressive enough, a bed or coffin in a room with no open roof for every guest (rooms may be shared), blood for every guest and night (vials in storage, or vessels at three each, the vials used up when the guests come). It also lists what may go wrong: an enemy strike on one night (raid points x1, x1.5, x2 by tier, warned at dusk), a plot or feud among the guests, mortals who could see too much. The guests are real members of the sect's courts, and at tiers 3 and 4 two or three elders of the 5th to 7th generation; ghoul retainers come with them. Each night has its own scene on the map and usually a choice: back one Prince or broker their quarrel, testify at a trial, name a grievance, ask the envoys for one thing, send a fighter with the war party, back a duellist, give vitae to the tub, take up a challenge at the danse macabre, break a tied vote. Rolls use the host's Social, Melee or Artistic skill. A good showing adds to the standing gained; at the end each guest of rank owes the host a boon (trivial, minor or major by tier; the Sabbat pays in standing). A guest killed costs the standing the gathering would have paid. A seat won (Archon, Bishop, Archbishop, Baron) shows under the standing bars. Once a season its holder can call a band of the sect's fighters and sit in judgment on a case for standing, and each year the sect's courts send a tithe of silver. Clan events run the same way, with the clan's own vampires as guests: a Brujah rant (respected), a Gangrel convocation outdoors (respected), a Toreador salon scored on the colony's art (known), a Ventrue oath-taking (a voice of the clan) and a Lasombra court of judgment (respected). They pay the clan's regard and a boon from its elder.
Sometimes gifts arrive with no name on them: blood vials, then something rare, then a hint. Weeks later the sender is named and the bill comes due.

With high Camarilla standing, three Kindred, enough wealth and a friendly court, you can petition for your colony to be recognised as a domain. An archon comes to inspect it over two nights. Then you assign offices to your own Kindred: Office Bonus Prince Sanctions your own Embraces and blood hunts Seneschal, Sheriff, Keeper of Elysium, Harpy A small bonus fitting the job

Once a season a domain (or an Anarch or Sabbat colony) can host a night for a court's Kindred: Elysium, a rant or an esbat. Guests keep to the party spot and leave before dawn. A quiet night earns standing, more in a fine room and more again with your own Toreador art on show. Violence against a guest, or an outsider seeing a vampire at work, ruins it.

Camarilla courts seat a Scourge, who destroys vampires of the 14th generation and higher. If a colony vampire's blood is that thin, the nearest Camarilla court can send its Scourge with a small band, by night, and the band goes for that vampire first. Your standing with the court doesn't stop it. A colony with its own domain can name a Scourge of its own in its offices. That stops the hunts and brings missions to cull thin-bloods for standing. A setting turns Scourges off.

A blood hunt is the Camarilla's death sentence, called for diablerie, a refused life boon, or a shattered Masquerade. The hunted vampire can't visit courts, archons raid far more often, and anyone may destroy it without penalty. Paying a life boon at a court lifts it.

While the colony shelters a vampire under blood hunt, the nearest friendly Camarilla court sends its hounds by night, at most every six days. The letter gives three answers: - Hand the vampire over. The court owes you a minor boon, +10 standing with the court and the Camarilla, the hunt is lifted, and the vampire is gone. - Let them search. Three of the court's Kindred walk round the home area for six hours. One who sees the hunted within 20 cells finds it: -10 standing with the court and the Camarilla, and the hounds attack. Obfuscate, a coffin or being away from the map keeps it out of sight. - Turn them away. -4 standing with both.

The Camarilla's list of the Kindred it most wants destroyed. Five Anathema roam the world map, whether the colony has Kindred or not, each a 6th-generation vampire with every Discipline it has at its limit, harder to hurt and quicker than any elder, guilty of some great crime. A name struck off is replaced a quadrum after the last one went on. Only a colony in the Camarilla knows the list: anyone else gets no letters, sees no marks and hears no rumours, and meets an Anathema as a stranger. - The mark. Each Anathema is a mark on the world map, 20 to 100 tiles from home, moving a few tiles every three days or so, and about one move in four it stops in a town. It shows only while it's within 25 tiles of a home or a colony caravan, or on a map. With the Core setting Show wanted marks always on, every mark on every wanted list shows all the time; what each one is still has to be learned. - The Red List window, from the Overview tab of the Kindred window or from the mark's button, shows only what the colony knows. The name is always known. Clan, generation, crime, retinue and each Discipline are rolled when the name goes on the list, and every few days a rumour adds one more thing or shows the mark for two days. Facing it tells its clan and retinue, seeing it use a power tells that Discipline's level, and knowing the clan names its clan Disciplines. - The hunt. A caravan sent to the mark always finds it, and fights it with up to 3 ghouls on a map of its own. By night it fights at once. By day it's already sheltered, in a haven one of its powers makes or dug into the earth, with its ghouls on guard. Opened before dusk, it's in the sun. - In a town. A caravan that walks into the town by night finds it among the townsfolk with its retinue, keeping to one spot. By day it's out of sight. It passes for a stranger as on a visit. - A visit. One within 12 tiles may cross the colony's land by night with its retinue. If it has never fought the colony, it doesn't know who lives there and walks on through. Hurt it or anyone with it, or use a power on any of them, and they all attack. One that has fought the colony before comes to stalk, waiting in the dark for someone alone. - The bounty, when the colony had a hand in its Final Death: +15 standing with the Camarilla, a life boon and +10 standing from the nearest Camarilla court, 3 experience for the vampire who did it, and a line in the chronicle. One that gets away stays on the list and comes back healed. The setting "The Red List" on the World page turns it off. Turned back on, a fresh list comes in one letter.

A Sabbat colony has no Prince. Instead: - Offices. The Ductus leads the pack, and the Pack Priest makes the Vaulderie stronger. - The Vaulderie. A button in the main tab, once a week at night, for two or more Kindred. Each pays a point of blood. Every pair gains Vinculum, a loyalty to each other, and every blood bond they held to a vampire breaks. - The creed. Each season the Sabbat thinks less of you for every vampire still on Humanity, and more for every one on a Path.

In a Camarilla domain, a colony vampire who dislikes the Prince (or a Brujah, Gangrel or Caitiff) may stir up trouble. You can give them a say or put it down, and putting it down can send them off to join the Anarchs.

Each Independent clan keeps a haven you can visit like a court, with one piece of business: Clan Business Giovanni Three corpses buy a trivial boon Assamite Five blood vials pay for one of your enemies to disappear Followers of Set A drug buys a string on a mortal in a court's city Ravnos A trivial boon buys a stolen item. Sometimes the owner finds out

A string is a mortal in another settlement who answers to you. Ghoul, bond or Dominate an outsider and let them go home, or work one from a caravan. Strings can be pulled for favours, and found out. Ventrue hold more. Followers of Set can make them with drugs. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material.
