Options → Mod settings → The Rim by Night. Every Rim by Night mod you have loaded shares this one window: a rail down the left lists each mod with its pages, and the arrow on a mod's row folds its pages away. Kindred has five pages: Rules, Learning, Display, World and events, and Event chances, where each Kindred event has its own slider from never to three times as often. The search box at the bottom finds a setting on any page of any mod by its name or description. Reset Kindred sits at the bottom too, and with a game loaded so does Remove Kindred from this game. A setting you have changed shows its name tinted with a reset arrow before it, each page and mod on the rail counts its changed settings, and Changed only by the search box lists just those. Learning holds the house rules for who may learn what: Koldunic Sorcery for any clan, Sanguinus for any clan, the Gargoyle rite for any clan, ghouls learning guarded Disciplines, and whether the Pyramid and the Prince's leave apply. It also holds the easier ways to out-of-clan Disciplines, all off by default: any Discipline self-taught, the out-of-clan experience cost, the chance a diablerie gives a Discipline dot (50%), neonates giving a dot, diablerie opening every Discipline the victim had to experience, and a growing derangement risk with each diablerie after the first. Rules holds At Humanity 0: lost for good (the book's rule), a long frenzy that leaves the vampire at Humanity 1, or rehab in a cell. See Humanity and frenzy. Setting What it does Vampires Sunlight damage How hard the sun burns a vampire caught outside by day. At 0% it does no harm at all. Blood used each night The blood a vampire burns to wake each evening. Lower it if feeding takes up too much of the colony's time. At 0% they only need blood for healing and powers. Blood to heal The blood a vampire spends to mend a wound. Lower it and a feeding goes further in a fight. Torpor length How long a vampire sleeps in torpor, which depends on its Humanity: a day at 10, a month at 1. A torpor sentence set by a court stays as it is. Frenzy difficulty Added to the difficulty of every frenzy and Rötschreck roll. Above zero the Beast gets loose more often, below zero less. Conscience difficulty Added to the difficulty of the Conscience roll after a sin. Above zero, vampires lose Humanity more often; below zero, less. Systems Vampires sleep by day Off, a vampire keeps a mortal's hours: it sleeps at night, works by day, and is never drowsy or hard to draft in daylight. Its schedule resets to a mortal's when you change this. The sun still burns unless that is off too. The sun burns vampires Off, sunlight does a vampire no harm and never sends it into Rötschreck, and it walks out under the sky like anyone. Orders come before shelter A vampire you wake or give an order to by day (prioritized work or any other right-click order) does it while it stays under a roof, then goes back to bed. On, it keeps at the order even out in the sun. Off, it drops an order that takes it into the sun to get under a roof or into bed. Either way, work it picked up on its own is dropped for shelter, and the red fear still takes over. Humanity Off, sins never cost Humanity or a Path's rating, and every vampire counts as at Humanity 7: no dice cap by day, no inhuman looks, no beast dreams, no fall to the Beast at 0. Mercy wins Humanity back Once a week, a vampire on Humanity who captured a downed enemy or recruited a prisoner rolls Conscience against its Humanity plus one. On a success it wins back a dot. Not in V20, where only experience buys Humanity back. At Humanity 0 What happens to a colony vampire whose Humanity falls to 0. Lost: it becomes a wight, turns on everyone and is never yours again (V20). Frenzy: the Beast rides it for a few hours, then lets go at Humanity 1. Rehab: it becomes a wight, but if you down it and hold it in a cell it rolls Conscience once a week, with extra dice for a colony vampire with Obeah on the map, and a success brings it back at Humanity 1. Frenzy and Rötschreck Off, the Beast never takes over. Vampires and ghouls don't frenzy or flee in fear, and fire nearby doesn't drive them back. A power used on purpose can still send someone into a frenzy. Hunger frenzy lasts until fed A vampire in a hunger frenzy only comes back to itself once it has fed enough or its time runs out. Off, it may pass early, like any other frenzy. Clan weaknesses Off, no clan or bloodline has a weakness, and ghouls take no taint from their domitor's clan. Turning it back on brings them back. Soften clan weaknesses Each clan's weakness still applies, in a milder form. Blood heals mortal scars Off, a vampire keeps the scars it had when it was Embraced, and blood heals only the ones since. On, blood heals those old scars as well. Draft vampires freely by day A vampire can be drafted by day with no roll and no blood spent. Off, it has to stir first: a roll with a threat on the map, or a blood point. Resonance The vessel's mood colours the blood a vampire drinks, giving a few bonus dice to the Disciplines that match it. Taken from the fifth edition; V20 has no such rule. Off, blood is only blood. Hemogen runs on vitae A vampire with Biotech's hemogen genes pays for hemogen powers from its vitae pool, and anything that gives hemogen fills the pool instead. Off, the hemogen bar is its own, filled and drained the vanilla way. Disciplines and rituals Koldunic Sorcery for any clan Any vampire can learn the Ways of Koldunic Sorcery from a teacher, at the out-of-clan price. Off, only the Tzimisce and their bloodlines can. Sanguinus for any clan A Discipline that only its clan can learn (Sanguinus, the Blood Brothers' shared flesh) can be taught to anyone. Its powers that work through a circle of brothers do nothing for a vampire without one. Gargoyle rite for any clan Any vampire who knows rituals can learn the rite that makes a gargoyle. Off, it stays a Tremere secret. Ghouls learn guarded Disciplines A ghoul can learn Protean, Thaumaturgy and a Discipline only one clan has from any domitor who knows it. Off, only from a domitor of that clan. Ghouls study lore A ghoul reads lore books and treatises under Research work like a vampire: experience, treatises for the Disciplines it has, and rituals a ghoul can cast. Off, ghouls leave the books alone. Ghouls get a full character sheet The Ghoul tab gains a page list down its left side, with the Virtues on its Sheet page and an Attributes page: Virtues, Willpower and Attribute dots a ghoul buys with its experience, at a vampire's prices. They count in its rolls. Off, a ghoul keeps a mortal's Willpower and Attributes, plus whatever it has already bought. Caitiff learn their sire's Disciplines easily A Caitiff learns only its sire's Disciplines at the in-clan price, and one with no known sire takes the three of a random clan. Off, a Caitiff counts every Discipline as its own. New powers start off the bar A colony vampire's new powers stay off the command bar until you turn them on in the Kindred tab. Off, each new power gets its button at once. Out-of-clan Disciplines Any Discipline self-taught Any Discipline a vampire could take lessons in can be bought with experience alone, at the self-taught price. A clan's own sorcery stays closed unless its own setting opens it. Off, as in V20, only Celerity, Fortitude and Potence can be learned without a teacher. Out-of-clan experience cost Multiplies what each dot of an out-of-clan Discipline costs, taught or self-taught. Clan Disciplines and a Caitiff's cost the same either way. Diablerie Chance to take a Discipline dot The chance a diablerie gives the diablerist a dot of one of the victim's Disciplines, if the victim had more of it. Not in V20, where diablerie gives only generation. Neonates can give a dot A neonate's blood can give a Discipline dot too. Off, only ancillae and elders have blood old enough. Diablerie opens the victim's Disciplines Every Discipline the victim had, and the diablerist could learn, can be bought with experience afterwards as if a teacher had started it. Not in V20. Each diablerie risks a derangement Every soul eaten makes the next harder to keep down: each diablerie after the first has a 10% chance of a derangement for every one before it. Not in V20. Clans and sects The Pyramid guards Thaumaturgy The colony's Tremere owe the Pyramid a yearly tithe, and a vampire of another clan seen casting Thaumaturgy by a Tremere or the Camarilla brings a Tremere hit team. Off, neither happens. A childe needs the Prince's leave In a sect that keeps the Traditions, a colony vampire who holds no office needs a permit to Embrace, and a childe made without one costs standing when the court meets it. Off, no permit is needed. The Masquerade Breaches have consequences Outsiders who see a vampire at work carry the story away, and the world reacts: warier visitors, then hunters, then the hunting order. Turn off to play without any of it. How much a breach counts How much each sighting adds to the colony's Masquerade breach score. How fast breaches fade How quickly the world forgets what it saw. Higher numbers bring the breach score down sooner. Move as a cloud A drafted vampire on the move, or a hostile one closing in, travels as a faint cloud of its strongest Discipline, and faster. Off, vampires walk like anyone else. Needs fighting motion on. Powers camera shake How hard big powers shake the camera: a lightning strike, a volcanic blast, the earth opening. At 0% the camera stays still. Powers sky flashes Big powers flash the sky in their colour, and storms tint it while they build. Off, the sky keeps its own light. Pale skin Show a vampire's skin drained to an ashen grey. It looks like any living person's again while it looks alive or wears the Mask of a Thousand Faces. Cappadocians are paler still. Only the look changes; hunters spot the pallor either way. How pale How far a vampire's skin is drained toward ashen grey. The world NPC Kindred How often vampires from outside the colony turn up: in the dark at night, in cryptosleep caskets, in rogue bands. 0% turns them off. Extra courts in a new world Every world gets one court of each sect and a haven for each Independent clan. This many more courts go to sects at random. Read when a world is made, or when the mod is added to a save. Court mission offers The chance each hour that a court posts a new mission, until it has three open. The default of 5% comes to about one a day; 0% stops new ones. Sleepers in ancient dangers The chance that one casket in a new map's ancient danger holds a Kindred instead of a soldier. Also scaled by the NPC Kindred setting. Psylinked Tremere With Royalty, the chance that a Tremere met outside the colony has a psylink of level 1 to 3. Its psycasts are random, from every psycast loaded, Vanilla Psycasts Expanded's paths included. At 0% none do. Background world Courts changing by themselves while you play: coups, rival schemes, blood hunts and cities changing sect. Switched off, the courts stay as they are. Sire calls A sire out in the world calling on its childe with demands. Wights come back A vampire lost to the Beast who escapes the map returns now and then as a night threat. The Red List A handful of Anathema the Camarilla wants destroyed roam the world map, each with a bounty. They roam either way, but only a colony in the Camarilla is told of them, sees them on the map or is paid for one. Turned off, they leave the world map; turned back on, a new list arrives in one letter. Scourges Camarilla courts seat a Scourge, who comes after colony vampires of the 14th generation and higher, and a colony with its own domain can name one. Off, nobody is sent and the office is gone from the domain page. Hunters among tavern guests The chance that a guest at the colony's tavern is a hunter, from a strong Masquerade to a broken one. The mod's chances run from 5% to 40%. At 0% none come this way. Blood market Vials, Kindred vitae and hemogen share one price that moves: hunter raids, blood hunts, the Scourge and a breach push it up, and selling a lot brings it down. Off, they keep their plain market value. Sect politics Archons, Sabbat packs and Anarch gangs sent against the colony, infiltrators, thralls of outside Kindred, Anarch unrest, Assamite contracts, Setite corruption and Tremere hit teams. Kindred attacks Rogue bands, elder raids, and the angry dead coming back to haunt the colony. Kindred visitors Kindred at the door, Path mentors, the occult trader, the ghoul black market, the anonymous benefactor and revenants asking to join. The lure A raiding vampire with Summon or Entrancement may call a lone colonist out past the walls before the raid comes in. The colonist resists like any mind power. A stranger at the door A colony with no vampire gets a pale stranger at its door by night, some time between day 15 and day 40, and again every 30 to 60 days until one is taken in. Off, the stranger only comes by chance.

With Odyssey your colony can live in orbit. The World of Darkness stays on the ground: nobody from these mods comes up uninvited unless "The World of Darkness reaches orbit" is on in Core's settings. Help you call still comes, by drop pod, and leaves on Royalty's shuttle. Without Royalty it stays aboard until the ship lands. The colony is whichever home holds most of your free colonists, so visitors go where your people are. Vampires don't breathe, so they can work outside without a vacsuit. The cold still hurts them, and unroofed the sun burns them up there as it does on the ground. No mortals come up, so bring blood packs on a long trip. A court's help and gifts come by drop pod.

Can I add this to an existing save? Yes. Nothing changes until someone becomes Kindred. Courts are placed when the mod is first loaded into the save. Can I remove it from a save? Yes, with the button made for it. Load the game, open the mod settings and press Remove Kindred from this game. Every vampire and ghoul becomes mortal again, the mod's items, buildings, creatures, factions, quests and sites are deleted, and the game is saved under a new name and taken back to the main menu. Then turn the mod off and load that save. Removing the mod without doing this first leaves the save broken. Do I need any DLC? No. It runs on Core alone and gets along with all the DLCs. Can a sanguophage be Embraced? Yes. It keeps its hemogen powers and pays for them in vitae, with no hemogen bar. See Feeding. Does it work with modded races? Yes, if the race is humanlike and has blood. The Kindred tab and recipes are added to every humanlike race at startup, and nothing assumes a human body layout. A pawn with no teeth gets no bite, and one with no heart can't be staked. What about other mods? The mod uses Harmony postfixes where it can, prefixed def names, and narrow XML patches. The full patch list is in the mod's repository. Mods that cure or block mental states also work on frenzies. Will it slow my game down? It shouldn't. Non-vampires cost nothing per tick, and nothing scans every pawn on the map. My vampire won't eat / won't go to bed / won't let the doctor tend it. Kindred don't need food or rest the normal way, and only blood heals them. See Being Kindred. My vampire burned to death at dawn. Check the dawn alert, give every vampire a roof within reach, and build coffins. Vampires caught outside try to dig in on soft ground, but rock and floors can't be dug. A colonist tried to kill my vampire in its sleep. That was a hateful mortal's "slay the monster" break. Watch for the warning thought and deal with them early. See Feeding. Hunters keep showing up. Your breach score is high. Stop making witnesses and wait for it to fade, or silence the witnesses before they leave. See The Masquerade and hunters. My tavern shelf has no prices button. Build a tavern counter on the map. The prices are kept on the counter, so a shelf only shows the button while a counter stands there, and a tavern area with no counter gets no guests. See The tavern. Does it work with Combat Extended? Yes. With CE loaded, the fangs and the mod's weapons become CE weapons, armour and the powers' projectiles hit in CE's units, and the hunters' guns are CE guns that need no ammo. My colony is in orbit and the courts have gone quiet. Courts deal only with homes on the ground. A colony that is all in orbit gets no offers, envoys or court services until it lands. Can I get into a hostile town without attacking it? Yes. A caravan standing on any hostile town gets Sneak in beside Attack, at night only, whoever is in it. The caravan walks onto the town's map unseen, and the town's people and guns can't go for anyone they haven't found. A townsman with a clear view may notice something move, less often in the dark, and the town then searches round that spot. A searcher who comes close may find who is there. Attacking anyone gives the attacker away. Will a town I visit again have the same people? Yes. Every town the colony walks into keeps its people between visits, unless they died or left. A friendly town stays friendly while you're there: its people only turn on you if the faction does. Where do I look something up in game? The grimoire, the book button in the bottom-right corner. Type a question on its Ask tab.

A tavern earns silver and brings mortals in after dark. For the colony's Kindred that means vessels who walk in on their own, and more for the Masquerade to worry about. It works in any colony, with or without vampires.

1. Build a tavern counter (Furniture tab, no research). It is also storage, set to drinks, drugs and meals. 2. Stock the counter, and any shelves in the tavern, with what you want to sell. 3. Optionally, paint a tavern area from the zone tab. The tavern is the counter's room (or the ground within 6 cells of it out in the open), plus any painted tavern area joined to that room, such as a patio through the door. Paint the door too, or the patio isn't joined. A counter standing on painted area out in the open makes that whole patch of area its tavern. 4. Optionally, mark beds For guests (any humanlike bed or coffin, modded beds too: with Ideology it is in the bed's For colonists / prisoners / slaves menu, without it a button of its own). Vampires staying with the colony, such as a fostered childe, sleep the day in these beds for free. There is no barkeep. Guests serve themselves and leave the silver on the counter, and haulers carry it off. Each counter is its own tavern, with its own prices, guests and night. A map can have several.

The counter's Prices button sets the price for everything, from 75% to 300% of market value (125% to start), or opens By ware..., a list of everything in the tavern where you can type a price in silver for each ware. A ware with no price of its own sells at the counter's. Every shelf in the tavern shows the same button, but only while a counter stands on the map, since the prices belong to the counter. Guests pay a fair price without thinking twice. Above it, fewer of them buy, and none at all once the price is a full market value over fair. Fair starts at 125% and rises: - with an impressive tavern room, half a percent per point; - by up to 25 points for a friendly faction; - by 25 points once the guest is drunk; - by 50 points while a vampire's Awe is in the tavern. A guest who turns a ware down shows "Too dear" over its head.

Most evenings (every 0.7 to 1.5 days) four to ten guests come from the factions that aren't hostile, with one more for every 15 points of the tavern room's impressiveness. One night in five is a busy night with twice the crowd, up to 20. They come one to three at a time through the evening, each party from its own faction, so the room fills with a mix. They buy a round, then sit at the tables, stand about talking or wander the tavern, buying another round now and then. They toast each other, boast and tell stories of the road, which shows over their heads and in the social log. Drinks, drugs and meals are used on the spot. Anything else goes home with them. Each party goes home after three to ten hours, or after the night's sleep if it rented a bed. Once you have a vampire and know a friendly court, one or two of its Kindred mix with them. They buy only blood, feed on herd in the tavern and leave two hours before dawn. Friendly visitors and a trade caravan's guards already on the map drop in after dark too, one or two at a time. The trader and its pack animals stay put.

The counter's Guests button opens a window with every kind of guest the loaded mods know, as a tree of checkboxes: mortals, then Kindred by sect, and with the other mods the Garou by tribe and their Kinfolk, mages by Path, and hunters. A new counter, and any counter from an older save, lets in mortals and Kindred of every sect, which is what the tavern always did: only the sect of the nearest friendly court actually comes. Only Kindred at the top of the list turns the counter into a Kindred-only room. The window also shows who of the kinds let in hates whom, the odds of a fight on a night, your other taverns side by side, and how many guests a night here brings and about what they spend. A row dimmed grey can't come right now; its tooltip says why. A guest let in at more than one of your taverns goes to the one without anyone it hates in it, and failing that the emptiest.

Guests who hate each other can come to blows, but only once one of them knows what the other is. Mortals are plain to see. A vampire passes for mortal until something gives it away: Auspex (Aura Perception), a Garou's nose, a hunter's second sight, Mage Sight, a power used where your colonists can see, or a kind your colony already has. Each hour both are inside, such a pair can roll. The roll is in the roll log: Temper dice, one more for drink and one for a crowded room, two fewer on neutral ground, one fewer for each bouncer and for a host with a calming power such as Awe. One or two successes are words and a shove, three a brawl (vanilla's social fight), five a killing: the two fight and the winner finishes the loser. - Neutral ground. A toggle on the counter: an Elysium, the Litany's truce, the Consilium's peace. Guests are slower to fight, but a vampire who kills under Elysium is blood hunted, and a Garou who breaks the truce leaves for the sept's judgment. - Bouncers. Pick one or two colonists on the counter. Each one in the tavern counts fully; any other drafted colonist there counts half. - A guest killed in the tavern costs regard with its sworn home, if you have one with its people, and its home hears of it. The loser of a brawl costs a little too. - Sabbat Kindred see the mortals around them as prey. Let both in and expect trouble.

A guest who bought something or rented a bed, and left without finding a price too dear, getting into a fight or running off, becomes one of the tavern's regulars. The tavern keeps six, and the oldest makes room for a new one. Regulars come back now and then with friends from their faction, and a message tells you who is back.

Up to two of these happen on a night, about three hours apart while guests are inside: - A brawl. A drunk guest picks a fist fight with another. Neither comes back as a regular. - A traveller's tale. Once a night at most, a guest tells of a trade caravan on its way, of raiders asking the road to the colony (both arrive in one to four days), or of a stash out in the wilds, which is offered as a quest. - Passed out. A drunk falls asleep in a free guest bed or on the floor, and leaves 10 to 40 silver for the trouble on waking. - A round for the room. A guest buys for everyone. For the next hour every guest inside buys one more drink whatever the price. - Dice with the house. A guest bets 20 to 60 silver. Half the time the stake lands on the counter, half the time the guest takes it from the silver lying in the tavern. - A drifter. Rarely, a guest tired of its own people asks to stay. Take it in and it joins the colony. Some things come on their own: - A minstrel. About one night in three, a party brings a minstrel. It plays an instrument standing in the tavern (Royalty or Ideology) or sings. While it plays, the other guests stay past their time and buy another round twice as often. - Dine and dash. Now and then a guest, twice as often a drunk one, takes a ware without paying and runs for the road. Arrest it to get the ware back, though its faction won't like it. The Open toggle on the counter closes the tavern. Guests already inside finish their visit, and no new ones come.

A bed marked for tavern guests is rented for 15 silver a night, plus a little for an impressive bedroom. The guest goes to bed in the small hours and leaves after it wakes. Keep the bed unowned, or a colonist with no bed of its own may claim it. With no beds marked, no rooms are let. If the Hospitality mod is loaded, its guest beds stay its own and our guests use only beds marked here.

- A guest asleep in a rented bed can be fed on. Whether it sleeps through is a roll, see feeding on a sleeper. A drunk guest makes that roll easier. - A drunk guest who is awake doesn't remember a careful feeding and isn't a witness. Anyone else who sees it still is. - Under the "animals and willing" feeding policy or looser, the feeding AI takes such guests by itself, and it still won't feed where an outsider can see. - A guest's drug high passes to the vampire who drinks from it, as with any vessel. Now and then a Society investigator comes in with the guests, more often the worse the breach score. See The Masquerade and hunters.

The tavern's night twin. In a newer colony, pick Only Kindred in a counter's Guests window instead. A map that already has a Kindred club area keeps it, and its zone buttons; a counter inside it works as below. - Once you have a vampire and know a friendly court, two to five of the nearest such court's Kindred come one or two at a time through the night and stay until two hours before dawn. A finer room brings them more often. - The club's shelves sell only blood: vials, Kindred vitae and hemogen, at the blood market's price plus your markup. - Herd. Prisoners and slaves get a Herd toggle. Guests feed on herd standing in the club and leave silver on the counter, more for a healthy vessel and a finer room. Nobody is fed on past the safe line. - Rumours. Now and then the guests' talk becomes a letter with something real in it: a sept (with Werewolf) or hunter cell (with Hunter) you didn't know, a raid that will come in so many days, or a plot at a court you know. A finer club talks more, and it never tells you the same thing twice. - Mortal tavern guests never step into the club, and a second counter outside it runs an ordinary tavern. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Pledge the colony to one court and its Kindred stop being names on a list. Each has a personality, means, a goal of its own and an opinion of you that moves with what you do. They hand you work, owe you boons, fight beside you and, if they come to hate you, work against you.

Open a court from the Courts page of the Kindred window (or visit it) and use Swear to this home on its Court page. You need: - a colony vampire Acknowledged at that court, - the court not shunning, banishing or blood-hunting the colony. One court at a time. Pledging doesn't stop you joining a coterie there. The court's roster fills to 8 to 12 named members, and new pages appear on the Kindred window's rail: People, Council and, while a war runs, War. Leaving costs 20 Standing. Loyal members drop to -5 regard, and the boons the court's members owe you shrink a size (trivial ones are gone). A court that falls or changes hands frees the colony with a letter.

The People page lists every named member: seat, coterie (clan for those in none) and regard, with a filter for friends, rivals and enemies. Click a member to see their personality, means, goal, friends and dislikes. You only see a member's personality and means once you've met them: talked to them in a town, finished a mission they gave, or read them with Aura Perception. Regard event Change A mission done for them +2 A mission done for their coterie or a friend +1 A step of their goal done +3 A gift from their row +1 per 500 silver, up to +3 a season Their mission refused or let lapse -1 (Proud -3) A mission done against them or a friend -3 Betraying their goal -10, for good Regard drifts a point toward 0 every season.

Personality How they pay and behave Greedy silver x0.7, Standing x1.5 Cautious silver and Standing x1.25, but the biggest boon they'll owe is a size smaller Loyal everything x1.25 while you never cross them or their friends; betrayal makes an enemy for good Conniving pays with a boon another member owes them Cowardly one more open mission, aimed at their rivals; pay x1.2 Proud Standing x1.5, silver x0.8; refusals cost 3 regard Zealous only the court's cause; those pay x1.5 Generous everything x1.3; now and then asks a favour back Vengeful bad blood never fades; an enemy at -5 Decadent pays in blood vials, rarely silver Paranoid regard grows half as fast; tells you what it wants only if you have a hold over it A coterie's eldest has the personality of its temperament: Tyrant Proud, Scholar Cautious, Trickster Conniving, Traditionalist Loyal, Schemer Paranoid, Zealot Zealous. Coterie-mates are friends.

Means come from the member's seat, wealth and the boons owed to them. A poor member offers one mission at a time and pays x0.6, a comfortable one two at x1.0, a rich one three at x1.4. Raiding a member's asset in a war costs them a point of wealth for a year.

Each member wants something, hidden until they count you a friend (regard +6) or you have a hold over them: a secret, or a major boon they owe you. A goal is three steps: two missions bent to it, then the prize. At the end a letter asks whether you hand the prize over or keep it. Keeping it is a betrayal. Goal What you get for it Collector a relic Lore hunter a named tome: Saulot's travelogue, a book of Lasombra poetry or the Ravnos Chronicle Power seeker silver by its means, and its vote for a year Revenge a major boon and the enemy's goods Diablerist a major boon and a secret on another member Freedom its regard stays at +6 or more for good Childe a minor boon now, its childe on your side later Golconda each colony vampire learns, about 6 experience Kingmaker the new Prince starts at regard +6 Homecoming a torpor crypt revealed Buried secret a life boon
What a member owes you, or you owe them, is a boon in the ledger on the Boons page, earned by your eldest vampire. Call in on a member's row cashes one in the boons' usual way.

Under Your seats on the Courts page, a colony vampire can take a seat. Officers pick Hound, Sheriff, Harpy, Keeper or Seneschal. A vampire becomes an officer by finishing a hunt for the Prince while established at the court with no scandal. The Primogen seat needs Primogen rank: visit the court with the vampire and use Claim the clan's seat, which needs the court's standing at 40 and no older blood of the same clan at court. Only vampires are offered the seats. A seat held by a member makes that member your rival, and the seat's duty for the season arrives as soon as you take it. Seat Duty each season Hound one hunt for thin-bloods and Caitiff made without leave Sheriff one mission against trouble Harpy attend the court's Elysium in person (a season with none asks nothing) Keeper host one Elysium at home, or finish the hosting mission the seat brings Seneschal judge one petition (a letter; Wits + Etiquette hints at the right answer) Primogen vote in the council A duty kept adds 3 Standing and a dot. Three missed in a row and the seat is lost, with 10 Standing, to the next in line, who starts at regard -3. The vampire's own tab shows its seat and when the duty is due, and an alert warns two days ahead.

Each season the Prince and Primogen vote on one or two motions: Embrace with leave or freely, war or peace, the hunt on thin-bloods and Caitiff, the Prince's tithe. Each member votes by personality, goal and friends. A colony Primogen votes too, and a member may offer a minor boon for your vote.

Rivals (-3 to -5) slander the colony (Standing lost if they win the roll) or stymie your next mission with their own people. Enemies (-6) send raiders: ghouls of theirs, coming in person if you hold something of theirs. Capture one and question them in prisoner talk to learn who sent them, then Accuse that member. An accusation without proof costs 10 Standing.

A war runs against the nearest court of another sect, started by the council's vote or the world. Its score starts at 50. 1. Incursions, a season: two or three skirmishes, +3 or -3 each. 2. Raids, two seasons: attack the enemy's herd, ghoul farm, chantry, haven or Elysium hall, and defend your own. 3. The end: at 70 or more, the final assault on their city; at 30 or less, the desperate defence of yours; otherwise a truce at year's end. Victory pays silver and one of their relics, and their court falls. Defeat makes your court fall. If three or more members survive, a letter offers to found it anew. The skirmishes come a few weeks apart. A war mission you let lapse is fought without you: the court's members against the enemy's, by their strength, and members can die in it. Hover over the stages, the score and the holdings on the War page for what each one needs.

The Backgrounds page on a vampire's tab buys rated Backgrounds with Standing at the sworn court: the new rating x 2, never experience. Leaving the court, or the court falling, halves every dot. Now and then a rival strikes at one of them, at most once a season: a letter gives six days (more with Contacts) to answer with a mission or a boon the rival owes, or the dot is lost. The "Rival strikes on Backgrounds" setting makes strikes rarer or more common, or turns them off. Background Each dot Allies armed mortals to call on any map with enemies on it; they never witness anything Contacts a day more to answer a strike, and a chance each season to strike back at a rival Fame more tavern guests and regulars; hunters 5% likelier to send an investigator Influence a caravan from the court's faction once a season; one more string on mortals Herd blood vials worth 4% of the pool a dot each season, at least one a dot; a die on hunting rolls in towns Mentor a court member of high enough rank (Acknowledged 1 to Prince 5) teaches its Disciplines for free Resources 100 x dots squared silver a season Retainers a ghoul in the court's town: a string that never fades, fed a blood point a season Status credit at the court as if ranked (1-2 trivial, 3 minor, 4 major, 5 life); +2 regard from every member Domain a mortal town within 40 tiles of the court where hunting never makes it warier Alternate Identity 10% chance a hunters' report loses this vampire at the false name; passes as mortal an hour past sunrise

The werewolves come from The Rim by Night: Garou, the series' Werewolf: The Apocalypse mod. In the game this page shows only when both mods are loaded. The werewolves' side of all this is on the page "Kindred and Garou", in the Garou chapter of the grimoire and on the Garou wiki. Garou call vampires leeches, and most of them count Kindred as creatures of the Wyrm, the corruption they exist to fight. Expect them to attack on sight.

- Embracing a Garou is offered, and the confirmation names the odds: the Garou is drained to death and almost never rises. Very rarely it comes back as an Abomination (see the Abominations page). A Garou deep in Harano, or of a fallen tribe, may ask for it. - Ghouling a Garou spends the vitae for nothing, and no blood bond takes one. - Kinfolk, the Garou's human families, can be ghouled and Embraced. The Embrace ends the wolf blood in them for good.

A vampire below Humanity 7, or on a Path of Enlightenment, smells of the Wyrm to a Garou. Their Gifts that hunt the Wyrm find it, hurt it more, and pay the Garou double experience for the kill. A vampire with Humanity 7 or more reads as something dead, but not the Wyrm's.

- A Garou's claws and bite are aggravated to a vampire. Fire is aggravated to both. - Garou heal fast, so a fight with one is long. Silver hurts them; ordinary blades and bullets barely slow them down. - Dominate and Presence work on a Garou, but not on one in a frenzy, and a Garou resists with Willpower plus Rage. - The Garou's war form terrifies mortals. It doesn't touch vampires, except one Gift, Terror of the Dire Wolf. Some Gifts are made for vampires: one burns the undead nearby with the light of the sun, some end a frenzy or force one, one stops vitae from healing, one steals a Discipline, and the oldest Silver Fangs can undo centuries of undeath at once.

Each point of a Garou's blood gives two vitae. It also leaves the vampire on edge for a few days: frenzy and Rötschreck are harder to resist, and they're quick to pick a fight. The Garou gains Rage, and may frenzy.

A colony can keep both, and it's tense. The Garou resent every vampire in it, more for one that smells of the Wyrm, and roll for frenzy when a vampire of the colony feeds in sight. Vampires near the colony's Garou are uneasy. The septs think less of the colony each day it keeps both. Friendship between a vampire and a Garou can still grow, slowly.

- A Garou pack hunt: a pack of Garou gathers at the edge of a colony with vampires and no Garou. A vampire with Humanity 7 or more can go out and talk them down, from the letter: Charisma plus Social against the pack's best Willpower. Fail, and they attack at once. - The Black Spiral and Sabbat raid: a rare raid by night of Garou who serve the Wyrm, with up to three Sabbat vampires among them. - Hunters come armed for every kind the colony holds. The Masquerade and the Garou's Veil are separate: a mortal who saw a vampire feed and a werewolf change counts against both. These events answer to the setting for Kindred's attacks.

Each side names the colony's pawn who hurt its own, for two quadrums or until that pawn dies: - A colony vampire who feeds on or kills kinfolk is named by the nearest sept. While they're on a home map, the Garou pack hunt comes three times as often, even to a colony with Garou of its own, and its letter names them. - A colony werewolf who destroys a court's vampire, or the childe of one of its members, is named by that court. Its sect's raids come as often as in a blood hunt, and its stalkers strike at the named werewolf first. In the background, septs and courts within 30 tiles of each other fight now and then: a sept's raid destroys one of the court's vampires, never its ruler, or the court's ghouls strike the caern. The court's chronicle says so. ← Kindred contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. An Abomination is a Garou who rose from the Embrace. It needs both this mod and The Rim by Night: Kindred loaded; with either alone, none of this happens. The Garou wiki has the same page from the werewolves' side.

- A vampire Embraces a Garou. Before it dies, the Garou rolls Gnosis at difficulty 6. A success is a quiet death, a failure a death in agony, and only a botch rises. That is about 10% at Gnosis 1, 6% at 3, 2% at 5 and under 1% at 7. The confirmation shows the odds. - An unwilling Garou with Willpower left, and not in Harano, spends it for a sure clean death. One that asked, or is willing, never does. - It rises a few hours later as a vampire of its sire's clan, one generation weaker. It keeps its forms, Rage, Gnosis, Gifts, tribe, breed, auspice and rank.

Humanity is replaced by Ego, the Hierarchy of Wyrm Taint. It starts at the Garou's Gnosis. - Ego never rises, and experience can't buy it, the Virtues or Willpower. - By day, Ego caps every dice pool. - Below 7 it smells of the Wyrm: Sense Wyrm finds it and the Banes treat it as a friend. - At 0 it is the Wyrm's. It leaves to join the Black Spiral Dancers and comes back with their raids as a nemesis. The sins on the list, worst first: breaking the Litany (10), feeding on a Garou or Kinfolk (9), hurting a friend in a frenzy (8), calling on a Bane (7), killing in a frenzy (6), killing a Garou, Kinfolk or wolf outside a fight it was attacked in (5), diablerie or torture (4), killing an innocent (3), a Bane fetish or fighting beside fomori (2), helping destroy a caern (1).

Rule What happens Dice pools Every pool is halved, never below one die. A point of Willpower gives full pools until sunrise, by the "Full pools tonight" button, or on its own when a fight starts at night Willpower Buys no automatic success One pool a turn No blood within a turn of spending Rage or Gnosis, and the other way round Healing Only with blood. No regeneration Gnosis Never refills Renown and rank Frozen at the Embrace Its blood Dead: it can't Embrace or make ghouls Silver Burns it in every form, Homid included Frenzy Anger is the wolf's frenzy, rolled on Rage. Hunger frenzy rolls Rage too Mood "Dead and cut off from Gaia", -12, for good. A new break, "walk into the dawn", sends it out to stand under the sky Its Gifts that use only Rage, or nothing, work as before. A Gift that calls on spirits reaches only Banes and tests Ego. About once a season a Bane offers a Gift of the Black Spiral Dancers, bought with experience.

- Courts: a court that learns of it, because one of its vampires saw it shift or the colony visited with it, calls a blood hunt and demands it. Hand it over, or refuse for -15 goodwill while it lives and court raids aimed at it. - Septs: a sept's Garou who sees it in a wolf's shape tells the sept: -20 goodwill while it lives, and the next raid comes for it. - Its own colony: colony Garou think 20 less of it, colony Kindred 5 less.

- A colony Garou deep in Harano, or of a fallen tribe, may ask a colony vampire for the Embrace. - A hunted Abomination may come in by night and ask for shelter. Take it in and the blood hunt and the sept's anger come with it. Turn it away and its hunters may pass through after it. Sometimes one comes to kill instead. A Garou is a werewolf: born of Garou blood, Changed for the first time as a young adult, and then never fully human again. This page covers what that means for a colonist.

One lunar cycle runs each quadrum, read from the date. Day of quadrum Moon Its auspice 1, 2, 15 New Ragabash 3, 13, 14 Crescent Theurge 4, 11, 12 Half Philodox 5, 6, 10 Gibbous Galliard 7, 8, 9 Full Ahroun The moon rises at 18:00 and sets at 6:00. The first time each night a Garou is outdoors under the moon, they gain Rage by its phase: 1 at the new moon, 2 at the crescent, 3 at the half and gibbous, 4 at the full. Under their own auspice's moon they fill to the top. Underground, or on a map with no sky, the phase still counts, but no one gains Rage at moonrise. The moon also sets how easily a Garou frenzies (hardest at the new moon, easiest at the full), and the Wyrm raids half again as often under the full moon.

Rage is the wolf's fury, from 1 to 10. The bar under the Garou's name shows what's there now against the permanent rating. Gaining it: - moonrise, as above; - half a point for each wound an enemy deals; - a quarter of a point when a packmate within 15 cells is hurt; - half a point an hour within 8 cells of Wyrm taint; - three points when a vampire drinks from them (with Kindred loaded). At rest, an hour after the last harm, Rage sinks back toward the auspice's starting Rage over a day. Spending it: - an instant shift to any form, for 1 Rage (Forms and shifting); - Fury, an ability every Garou has: 1 Rage, and for four hours the Garou strikes in melee a quarter faster; - staying on their feet past the point where they'd go down, a point every three seconds, as long as Rage lasts. Not with no legs, nor when knocked out cold. A downed Garou who gets Rage back stands up again; - the Gifts that cost Rage. High Rage is what makes frenzy likely. See Frenzy, the Litany and Harano.

Mortals feel the predator in a Garou. A mortal colonist who isn't kinfolk is uneasy within 12 cells of a colony Garou whose permanent Rage is above their Willpower: -2 mood when it's 1 or 2 points above, -4 at 3 or 4, -6 past that. Kinfolk, psychopaths and bloodlust pawns don't mind. - A Garou's social impact falls 5% for each point of Rage above 3, and in Homid their trade prices are 1% worse per point of Rage. Kin get the same penalty as anyone else. - Taming and training go at 0.8 the chance, 0.6 above Rage 6. Not in Lupus, nor for a Garou who knows Beast Speech. Tame animals don't turn on anyone. The setting "The Curse" scales all of it, and at 0% turns it off.

Gnosis is the Garou's tie to the spirit world, from 1 to 10. It powers Gifts and fetishes, and a Garou needs it to step sideways. Getting it back: - Seek Gnosis: a button on the Garou. They meditate where they stand, rolling Wits and Enigmas at difficulty 8. Each success brings back a point of Gnosis for each hour spent. Once a day, and one harder for each further day that week. - standing near the colony's caern, which gives a quarter of a point a level every so often; - a spirit's favor, paid for with chiminage; - the Reawakening, a Gnosis caern's Opened Caern rite, and a few Gifts and rites.

Willpower is set by the tribe. It holds off frenzy, makes a roll succeed, and pays for some Gifts. A Garou gets a point back for a deed on their auspice's own Renown track, all of it for a quest done, and a point at a time from their pack's shared pool when they run below 2. How a Garou spends it is set on the form bar: Resist frenzy spends a point to hold off a frenzy when Rage boils over.

Garou regenerate. Every second, the worst wound that isn't aggravated loses 4 HP, and each HP healed costs nutrition. A starving Garou doesn't regenerate. - A Homid in Homid form and a Lupus in Lupus form heal as a mortal does. In any other form they regenerate. - A Metis regenerates in every form. - Aggravated wounds don't regenerate: silver, fire, and the claws and fangs of supernatural things. They heal at a mortal's pace. A regenerating Garou shows it with a green-gold glow and sparks, even when it's down and can't move, so you can tell a Crinos lying in the dirt is mending. - Lost parts grow back: in a day, or in three days for a part lost to silver or claws. The setting "Regeneration" scales how fast it goes.

Silver is a Garou's bane. A blade or blow of silver deals aggravated damage to a Garou, and hits half again as hard. Anything made of silver counts, modded items included. A Homid in Homid form or a Lupus in Lupus form takes silver as a mortal does. A Metis is burned by it in every form. The Merit Silver Tolerance takes the extra harm away, though the wound is still aggravated. The setting "Silver damage" scales the extra harm.

Garou eat half again as much as a mortal in Homid and Glabro, twice as much in Crinos and Hispo, and a fifth more in Lupus. Raw food doesn't bother them. They won't eat human flesh unless ordered to, and doing it breaks the Litany.

A mortal who sees a Garou in Crinos within 15 cells is overcome by a primal terror, checked once per mortal. How they react depends on their Willpower: Willpower Reaction Remembers 1 Collapses, catatonic, for about an hour No 2 Flees the map in a panic No 3 Hides until it passes No 4 Attacks with whatever is in hand No 5 Flees, shutting doors behind them No 6 Drops their weapon and begs No 7 Fights or flees as a soldier would Explains it away 8 Keeps watching, curious Explains it away 9 Fights on, in a bloodlust Yes 10 No reaction at all Yes Kinfolk, other supernatural beings, mechanoids and animals don't suffer it. A mortal's Willpower is the same each time, raised by the Nerves trait and by True Faith. The few who keep their wits are a danger to the Veil. ← Garou contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. What's on a Garou besides their tribe, breed and auspice: Attributes, Merits and Flaws, and two Backgrounds, Totem and Ancestors.

The nine Attributes of the tabletop game, on the Garou tab's Attributes page: Strength, Dexterity, Stamina, Charisma, Manipulation, Appearance, Perception, Intelligence and Wits. They're read from the colonist as they are: skills, health and traits. Becoming a Garou doesn't change them. Experience raises them a dot at a time, at the current rating times four, as in W20: hover the next dot for its cost and click it to buy. The forms add their own dots on top while the Garou is in them; see Forms and shifting. Crinos can take Strength to nine. Each rank past Cliath adds a tenth to what an Attribute dot gives, Stamina aside. Gifts and rites roll Attributes too: Seek Gnosis rolls Wits, shifting rolls Stamina.

A starting Garou picks a Merit and a Flaw in the making menu, or none. Core's Merits at making setting allows up to five Merits, each one past the first with a Flaw of its own. A Garou made any other way, at the First Change or as an outsider, rolls: usually nothing, sometimes a Merit or a Flaw, now and then one of each. They're never bought. They show on the Sheet page; click one to read it here. Some pairs can't go together: Calm Heart and Short Fuse, Iron Will and Weak-Willed, Acute Sense and Bad Sight, Long-Distance Runner and Lame, Immune to Wyrm Emanations and Taint of Corruption.

Merit What it is Acute Sense Sharp-eyed even for a Garou. Sees better than anyone around them. Long-Distance Runner Can run fast and keep running. Moves quicker than others, in every form. Huge Size Close to seven feet tall in human form, and huge in the others. Takes a beating better than most. Metamorph Changes shape as easily as breathing. Every shift works, with no roll. Calm Heart Stays calm when others wouldn't. Frenzy is two harder to fall into. Iron Will Hard to get inside. Three more dice against Gifts and powers that work on the mind. Natural Channel Slips through the Gauntlet more easily than most. Stepping sideways is one easier. Immune to Wyrm Emanations Gaia guards this one against the Wyrm's poisons. Toxins and toxic air do far less. Silver Tolerance Silver still leaves wounds that heal slowly, but it hits no harder than steel.

Flaw What it is Hard of Hearing Misses sounds others catch. Bad Sight Poor eyesight that nothing fixes, and regeneration doesn't touch it. Lame Old damage to the legs that never healed right. Walks slowly, with a heavy limp. Short Fuse Rage burns hotter in this one. Frenzy is two easier to fall into, and the Thrall of the Wyrm can take them at any time. Weak-Willed Easily pushed around. Never resists a Gift that works on the mind, and Willpower never goes above 4. Pierced Veil Mortals see this Crinos for what it is and remember it. No Delirium, so every witness costs the Veil. Harano Prone Falls into dark moods easily. Every loss sinks twice as deep into Harano. Taint of Corruption The Wyrm touched this one long ago, and the mark stays. Sense Wyrm finds them, and no rite washes it off.

Each Garou's standing with the totem spirits, from 0 to 5. A pack pools its members' dots to win a totem's favor: the dots together must reach the totem's cost. A Garou starts with 1 or 2 dots and buys more on the Pack page at 2 experience a dot. See Packs and kinfolk.

How readily the Garou's ancestor spirits answer, from 0 to 5. A Garou starts with 0 to 2 dots and buys more on the Sheet page at 2 experience a dot. Once a season, Call the ancestors rolls these dots at difficulty 8. Pick a skill: each success lends four levels of it for four hours. With no dots, the button doesn't show. ← Garou contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. A fetish is an item with a spirit bound into it. A talen holds a spirit for one use.
Each fetish has a level and a Gnosis rating, shown on the item.

Right-click the fetish with a Garou and pick Attune. The Garou sits with it for an hour, pays a point of Gnosis and rolls Gnosis against its rating. One success is enough. A weapon goes into the hand, anything else into the inventory. - Only a Garou can wake the spirit in it. - A fetish serves one Garou at a time. Attuning it takes it from whoever had it. - On a failure the spirit sulks and won't listen until tomorrow. - The labrys won't serve a man.

While its Garou carries it (in hand, in the inventory, worn, or held through a form), the spirit is awake: it gives what it always gives, and a button for each power. Each power is woken with a point of Gnosis when the Garou has one, or a Gnosis roll at the fetish's rating when they don't. Put down, or in anyone else's hands, the fetish sleeps. A spirit woken in a frenzy, or turned on someone who isn't hostile, takes offence and won't answer for three days. The klaive, the grand klaive and the Jarlhammer are silver. A klaive costs its Garou a die of Gnosis, a grand klaive two.
A fetish the Wyrm has bent can't be attuned or woken, and fouls the ground around it about once a day while it's kept on the map. The Rite of Cleansing makes it an ordinary fetish again.

A talen needs no attuning. Use it from the inventory or the ground: a Gnosis roll at its rating, then it's gone. Bane arrows fly at the nearest hostile spirit and the moon sign at the nearest Garou; the rest work on the user.

- The Fetish choice in the making menu: one fetish up to level 2, level 1 for a cub, attuned from the start. - Septs sell a few, and buy them back, and sometimes pay for a mission with one. - The Wyrm: Pentex plants and Black Spiral Dancers carry tainted ones. - Making them, with the Rite of the Fetish or the Rite of Binding.

A few fetishes hold a spirit that tires. They show their uses left on the item, and once the uses are gone the power stays greyed until the spirit wakes again: - The moon-tooth knife wakes once, then not again until the next full moon. - The Rage-stone wakes once, then not again until the moon its bearer was born under. - The bane-glass has three looks. After that, its bearer can feed it a point of Gnosis for each one more, with the button under its power.

Both rites need a spirit of the item's kind within 8 cells of the ritemaster, willing to go in, and the vessel beside them. A spirit is willing once its chiminage is paid or a Gift has befriended it. A bane doesn't bargain: it goes in calmed or beaten down. The vessels are ordinary materials, named on the item's page. - The Rite of the Fetish (level 3) makes one fetish, of any level up to the ritemaster's rank. - The Rite of Binding (level 1) makes a talen for each success, up to three.
A scrap of tattooed skin with a Homid ancestor bound in it. Woken, it lets its Garou live a day as one born human: silver is no worse than steel, but the wounds don't knit by themselves either.
A hickory flute hung with songbird feathers. Its tune calls up memories of a whole world, and every angry creature that hears it stops fighting.
A plain sack with a magpie spirit bound in it. It holds three times what it looks like it should.
Mirrored sunglasses with a glass elemental bound in them. A mirror always to hand: the Gauntlet is two lower to step sideways.
A silver bracelet carved with glyphs to Luna and a night spirit bound in it. Woken, it hides its Garou in the shadows; only the eyes shine.
A small gold earring with a servant of Falcon in it. It trembles at every lie its wearer hears.
A carved, covered cup said to be unicorn horn. Any poison poured into it turns harmless.
A belt of lizard hide with a chameleon spirit bound in it. Woken, the Garou's fur takes the colors of the land around.
An ugly iron dagger with a vengeance spirit in it. Held and woken, it tugs toward whoever wronged its Garou.
A many-colored gem with a dream spirit in it. Held near a sleeper and woken, it plays their dreams in its depths.
A human hair set in an iron ingot with a predator spirit bound in it. Woken, the ingot pulls toward spirits.
A scrap of a bane wrapped in cloth and worn as an amulet. Woken, it makes the banes around take its Garou for one of their own.
A carved wolf mask with an animal spirit bound in it. Woken, it pulls its Garou into the wolf's shape and holds them there for an hour.
A flint knife curved like a crescent moon, with a cobra spirit in the blade: the Silent Striders' own. Its cuts are aggravated, and woken after a strike it drinks the foe's Gnosis.
A dagger carved from a great beast's tusk, with a snake spirit in it. Woken after a strike, it bites deeper into the wound.
A snow-white partridge wing on a gold chain, with a spirit of forgetting in it. Swept around someone in a circle, it sweeps away a memory, and with it their fear.
A small gold half-moon pendant with a lune bound in it. Woken at night, its wearer vanishes from every sense but touch, a minute a success.
A tiny tubular bell with a turtle spirit in it. Rung, its chimes keep hostile spirits away for a day.
A bullwhip woven with gold nuggets, with a spirit of flame bound in it. Woken, it bursts into fire against whatever it strikes.
A whistle of bone with a wind elemental in it. One long blast calls a freezing, snow-laced wind on the Garou's pursuers.
A full-length cloak of a thousand colored feathers with a bird spirit bound in it. Woken, it carries its wearer through the air.
A one-handed hammer of silver-laced iron with a war spirit in it: the Get of Fenris's own. Its blows are aggravated, and thrown it flies back to its Garou.
A silver dagger with a war spirit bound in it, the signature weapon of the Garou. Its cuts are silver: no Garou soaks them. Carrying one dulls its Garou's Gnosis by one.
A massive double-headed axe dedicated to Isthmene, the Gorgon of battle: the Black Furies' own. Its blows are aggravated, and woken it grants the Spirit of the Fray. It answers no male.
An amber talisman holding one human hair, with a trickster spirit bound in it. Woken, people see an ordinary person, whatever form the Garou wears.
An ivory whistle with a screech-owl spirit in it. Its wail tears at every spirit in sight.
A tablet with a bee spirit in its circuits: the Glass Walkers' own. Its hive of files keeps the Garou's notes and research in perfect order.
A length of braided hemp cord with a flock spirit in it, enough for a whole pack. Woken, its Garou shares Gnosis with every packmate near.

An immense silver sword with a war spirit and a fire spirit bound in it: the klaive of a legendary hero. Its cuts are silver, and woken the fire spirit shields its Garou from flame. Carrying one dulls its Garou's Gnosis by two.
One of the seven great hammers of the Get of Fenris, silver-laced iron with spirits of war and silver in it. Its blows are silver, and woken it blazes with fire.
Carved divination stones with a spirit of time bound in them. Cast and woken, they show what is to come.
A knife ground from a wolf's tooth, with a Lune bound in it. Woken, it makes its bearer's blows bite deeper for two hours. The Lune wakes once, then sleeps until the next full moon.
A red river stone that holds a little fury. Woken, it gives its bearer a point of Rage. It fills again under the moon its bearer was born under.
A shard of smoked glass with a watcher spirit in it. Looked through, it shows the Umbra's edge for a day, banes and all. Three looks, and then it needs a point of Gnosis for each one more.

Talen What it is ← Garou contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Portions of the materials are the copyrights and trademarks of Paradox Interactive AB, and are used with permission. All rights reserved. For more information please visit worldofdarkness.com.
An obsidian-headed arrow with a war spirit in it. Woken, it flies at the nearest hostile spirit and never misses.
A wooden bat figurine with a bat spirit in it. Woken, it flies off to scout and shows every foe on the map before it turns to sawdust.
A small jar of dust with a spirit of death in it. Sprinkled on the newly dead, it lets them speak: what they knew is the Garou's.
A dried, glyph-painted gourd with a healing spirit in it. Crushed over a wound, it heals even aggravated wounds.
A moonbeam caught in a crystal by a lune. Woken, it keeps its Garou safe on a journey through the spirit world: spirits ask no price and leave them be.
A wax seal with the sign of the full moon and a lune in it. Thrown down before a Garou, it forces them into Lupus.
A vial of night distilled. Drunk, it turns its drinker to shadow for an hour.
A hollow reed with an air elemental in it. Through it, its Garou breathes anywhere: under water, in smoke or in poison.
A sigil with a captive Wyrm spirit in it. Woken, every servant of the Wyrm on the map shows its true form; then it burns up in green fire.
Every Garou has five forms. The one they were born in is their breed form: Homid for a Homid, Lupus for a Lupus, Crinos for a Metis.

Form Strength Dexterity Stamina Manipulation What it's like Homid +0 +0 +0 +0 The human form. Anything can be worn or held, and nobody looks twice Glabro +2 +0 +2 -2 A near-man brute. Clothes and armour still fit, just. Mortals see an ugly man and nothing worse Crinos +4 +1 +3 -3 The war form. Claws and bite deal aggravated wounds. A fifth faster. Mortals who see it suffer the Delirium Hispo +3 +2 +3 -3 A dire wolf as big as a horse. Half again as fast, a crushing aggravated bite, sharper sight and hearing, no hands Lupus +1 +2 +2 -3 A wolf. Twice as fast as a man, the keenest senses of any form. Outsiders see only a wolf The Attribute changes show on the Garou tab's Attributes page while the Garou is in the form. Crinos, Hispo and Lupus also change how much a Garou eats; see Being Garou.

Form What stays Homid Everything Glabro Everything Crinos Melee weapons. Clothes, armour and guns come off Hispo, Lupus Nothing worn or held By default, what a form can't hold drops at the Garou's feet, as at the table. With the setting "Gear stays with the Garou" on, it goes with them and comes back when they change back. Hispo and Lupus have no hands, so the Garou can't do work that needs them.

Select the Garou and use the form bar: five buttons, one per form. Hover one to see how the change would go. - Back to the breed form is always instant and free. - Slowly, by roll: Stamina plus Primal-Urge at difficulty 6. Each form passed through on the way needs a success and takes two seconds. A failed roll means the change doesn't happen. - At once, for 1 Rage: straight to any form. The Merit Metamorph makes every shift succeed as if with five successes. Some Gifts hold a body in its shape, and then no shift works.

The form bar has two switches. Switch What it does In fights When a fight starts, or when drafted with enemies on the map, the Garou changes form for a point of Rage, picked as below. Drafting with no enemies on the map changes nothing. An hour after the fight they go back to the resting form. On by default Willpower When the Garou spends Willpower. Never; To resist frenzy (the default), a point holds off a frenzy when Rage boils over, but never the Thrall of the Wyrm; Freely, which also spends a point on each Gift roll for one sure success. A save from before this habit keeps what the old Resist frenzy switch said The fight form is the first of these that fits: 1. Lupus, at double speed, when the Garou is running away. 2. Glabro with a gun in hand, since Glabro can still hold one. 3. Glabro in sight of outsiders, to spare the Veil, until below 60% health. 4. Hispo to run down a target more than 15 cells off or fleeing, back to Crinos within 5. 5. Out of Crinos while holding back a frenzy: on "Resist frenzy", with the Rage to frenzy, and the moon not their auspice's. Crinos makes frenzy easier. 6. Crinos against a mortal who suffers the Delirium. 7. The auspice's lean (Ahroun Crinos, Ragabash Glabro), then the tribe's (Red Talons and Silent Striders Hispo), then Hispo for a Lupus, then Crinos. Hispo and Lupus only come with empty hands. Allied Garou of other factions cast their Gifts once they have a target or are hit, and once hit they fight with the tactics of an enemy pack. A Garou in a frenzy takes the war form on their own. See Frenzy, the Litany and Harano.

An outsider who sees a Crinos may remember it, and so may one who sees a Garou change into any form, or a Hispo walking about. Each who leaves the map remembering hurts the Veil. See The Veil, septs and hunters. ← Garou contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Garou have no Humanity to lose. What holds them back is the Litany and what other Garou think of them. What breaks them is frenzy, the Thrall of the Wyrm and Harano.

When something provokes a Garou, they roll their current Rage against a difficulty set by the moon. Four or more successes and the wolf takes over. Moon New Crescent Half Gibbous Full Difficulty 8 7 6 5 4 Rank 3 adds one to the difficulty, ranks 4 and 5 add two. The Merit Calm Heart adds two, the Flaw Short Fuse takes two off, and the setting "Frenzy difficulty" moves every roll. What provokes a roll: - a wound, once a fight: the first wound after an hour without one; - an insult; - starving, or being caged, about once an hour; - a duel for the pack's lead; - with Kindred loaded, a vampire drinking from them or feeding in front of them. Holding it off. With the Willpower habit on To resist frenzy or Freely (on the form bar; To resist frenzy by default), a point of Willpower stops it. Nothing stops the Thrall. Berserk. The Garou takes the war form and attacks: strangers first, kinfolk and packmates last. A Garou whose permanent Rage is higher than their Gnosis goes for packmates too. It lasts at least an hour, as a vampire's frenzy does, and the player can't give the Garou orders until it ends. After that it ends once no foe is in sight and a Willpower roll against current Rage succeeds, tried every few seconds. The fox frenzy. A Garou below half health, or facing three foes or more, runs instead. Drafted Garou frenzy too; you get a message, not a choice. A frenzy costs a point of Wisdom, and hurting the colony's own Garou or kin in one costs three more. The Rage running high alert lists the Garou with enough Rage, under tonight's moon, that the next wound or insult could set off a frenzy. Keep them away from trouble or let them rest.

Six or more successes on a frenzy roll is the Thrall, but only for a Garou who carries Wyrm taint or broke the Litany this season. A clean Garou never falls to it. The Flaw Short Fuse makes it always possible. In the Thrall the Garou attacks anyone, packmates included, and no Willpower holds it off. It ends as a frenzy does, costs four Wisdom, and leaves Wyrm taint behind, deeper each time: faint, marked, one step from the spiral, lost. A letter warns you one step before the end. At the last step the Garou is lost for good: they have danced the Black Spiral and join the Wyrm's servants. The Rite of Cleansing washes taint out.

The Garou's code. Breaking a tenet costs Honor, and often Wisdom, shown over the Garou with a message. Breaking it in front of other Garou of the colony costs half again as much. A tribe may weigh a tenet more or less. A Garou who broke a tenet this season can be the subject of a punishment rite, and can fall to the Thrall. What breaks it in game: Tenet Broken by Honor Wisdom Garou do not mate with Garou Two Garou becoming lovers or marrying 3 2 Accept an honourable surrender Killing a downed person, a prisoner, or an execution. Fomori, Black Spiral Dancers and vampires who read as Wyrm don't count 3 1 Do not eat the flesh of humans Eating human flesh, or a meal made with it 3 2 Keep the Veil closed Each outsider who leaves remembering the Garou. See The Veil 2 2 Fight the Wyrm wherever it is With Kindred loaded, striking someone fighting the colony's vampire, once a day 2 0 The other tenets are listed for their meaning and kept on trust. Tenet What it is Garou do not mate with Garou Two Garou together make a Metis, born deformed and barren. The Litany forbids it. Fight the Wyrm wherever it is No Garou leaves the Wyrm's servants alone once they know of them. Respect another's territory A sept's land is its own. Hunting or settling there takes leave first. Accept an honourable surrender A beaten foe who yields is spared. Killing a captive is a crime, not a victory. Submit to those of higher station The lower-ranked defer to the higher, and challenge only in turn. The first share of the kill to the greatest in station At a feast, the highest-ranked eats first. Do not eat the flesh of humans People are not prey. A Garou who eats one has taken a step toward the Wyrm. Respect those beneath you: all are of Gaia Kin, captives and animals are Gaia's too. They aren't to be harmed for no reason. Keep the Veil closed Humans must not learn what the Garou are. The last time they did, they hunted the wolves nearly to the end. Don't let your people carry you A Garou who can no longer do their part steps aside rather than be carried. In peace, the leader may be challenged In peace, any Garou may challenge for a higher place. This one permits rather than forbids. In war, the leader is not challenged When the sept fights, its leader is not questioned until the fighting is over. Never let a caern be violated A caern is Gaia's own ground. Losing one through carelessness is among the worst things a Garou can do.

Harano is a grief for the dying world. Any Garou can sink into it. What sinks them: - a Garou of the colony dying on the same map; - the Thrall; - losing the caern. You need RimWorld 1.6 or 1.7, Harmony and The Rim by Night: Core. Load order: Harmony, Core, then Garou. No DLC is needed. The Rim by Night: Kindred can load alongside it; see Kindred and Garou. The mod is safe to add to a running save. Your colonists stay mortal until you make one a Garou, a kinfolk colonist goes through the First Change, or a lost or stray cub turns up.

Four scenarios start you with Garou. Scenario Who you start with Garou pack Three Cliath and two kinfolk, already a pack under a totem Lone cub One Garou of rank 0 who hasn't had the Rite of Passage, and no sept Kinfolk family Five kinfolk, one of whom has the blood to Change Lost tribe Three Garou and two kinfolk, all of one tribe, already a pack Each colonist in these scenarios starts with one random weapon in hand, picked from the scenario's own list. Some scenarios add a steel helmet, a robe or both. None of the weapons are silver. To make your own, add the "starting Garou" part in the scenario editor. It sets how many of the first colonists are Garou, how many after them are kinfolk, whether the Garou are cubs, whether they start as a pack, and whether everyone is of one tribe.

1. Select a Garou and open the Garou tab. The Sheet page shows tribe, breed, auspice, tonight's moon, and Rage, Gnosis and Willpower. 2. Look at the form bar above the buttons. Gifts are powers taught by spirits. Each belongs to one or more lists: a breed's, an auspice's or a tribe's. Each has a rank from 1 to 5, and a Garou can't learn one above their own rank.

Select the Garou. Their Gifts sit on tiles above the buttons, one tile per list: breed, auspice, tribe, and "other Gifts" for the ones learned from someone else's list. Hover a Gift for what it does, what it costs and what it rolls. - Cost: Rage, Gnosis or Willpower, by the Gift. A Gift with no cost shown is free. - The roll: most Gifts roll a pool against a difficulty, often against the target's Willpower. The successes set how strong or long it is. A failed roll still spends the cost. - Limits: no Gifts in a frenzy. Some Gifts need a form, or open sky, or a target asleep; the button says why when it can't be used. - Always on: a few Gifts are passive and have no button. Spirit Speech is one. - Ending one early: a Gift that lasts has an End button while it runs. - From a caravan: Tech Speak is the one Gift a Garou can use on the world map. Its button is on the caravan. - On their own: an undrafted Garou who is set to attack, or has just been hurt, uses Gifts with a fighting use against enemies nearby, as Kindred do with Disciplines. Right-click a Gift's icon to open its page in the grimoire. Click the tile's name for the list's page. Some Gifts are seen by outsiders: anything that calls, makes, moves or remakes something. A witness who keeps their wits counts against the Veil. A Gift worked in Crinos adds nothing; the war form is breach enough.

Open the Garou tab, Gifts page, and press Learn a Gift.... The list shows the Garou's own Gifts first, then everyone else's. The list on the left narrows it to the breed, the auspice, the tribe or Other lists, and to one rank. A Gift needs three things: 1. Rank. The Gift's rank can't be higher than the Garou's. 2. Experience. The Gift's rank times three from the Garou's own breed, auspice or tribe, times five from any other list. Some Gifts need another Gift first. 3. A teacher. One of these: Teacher How it works A spirit, called "Call a ... spirit to teach it": a point of Gnosis and about an hour and a half of meditation, then Gnosis against 5 plus the Gift's rank. A failure spends the Gnosis and the Gift stays unlearned A higher-ranked Garou "Learn it from ...": five lessons, one a day, taken during research work A spirit in the Penumbra Talk to a spirit of the Gift's kind and pay its chiminage. See The Umbra and spirits The Gift's page says which kind of spirit teaches it. Learning a Gift is worth a point of Wisdom, and teaching one is worth Honor and Wisdom. See Renown, rank and experience.

Where everything is on screen, and what each tab, button and menu option does. Almost every line in the mod's windows has a tooltip; hover over it for the details.

Select a Garou and open the Garou tab next to Health and Needs. The heading gives the Garou's tribe, auspice, breed and rank, with Rage and Gnosis as bars under it. The pages are down the left side. A gold number beside Growth means the Garou has the Renown for its next rank or Ambitions to pick from. Click a heading's name to fold the section under it; the page remembers that until you quit the game. Click a tribe, breed, auspice, merit, rite or totem to read its page in the grimoire, and the ? at the end of a heading opens the guide on that subject.

Hover the next dot for its cost and click it to buy (Rage and Willpower cost the current rating, Gnosis twice it). Ancestors too
The nine Attributes in three columns, Physical, Social and Mental, with the current form's changes. Hover the next dot for its cost in experience and click it to buy. See Character sheet.
The Gifts the Garou knows, under their rank; click one for its page. Learning shows any lessons under way and the Learn a Gift... button. See Gifts.
Rituals, the rites the Garou knows, lessons under way, and Learn a Rite.... With a caern on the map, its level and type. See Rites and the caern.

Your own Garou only. Habits holds the resting form. In a fight picks the fighting style, with Shift in fights and the Willpower habit, the same switches as on the form bar; click one to change it. The Veil has the cover-up switch and each witness on the map with the surest way to deal with them.

See Forms and shifting. Gift tiles sit beside it: one tile for the breed's Gifts, one for the auspice's, one for the tribe's, and "other Gifts". Click an icon to use it, right-click it to read the Gift in the grimoire, and click the tile's name for the breed's, auspice's or tribe's page. A difficulty set by the target reads as a rule until the Gift is aimed ("against the target's Willpower"). The roll log puts the same parts in a grey line under each roll, and a Gift's grimoire page has the formula in a box at the top.

It goes after the nearest enemy anywhere on the map and fights as an enemy of its kind would: powers first, closing in unseen, pulling back to heal when badly hurt. Anyone with a gun backs away from melee fighters and looks for cover. A pawn scared by a power stays on the map and goes back to the fight when the panic ends. Your orders come first, and once one is done it goes back to the hunt. Undrafting ends it. While it's on, a Pick target button chooses the enemy it goes after. Once that enemy is down or gone it picks the nearest one again, and clicking the button clears the target early. A power aimed out of range or out of sight walks the pawn closer, then casts.

Select a kinfolk human or wolf. Blood shows the tribe, the strength of the blood, whether they could still Change, and which moments could still wake it. Pack shows the pack they stand with, and Join a pack.... See Packs and kinfolk.

On the bar at the bottom of the screen. While the colony has two or more kinds from the Rim by Night mods, only the window used last keeps its button, and a list down the left side of each window names every one with its pages, so a click opens any page of any of them; the Core setting One bottom-bar button turns that off. Its pages: Page What it shows Overview The Veil's level and score and, once the colony has a caern, the sept's offices. Click an office to seat a Garou in it or leave it vacant. See The colony as a sept Septs Each sept the colony knows, nearest first, with who leads it; hover a row for how far away it is. Open opens the sept's window; a click on the rest of the row finds it on the world map The world's news and the colony's own story are on the Chronicle and Our story pages under Rim by Night, at the top of the list down the window's left side. Each page holds the lines of every mod you have loaded; click a mod on its left for only that mod's lines, or a name under it for one colonist or home. Garou write frenzies, First Changes, ranks won, rites led and Wyrm creatures killed there, and the Nation's news names its septs. The moon calendar, opened from the moon beside the clock, lists the quadrum's fifteen nights. Each night shows its moon, the auspice it gives, the nights for Caern Building, the moot and the season's rite, and the full moon's extra Wyrm raids. Click a night to see its Rage at moonrise and frenzy difficulty. On the right, each of the colony's Garou shows tonight's Rage and how many days until their own moon. See The moon.
