Rites are the Garou's ceremonies. They mark rank, bind packs and spirits, cleanse taint, honour the dead, punish the guilty, and open and keep the caern.

1. Select the Garou who will lead it, the ritemaster, and press Perform a rite. 2. Pick the rite, then its subject or place if it asks for one. 3. The colony's Garou on the map come to join the circle. Kinfolk come too for Caern Building. 4. When the rite ends, everyone within 6 cells of the ritemaster is the circle. A rite takes half an hour a level. Call off the rite sends the circle back to work, and the rite isn't performed. - The roll depends on the rite's type, as at the table. Every five Garou past the rite's minimum take one off the difficulty, never below 3. The Master of the Rite rolls a die more at home. - Too few: a ring on the ground marks the circle while a rite runs, and only those inside it count. If the time is up with fewer Garou in the ring than the rite needs, the ritemaster says so and waits until enough arrive. Give the ritemaster another order to call it off. While a rite runs, no one in the circle falls asleep or starves: they get very tired and urgently hungry, and no worse. - Failure wastes the time. A botch offends the spirits and costs the ritemaster two Wisdom. - Rites cost no experience.

Rituals is the lore of the rites, on the Garou tab's Rites page: a dot for every two rites known, one more for Theurges and Philodox. A rite's level can't be higher than the Garou's Rituals. A new Cliath knows one random level 1 rite, a Theurge two. A cub gets theirs at the Rite of Passage. To learn more, press Learn a rite... on the Rites page: - from a Garou here who knows it: two lessons a level, one a day, half as many for a Theurge; - from a lune in the Penumbra, for its chiminage. See The Umbra and spirits.

- The Moot Rite happens at each full moon when the colony has a caern and two Garou, as a gathering like a party. At the moot: - the colony Garou with the most Renown since the last moot, at least 3, is hailed: a point of Glory and a good mood; - any who broke the Litany since the last moot and haven't done the Rite of Contrition are judged: a point of Honor lost and a bad mood; - a colony Galliard tells the best tale since the last moot of a colonist's capture, kill or death. Its hero gains a point of Glory if Garou, the teller a point of Wisdom, and everyone there is cheered. - Gathering for the Departed happens after a colonist dies, as a funeral. - A Garou who knows a minor rite performs it in free time as recreation, once a day, for its blessing. You can call off any of these.

Needs three Garou Rite of Accomplishment 2 Renown Turns ten temporary Renown into a permanent dot, and raises the rank when the Renown is there. These are led on a Garou of the colony who broke a tenet of the Litany in the last season. One called on a Garou who hasn't fails, and the ritemaster loses 5 Honor for it. Rite Level What it does Rite of the Jackdaw 1 The offender blurts things out and insults people, a day a success Rite of Ostracism 2 Costs Renown, and packmates think less of the offender until the next moon phase Stone of Scorn 2 Costs 8 Honor and 2 Wisdom Voice of the Jackal 2 Costs Renown, and the offender's social skills drop until the ritemaster lifts it The Hunt 3 The offender is cast out and runs for the map edge. Bringing them down pays the hunters 2 Honor Satire Rite 3 At the caern, against the offender's rank plus 4. They lose a rank. A botch costs the ritemaster 5 Wisdom

Each is held at the caern on the eighth day of its season, by two Garou at least. The caern's level makes them easier. Rite When What it does Rite of the Winter Winds Winter Scares off the next Wyrm raid that season Rite of Reawakening Spring The circle steps sideways and fights three waves of banes. Kill them all and Gnosis fills, and crops grow faster for the season The Great Hunt Summer Gaia names a quarry of the Wyrm. Bring it down by midnight for 3 Glory each. Rite of the Opened Sky Accord 4 A rain dance calls down a cleansing rain over the caern. It washes out the Wyrm's taint, and for two more Gnosis a level it heals everyone under it who isn't an enemy. Vampires and the Wyrm's creatures are left in agony, but not cleansed. One Gnosis at the caern, ten anywhere else. Moot Rite Caern 1 The gathering at the caern, once each lunar cycle. The whole colony takes heart, the ritemaster earns Honor, and each moot held makes the caern stronger. Rite of the Opened Caern Caern 1 The ritemaster wrestles with the caern's spirit to draw out its power, of whatever kind the caern holds. Losing badly burns them. Rite of the Opened Bridge Caern 4 The ritemaster lays a pathstone at the heart of the caern and calls on its totem to open a road through the Umbra to the nearest friendly sept. For a year, renewed at every moot, colonists can cross from the caern to that sept and back, and the sept's Garou come at once when the Wyrm attacks. Rite of Caern Building Caern 5 The greatest rite: a night-long working at a cleansed place of power, begun at dusk under a waxing moon. Three or more Garou pour in thirty Gnosis between them, kinfolk a point each, and every Garou gives up a point of Gnosis for good. The Wyrm will come while it runs. Failure burns everyone in the circle. Gathering for the Departed Death 1 A howl for the dead, over their body. Everyone nearby mourns together, and the Garou's despair eases a little. Breath of Gaia Minor 0 A deep breath of clean air at dawn, to honor Gaia. The body fights off sickness a little better for a day. Greet the Moon Minor 0 A howl to Luna, outdoors under tonight's moon. The Garou is steadier for a day. Hunting Prayer Minor 0 A quiet word to the spirits before the hunt. The Garou stalks a little quieter for a day. Prayer for the Prey Minor 0 Thanks given to the animals the Garou kills. Nothing of the prey goes to waste for a day. Rite of Binding Mystic 1 A willing spirit is bound into a talen: a one-use charm that does its task and lets the spirit go. One talen a success, up to three. Rite of Summoning Mystic 2 Performed in the Penumbra, where it comes easiest: a spirit of the chosen kind is called to the circle. Rite of the Fetish Mystic 3 A willing spirit is bound into a cleansed vessel for good, making a fetish of any level up to the ritemaster's rank. Rite of the Totem Mystic 3 Garou with no pack call a totem spirit and bind themselves to it as a pack. Their Totem dots together must reach the totem's cost. Rite of the Jackdaw Punishment 1 Open-mouthed sigils are carved and laid around a Garou who broke a promise of secrecy. For a day per success, they can't stop telling everyone about their own petty secrets. Rite of Ostracism Punishment 2 One by one the circle names the offender, says they have no such kin, and turns away. The offender loses Renown, and their packmates shun them until the moon turns. Stone of Scorn Punishment 2 A stone passes around the circle, and each Garou carves a mark of shame on it and tells a mocking tale about the offender, who has to sit and listen. The offender loses a great deal of Honor. Voice of the Jackal Punishment 2 Ash is blown in the face of a Garou who shamed the whole sept. They lose Renown, and their voice becomes a shrill whine that hurts every dealing with others until the punishment is lifted. Satire Rite Punishment 3 A song of ridicule performed at the caern while the offender watches, remembered for generations. The offender drops a rank. If it goes badly wrong, the song turns on the ritemaster. The Hunt Punishment 3 Called against a Garou guilty of a capital crime. The offender is cast out of the colony and runs, and the hunters give no quarter. Whoever brings them down earns Honor. Rite of Accomplishment Renown 2 The Garou's deeds are told and honored. Every full measure of temporary Renown becomes a permanent dot, and a Garou with the Renown for the next rank takes it. Rite of Passage Renown 2 A cub proves themselves before the tribe and becomes a Cliath, with a Cliath's Renown and the Gifts of their auspice and tribe. Rite of Reawakening Seasonal 2 At the spring equinox the ritemaster leads the circle sideways into the Penumbra, where banes come at them in waves. If every bane falls, Gaia wakes: the circle's Gnosis fills, and the crops grow faster for the rest of the season. Rite of the Winter Winds Seasonal 2 On the longest night the circle howls, grabs burning branches and runs through the dark making every frightful noise it can, to scare the Wyrm's servants off. The next Wyrm raid this season doesn't come. The Great Hunt Seasonal 2 At midsummer Gaia names a servant of the Wyrm, and it comes. Kill it before midnight and the circle wins Glory. Let it get away and they lose Glory, and every rite is harder for a year. The Long Vigil Seasonal 3 At the autumn equinox the caern is hung with the year's trophies, and the circle tells their stories around a bonfire until dawn, then burns them. Until winter the circle rolls a die more on Rage and is in better spirits.
A caern is a place of power the Garou have woken. The colony can have one.

1. Mark a place of power. It's in the Misc build menu. It must be outdoors, on wild natural ground, with no more than two colony buildings within 15 cells. 2. Cleanse it. Perform the Rite of Cleansing there. 3. Perform the Rite of Caern Building at it. It must begin at dusk, between 17:00 and 22:00, under a waxing moon (days 2 to 5 of the quadrum), and it runs through the night. - It needs three Garou and 10 Gnosis in the circle. Kinfolk give a point each, and every Garou gives up a point of permanent Gnosis. - The Wyrm feels it. Its servants come before the night is out: keep them away from the circle. - Wits plus Rituals at 8. The successes set the level: 1 to 3 make level 1, 4 to 6 level 2, 7 and 8 level 3, 9 or more level 4. - Failure burns the circle. The land around it sets the caern's type: water, geysers, trees, rock, hills or ruins. The rite also picks the caern's totem, who shows itself at moots.

- Garou within 12 cells get back a quarter of a Gnosis a level, every so often. - The Gauntlet is thin there: easier to step sideways, and a Garou with no Gnosis left can still cross back at the caern. - Every three moots held at a level raise it by one, up to 5. - The Rite of the Opened Caern gives by type: Gnosis, Rage, Willpower, healing or a view of the land at once, or for the other types a blessing that lasts half a day a level. Type The Opened Caern gives Enigmas Faster research Gnosis Gnosis for the ritemaster Healing The ritemaster's wounds closed Leadership Words that carry more weight Rage Rage for the ritemaster Stamina Blows land softer Strength Blows land harder The City Better trades Visions The land around it shown Will Willpower back Wisdom Everything learned faster The Wyld Something different every time

The Wyrm wants the caern. About half its raids go for the circle first. Enemies who hold the circle for three hours with no colony Garou in it cost a level, and at 0 the caern dies and needs Caern Building again. Losing the caern sends every Garou of the colony toward Harano. Spirit poachers: 3 to 5 trappers of an enemy faction come to hold the caern and bottle its spirits. While they hold it, it loses levels as when it's overrun. Each one killed or downed breaks its traps: the colony's Garou on the map get their Gnosis back, and the one who did it gains a point of Honor. Left alone, they leave after half a day.

The Rite of the Opened Bridge needs a pathstone, carried or lying near the ritemaster. One lies on about one Penumbra map in ten, guarded by a spirit, and a sept sometimes pays one for a mission. It needs a sept that isn't hostile, and rolls Wits plus Enigmas at 8 less the caern's level, three dice more when the pack's totem is the caern's. The bridge runs for a year from the caern to that sept. Cross the bridge, on the caern, sends everyone standing in the circle to the sept. Cross the bridge home, on the caravan, brings them back. While it holds, the sept comes at once when the Wyrm attacks. A moot renews it. ← Garou contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Options, Mod settings, The Rim by Night, then Garou on the rail down the left, which every Rim by Night mod shares. Four pages: Rules, Rites and spirits, World and events, and Event chances, where each Garou event has its own slider from never to three times as often. The search box at the bottom finds a setting on any page by its name or description. Reset Garou sits at the bottom too, and with a game loaded so does Remove Garou from this game. A setting you have changed shows its name tinted with a reset arrow before it, each tab counts its changed settings, and Changed only by the search box lists just those. Rules: Garou Setting What it does Default Experience gained Scales all experience a Garou earns, 25% to 300% 100% Renown gained Scales the Renown earned for deeds, and so how soon a Garou rises in rank, 25% to 300%. Renown lost for breaking the Litany stays as it is 100% Rage gained Scales the Rage from the moon, wounds, insults and the rest, 0% to 300%. At 0% a Garou only has the Rage they start the night with 100% Regeneration Scales how fast wounds close on their own, 0% to 300%. Aggravated wounds still won't regenerate 100% Silver damage Scales the extra harm silver does, 50% to 200%. At 100% it hits half again as hard as steel 100% Frenzy difficulty Added to every frenzy roll, -3 to +3. Higher means fewer frenzies As in W20 Kinfolk who Change The chance a kinfolk with the blood goes through the First Change, from thin blood to strong. Shown as the lowest and highest chance; the highest goes up to 100% 10% to 50% The Curse Scales how much a Garou's Rage unsettles mortals, 0% to 200%. At 0% the Curse is off. See Being Garou 100% Gear stays with the Garou What a form can't wear or hold goes with the Garou and comes back when they change back. Off, it drops at their feet Off Rules: Systems Setting What it does Default Frenzy Off, wounds, insults and hunger never send a Garou into frenzy or the Thrall of the Wyrm. A Gift that calls up a frenzy still does, and so does the First Change On Harano Off, losses no longer sink a Garou into Harano. Harano they already have fades as usual On The Litany Off, breaking a tenet costs no Honor or Wisdom and doesn't count against the Garou this season On The Delirium Off, no one panics or flees at a Crinos, and colonists aren't shaken. Outsiders remember what they saw, as with the Pierced Veil flaw, so the Veil suffers more On Challenges for alpha Off, packmates never challenge the alpha on their own On Wounds roll for frenzy once a fight Only the first wound of a fight, after an hour without one, rolls for frenzy. Off, every wound does On The Thrall needs taint Only a tainted Garou, one who broke the Litany this season, or one with Short Fuse can fall to the Thrall. Off, any Garou can, as in W20 On Black Fury men are born Metis Off, a man can be a Homid or Lupus Black Fury too On Rites and spirits Setting What it does Default Garou to build a caern The circle the Rite of Caern Building needs, 1 to 6 3 Gnosis to build a caern The Gnosis the circle pours in, 0 to 30. Each Garou still gives up a permanent point 10 Totem tasks The chance each lunar cycle that a pack's totem asks a task, 0% to 100% 50% A misused spirit stays silent Days a fetish's spirit won't answer after it is misused, 0 to 10 3 days A Gnosis point wakes a fetish Off, every use of a fetish is a Gnosis roll On Moon bridges on the world map Off, the Gifts that jump across the world map are greyed out On World and events Switching one off stops it from happening again. Anything already under way plays out. Setting What it does Default The Wyrm attacks Fomori, Black Spiral Dancers, Pentex First Teams and banes come for colonies with Garou, and Pentex opens plants nearby On The Wyrm's Hunted Five of the Wyrm's servants roam the world map, with Renown for each. Off, they leave the map On The Veil Outsiders who keep their wits after seeing a Garou spread the word, and hunters come On Veil damage Scales how much the Veil score rises for each outsider who leaves with what they saw, 0% to 300% 100% Veil healing Scales how fast the Veil score falls back each day, 0% to 300% 100% Kinfolk events Kinfolk and wolves of the tribe come to join, and lost and stray cubs turn up On Towns for each sept One Garou Nation sept for this many ordinary towns, 3 to 30. Lower means more septs. Takes effect on a new world 10 The Core settings, under The Rim by Night: Core, hold "Grimoire" and "Power tiles", the hunter setting the Veil's hunters need, and "Nemeses": enemies who get away come back with their next raid. Its World and rules page also holds when the first stray cub can come, cover names for the monster factions, lupus ignoring moods a wolf wouldn't feel, and prisoners keeping their secret.

With Odyssey your colony can live in orbit. The World of Darkness stays on the ground: nobody from these mods comes up uninvited unless "The World of Darkness reaches orbit" is on in Core's settings. Help you call still comes, by drop pod, and leaves on Royalty's shuttle. Without Royalty it stays aboard until the ship lands. The colony is whichever home holds most of your free colonists, so visitors go where your people are. Keep Garou in their breed form in vacuum. Any form that can't wear clothes pulls the vacsuit off, and a frenzy forces the shift. Outside the ship that kills. - A caern can't go on an asteroid, but it can go on a gravship's deck, indoors or out, and it flies with the ship. Where the ship lands on a map with its own caern, the ship's caern sleeps until you lift off again. - The raids a caern draws reach a ship's caern by drop pod. - In orbit a Garou can step sideways only at the ship's caern. That Penumbra holds only the Weaver: webs, the caern's reflection and Weaver spirits. Banes come only if the crew is miserable or the ship is tainted. - Luna still shines. Rage at moonrise and the moon's Gifts and rites work outdoors. - Far from Gaia: a Garou's mood sinks the longer the trip lasts, and Harano gets more likely. There's no Gnosis from meditation up there. Back on the ground the feeling fades over a day.

Can I add this to an existing save? Yes. Nothing changes until someone becomes Garou. The septs appear the first time the colony has a Garou. Can I remove it from a save? Yes, with the button made for it. Load the game, open the mod settings and press Remove Garou from this game. Everyone on the Penumbra comes home first. Then every Garou becomes mortal again, kinfolk lose their blood, and the mod's items, buildings, spirits, factions, quests and sites are deleted, the septs and the homestead with them. The game is saved under a new name and taken back to the main menu. Turn the mod off and load that save. Removing the mod without doing this first leaves the save broken. With Kindred still loaded, Core stays and keeps what Kindred needs. My colony has no Garou. How do I get one? A kinfolk colonist can go through the First Change (see Packs and Kinfolk). Without kin, wait for a stray cub: a rare offer in the Quests tab about a hurt, half-wild stranger at the edge of your land. Accept it and they're the colony's first Garou, and kin and lost cubs start coming after that. Do I need any DLC? No. It runs on Core alone. Does it work with Kindred? Yes. See Kindred and Garou. Does it work with modded races? The Garou tab and silver are added to every humanlike race at startup, and nothing assumes a human body layout. A form changes stats and looks, never the body. Does it work with Combat Extended? Yes, through The Rim by Night: Core. With CE loaded, the claws and bites, the fetish weapons, the Gifts' armour, projectiles and damage are all in CE's units. Will it slow my game down? It shouldn't. Pawns who aren't Garou cost nothing per tick, and nothing scans every pawn on the map. My Garou keeps frenzying. Watch the moon: the frenzy roll is at 4 under the full moon and 8 under the new. Keep high-Rage Garou out of fights and away from insults, keep them fed, and leave Resist frenzy on. Calm Heart helps. The setting "Frenzy difficulty" moves every roll. My Garou won't heal. Silver, fire and supernatural claws leave aggravated wounds, which don't regenerate. A starving Garou doesn't regenerate either. A Homid in Homid form heals as a mortal does: change forms. My Garou went over to the Wyrm. They fell to the Thrall too often. Each time leaves deeper taint, and a letter warns you one step before the end. Clean taint with the Rite of Cleansing, and keep tainted Garou and Litany breakers calm. My Garou can't step back from the Penumbra. They're out of Gnosis. Walk them to a thin spot, the glowing places out in the wild, or the caern. Hunters keep showing up. The Veil is falling. Deal with witnesses before they leave, keep Crinos out of sight of outsiders, and the score fades by a point a day. Can I get into a hostile town without attacking it? Yes. A caravan standing on any hostile town gets Sneak in beside Attack, at night only, whoever is in it. The caravan walks onto the town's map unseen, and the town's people and guns can't go for anyone they haven't found. A townsman with a clear view may notice something move, less often in the dark, and the town then searches round that spot. A searcher who comes close may find who is there. Attacking anyone gives the attacker away. Will a town I visit again have the same people? Yes. Every town the colony walks into keeps its people between visits, unless they died or left. A friendly town stays friendly while you're there: its people only turn on you if the faction does. Where do I look something up in game? The grimoire, the book button in the bottom-right corner. Type a question on its Ask tab.

With dev mode on, the debug actions menu has a "The Rim by Night: Garou" category. Make Garou turns a colonist into a Garou with rolled defaults, and Open making menu lets you choose instead. Others set the form, give Gifts, rites, Merits and Renown, change rank, provoke a frenzy or the Thrall, fill or empty Rage, Gnosis and Willpower, bring on moonrise, make kinfolk and set off their First Change, form a pack or break its Ban, pull a Garou into the Penumbra, place a thin spot, and Make mortal.

Pledge the colony to one sept and its Garou stop being names in the chronicle. Each has a personality, means, a goal of its own and an opinion of you that moves with what you do. They hand you work, owe you debts, run beside you and, if they come to hate you, work against you.

The Sept window's Nation section names the nearest sept the colony knows, with Swear to this home. You need: - a colony Garou, - the sept met and the Garou Nation at peace with the colony. One sept at a time. Its roster fills to 8 to 12 named Garou from its warriors, in packs of two and three; packmates are friends. New pages appear on the Sept window's rail: People, Council and, while a war runs, War. Leaving costs 20 goodwill with the Nation. Loyal Garou drop to -5 regard, and the debts the sept owes you shrink a size. A sept that falls frees the colony with a letter.

Every sept the colony knows can owe it debts, trivial, minor, major or life, as Kindred courts do. A sept's mission pays one when it's done: trivial for an early colony, minor once raids come at a mid-game size, major for the hardest. Once sworn, the sept's Garou owe you debts for their own errands too. Spend them on the Debts page of the Garou tab. Ask lists what a sept does for a debt, and a bigger debt covers a smaller service: two talens (trivial), a few of its fighters at the door or the elders teaching your Garou 3 experience each (minor), a fetish (major), one of its five greatest fetishes (life). Ledger lists each debt with who owes it and why; Call in on a row picks what that debt pays for. Trained wolves bought from a sept are paid in debts too. Leaving a sworn sept shrinks its debts a size.

The People page lists every named Garou: office, pack (tribe for those in none) and regard, with a filter for friends, rivals and enemies. Click a Garou to see their personality, means, goal, friends and dislikes. You only see a Garou's personality and means once you've met them: talked to them in their town or finished a mission they gave. Regard event Change A mission done for them +2 A mission done for their pack or a friend +1 A step of their goal done +3 A gift from their row +1 per 500 silver, up to +3 a season Their mission refused or let lapse -1 (Proud -3) A mission done against them or a friend -3 Betraying their goal -10, for good Regard drifts a point toward 0 every season.

Personality How they pay and behave Greedy silver x0.7, goodwill x1.5 Cautious silver and goodwill x1.25, but the biggest debt they'll owe is a size smaller Loyal everything x1.25 while you never cross them or their friends; betrayal makes an enemy for good Conniving pays with a debt another Garou owes them Cowardly one more open mission, aimed at their rivals; pay x1.2 Proud goodwill x1.5, silver x0.8; refusals cost 3 regard Zealous only the war on the Wyrm; those pay x1.5 Generous everything x1.3; now and then asks one back Vengeful bad blood never fades; an enemy at -5 Rage-driven asks only for fights, and pays in Glory: a point per 500 silver of the job to each colony Garou there Harano-struck asks for one mission fewer, all cleansing fights; regard grows half again as fast

Means come from the Garou's office, wealth and the debts owed to them: a poor one offers one mission at a time and pays x0.6, a comfortable one two at x1.0, a rich one three at x1.4. Each Garou wants something, hidden until they count you a friend (regard +6) or you have a hold over them. A goal is three steps: two missions bent to it, then the prize. At the end a letter asks whether you hand the prize over or keep it. Keeping it is a betrayal. Goal What you get for it Collector a fetish Lore hunter a fragment of the Silver Record (teaches a rite) or a Black Spiral's confession (experience) Power seeker silver by its means, and its vote for a year Revenge a major debt and the enemy's goods Freedom its regard stays at +6 or more for good Childe a minor debt now, its cub on your side later Cleansing the Wyrm each colony Garou learns, 3 experience Kingmaker the new Sept Leader starts at regard +6 Homecoming another sept, met Buried secret a life debt

Under Your seats in the Nation section, a colony Garou can seek one of the sept's seven offices. The Garou holding it takes the challenge: Willpower plus rank against 7, one harder for each rank the holder has over yours. A vacant office is simply taken. The Sept Leader needs rank 5 and beats the elder. A Garou can't hold an office here and one at the colony's own caern. Office Duty each season Sept Leader lead one moot Master of the Rite one rite for the sept Warder defend the caern once Guardian one patrol of the bawn Den parent foster a cub when the sept asks Talesinger attend every moot Truthcatcher judge one dispute (a letter) A duty kept adds 3 goodwill and a dot. Three missed in a row and the office is lost, with 10 goodwill, to the next in line, who starts at regard -3. A finished moot counts as attended. The Garou's own tab shows the office and when its duty is due, and an alert warns two days ahead.

Each season the Sept Leader and the elders (rank 4 and up) vote on one or two motions: cubs with leave or freely, war on the Wyrm or waiting, hunting outsiders, the share owed to the caern. A colony Sept Leader votes too, and a Garou may offer a minor debt for your vote.

Rivals slander the colony or stymie your next mission with their own people. Enemies send Kinfolk raiders. Capture one and question them in prisoner talk to learn who sent them, then Accuse that Garou. An accusation without proof costs 10 goodwill.

A war runs against the Wyrm's nearest settlement, a Hive or a Black Spiral den, started by the council or the world. Its score starts at 50: a season of incursions, two of raids on their warrens and labs while you hold your bawn, Kin village, guard post and fetish hoard, then the final assault at 70, the desperate defence at 30, or a truce. With the Wyrm turned off in settings there's no war. The skirmishes come a few weeks apart. A war mission you let lapse is fought without you: the sept's members against the enemy's, by their strength, and members can die in it. Hover over the stages, the score and the holdings on the War page for what each one needs.

The Backgrounds page on a Garou's tab buys rated Backgrounds with standing at the sworn sept: the new rating x 2, never experience. Leaving the sept, or the sept falling, halves every dot. Now and then a rival strikes at one of them, at most once a season: a letter gives six days (more with Contacts) to answer with a mission or a favour the rival owes, or the dot is lost. The "Rival strikes on Backgrounds" setting makes strikes rarer or more common, or turns them off. Background Each dot Allies armed mortals to call on any map with enemies on it; they never witness anything Contacts a day more to answer a strike, and a chance each season to strike back at a rival Fame more tavern guests and regulars Influence a caravan from the Garou Nation once a season Kinfolk kin join 25% more often; call one of the kin village's own, as many alive as the dots, while it stands Mentor a sept member of high enough rank (a member 1 to the leader 5) teaches its tribe's Gifts, paid in experience Resources 100 x dots squared silver a season Rites one rite a season of a level up to the dots, taught by the sept without a teacher on the map Fetish a fetish of up to that level lent by the sept, already attuned; the making menu's fetish is this loan Ancestors and Totem show on the page too, from the sheet. They come with birth and the pack and are never bought.

Under World on the Garou settings page: the sworn sept on or off, the war chance, enemy acts a season and how fast regard fades. Beside the world lies the Umbra, the spirit world. The part closest to the physical world is the Penumbra, and a Garou can walk there.

The Penumbra is a map of its own, a mirror of the home map. It has the home map's ground, rock and trees, full grown, but nothing the colony built. Where the colony built, a faint Weaver's web covers the ground, brighter where a building takes power, and it slows whoever walks through it. The caern and places of power shine. Old ruins stand solid, and so do masterwork and legendary art. Wild plants glow, and small lights drift up from plants, webs and blight. The home map's Wyrm taint shows as blight, and banes come up out of it. The nights are moonlit: the darkest at the new moon, almost day at the full. - Wyld glades: one for every 400 wild plants at home, 3 at most. Each is a lush circle with spirit fruit, a point of Gnosis each, and sometimes a Curiosus. - Lingering trees: a stump at home stands here as a faded tree, 12 at most. Lay it to rest for a point of Wisdom, and the nearest nature spirit counts it as chiminage. - Shadows of suffering: graves, corpses, prisoners and colonists in a mental break at home each leave a shadow. Every four of them bring up a bane, three at most. - Something new each trip: each Penumbra holds one of a lost spirit whose first lesson is free, a nest of two banes on blight, or a talen lying on the ground. A message says which. The map is made the first time someone steps sideways, and thrown away when none of the colony is left in it. A large home map gets a smaller Penumbra, 250 cells wide at most. Anyone who dies in the Penumbra stays there, with everything they carry.

The wall between the worlds. Its strength is the difficulty of crossing it, set by how much the colony has built within 15 cells. Around the Garou Gauntlet At most 2 colony buildings 5 Up to 15 6 Up to 60 7 More 8 Near a caern 5 less the caern's level, never under 2

Select a Garou and press Step sideways. They stare into a reflection and roll Gnosis against the Gauntlet. - A reflection: still water next to the Garou, or a pocket mirror in the inventory at one harder. The pocket mirror is made of steel at a crafting spot or machining table. Mirrorshades take two off. - The roll: one success takes five minutes, two thirty seconds, three crosses at once. - Failure: the Gauntlet won't give for an hour. - A botch: the Garou is caught in the Gauntlet, stuck between the worlds for an hour. - Packmates within 6 cells cross on the same roll, with their gear. - The Merit Natural Channel makes it one easier. Step back is the same roll from anywhere in the Penumbra, with no reflection needed.

A Garou with no Gnosis can't cross either way, except at the caern or a thin spot. Each Penumbra map has three thin spots, glowing, out where the land is wild, with a Gauntlet of 3. A Garou can cross there within 3 cells. Thin spots are springs of Gnosis too. A Garou within 3 cells of one gets back a quarter of their Gnosis every so often, and within 8 cells of the shining caern half, whatever its level.
Peek across rolls Gnosis against the Gauntlet. For an hour the Garou sees the home map's people and animals as grey shadows, hostile ones in red.
Once an hour, a colony Garou within 4 cells of Wyrm taint or a bane on the home map has a small chance of being dragged into the Penumbra, with a letter. Getting back is the usual roll.

Kind Where they come from Nature spirits One for every 40 trees on the home map, up to 5 Pattern spiders Weaver spirits, one for every 30 colony buildings, up to 3 Lunes Moon spirits: one, or two at the full moon Animal spirits One for every 8 wild animals on the home map, up to 3, each named for one of them Elementals Earth for a lot of natural rock, water for a lot of water, fire for a geyser or a fire, glass for six or more colony lights, electricity for a generator Banes The Wyrm's spirits, always one or two. They hunt whoever of the colony comes within 12 cells Curiosi Puzzle spirits, sometimes in a glade Englings One at the full moon, the prey of the Sacred Hunt No more than 12 at once. Spirits don't eat, sleep, bleed or leave a body. Banes come in kinds. Each acts at most once an hour: Bane What it does Scrag Provokes a frenzy in a Garou within 8 cells Drattosi Attacks other spirits within 15 cells Psychomachia May cross over and ride an animal at home Killing a bane in the Penumbra lifts the blight within 6 cells. Blight lifted in the Penumbra, by a rite, a Gift or a kill, lifts the Wyrm taint at the same place at home. Curiosi set a puzzle: Solve its puzzle for a point of Gnosis, Perception plus Enigmas at 9. Each success gives a point of Gnosis and one of Willpower. Englings come at the full moon. Killing one is the Sacred Hunt: every Garou within 20 cells gets their Gnosis back in full.

A spirit beaten down doesn't die. It slumbers for six hours, then fades away. Until then a Garou can drain it for a full Gnosis pool; that costs a point of Honor unless it's a bane. The Rite of the Fetish can bind any slumbering spirit.

Right-click a spirit with a Garou who has the Gift Spirit Speech, or with a Theurge within 10 cells, and pick Talk to .... Spirits won't help for nothing: each asks its chiminage, an offering carried in the inventory (wood or berries, silver or gold, steel or components, kibble or pemmican) or, sometimes, a bane driven off. Each kind has two offerings, and a spirit takes whichever of them the Garou carries. The Step sideways tooltip and the spirit's grimoire page list them. The talk window opens, with the price at the top. Pick what to ask for: - its favor, filling the Garou's Gnosis; - its Charm, a favor of its kind: nature spirits cleanse blight, water spirits heal wounds, animal spirits send their kin home, elementals cross over as an ally for a day, and Weaver spirits repair the colony's buildings; - a lesson, picked from the Gifts whose teacher is its kind (lunes teach rites too). Then pick how to bargain. The Garou haggles first, then pays from what they carry: Way Roll Each success If it goes wrong Respectfully Charisma + Social at 6 15% off A failure pays the full price Flatter Manipulation + Social at 7 15% off A botch offends it Threaten Strength + Social at 8 25% off A failure offends it The price never goes below half. An offended spirit asks half again and gives nothing this time. Three successes also win a warning: the spirit tells of a Wyrm nest nearby, which goes on the map (see Pentex). A spirit bargains two to four times a day. Paying chiminage is a promise kept: a point of Wisdom. Then the spirit asks again for the next favor. A paid spirit is also willing to go into a fetish or talen. A day's service: right-click a spirit that isn't a bane and pick Bargain with ... to have it serve the Garou for a day instead of asking a favor or a Gift. It asks Gnosis (1 to 5 by how strong it is), its offering, or the bane it wants gone, dead. The same three ways of bargaining apply, at the same difficulties. A bargain leaves no grudge. A mage can strike the same bargain for Mana. Caern tradition: a Gift asked for away from a caern of the Gift's level or higher costs double. Moods: an animal spirit is offended once the colony has taken 30 meat or more from its kind, and a nature spirit by 10 or more stumps. Either way its price doubles. A Weaver spirit is pleased by 150 or more buildings and halves its price. The Rite of Summoning, led in the Penumbra, calls a spirit of the kind you pick.

Strong spirits cross over now and then. Half of the Wyrm's raids bring one or two banes in their own shape; they come apart after half a day. At a moot, the caern's totem shows itself and stays three hours beside the ritemaster.

About one Penumbra map in ten holds a pathstone, guarded by a spirit. It's what the Rite of the Opened Bridge needs. The Litany forbids letting humans learn what the Garou are. The Delirium hides most of what they see. The danger is the few who keep their wits.

An outsider becomes a witness when they see a colony Garou: - in Crinos, and have the Willpower to keep their wits (see the Delirium); - change shape into any form; - walk about as a Hispo, on the colony's map or in a settlement; - work a Gift no mortal could explain (one worked in Crinos adds nothing); - or see a body a Garou tore open with claws or teeth, until it's buried, burned or rotted away. A message names each witness. At Willpower 9 or more they remember; below that they explain it away. Kinfolk, fomori and the colony's own don't count. Dealing with them. Kill, imprison or recruit a witness before they leave the map, or make them forget. The "Witnesses on the map" alert lists everyone left. Talking them out of it. Select any colonist, right-click the witness and pick Talk ... out of what they saw. You get two tries a day: Way Roll What happens Explain it away Manipulation + Social at 7 On a success they believe it was nothing Bribe 40 silver They always take it. Seven in ten keep quiet; the rest talk anyway, and you aren't told Threaten Strength + Social at 7 On a success they swear to keep quiet. On a failure they run, and a witness who runs off the map counts Delirium A point of Rage A Garou lets them see the wolf for a heartbeat, and the Delirium takes the memory. Always works

Each witness who leaves the map adds to the Veil score: 10 for one who remembers, 3 for one who explained it away, twice that for a trader. It fades by 1 a day. A Garou seen by a mortal who will remember loses 5 Honor, once a day at most, and breaks the Litany for each such witness who gets away. Level Score What happens Quiet under 20 Nobody outside is talking about wolves Rumours 20 Travellers tell stories. Hunters start visiting as travellers, carrying silver Hunted 50 The stories reached hunters. Bands of them come by day Exposed 80 The hunting order sends everything it has. The septs think 30 less of you A letter marks each level, and an alert stays up from Rumours on. The Garou tab shows the score. The setting "The Veil" turns witnesses and the hunters they bring off.

Once 12 points of the Veil are laid on one Garou, your sworn sept (or the nearest one you know) sends a letter asking who did it, at most once every 15 days: - Name them. The sept deals with it and cleans up half of what that Garou cost the Veil. The Garou is sore about it for ten days. The Nation thinks 5 better of you. - Take the blame as a colony. The Nation thinks 5 less of you. - Refuse. The Nation thinks 15 less of you.

A hunting order, the hunters of The Rim by Night: Core. - The raid comes by day once the Veil is Hunted, a probing band below Exposed and the whole order at Exposed. The band pulls back at nightfall. It also needs Core's hunter setting. - Silver. Every hunter's melee weapon is remade in silver. - Finishing. A hunter goes for a downed Garou first and kills them where they lie. - Visits. From Rumours on, hunters come as travellers now and then, more often as the Veil falls.

The septs trade as an ordinary-looking faction whose name, color, people and post labels change every game, so its name tells you nothing. 3 to 8 days after the colony's first Garou, the nearest sept sends a letter naming only itself. It's a faction like any other, though it never raids. The other septs stay off the world map one by one until you learn of them. A letter from a sept shows it, your Garou can meet its people, and a sept you know will now and then vouch for another. News of a sept you haven't met doesn't reach you, though once you know one sept you hear that a new one was founded, with no name or place. - Each sept leans to a tribe and keeps a caern of a type and level, shown on the world map. A sept whose tribe has a grudge with yours starts out liking you less. - Trade. Septs sell plain goods and a few fetishes and talens, and buy them back. Their caravans and visitors come as any faction's do. - Missions. Once the Nation knows you, it asks for help: shut down a Pentex plant, or kill the banes a sept's Theurges saw coming, which cross into your map a few hours after you accept. Each done is worth 15 goodwill; one let lapse after 15 days costs 7. Taking in a lost cub is worth 15 too. - More missions from the nearest sept you know: host a small moot of its Garou for a day and a half while the Wyrm's creatures come for them, lend it one of your Garou for five days (they come back with 2 Honor), clear a bane nest where the Gauntlet wore through, or break a fomori camp and take in the Kinfolk found alive there. Each pays a fetish or a pathstone and 10 goodwill; one let lapse costs 5. - Totem tasks and vengeance show in the Quests tab while they last: the totem's task for this lunar cycle, and an oath to avenge a fallen sept. - Talking. In a sept's town, select a colonist and right-click anyone of the sept to Talk to them. See Talking to people. - Help. When the Wyrm raids and the Nation is your ally, half the time a pack of three sept Garou arrives to fight beside you. With an Opened Bridge, they come at once. - Moon bridges. Gifts that open moon bridges reach twice as far to a sept or caern.

Once the colony knows a friendly sept, its Garou ask things of you now and then. Each request comes as a letter in the Quests tab that you accept or refuse; each has its own switch in the settings. - Rescues. A wounded Garou with fomori an hour or two behind asks to be let in for a day; a Ronin cast out by its sept begs five days' shelter (this costs 6 goodwill with the Nation up front, and kept safe to the end the Ronin joins you); a Garou pinned with silver is left at the map's edge for hunters, and once carried to a bed the silver comes out and the hunters come looking. A life saved is 3 Honor, and the sept owes you aid. - Fighters on call. Each debt is one pack sent to fight beside you. The Overview page of the Garou tab shows how many the septs owe on its Fighters on call row; Call in sends for one. - Theurges. Your caern and fetishes draw Theurges of other septs. A caern level counts 5, each fetish 2 a level, talens 1 each up to 5. At 6, 15 and 30 points a Theurge asks to commune at the caern or sit with a fetish for 2, 4 or 6 nights, for 1 to 3 Honor and goodwill. - The Uktena ask for any Wyrm-tainted fetish you keep, to lock it away: 2 Honor, 2 Wisdom and 8 goodwill. Refuse and each of your Uktena loses 2 regard with the tribe. - Black Spiral Dancers raid at night for a fetish of level 3 or more, and the letter says which. - Teaching. A sept Garou asks one of yours to teach a Gift or rite it knows: right-click the guest with the teacher, one lesson a night. All lessons given earn W20's Honor and Wisdom for teaching and 5 goodwill; leaving lessons ungiven costs 4. - Favours, about one letter every ten days between them: - keep a wounded elder for a season (half the time the Wyrm finds it here): 3 Honor, 10 goodwill and a debt; - keep a sept's fetish for a season; it comes by drop pod, and the sept takes it back from a home map at the end (3 Honor, 10 goodwill and a debt; missing, 15 goodwill lost); - foster a cub: three lessons from a Garou of rank 2 or more, 2 Honor, 2 Wisdom and 10 goodwill; the cub goes home once taught, or after a season; - let a hunting pack run your land for two days (about four wild animals go with them); - hand over a weapon or work of art of good quality or better as a fetish's housing: 2 Honor, 10 goodwill and a talen back; - neutral ground for two feuding packs of two septs, one night at the caern or best hall; - a Garou maimed by silver asks a doctor of Medicine 8 or more to operate: 2 Honor, goodwill and a debt; - lend a Kinfolk with a skill of 8 or more for a season: goodwill and a debt when they're back.

From Fostern (rank 2) on, a Garou's own tribe asks things of it, about one request a season between all the tribes. The Character tab shows each Garou's regard with its tribe, from -10 to 10. A request done raises it by 1 at Fostern, 2 at Adren and 3 at Athro or higher, with Renown; refused or failed, it falls by 1. Tribe What it asks Black Furies guard a sacred grove on your land for 15 days; the Wyrm may come Bone Gnawers 20 meals for a poor settlement Children of Gaia host two quarrelling septs' Garou for a night and settle it Fianna tell a visiting Galliard the colony's tale (a Social roll) Get of Fenris raze a Pentex site (a mission) Glass Walkers 6 components Red Talons drive a human camp out of the wild (a mission) Shadow Lords back a Shadow Lord's rise (4 goodwill with the Nation) Silent Striders run a message: the Garou is away 6 days Silver Fangs lead any rite within the season Stargazers answer a visiting Stargazer's riddle (an Intellectual roll) Uktena clear a bane nest (a mission) Wendigo answer a wrong against the land (a mission)

With a caern and the Nation's goodwill, the colony can host moots. A sept writes when one opens, and the Garou tab has an "Ask to host a moot" link for the highest one open now (greyed with the reason when none is). Each is hosted once a year at most. Goodwill Moot Nights Needs 20 The neighbours' moot 1 a caern 40 A Hearing: a famous pack's tale, then the colony judges its Renown 2 a caern of level 2 60 A Grand Moot of the host's tribe, kept the tribe's own way, then a council 2 a caern of level 3, a sept office held 80 A Concolation: five elders speak, the great matter is voted, a war party sets out 3 a caern of level 4, an office, a host of rank 4; a season's notice The preparation window lists meals for every guest and night. The Wyrm may strike on one night. Each tribe's Grand Moot opens with its custom: the Furies' sacred hunt, the Gnawers' feast and old debts, the Children of Gaia's meditation or revel, the Fianna's epics, the Fenris brawls and ordeals, the Walkers' planning meeting, the Talons' run with wolves, the Shadow Lords' pomp under a storm, the Striders' races and tales, the Fangs' candle-lit procession, the Stargazers' riddles, the Uktena's hidden lore and the Wendigo's old ways. The host's skill rolls decide each night. A good showing pays goodwill and Renown; a Grand Moot or Concolation that goes well names the host to an office at a neighbour sept: once a season it can call the sept's fighters and sit in judgment (a Social roll), and each year the sept sends 300 silver and a talen. The Concolation's vote can set the colony on a Pentex or bane nest mission. A guest who dies or is hurt in your care costs 10 goodwill and the sept's chronicle remembers it. The Nation goes on without you, and the Chronicle page under Rim by Night keeps its news. Elders are challenged, cubs go through the First Change, and packs go after the Wyrm and don't come back. A caern can grow stronger or lose a level to banes, and a caern that loses its last level falls: the sept is gone and Pentex builds on the ground. Pentex also opens plants near septs, and each one costs the nearest sept a caern level every season until someone shuts it down. You get a letter when that happens, and shutting the plant down earns 10 goodwill with the Nation on top of the Glory. While the Nation is short of the septs it started with, it founds a new one about once a year. With Kindred loaded, septs fight the vampire courts near them, and with Imbued, hunter cells hunt them. A sept no rival can reach may be struck by the Wyrm instead.

Select a colonist and right-click someone to talk to them: a prisoner (Question ...), a witness, or someone in a sept's, court's or hunter cell's town (Talk to ...). Your colonist walks over and the talk window opens. Pick what to ask about, then how to put it. Each way shows its roll under the button. Way Roll Kindly Charisma + Social at 6 Firmly Manipulation + Social at 6 Threaten Strength + Social at 7. It hurts their mood Bribe 40 silver, always answers. A Garou of the sept costs double and its leader triple Renown Charisma + Social, plus a die for each rank, at 6. Only with Garou and Kinfolk Each roll is a point harder against anything supernatural. Nobody lies, so a poor roll just gets nothing. Prisoners. Any Garou can question a prisoner, two to four times a day. Ask where it comes from (its home goes on the map), what it knows, or what it is (a monster you took for a mortal gives itself away). A fomor or a Pentex agent names a Pentex site, and a Black Spiral Dancer the way to its Hive. A threat hurts the prisoner's mood and makes it harder to recruit, but leaves no wounds. Townsfolk. Each person in a town answers one question, then wants three days before the next (a setting). You can ask: - Small talk. The weather, the neighbours, whatever is on their mind. It costs nothing, always gets an answer, and can go on all night. - What's the news? Word of the world's septs, courts and cells. - Where is... Pick a place from what they could know of: a Wyrm nest (a sept's Garou and Kin, to a Garou), or another sept you don't know yet (Garou speaking to Garou). The question only shows up when there's somewhere to ask about. - Have you seen... A colonist someone took. The settlement holding them goes on the map. - What troubles you? The Wyrm has dug in near the sept: a Pentex site or a corrupted factory to clear. A threat costs the town 3 goodwill whatever the roll. A Garou talking in a court's or a cell's town passes for an ordinary visitor. Asking kindly and bribing are safe. A threat gives it away one time in five, a failed roll one in ten and a botch one in two. Found out, the town turns on the colony.

A sept's elder and notables have names, the rest are a headcount, and they outlive its fall. Some die, some go missing, and the rest go to another sept, their own tribe first, or found a new one. Kinfolk go to the nearest sept. The same happens when the sept's settlement is razed, by you or by another mod. - The Veil. Each sept has a rating, shown in words on its inspect pane once you know it. Pentex sites nearby, wars and your own Garou breaching the Veil wear it down; time and rites mend it. A sept with a thinner Veil is attacked more often. - Sieges. When a war is about to break a sept you know, it is under siege for a few days first, and a quest lets you go and help. Who dies on the map is dead in the world. - Letters. A sept you know falling gets a letter: who did it, if anyone knows, a few of the dead, who is missing. Taking a sept yourself says so. Galliards at moots bring rumors of the rest. - Refugees. Survivors who like the colony and are within reach may ask to join, as an offer in the Quests tab open for two days. With a caern, survivors of a nearby sept may ask to make it their sept. - Vengeance. A sept lost to a war, a taken town or the Wyrm puts your Garou under an oath for 30 days. Until it's settled they are unhappy about it, the sept's own tribe more so. The first of the foe one of them kills settles it, with Glory for everyone in the fight and a good mood for every Garou in the colony. Losing a second sept to the same foe renews the oath. Core's settings, under The world of darkness, have a switch for all of this (off: a fallen home's people just vanish), a bloodiness slider for falls with no battle, and a world pace slider.

A caravan at a friendly sept has a Rank challenge button. The sept's elders set a challenge for one of its Garou who has a full ten temporary Renown or enough for the next rank: Willpower plus rank against 7. Winning does what the Rite of Accomplishment does. Losing costs 1 Honor, a botch 3.

A sept's people split into packs: two to four, each around its strongest member, the elder's own first. Each has a temperament that sets what it wants, what it pays in, which others it gets on with and which it feuds with. The Packs page of the sept's window shows them as cards: temperament, members, power out of 20 in ten cells, and a bar for what they think of you. While you're sworn there, that bar is the average regard of its members. Pick one to see its leader, members, allies and feuds, and Ask them for work: one of their own missions, once every five days, shown in the Quests tab to accept there. Done, the pack gains a point of power and 2 regard. A pack that thinks -5 of you or worse gives no work. When a rival comes within two power of the elder's pack and stays there for 30 days, it challenges the elder for the sept's lead, as W20's challenge for rank. The showdown comes 20 to 40 days later: a duel or the moot's word. Each side's chance is its power against the other's; a deciding mission done for a side counts two. Back a side from the page: 6 standing if it wins, 6 lost if it doesn't, and the winners' regard moves the same way. Plotters who win take the lead, and nobody plots again for 60 days. Temperament Wants Missions Warlike the Wyrm's servants dead a bane for the pack, the watch in the bawn Wise the spirits heard, the lore kept word to another sept, a bane Cunning to win without a fair fight word to another sept, a bane Traditional the Litany kept, the caern held the watch in the bawn, word to another sept Wild to run free and fight a bane

Once the colony has a caern, it's a sept. The Sept tab, on the bar at the bottom, shows the Veil and one row per office. Each office takes one colony Garou of rank 1 or more, and one Garou holds one office. A year in office is worth Glory, Honor and Wisdom. Office Bonus Sept leader A stronger moot for everyone, and 1 Honor for the leader at each moot Master of the Rite A die more leading a rite on a map with a caern Warder 1 Rage an hour while enemies are on the caern's map Guardian Sight and hearing up a tenth Den parent The colony's cubs and kinfolk on the map learn a quarter faster Talesinger Each Garou's deed worth 2 Renown or more is worth 1 more Truthcatcher A title only Without a caern the colony is a pack, not a sept, and the offices stay empty. ← Garou contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. The Wyrm is corruption, decay and destruction gone mad, and the Garou's oldest enemy. Its servants come for colonies with Garou. The setting "The Wyrm attacks" turns all of it off.

Taint lies on the ground as well as in creatures. Select a Garou to see it on the map. - Each hour a few tainted cells spread onto their neighbours, more the bigger the patch, up to 600 cells. Plants on a few of them wither. - A fomor or a bane-ridden beast that dies spills a small patch where it falls. - A Garou within 8 cells of taint gains half a point of Rage each hour. - A Garou near taint can be pulled into the Penumbra. - The Rite of Cleansing, aimed at the ground, lifts it in a circle, wider with each success. The Rite of the Opened Sky clears it under its rain. Taint in a Garou comes from the Thrall of the Wyrm. Sense Wyrm finds the tainted, the Wyrm's servants and, with Kindred loaded, some vampires.

Enemy What they are Fomori People possessed by banes and twisted. Each has one or more powers, and the Delirium doesn't touch them Banes The Wyrm's spirits. In the Penumbra they attack whoever comes near. On the home map one rides the biggest wild animal it can find, or walks in in its own shape. Its blow can get inside a mortal colonist (see Possession) Black Spiral Dancers Fallen Garou, a fourteenth tribe. They fight in Crinos with claws, frenzy and Gifts, and raid by night. A colony Garou lost to the Thrall becomes one Pentex A corporation that serves the Wyrm. It opens plants near the colony First Teams Pentex mercenaries: gunners, blades with silver, and a few fomori

Every fomor has Armored Skin or Berserker, and often one or two more: Power What it does Armored Skin A quarter less damage from everything Armored Hide, Cancerous Carapace Hide or growths that blades slide off. Not both on one fomor Exoskeleton A bony shell: stronger and harder to hurt Berserker Hits harder and faster, and a wound can send it into a frenzy Body-Barbs Blades of bone from its joints Claws and Fangs Wounds like a werewolf's, aggravated Darksight Sees as well in the dark as in daylight Extra Limbs Extra arms or tendrils to strike with Noxious Breath Fumes that burn the lungs of anyone close Some have a power of the mind as well: Power What it does Cause Insanity A colonist it can see within 15 cells goes psychotic for two hours, unless they make Willpower at 7 Echoes of Wrath A colonist it can see goes berserk for a minute, unless they make Willpower at 7 Animal Control Once a fight, the wild animals within 30 cells join its side and its raid Brain Eating Its blows gnaw at the mind: less Consciousness and half the learning, for three days

Black Spiral Dancers start with Resist Pain, Resist Toxin, Sense Wyrm and Shroud. Some also have: Gift What it does Bane Protector A bane fights beside them Ears of the Bat Finds anyone hiding within 20 cells and ends their hiding A Thousand Voices Mortals within 15 cells who fail Willpower at 6 run. Garou aren't fooled Allies Below Everyone within 10 cells is knocked down for five seconds unless they make Willpower at 6 Wyrm Hide, Horns of the Impaler Hide and horns for the fight

A bane's blow on a mortal colonist gets inside unless they make Willpower at 6. Garou, kinfolk and vampires are safe. The possessed colonist goes psychotic, and a day later becomes a fomor and joins the Wyrm. The Rite of Cleansing on them, or the Opened Sky's rain, drives the bane out before then.

A fomor, a First Team mercenary or another of the Wyrm's servants who gets away from a fight with the colony can come back as its nemesis: renamed, scarred, harder to hurt the way it was hurt, and with the Wyrm's next raid. A Garou who puts one down earns 3 Glory on top of the kill.

The Garou Nation's list of the Wyrm's servants it most wants dead. Five names roam the world map, whether the colony has Garou or not. Only a colony the Nation knows is told of them: anyone else gets no letters, sees no marks and earns nothing for one. - Who is on it. Most are Black Spiral packs: an Adren or Athro Dancer with two to four more. One name in four is a great Wyrm beast, a Nexus crawler or a Hellbeast, which comes alone and is far past a pack of Garou alone. All of them shrug off half of every wound. - The mark. Each is a mark on the world map that moves every few days and shows only within 25 tiles of a home or a caravan. Read the Wyrm's Hunted on the Sept window's Overview opens the list, which shows only what the colony knows. Rumours fill in the rest. - Meeting one. Send a caravan to its mark to hunt it. It's found at its camp, a Black Spiral pack in its Hive, a beast in the caved-in lodge it made its den, and holds it a few hours before coming out at you. One within 12 tiles can come to the colony: a pack that has never crossed it walks through unless harmed or touched by a Gift, and a beast, or a pack that knows the colony, attacks. - The reward. The Garou who kills one earns 4 Glory (6 for a beast) and 1 Honor, and the sworn sept gains 10 standing (without one, the Nation's goodwill rises by 10). The kill goes in the Nation's chronicle and can be the subject of art. - Setting. The Wyrm's Hunted turns the list off.

- Fomori raids, Black Spiral Dancer raids (by night, rarer) and First Team raids are threats like any raid. They take a raid's slot, never add one, and only come to a colony with a Garou. - They come half again as often to a colony with a caern and under the full moon, and a little more for each dot of the colony Garou's Renown. - About half of the Wyrm's raids on a colony with a caern go for the caern's circle first. See Losing it. - Half of them bring one or two banes. - A bane-ridden beast: a bane takes the biggest wild animal on the map. It grows stronger and mad, and its death taints the ground. - The Rite of Caern Building always brings the Wyrm, and lost cubs are sometimes followed.

A Pentex subsidiary opens 3 to 8 tiles from a colony with Garou: a plant on tainted ground, guarded by First Team mercenaries and fomori. While it stands, its runoff seeps into colonies within 8 tiles every few days, and it sends its First Team now and then. Send a caravan, clear it, and leave its map with no enemy standing: it closes for good, and each Garou who was there earns 3 Glory. Septs also ask for this as a mission. A captured fomor or Pentex agent can be made to name a site, a Black Spiral Dancer a Hive, and a spirit or a sept may warn of one (see Talking to people). Two rarer sites turn up later in a game, cleared the same way: Site What's there Corrupted factory Fomori guards and taint 30 cells around. Its waste seeps into colonies within 8 tiles and it sends fomori raids. 4 Glory when it's shut down Black Spiral Hive The Dancers' den: Black Spiral defenders, four banes, green balefire and taint 35 cells around. It sends Black Spiral raids. 6 Glory when it's broken

Now and then a trader caravan that looks like any trading faction's sells plain goods at half price or less. It's Pentex. Each hour its traders stay, they taint a small patch where they stand. Sense Wyrm sees through them, and then they drop the act and attack. ← Garou contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Three things make a Garou who they are: the tribe they belong to, the breed they were born as, and the moon they were born under. Each gives a list of Gifts the Garou learns cheaply. See Gifts.

Thirteen tribes can be played. The tribe sets the Garou's starting Willpower and names its totem. It also changes how the Litany weighs on them and how easily they fall into Harano. - The Black Furies are nearly all women: a man is born to the tribe only as a Metis. - The Red Talons take no homids. - The Children of Gaia count a beaten foe's surrender and the weak twice as dear, and the Get of Fenris care little for surrender. See the Litany. - The Children of Gaia and the Fianna fall into Harano half again as deep. A fourteenth tribe, the Black Spiral Dancers, belongs to the Wyrm and is never the player's. See The Wyrm. Tribe What it is Black Furies Defenders of the wild places, and of women and children who have nowhere else to turn. Nearly all of them are women. A man is born to the tribe only as a Metis. Bone Gnawers Scavengers who live on the edges of cities, among the poor and the forgotten. Other tribes look down on them. They survive anything, and they eat anything. Children of Gaia Peacemakers and healers. They hold that the Garou's worst wounds are the ones they give each other, and they show mercy where other tribes would not. Fianna Bards and revellers who love a song, a drink and a fight in about equal measure. They keep the old tales alive, and some say the fey still walk with them. Get of Fenris Warriors who measure everything by strength. They don't forgive weakness in others or in themselves, and they meet the Wyrm head on. Glass Walkers The Garou of cities and machines. They believe the fight has to be won where people live, and they put technology to work for it. Red Talons Wolves who want humanity gone and the world given back to the wild. They take no human-born Garou, and their kin run on four legs. Shadow Lords Ambitious and ruthless politicians who believe the Garou need a strong hand, and that the hand should be theirs. Silent Striders Wanderers and messengers who never stay long in one place. They travel faster than anyone and carry word between septs, and the dead follow them. Silver Fangs The royal line, which has led the Garou for as long as anyone remembers. Proud and noble, and prone to madness from breeding too long within their own line. Stargazers Seekers who look for balance through discipline and patient thought. They keep their Rage on a shorter leash than most Garou. Uktena Keepers of hidden lore. They study the mysteries other Garou avoid, and they watch over things that were bound away long ago and must stay bound. Wendigo Fierce guardians of the cold northern wilds. They are hard as the winter they live in, and slow to trust the tribes who came from across the sea. Black Spiral Dancers Garou who walked the Black Spiral Labyrinth and came out serving the Wyrm. Mad, twisted and many of them Metis, they breed in hives under poisoned ground and hate the other tribes more than anything alive.

Some tribes have old quarrels. Two Garou of feuding tribes think 10 less of each other, halved when they're packmates. Kinfolk don't hold grudges. A sept whose tribe has a grudge with your colony's starts out liking you less. Tribe Feuds with Silver Fangs Shadow Lords Red Talons Glass Walkers, Bone Gnawers Wendigo, Uktena Black Furies, Fianna, Get of Fenris, Shadow Lords, Silver Fangs Get of Fenris Children of Gaia, Black Furies

Breed Born as Breed form Starting Gnosis Primal-Urge Homid Human Homid 1 1 Metis The child of two Garou Crinos 3 1 Lupus A wolf Lupus 5 2 - A Homid in Homid form and a Lupus in Lupus form heal as a mortal does and take silver as a mortal does. In any other form they regenerate, and silver burns. - A Metis regenerates in every form, and silver burns them in every form. Metis turn up only as lost cubs or in a scenario. - Primal-Urge is rolled with Stamina for a shift. Breed What it is Homid Born human and raised among people, with no idea what they were until the First Change. Homids handle tools, trade and talk well, but the spirit world comes to them slowly. Metis The child of two Garou, which the Litany forbids. Born in the war form, always marked by some deformity, and unable to have children. Raised inside a sept, a Metis knows Garou ways better than anyone, and many Garou still look down on them. Lupus Born a wolf, and a wolf at heart in any shape. Lupus are at home in the wild and the spirit world, and have a hard time with tools and polite talk.

The moon on the night of the First Change sets the auspice. A starting Garou can pick one in the making menu, or take tonight's moon. An imbued hunter is still human. They don't heal faster, they don't frenzy, and a bullet hurts them like anyone else. What they have is sight, Conviction, Edges and each other. They also stand and fight where another colonist would run, until they're below half health or hiding. The Ignore response still holds them back.

A colonist who sees a monster hurt someone (a vampire feeding, a Garou's blow, a afflicted attacking) rolls for the Imbuing. The base chance is 2%. Brave, Kind or Tough colonists roll twice as often, Wimps half as often, and nobody in a mental break is chosen. Each monster can imbue at most one colonist a day. A colony with more than three hunters gets at most one new one a season. What the colonist does in the next three seconds picks the Virtue: They... Virtue Attack the monster Zeal Rescue, tend or carry someone hurt, or capture the monster Mercy Anything else: run, hide, watch Vision Traits and passions then pick the Creed within that Virtue; see Creeds and Virtues. A letter from the Messengers names it. The new hunter starts with two points in the Creed's Virtue and one more rolled among the three, Conviction at the Creed's level, and the first Edge of the Creed's path. Every hunter also holds True Faith 5, the most there is: vampires fear it, and it adds to Willpower.

A colony with no hunters gets a visitor by night some time between day 15 and day 40: a stranger who has just been Imbued, running from the monster that woke them. They come as an offer in the Quests tab, open for two days. Let it run out, and they leave and take the monster with them. Accept it, and they join as a hunter with a Creed of their own (more often a Vision Creed, as they ran) and its first Edge. Two to five hours later, once it is dark, the monster comes after them alone: a shambler, or with Kindred or Garou loaded a young vampire or a fomor. It is the new hunter's first horror; see Hunter tools. Turned away, the stranger comes again 30 to 60 days later, until the colony has a hunter of its own. The Imbued settings can turn this off.

A colonist who misses the roll by a little becomes a Bystander. They get no sight and no Edges, but they know monsters exist: they panic a little less, and they work 10% faster at research and tending.

Conviction (1 to 10) is the hunter's certainty that they're doing right. It pays for second sight and for most Edges above level 3. It comes back after each threat ends, up to the Creed's level, and deeds raise it past that. At 0 the hunter is an ordinary person to every monster, and a mood thought says so. At 10 the hunter can cash it in for a Virtue point, which leaves them at 3.

When a hostile monster comes within 15 cells and in view, or aims a power at the hunter, the hunter spends 1 Conviction at once. For three hours: - Every monster they see gets a mark over it. The mark says "not human", not what kind. - Their mind is closed: no Dominate, no Presence, no Delirium, no possession. - Each monster seen this way is known to the hunter from then on (the Imbued tab lists them). - Illusions they see are marked "false". They won't aim at one, and one blow from them ends it. A vampire's phantom beast gets no mark, but a blow ends it too. - Smoke no longer spoils their aim, though they won't pick a new target through it on their own. Some monsters are too strong to see: an elder vampire, a Garou of rank 4 or more, a necromancer. The hunter rolls their primary Virtue plus Awareness at 6 (8 against the very oldest). On a failure that one monster stays hidden from them for the three hours, and its powers can still reach their mind.

Every hunter in the colony is in its cell. Cell members think a little better of each other, and when one hunter's sight wakes, the others within 10 cells who can see them spend their own point at once instead of waiting to see the monster themselves. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. A monster in your prison is someone a hunter can talk to: about who it was, what it wants, what hurts it, who else is out there, and whether it could be something better. The other cells talk too, on notes left on the Hunters' Board.

Only a hunter can talk to one, and only a prisoner the colony knows for a monster. One that still looks mortal has to be found out first (second sight, a clue, a dissection). Shamblers have nothing to say. Talk to (name) is on the right-click menu. The hunter walks over, the talk window opens with the monster's file beside it, and everything it says is written into the file under What it told us. A monster that's asleep, raging or out of patience says so instead. Topic What it gives Who it was Its life before. Its clan or tribe shows in about a third of the answers What it wants What it's after, in its own words What it is Its kind's weakness. The first true answer adds half an autopsy's worth to the colony's file and counts as a Visionary's deed Others The first thing it can give up: the culprit of a town case you're working, a lair (you get the site), or a vampire court or Garou sept near the colony Redemption See below Its word It swears to leave the colony alone if let go. It can only swear once The tones are the ones for talking to townsfolk: Kindly (Charisma + Social at 6), Firmly (Manipulation + Social at 6), Threaten (Strength + Social at 7, two patience). An Innocent rolls two dice more. A failed question gets a refusal, and a botched threat ends the talk for the day. Its patience is the same 2 to 4 a day as anyone's.

About three times in ten (four in ten when threatened) a monster lies about who it was, its weakness, or the others, half as often once it's past half redeemed. A lie gives nothing. A hunter with the Pierce Edge always catches it, and a Judge catches it on Perception + their first Virtue at 7. A caught lie is marked in the file.

After every question the monster rolls its Manipulation + 2 against the hunter's Willpower, both at 6. If it wins, it says something that gets under the hunter's skin: - Doubt. The hunter loses a point of Conviction. Not an Innocent. - Its words linger. A mood hit for a few days, twice as long for an Innocent. - Anger. Now and then the hunter's next question comes out as a threat whatever they picked.

Asking about redemption is a roll like any other, once a day per monster, and fills a pool to 100. - Kindly: 4 points per success. - Firmly or Threaten: 7 points per success, but each talk hurts it and it takes it badly. - A Redeemer fills it twice as fast. An Avenger who tries takes -3 mood for 3 days for having talked to it like a person. - Beyond redemption: a vampire below Humanity 4 on Humanity can't be reached. One on a Path still can. At 100 it joins the colony. Every Mercy hunter in the colony gains a point of Conviction, and the one who did it gets a Redeemer's deed. One broken by force rather than talked round remembers it. - A revenant is laid to rest instead, and the colony is glad of it. - A necromancer lets its dead go and gives up the power. - A traitor. A vampire or Garou that gave up others counts as one to its own. If its old faction is hostile, it raids the colony 10 to 20 days later to get it back.
Letting it go on its word

Once it has sworn, Let it go on the word given sets it free. Whether it keeps its word is rolled then: 30%, plus 5% for every kindly answer it gave (less for every threat), plus 20% if it's past half redeemed, at most 80%. - Kept: once within a year, it sends you a letter warning of an attack by its own kind. - Broken: it comes back 5 to 15 days later, with others, as a first horror does. A vampire or Garou let go after giving up others has left its sect or sept by the time it's off the map.

A Hunters' Board also takes the other cells' notes. Nobody sees them come: one is pinned in the night every 1 to 3 days, and sooner after something the cells would talk about. Only the board shows them. Its inspect line counts the notes nobody has read, and they stay sealed until someone does: a sealed note shows only what kind it is ("A lead", "Everyday talk"), and the writer stays a surprise. - Read the board (the board's button) opens the Hunters tab on the board, with the clippings of solved cases on a second tab. - Send someone to read (in the notes window) sends the nearest free colonist over. Colonists also read it in their free time, as recreation. Reading takes about an hour, and good or bad news in the notes shows in their mood. Each note is signed with a handle. Hover over it to see the hunter's real name and cell. Up to 40 notes stay up; older ones come down. Notes What they are Cells A cell's own life, a cell under attack, a hunter killed, and the warning after a trap Deeds Talk of the colony's own work: a case solved, a monster killed, redeemed, let go or dissected World Word of the world, the same rumors a caravan brings Leads A lair or a town with something wrong in it. Follow it for the site, or test it first Talk Arguments between the Creeds, at most one note in five Everyday The weather, lost knives, a fair in town. Now and then one ends with a lead Yours The colony's own notes Notes about deeds and arguments get 2 to 4 replies from other hunters, each in their Creed's voice.

About one lead in eight was pinned by monsters who read the board. It's written the same way, but more of them wait at the site than it says, and afterwards a note warns the cells about the handle that wrote it. Test it for bait before following a lead: a hunter with Pierce always tells, and a Judge rolls Perception + their first Virtue at 7 and on a failure can't tell. The result is written on the note.

Pin a note puts up one of the colony's own, each kind once a week: Note What it does Share a finding Needs a file from the autopsy table or something a monster told you. The cells' goodwill goes up by 5, and they reply Ask for help A few of the cells' hunters walk in to fight beside you, as an ally's military aid. Needs the cells friendly. Works without a comms console Warn of one that got away Needs a monster you let go or one that escaped.
