At the Imbuing a hunter gets the book's five dots of Background, spread at random over its nine. Only the five that change play are kept, so most hunters have two or three dots between them. Background What it does Destiny Once a day for each dot, a botched Edge roll is rolled again Arsenal 3% better prices a dot when this hunter trades with a hunter cell's post, and a crate of hunter weapons worth 150 silver a dot each season. A hunter who starts with it packs an extra hunter weapon a dot: a stake crossbow, a fire lance, an aspergillum, an incendiary shotgun Mentor An older hunter visits now and then with a monster's weakness or the lair of a monster the colony knows. More dots, more visits Contacts One person a dot in a town near the colony, who tells the hunter what they see. See Contacts and allies Allies One friend a dot in a town near the colony. They count as contacts too, with the same favours Hunters from a save made before Contacts and Allies came in roll those two dots once, the first time the save loads. Arsenal, Mentor, Contacts and Allies sit on the tab's Backgrounds page, beside the Backgrounds every kind shares: Fame, Influence and Resources, and Mentor, Contacts and Allies doing more there. They rise only with standing at the sworn cell, never with experience. Destiny shows lower on the same page, with Awareness, and is never bought.
The feel for when something isn't human. A hunter gains a dot for every three monsters they've come to know, up to 5. Each dot is a die more when second sight meets a monster too strong for it.

Once, a hunter can swear against one kind of monster, from Swear against a kind... on the Hunt page of her tab. It can't be changed. Her blows on that kind do 10% more, counted with the colony's files under their 25% ceiling. Tracking it by its footsteps and Pinpointing it get a die more; tracking or Pinpointing any other kind gets a die less.

A hunter has the same nine Attributes as everyone in The Rim by Night, read from their skills and health. Experience raises them: a dot costs four times the current rating, up to 5. Each dot past an ordinary person's gives the same small bonuses it gives Kindred and Garou (melee damage for Strength, dodge for Dexterity, and so on). Willpower is the ordinary kind. It pays for mundane feats, never for an Edge's cost, and a dot costs its current rating. The Willpower habit on the tab says when the hunter spends it: Setting What happens Never spend Willpower is never spent on rolls To resist the mind The default. A point goes against a monster's power over the mind (Dominate, a Gift of fear, a Mind spell) and makes it one step harder Spend freely As above, and a point on each Edge roll and each Virtue roll to sway someone, for one sure success

Each colony hunter works toward one goal at a time, taken from the hunt. A letter offers three, and one of them suits the hunter's Creed. The tab shows the goal and how far along it is, and so does the Quests tab. Only what happens after it is taken counts. A met ambition pays its experience the same day, and a new letter comes the day after. There is no deadline and no failure. Drop one, or turn all three down, and another letter comes in five days. Goal Who draws it What to do Pays Close a case Anyone See one of the colony's cases through to the one behind it. 5 Destroy a monster Anyone Kill two monsters with your own hands. 5 Save someone Anyone Get someone away from a monster that has hurt them, or stand over them while they're down. 5 Redeem a monster Anyone Talk a captured monster into turning from what it is. 7 Find a lair Anyone Get a lead to where a monster sleeps. 3 Hold the line Defender Go a whole season without a colonist dying. 5 Spare a monster Innocent Let a beaten monster live, or let one go on its word. 5 Take the blow Martyr Stand between a monster and someone who is down. 5 Three monsters Avenger Kill three monsters with your own hands. 7 Unmask them Judge Show two monsters for what they are, to yourself or to everyone. 5 Mend the hurt Redeemer Heal two people a monster has hurt. 5 Learn the truth Visionary Learn three things about monsters: from a body, a book, a captive or a case. 5

A hunter earns 0.3 experience a day, plus some for each kill, twice as much for a monster. The Experience gained setting scales it. Creed Virtue Conviction Path What it is Avenger Zeal 4 Vengeance The monsters have to be destroyed, every one of them, and the Avenger means to do it. Of all the hunters they are the readiest to fight and the least willing to stop. Defender Zeal 3 Defense Someone has to stand between the monsters and the people they prey on. The Defender guards a home, a family or a whole colony, and fights to keep it safe. Judge Zeal 3 Judgment Not every monster is the same, and not every one deserves the same end. The Judge weighs what a creature has done before deciding what to do about it, then acts without flinching. Innocent Mercy 3 Innocence The Innocent sees the monsters as they are and isn't afraid of them. They ask questions where others would shoot, and trust that understanding can do more than a weapon. Martyr Mercy 4 Martyrdom Whatever it costs, the Martyr pays it so that no one else has to. They take the blow meant for someone else and count their own pain as the price of saving others. Redeemer Mercy 3 Redemption Something human may still be left inside a monster. The Redeemer looks for it, and tries to bring it back before deciding the creature is beyond saving. Visionary Vision 3 Vision Why were they chosen, and what for? The Visionary wants to know what the monsters are, what the Imbuing means and where it all leads, and looks for the answers before anything else. Within the Virtue the act picked, the Creed leans by what the colonist is like: Virtue Creed Leans to it Zeal Avenger Bloodlust, a Melee passion Zeal Defender Kind, or a loved one hurt by the monster Zeal Judge An Intellectual or Social passion Mercy Innocent Young adults, under 21 Mercy Martyr Masochist, or a loved one killed Mercy Redeemer A Medicine passion Vision Visionary Everyone

Mercy, Vision and Zeal run from 0 to 10. The Creed's own Virtue, the primary, is never passed by the other two. Virtues rise only one way: cashing in 10 Conviction with the Imbued tab's Choose a Virtue link. The alert "Hunter can raise a Virtue" shows when one can. Both list the Virtues that may rise and the Edges each would open, and the hunter drops to 0 Conviction after.

Each deed gives 1 Conviction, once a day for each kind. Creed The deed Avenger Kills a monster, or fights three at once and lives Defender Carries a colonist a monster hurt to safety, or takes a monster's blow with a downed or non-fighting colonist within 2 cells Judge Shows a disguised monster for what it is Innocent Talks to a monster and walks away Martyr Gets hurt by a monster standing over a downed friend Redeemer Heals someone a monster hurt, or spares a downed monster Visionary Learns a weakness, a past or a lair Any hunter also gains a point for killing a monster with fire, a trap or sunlight, and for winning an argument with a hunter of another Creed.

Acting against the Creed costs a point: an Avenger fleeing a fight they could take, a Defender leaving a downed colonist to a monster, a Redeemer executing a prisoner, a Visionary striking first at a monster they know nothing about, an Innocent standing by while a monster feeds. Judges and Martyrs have none.

At 7 in any Virtue, and at each point after, the hunter gains a derangement that fits it: Zeal leans to paranoia, obsession and mania, Mercy to multiple personalities and hysteria, Vision to schizophrenia and obsession. Seeing a loved one or another hunter killed by a monster calls for a Willpower roll at 7, and a failure brings one too. Core's settings can turn derangements off. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Edges are the powers the Messengers give. Each Creed has a path of five, from level 1 to 5, and each Edge belongs to the path's Virtue.

- A level costs its number in points of its Virtue: level 1 costs 1, level 3 costs 3. - Edges go in order on a path. The next one on the hunter's own path comes first. - Other paths open too, for any Virtue the hunter has points in, but never past the best Edge on their own path. - Level 5 opens only at 10 in the primary Virtue, and only on the hunter's own path. - When a new Virtue point makes an Edge affordable, the alert "Hunter can learn an Edge" shows on the right. Click it to jump to the hunter, then press Learn an Edge on the Imbued tab. Unspent points keep. A new Edge is ready at once. Unspent points show under each Virtue on the Imbued tab, with a link to pick an Edge.

Each path gets one tile on the gizmo bar. Click it, pick the Edge, then the target. Most Edges roll an Attribute plus the Virtue against a difficulty, usually 6, and the successes set how strong or how long it is. Some cost Conviction to start, shown in the tables below. Edges that work on monsters do nothing to people or to other hunters.

The tab's Risking Conviction row sets the hunter's habit: Setting What happens Never No risk When desperate Risk 2 when hurt, outnumbered or outmatched Always risk 2 Risk 2 whenever possible Once an hour the next Edge roll takes the risked points as extra dice. A success keeps them and adds one more. A failure loses them; a botch loses all the hunter's Conviction. Autocast sets whether a hunter uses Edges on their own in a fight, as for Kindred and Garou.

You need RimWorld 1.6 or 1.7, Harmony and The Rim by Night: Core. Load order: Harmony, Core, then Imbued. No DLC is needed. Kindred and Garou can load alongside it, in any combination; see Living with monsters. The mod is safe to add to a running save. Your colonists stay ordinary until one of them sees a monster hurt someone and the Messengers choose them.

Three scenarios start you with hunters. Scenario Who you start with Fresh cell Three new hunters, each with the Imbuing's three Virtue points and one Edge Lone survivor One new hunter. A shambler raid comes about two and a half days in Hunting party Four veterans with six to eight Virtue points, two or three Edges each and hunter weapons, and a revenant's lair on the world map When the game starts, each hunter opens a making menu: pick the Creed, where the free Virtue point goes, where a veteran's extra Virtue points go, any Edges past the first, and five Background dots. Anything left unpicked is rolled when you close it. Each colonist in these scenarios starts with one random weapon in hand, picked from the scenario's own list. Some scenarios add a steel helmet, a robe or both. Arsenal packs an extra hunter weapon a dot on top. To make your own, add the "starting hunters" part in the scenario editor. It sets how many of the first colonists are hunters.

Any adult colonist who sees a monster hurt someone within about 15 cells rolls for the Imbuing. The chance is small (2%, more for the brave and the kind), and the colony gets at most one a day from the same monster. What the colonist does in the next few seconds picks their Virtue: fighting the monster leans to Zeal, helping the hurt to Mercy, anything else to Vision. Someone who just misses the roll becomes a Bystander. See Being imbued. Without Kindred or Garou, the monsters that set this off are the afflicted. See The afflicted.

1. Open the hunter's Imbued tab: Creed, Virtues, the first Edge, and the Background. 2. Set the hunter's risk policy and autocast in the tab's Habits rows. 3. Keep fire close: torches, a campfire, incendiaries. The afflicted burn. 4. Bury your dead. Corpses left lying out can get up when the map is haunted. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Hunter cells trade as an ordinary-looking faction whose name, color, people and post labels change every game, so its name tells you nothing. Other cells of hunters, scattered across the world. They stay hidden until one reaches out: 3 to 8 days after the colony's first hunter, the nearest cell sends a letter naming only itself, and the cells are allies from then on. The other cells stay off the world map one by one until you learn of them. A letter or call for help from a cell shows it, a raid shows where it came from, your hunters can meet its people, and a cell you know will now and then vouch for another. Hunters don't get a list of monsters either. A town's inspect line says who lives there only after a hunter has seen them for what they are on that map: "Found out here so far", as a share of the town, counting each person once.

Four cell settlements, two of them within reach of the colony. Their people are cell members (Bystanders with guns) and hunters with a Creed. Each cell sells the Core hunter weapons (stake crossbow, fire lance, aspergillum, incendiary shotgun) with plain supplies, and buys anything of value. A hunter with Arsenal gets better prices.

In a cell's town, select a colonist and right-click anyone of the cell to Talk to them. The talk window works as it does in a case: pick what to ask about, then how to put it (Kindly, Firmly, Threaten, Bribe). Each person answers one question, then wants three days before the next (a setting). Nobody lies, so a poor roll just gets nothing. - Small talk. The weather, the neighbours, whatever is on their mind. It costs nothing, always gets an answer, and can go on all night. - What's the news? Word of the world's cells, courts and septs. - Where is... Hunters speaking to hunters can ask the way to the nearest cell you don't know yet. The question only shows up when there is one. - Have you seen... A colonist someone took. The settlement holding them goes on the map. - What troubles you? Something is feeding on a town nearby, and the cell hands you the case. A hunter can also put Conviction behind any question, here or anywhere else the window opens: a point of Conviction for Charisma + Social at 6 with one success already counted. A threat costs the town 3 goodwill whatever the roll. A hunter talking in a court's or a sept's town passes for an ordinary visitor. Asking kindly and bribing are safe. A threat gives it away one time in five, a failed roll one in ten and a botch one in two. Found out, the town turns on the colony. The same right-click questions a prisoner that isn't a known monster (Question ...), for where it comes from, what it knows and what it is, and talks a witness out of what they saw.

Cells hunt the courts and septs near them, and get hunted back. A cell's hunters have names and outlive its fall: some die, some go missing, and the rest go to the nearest cell or start a new one. While the network is short of its cells, new ones are found about twice a year. - Exposure. Each cell has a rating, shown in words once you know it. Every hunt it makes and every witness who gets away raises it; lying low lowers it. A more exposed cell is struck more often. - Sieges. When a war is about to break a cell you know, it is under siege for a few days first, and a quest lets you go and help. - Requests. The nearest cell you know asks for help through the storyteller: keep a witness for two days (about one time in three the witness is one of the hidden dead, and shows it the first night), hold a captured walking dead as your prisoner for five days until the cell comes for it, lend one of your hunters for five days (they come back with a point of Conviction), or bring stakes, holy water, silver nitrate or salt by caravan. Each pays silver and one of the arsenal's weapons, with 10 goodwill. - The Messengers' errands show in the Quests tab until the spot fades at dusk. - Letters. A cell you know falling gets a letter, and taking one yourself says so. The other cells traffic brings rumors of the rest. - Refugees. Hunters who like the colony and are within reach may ask to join, as an offer in the Quests tab open for two days. Your hunters gain Conviction against whatever kind of monster did it. Core's settings, under The world of darkness, have a switch for all of this (off: a fallen home's people just vanish), a bloodiness slider for falls with no battle, and a world pace slider.

The colony's standing with Hunter-Net is its goodwill with the cells. Each solved case raises it by 10 to 25, more for a harder case. Standing What it opens 20 Tips: every four days or so an open case gets a letter from a cell that knows the town. It tells what kind of monster did it, or once that's known, rules out an innocent suspect 40 A Hunter-Net trader caravan comes by now and then, selling the arsenal, medicine and chemfuel 60 Call a cell in the case window: two hunters come to the case's town or lair, once every ten days 80 Rumours come from 8 tiles farther, and cases pay a quarter more
One time in three, a cell sends word of an afflicted raid or a revenant's visit before it comes: what's coming, and in 6 to 12 hours.

Now and then a cell 2 to 8 tiles off is attacked by the dead and asks the colony to come. The call is a quest: take it within a day or two, and the cell's three hunters hold for three days after. Arrive in time and keep one alive, and the cell pays 300 silver and the net thinks better of you.
The other cells are an ally, so the comms console's call for military aid reaches them, and a few hunters come to fight beside the colony. Without a console, pin Ask for help on the Hunters' Board.

Once the colony knows a friendly cell, the cells and the Creeds write with requests. Each answers with Accept or Refuse; a refusal is noticed. Every one has its own switch and frequency in the settings. - Case files. Once your hunter notes are worth it (autopsies and copied files), a cell asks to read them for 2 to 6 nights. The monsters in them may come to burn them. - Teaching. A guest asks to learn a skill one of your colonists has at 10 or more, what your notes know of a monster kind, or an Edge one of your hunters has, one lesson a night (right-click the guest). - Rescues. A hunter chased by a monster (it follows after dark), a hunter wanted by a cover-up (the law may come), and a hunter left bound at the map's edge (carry them to a bed). Each saved life leaves the cells owing help: the Fighters on call row on the Overview page counts it, and Call in brings a few of the net's hunters to fight. - Favours. Hold a cell's captive monster for a season (it comes drugged by drop pod; carry it to a prison bed), foster a new imbued, send stakes, silver or silver nitrate, host two cells at odds for a night, patch up a hurt hunter, lend a skilled colonist for a season. - Creed requests. Each Creed asks its own: the Avengers a monster put down (a lead opens), the Defenders a family guarded, the Judges a ruling on a monster you hold, the Innocents one spared, the Martyrs a risk taken for another cell, the Redeemers a monster talked round, the Visionaries what the Messengers want (a case opens). They pay more by the worth of the hunter's Edges, the sum of their levels, in steps at 3, 6 and 10. A guest hurt or killed in your care costs 10 goodwill.

The Hunter-Net page has an "Ask to host" link for the highest meeting the colony can host now (greyed with the reason when none is), and a cell writes when one opens. Each is hosted once a year at most. Goodwill Meeting Nights 40 Regional meet: leads shared round a table, then a hunt planned, which opens a lead 2 60 Creed summit: Mercy, Vision and Zeal argue what the Messengers want, then the net votes on its aim 2 80 Great hunt: cells muster at the colony, plan a strike on a nest (a lair opens) and march out 3 Each needs free beds and meals for every guest and night; the dead may strike on one night. The host's skill rolls decide each night, and a good showing pays goodwill and xp for the host.

Each dot of Contacts or Allies a hunter has is one person living in a town near the colony. They show on the Contacts page of the Hunters tab, under the town they live in. They need no looking after. Once a week each can be asked for one favour: - Goodwill: they put in a good word, and the town's faction thinks better of the colony. - Sighting: they name something they saw that wasn't human, and a lead to a lair opens near their town. A monster that learns one's name ends it. That happens when a hunter lets a captured monster go on its word, and to all of a hunter's people when the hunter is taken prisoner. The dot finds someone new a season later. A contact whose town is destroyed is gone too.

A hunter with the Mentor Background is visited now and then by an older hunter, more often for more dots. The mentor brings either the weakness of a monster kind the colony hasn't pinpointed (from then on, the colony's hunters hit that kind a quarter harder), or the lair of a monster one of the colony's hunters knows.

About one in four of Core's wandering travellers and order hunters is imbued, mostly Avengers, Defenders and Judges, with two or three Edges. They see through a vampire's mask without a roll, and a mendicant hunter goes straight for a masked vampire. They use their Edges in a fight. A setting turns them off.

How much of the cell the world has seen, from 0 to 100, shown on the Hunters tab's Overview. A mortal from outside the colony who sees one of your hunters use an Edge (1.5) or kill a monster (4) adds to it once they get away from the map, twice that for a trader. One caravan's story counts for 10 at most. It falls by about a third of a point a day, slower once it's high. Level Score What happens Quiet under 20 Nothing Talk 20 The Hunter-Net scolds the hunter most to blame: one point of Conviction lost Police 40 A patrol asks about a hunter seen with a weapon. Hand the weapon over, or turn them away and the nearest town thinks 15 less of you Press 60 Every faction with towns thinks 10 less of you Burned 80 The nearest hostile monster home learns where the cell lives and raids within three days (the walking dead, if there's none). Something picks up the cell's trail, and a new case opens Once 12 points are laid on one hunter, your sworn cell (or the nearest one you know) asks who did it. Name them and half of it is cleaned up, take the blame as a colony, or refuse. Standing with the Hunter-Net moves 5 up, 5 down or 15 down.

Hunter-Net's list of the monsters it most wants dead. Five names roam the world map, whether the colony has an imbued or not. Only a colony with an imbued is told of them. - Who is on it. One kind for each monster mod you have loaded: a vampire with Kindred, a Black Spiral Dancer with Garou, a Seer of the Throne with Awakened. With Imbued alone the list holds only the walking dead's worst: a necromancer with its shamblers, or a revenant. All of them shrug off half of every wound. - What it is. The list never says. Only second sight tells: once one stands on a map with one of your imbued, its kind, its followers and its powers show in its file. - The mark. Each is a mark on the world map that moves every few days and shows only within 25 tiles of a home or a caravan. Read Most Wanted on the Hunters window's Overview opens the list. - Meeting one. Send a caravan to its mark to hunt it. It's found where its kind lives: a vampire's haven, a werewolf's den, a Seer's safehouse, a necromancer's house or a grave chapel, and holds it a few hours before coming out at you. One within 12 tiles can come to the colony: a monster that has never crossed it walks through unless harmed or touched by an Edge, and the walking dead, or one that knows the colony, attack. - The reward. The imbued who kills one gains 3 Conviction, and the sworn cell gains 10 standing (without one, the Hunter-Net's goodwill rises by 10). The kill goes in the chronicle and can be the subject of art.

A tavern counter (Furniture tab) works for a hunter colony too. Its Guests button lets in the hunters of the nearest cell you know, besides townsfolk. A party of hunters brings word of a lair one time in eight. Their second sight shows them what any guest is, and they hate vampires, werewolves and the Wyrm's things, so mixing them with Kindred or Garou guests makes for fights. Pick a bouncer or two. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. The table, the horror and the last stand
Hunters are mortals, so most of this rewards getting ready before the fight. All of it works without Kindred or Garou.
The table, the horror and the last stand

Build it from the Misc tab. Then lay a subject on it: a downed monster, a staked vampire, any downed person, any prisoner, a person's corpse, or a piece of a first horror. Animals, insects and machines don't count. Right-click the subject and pick Carry to the autopsy table (anyone can do this), or use vanilla's Carry while drafted. Straps stop a downed subject crawling off and hold a prisoner down until someone carries them away. Nobody sleeps on the table. Hold the subject, on the table's buttons and on by default, keeps a strapped prisoner there: wardens don't take them back to the cell, and they bring food to the table. Turn it off and wardens take the prisoner back.
The table, the horror and the last stand

What happens to the subject is set on the table's Bills tab, as on any work bench: Examine, Test for weakness, Dissect or Study a horror's piece. A hunter or Bystander on research work does the bill. Repeat counts, pausing, the search radius and the filter work as on any bench. - What's on the table first. A prisoner, a staked monster, a corpse or a horror's piece lying on the table goes to the first bill that fits it. The corpse filter is only asked of corpses. - Fetching. With the table empty, a bill brings the nearest corpse its filter takes. Test for weakness also brings the nearest item of each method ticked under Test with in its Details: silver, fire (chemfuel) or holy water. Untick a method to keep its item. A horror's piece is carried there by hand. - The filter. A new bill takes supernatural corpses only. Untick or tick the kinds under Corpses > Supernatural corpses, and allow mortal corpses under humanlike corpses. - Test for weakness. Each Test tries one method on the subject's kind. A miss is ruled out for that kind, colony-wide, and the next Test brings a method not yet tried. A hit on two successes gives the weakness letter, and so does ruling out all three. Either way the kind is solved and Test bills pass it over. A hit on one success only shows it reacted, so that method stays open. Only the solving Test gives the file its point. Which method hits: vampires (and ghouls) fire and holy water; Garou, Ratkin, Gurahl and Mokole silver; the walking dead fire; fomori holy water. Corax, Nuwisha, Ananasi, Kitsune and necromancers take none of the three. - Spent subjects. A subject that has given all its points is passed over, and Examine looks at each subject once. After an Examine a corpse is free to be hauled off. The same filters are in every stockpile, shelf and bill in the game, so a crematorium can burn only plain people and a freezer can keep only the monsters. Supernatural corpses sits under Corpses, beside humanlike corpses, with a row for each kind whose mod is loaded: vampires, ghouls, werewolves, fomori, Fera, hunters, the walking dead, necromancers and mages, and other supernatural corpses for anything else. Procedure Time Roll Gives To the subject Examine 15 minutes Perception + Intellectual at 6 Monster or person, the kind on 2 successes, half a point Nothing Test 30 minutes, uses up one silver, chemfuel or holy water Perception + Intellectual at 7 The kind's weakness on 2 successes, 1 point One wound of the item's damage Dissect 3 rolls, an hour each Stamina + Intellectual at 7, added up Up to 2 points, and proof for a case See below Holy water comes in flasks: three from 20 silver and 10 steel at a smithy, once Smithing is researched, or bought from a trader who stocks the arsenal. The item must be on the map and not forbidden. A failed Examine says nothing. A botch reads a person as a monster or a monster as a person. Dissection total Corpse Living or staked Any roll botches Ruined, no points Wakes if it can; a stake slips 0 to 2 Ruined, 1 point Dies, 1 point 3 to 5 Used up, 1 point Dies, 2 points 6 or more Used up, 2 points Lives, badly wounded and missing a part, 2 points
The table, the horror and the last stand

Before each procedure, a subject may get up: - Staked: never, unless a botch slips the stake. - In torpor with no stake: 10% for Examine, 25% for Test, 50% for each Dissect roll. - A downed Garou: the same, doubled while it mends. - A dead one's corpse: 10% a procedure while a necromancer or revenant is on the map.
The table, the horror and the last stand

The colony keeps one file for each kind of monster, and one subject gives at most 2 points ever. Points What it does 1 The file shows on the Imbued tab 3 Every colonist's blows on that kind do 10% more 6 25% more Two subjects of one clan or tribe add 10% against that clan or tribe. Nothing adds up past 25%, counting Pinpoint. A fomor has its own file. A ghoul gives half a point to the vampire file.
The table, the horror and the last stand

The first study writes a book of hunter's notes beside the table. A hunter or Bystander can right-click it to write a copy, which holds what was known that day. The bonuses use the most complete copy on a home map. Lose every copy and the files go to zero, and subjects you've used stay used, so keep a copy somewhere safe.
The table, the horror and the last stand

A person gives no points. Examining one costs nothing. - A corpse: only the one cutting minds, at -10 mood for 30 days. A hunter doesn't mind unless their beliefs forbid it. Psychopaths don't mind. - Someone alive: they die, the one cutting takes -25 mood for 60 days, the colony reacts as to an organ harvest, and a hunter loses 2 Conviction. Their faction never learns of it. A dissection is also proof: a monster's case gains the successes and its kind, and an innocent's closes. Any finding counts as a Visionary's deed. A Redeemer who dissects a living monster pays as for an execution.
The table, the horror and the last stand

A cork board of clippings two cells wide, built from 20 wood (Misc). Each solved case adds one, and hovering over it lists them: when, who and where. Colonists who see it feel better the more cases it holds: +1 mood at 1 solved case, +2 at 3, +3 at 6, +4 at 11. The board also takes the other cells' notes: see the Hunters' Board.
The table, the horror and the last stand

Two solved cases in five leave something of the culprit's, named for it: a tooth, a ring, a claw, a locket, a key or a hat. It says who it was taken from and where, and it's nice to look at (beauty 12).
The table, the horror and the last stand

Now and then a reward or a ruin turns up something odd: a yellowed knucklebone, a knotted rope, a water-stained notebook. Right-click it and pick Study the odd relic to carry it to a case board or a research bench and work out what it is. A hunter who sees it with second sight knows it at a look. - The saint's knucklebone, carried, ends a frenzy, a fear or a madness that no mood caused, once a day. - The hangman's rope is thrown over a monster and holds it like a net. It holds two, then needs a week to get its grip back. - The dead hunter's notebook gives one clue on an open case, then it's used up.
The table, the horror and the last stand

The hostile monster behind a hunter's Imbuing gets a name, and the game remembers it. All three hunters in A fresh cell share one. A monster from inside the colony, or one that wasn't hostile, leaves no horror. Below half health it runs for the edge of the map, though you can still kill it if you trap it or burst it down. It comes back once a season, after dark, leading a raid with more followers each time. A part cut off it lands as its own item, named for it, at any gore setting, and doesn't rot. Study it on the table and the colony's blows on this monster do 10% more, up to the same 25%. Kill it, and every hunter it made fills up to their Creed's starting Conviction and gains a point of Virtue.
The table, the horror and the last stand

Build a bait stake and bind a live animal or a corpse to it: right-click the body and pick Bind to the bait stake. The next group of monsters on the map goes for the bait first. It takes the body when it gets there, and then attacks as usual. If it gets hurt on the way, it forgets the bait. A live animal is walked over on a rope. To untie the body, select the stake and press Release. Ordinary raids ignore the stake, and it doesn't bring a raid sooner. A few nights after the binding, the stake also calls one monster of its own, at night: a shambler, or with Kindred or Garou loaded a young vampire (generation 10 to 13, or a shovelhead) or a fomor. With Garou, one in ten is a Black Spiral Dancer, which is far more dangerous. It waits a way off while anyone of the colony, or a turret, within 12 cells can see the stake, so hide behind a wall or further back. When nobody is watching it creeps up, feeds for 2 to 4 hours and leaves. Attacked, it fights back; at half health, or when the day comes, it runs. One body draws one lone monster. The Imbued settings can turn this off.
The table, the horror and the last stand

A hunter a monster downs, with 3 or more Conviction, burns all of it by themselves, once in a fight. Creed The last stand Avenger Gets up and fights on for half an hour Defender Monsters nearby can attack only them for a while Judge Every monster in sight is exposed and marked, and takes 25% more damage for the rest of the fight Innocent Monsters nearby stop and stare Martyr Heals everyone nearby Redeemer The nearest monster runs or stops fighting Visionary Shows that monster's lair on the world map If a monster kills a hunter, one Bystander who saw it has an even chance of being imbued, whatever the limits on new hunters say.
The table, the horror and the last stand

Tame animals can learn more than guard and attack. The extra roles show on the vanilla Training tab, are taught by a handler over several lessons, and fade the same way when nobody keeps them up. Each needs guard (obedience) first. Role Who can learn it What it does Guard post body size 0.4 or more Holds a spot you pick with its Guard post button (or right-click, Guard this spot), and goes for any enemy within 8 cells of it Watch any Raises the alarm when it sees an enemy, day or night, and wakes everyone asleep. Once an hour Sniff out an animal with a nose Barks at anyone within 12 cells who hides what they are. A pawn hidden by a power shows for an hour; a guest or prisoner in disguise is known for good Track after sniff out Follows a trail you pick with its Track button: a fled prisoner, quarry marked for hunting, an enemy unseen. It stays close and sniffs them out Scouting a bird that really flies Circles a spot, shadows someone, or flies out over the land and comes back with what it saw Messenger a flier, or body size 0.3 or more Tends one of your town contacts, or asks an allied town for a trade caravan on the comms console's terms (15 goodwill, once every four days) Hunt a predator Once a day brings back one or two small animals from round here, about half of them still alive Fight beside after attack Defends its master without an order, and fights better at their side for an hour Spirit scout a familiar only Looks across to the spirit side for three hours, once a day, and comes back with what waits there Selected, a trained animal shows a line to its guard post or to the one it's tracking. The kennel (Misc tab) takes up to six of your animals: they learn half as fast again and forget at half the rate. Name a kennel master on it, and that colonist trains the kennel's animals before any other handling work. At a case's town, a dog trained to sniff out turns up one more clue, once a case. A tracker can follow the case's suspects too. Members of your sworn cell sell trained dogs. Ask for a trained animal is on each member's row, paid with the favours that member owes you: a trivial favour counts 1, a minor 2, a major 3 and a life debt 4. An animal costs 1, plus 1 a role, plus 1 for every 500 silver it's worth, and comes by drop pod.
The table, the horror and the last stand

About once a season a letter marks a spot on your own map, with a line like "Be at the old well before dusk." The first hunter to go earns a point of Conviction and finds a survivor, a clue or an ambush. Ignore it and it fades, with no other cost.
The table, the horror and the last stand

A Redeemer can right-click a downed monster and pick Spare. They help it up and it leaves unharmed. It isn't hostile while it goes, it may come back, and the Redeemer earns the deed. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Select a hunter and open Imbued. At the top are the Creed and primary Virtue, then Conviction and Willpower as bars. The pages are down the left side. A gold number beside a page counts what you can do there now: a Virtue to raise, Virtue points for an Edge, or Ambitions to pick from. Click a heading's name to fold the section under it; the page remembers that until you quit the game. Page What it shows Sheet The Creed, its deeds and its betrayals (hover for more); Mercy, Vision and Zeal as dots, the primary marked, with Virtue points not yet spent on an Edge ringed in gold; Willpower Attributes The nine Attributes in three columns, Physical, Social and Mental. Hover the next dot for its cost in experience (the header shows how much there is) and click it to buy Edges Every Edge the hunter has, and Learn an Edge... when points are waiting Growth The hunter's Ambition. Your own hunters only The hunt The seat the hunter holds at the cell the colony is sworn to, every monster this hunter knows for what it is, and the colony's open files Backgrounds The Backgrounds every kind shares, then Awareness and Destiny Conduct The habits: risking Conviction, autocast, Willpower and the fighting style. Click a habit to change it. Your own hunters only At the foot: Roll log, the colony's last rolls and how each came out, and Cases, which opens the Hunters tab on its cases.

A button on the bottom bar once the colony has a hunter. While the colony has two or more kinds from the Rim by Night mods, only the window used last keeps its button, and a list down the left side of each window names every one with its pages, so a click opens any page of any of them; the Core setting One bottom-bar button turns that off. Its six pages: Page What it shows Overview The Hunter-Net's goodwill toward the colony, the nearest or sworn cell, the help cells owe you, then the hunt: how many cases are open, a captive you hold for a cell, and how long the dead stay quiet Cells Each cell the colony knows, nearest first, with who leads it. Hover a row for how far away it is and how many hunt there. Open opens the cell's window; a click on the rest of the row finds it on the world map Cases The case window Hunters' Board The notes and clippings on the colony's Hunters' Board, once one is built. The board's own button opens this page The world's news and the colony's own story are on the Chronicle and Our story pages under Rim by Night, at the top of the list down the window's left side. Each page holds the lines of every mod you have loaded; click a mod on its left for only that mod's lines, or a name under it for one colonist or home. Hunters write who was imbued, last stands, monsters put down and dissections there, and the cells' news tells of battles won and lost, new hunters called, hunters gone missing and monsters put down.

One tile on the gizmo bar for each path the hunter has an Edge on. Click it for the path's Edges, pick one, then pick the target. An Edge that can't be used now is greyed, with the reason. Hover an Edge to see its roll: the Attribute and Virtue with their dice, the total and the difficulty, or the rule for it before a target is picked ("the target's Stamina + 2"). Conviction risked shows up only in the roll itself. The roll log puts each roll's parts in a grey line under it, and an Edge's grimoire page has the formula in a box at the top.
While a hunter's second sight is up, every monster in sight has a mark over it. With Discern, Witness or Illuminate the mark names what kind it is.

A drafted colonist has an Unleash button beside Fire at will. It goes after the nearest enemy anywhere on the map and fights as an enemy of its kind would, Edges first. Anyone with a gun backs away from melee fighters and looks for cover. A pawn scared by a power stays on the map and goes back to the fight when the panic ends. Your orders come first, and once one is done it goes back to the hunt. Undrafting ends it. While it's on, a Pick target button chooses the enemy it goes after. Once that enemy is down or gone it picks the nearest one again, and clicking the button clears the target early. An Edge aimed out of range or out of sight walks the hunter closer, then fires.

Most menus open a list beside the window you clicked in, or above the gizmo. A long list has filters down the left with a count beside each, and Can pick only hides what can't be had yet. Click a row to read about it on the right, then press Choose, double-click it, or press Enter. A greyed row says under it what's missing. A list with nothing to read takes the row on one click.

A monster among your visitors or colonists leaves marks. Hunters read them, work out who it is, and then go and find where it sleeps.

A monster that isn't the colony's open enemy leaves clues on a home map, or in a town the colony has a case in. Each one fades in 15 days. A monster the colony's hunters already know leaves none, and neither does a kill in a fight against the colony's enemies. Clue Where it's left Read well, it gives Fang marks A body a vampire drank dry (Kindred) Who was near, and the kind Claw marks A body a Garou killed (Garou) Who was near, and the kind Disturbed ground Where a dead one got up on a map a revenant haunts Who was near, and the kind A fomor's taint Where a fomor used a power (Garou) Who was near, and the kind Witness's account Where an outsider saw a monster break the Masquerade or the Veil (Kindred or Garou) Who was near Tracks that stop Where a power carried a monster more than 6 cells at once, or off the map A description Strange blood Where a monster was hurt, one every four hours A description Tracks Round a prowling visitor's target's bed, on its first night Who was near, as two sources Torn carcass Where a prowling visitor killed an animal, on its second night Who was near as two sources, and the kind Hidden things In a culprit's belongings, when a hunter searches them (the hunter walks to the person's bed, or to them if they have none) The culprit as two sources, and the kind A clue remembers the monster that left it and up to five others within 15 cells.

Examining a clue is research work, for hunters and Bystanders only; to anyone else it's a stain. It takes ten seconds and rolls Perception + Intellectual at 6, and the clue is used up. Nothing is added up for you: the reading goes in the case window and you piece it together. - Who was near. The reading lists everyone who was close, in no order. Each success rules out one innocent, but it always leaves at least one beside the one who did it. - A description. Strange blood and tracks that stop name nobody. Each success gives a piece of what whoever left it looks like: a man or a woman, young, middle-aged or old, thin, heavy, big or ordinary, the colour of their hair, what they wear and its colour, a scar or a missing part, the weapon they carry. Each piece goes on the case, and a suspect's file ticks or crosses it against how they look now. - The kind. A kind's own mark read well shows what did it, and so does a hunter with Discern or Witness up. - A botch looks like any poor reading, but it rules out the one who did it. Some Edges add more: Witness shows past meetings of monsters in sight, Pierce's touch tells a suspect's word true or false, and Delve reads every clue within 8 cells at once. Pierce and the autopsy table count as two sources against a monster and show its kind.

A revenant or a hidden one doesn't come alone. It arrives with two or three ordinary visitors of the same faction, and they all stay a few days. On its first night it leaves tracks round its target's bed. On its second it kills a farm animal, or a colonist's pet if there's no livestock, and leaves the carcass. On its third it attacks its target. A body that gets up on those nights leaves disturbed ground too. Read the clues and name it before the third night, and it fights or runs. Otherwise the fight is at the target's bedside. Name it on too little and nobody believes it: it strikes the next night.

While the colony has a hunter, word comes now and then of an attack in an ordinary town within 12 tiles (or 12 tiles past the nearest one, if none is that close): a letter and a quest that name the town and say what was found, never what did it. Each case has ten days. No new rumour comes while a case is taken, and each one still waiting makes the next half as likely. Rumours are in the Hunters group on the settings page, with their own on/off and frequency. About one rumour in four comes from a monster that got away from an earlier case, and the case window says so. Send a caravan and walk in as guests. Three or four clues lie about the town. After the first, about one in four is a red herring: blood from a bar fight, a dog's tracks, a drunk's story. Two successes see it for nothing; a worse reading takes it at its word. Leave and come back, and the unread ones are still there. Every town the colony visits keeps its people, case or not: whoever you met there is there again next time, unless they died or left. Right-click a townsperson to work on them: Action Roll What it gives Talk to See Talking What they know, as long as their patience lasts Go through their things Dexterity + Intellectual at 7, once a person The culprit's hold hidden things to examine. An innocent's are clean. A botch is seen, and the town shuts the case for three days Watch them through the night None. Start between 18:00 and 2:00, it lasts until 6:00 The culprit is caught in the act and named. Anyone else slept. Broken off, it tells nothing

Talk to (on the right-click menu, or in a suspect's file) sends the hunter over. If the person won't talk, they say why. If they will, the two stand facing each other, and their file opens with the talk window beside it. Close the talk window to let them go. Pick what to ask about, then how to put it: Topic What it gives The attack Someone who saw it names the culprit (two sources) and what it is. Someone who heard of it gives pieces of a description. A botch, or the culprit itself, names someone innocent Where were you last night An alibi: a place, and usually someone in town who can say so. The culprit always lies about it, and about one innocent in four lies too (an affair, a theft, a debt), the same ones every time Someone Pick a person. If they're the one an alibi named, they confirm it or break it, and a broken alibi counts as a source. Otherwise they say they know them or don't, and now and then that they saw them out that night A clue Pick a clue you've read. The culprit, on a success, slips: it shows what it is, or places itself once more, and it always learns the hunters are onto it. An innocent the clue listed, or whose alibi broke, explains it away and is ruled out, for 3 of the town's goodwill Tone Roll Risk Kindly Charisma + Social at 6 None Firmly Manipulation + Social at 6 None Threaten Strength + Social at 7 Costs two patience. A failure makes the whole town warier (+1 to every roll, up to +2). A botch shuts them for good Bribe None, 40 silver from the hunters' pockets Always talks, but lies three times in ten Each person has 2 to 4 patience a day, always the same for the same person. A question costs one, a threat two. When it runs out they say so and walk off; ask again tomorrow. What they said stays in the talk window under Said so far, and in the case's answers.

Visitors and traders passing through a case's town can be suspects, and about one case in seven the culprit is one of them. Travellers leave 1 to 3 days after the colony arrives, or at once when the culprit among them is warned. A suspect's file shows when they're due to go. Track one who left (Perception + Animals at 6, from where they walked off) to find the town they went to. If it was the culprit, the case moves there. The culprit isn't always local: - About four times in ten it lives in the town. - About one time in seven it's a traveller passing through (see above). - About one time in four it lives in another town 2 to 8 tiles on. Three sources against it name that town, and the case moves there with one or two more clues. - The rest of the time it has a lair. Three sources against it open a lead to it, and it waits there. The culprit learns the hunters are onto it when it's questioned itself, when three sources place it, or when it's named and not believed. Half a day later, while the colony is there, it kills someone who answered the hunters and leaves its mark on the body, or it goes to its lair and leaves a lead. Name What happens Right, believed As at home, and the case is solved (see Solving a case). The body can go home for the autopsy table Right, not believed Nothing, and the culprit knows now. It can't be named again until a new source places it Wrong As at home, and the town wants the hunters gone: for three days nobody there can read a clue, ask a question or name anyone, and the deadline keeps running Killed without naming The usual penalties for attacking your hosts It runs off the map A lead to its lair Killing the culprit at its lair solves the case too.

Reward How much Silver 200, plus 100 for each red herring, 200 if the case moved to a third town and 300 for a lair. Half as much again if solved within half the deadline Goodwill The town's faction: 10, plus 5 a point of the same, up to 30 Hunter-Net standing 10 to 25, by the same points (see Standing) Conviction A point to every hunter there Skill 800 Intellectual and 800 Social to every colonist who worked the case: read its clues, talked to its people, searched or watched them, or named it A keepsake Two cases in five: something of the culprit's (a tooth, a ring, a claw, a locket, a key, a hat), worth looking at A clipping Pinned up on a Hunters' Board, if the colony has one Miss the deadline and a second rumour comes from the same town, with more dead and ten more days. Miss that one too and the trail goes cold. A few days later the monster turns up at the colony among visitors, prowling.

The Cases page of the Hunters tab (also the Cases link at the foot of the Imbued tab) is the case window. Open cases are on the left with their days left, then Others: everyone with evidence who isn't in a case, and every monster a colony hunter knows that isn't an enemy. Solved and cold cases sit below. The right side shows the chosen case: where it is, how long is left, what did it once something showed the kind, and how many clues are read, then three tabs: - Suspects: everyone the case has turned up, in three groups one under the other: still in it, ruled out by a reading, and crossed off by you. Hover a name for how they look and what placed them; click it for their file: their portrait, age and where they live (or who they travel with, and when they leave), then Looks (how they look now beside each thing said of the culprit, with a tick or a cross), Alibi (where they say they were, and whether it held) and Evidence (what placed them, what ruled them out, how many sources, whether they were searched or have left). Actions (on the row and in the file) are talk, track, name, and cross off or put back; crossing off is only for your notes. A greyed name says why underneath. Track finds them: on a map, at a lair a lead names, or in their town. Someone who walks off a map while a suspect leaves footsteps for two days. The tab's hunter, standing where they left, gets one try to follow them (Perception + Animals at 6): a monster's lead to its lair, anyone else's to the nearest town of their own. - Clues: a card a clue, two across, with who read it and how well, the people near it as tags (struck through where ruled out) or the description it gave. A tag in the corner says what it showed. Unread ones have a link to where they lie. - Answers: a transcript: who said it and which hunter asked, searched or watched them, then what they said or what the hunter found. At 60 Hunter-Net standing a live town case has a Call a cell link: two of a cell's hunters come to the case's town or lair and fight beside the colony's people there, once every ten days. Clues read at home go in a home case, which goes cold 15 days after its last clue.

The tab's hunter can name a suspect on the same map once something showed what kind of creature did it and two sources place them there, or when a colony hunter already knows them. Being nameable doesn't make someone guilty. A right name is believed about two times in five with two sources, seven in ten with three, and always with four or more, or when a hunter knows the monster. Caught in a stakeout, it's always believed. - Right: everyone who can see the monster sees it for what it is, every colony hunter knows it, and a visitor fights as any enemy of ours does or runs. A Judge gains a point for it. - Wrong: the innocent thinks much less of the hunter for 30 days, their faction loses 10 goodwill, every colonist is uneasy for three days, and a Judge loses a point. Showing a monster for what it is, by naming it or with Expose, depends on who it lives among: Where What its people do A settlement of its own kind (a Kindred court, a sept, a Pentex front) The settlement turns hostile at once An ordinary town It's nobody's to defend, so killing it costs nothing. Half the time the other monsters hiding there turn on the hunters Visiting the colony, from a faction of its own kind That faction loses 25 goodwill Visiting the colony, from an ordinary faction It's nobody's to defend Witnesses who saw a monster that isn't the colony's don't count against the Masquerade or the Veil.

A lead opens a lair on the world map 2 to 8 tiles away, as a quest in the Quests tab that ends when the lair is cleared: - A monster named while visiting gives its lead when it leaves the map. - A town case whose culprit has a lair gives it once there's enough evidence. - A witness who got away with what a visiting monster did tells the other cells, and that monster gives its lead when it leaves. A colonist's breach never does. - A monster a colony hunter is trailing gives it as it goes. - Pinpoint at three successes gives the lair of the monster's kind. - A mentor can bring one. Lair Whose Haven A vampire's (Kindred) Den A Black Spiral Dancer's, with the Wyrm (Garou) Pentex subsidiary A fomor's (Garou) Grave The hidden and shamblers Necromancer's house The necromancer and the dead Revenant's old home A revenant Send a caravan. The named or trailed monster waits there if it's still alive. Once no enemy is left standing, every colony hunter there gains a point of Conviction, and an afflicted lair keeps shambler raids and revenant visits away for a season. Each lair also holds a hunter weapon near the middle. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Vampire and Garou colonists are allowed beside hunters. A hunter who comes to know a colonist is a monster knows it for good, and how they live with it depends on the Creed. There's no mood penalty, and it doesn't fade.
How a hunter comes to know

- Second sight marks the colonist while it's up for another reason. - The hunter sees the colonist feed, take a shape no person has, or use a power. - Discern, Witness or a named suspect shows it. The Imbued tab lists every monster a hunter knows.

Creed Toward a known monster colonist Avenger Denounces it and fights it more often. Rarely, a righteous fury: they go for the monster with whatever is at hand, three times as likely for a day after seeing a monster feed or hurt someone Defender Squares up to it if it hurts one of the colony in sight Judge Argues about it, and weighs it in talks with other colonists, who come away thinking better or worse of it Innocent Talks to it without fear Martyr Denounces it, and squares up to it if it feeds on anyone in sight Redeemer Reminds it of what it was. A vampire may win back a dot of Humanity, a Garou loses a point of Rage. It can start a fight Visionary Asks it questions

- Vampires are monsters to second sight, masked or not. Elders of generation 8 or lower are hard to see; generation 5 and older are harder. - Expose breaks the Masquerade for everyone who sees it. - Fang marks on a drained body are clues.

- Garou are monsters in every form, Homid too. Rank 4 and 5 are hard to see. - Expose breaches the Veil. Becalm can end a frenzy. - Suspend seals the map: no stepping sideways, no spirits called up, no shadow crossings, for an hour. - Claw marks and a fomor's taint are clues, and a fomor's lead is a Pentex subsidiary. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Imbued The Rim by Night: Imbued brings Hunter: The Reckoning (1999) to RimWorld. A colonist who watches a monster hurt someone can be imbued: the voices called the Messengers wake them up, and from then on they see monsters for what they are. They get a Creed, the three Virtues of Mercy, Vision and Zeal, Conviction, and Edges to fight with. The afflicted are the mod's own monsters, so it plays on its own. With The Rim by Night: Kindred or Garou loaded, hunters go after vampires and werewolves too. > In development. Balance will change and bugs are likely. Keep a backup of any save you add > the mod to.

Second sight won't open for them, they can't use Edges that cost it, and to every monster they're ordinary people. It comes back after the next threat ends, and every deed of their Creed adds a point. Clue to examine A monster left marks here. Hunters and Bystanders examine clues as research work; each reading adds evidence to the suspect list. Clues fade in 15 days. Open a hunter's Imbued tab and press Cases. The dead may rise This map is haunted, and its dead are lying in the open. Any of them may get up at night as a shambler. Bury or burn them. Every health condition, state and effect a pawn can carry, as shown on its Health tab. Condition Bad What it does Attributes Strength, toughness and the rest, each dot above a living person's average worth a little. Attributes Strength, wits and the rest, raised by hard experience past what this person started with. Becalmed Yes Everything feels less urgent. Striking out or hurrying takes an effort. Blustering Ready to shout a blow aside, on herself or anyone she can see. Bound Yes Tied hand and foot and left out as bait. Carried to a bed, the ropes can be cut. Branded Yes A hunter's burning mark, plain to every imbued eye, and no disguise hides it. Burdened Yes Held to the spot by a hunter's stare. It can still fight, but it can barely move. Burning Something like lava runs under her skin. Whoever she strikes by hand, or who strikes her, is burned. Bystander Saw a monster for what it was and can't forget it. Knows the monsters are real, though nothing protects them from them, and will stand by the people who hunt them. Called out Yes A hunter has called it out, and it has eyes for no one else. Carrying a vision Has seen what's coming here. When it's close, she'll know what it is. Cleaving Her melee blows do extra lethal damage. A real weapon wears under the strain. Confronted Yes A hunter holds its gaze. Going for her takes more will than it may have. Demanding Paid in pain for strength: her Mercy is added to her Strength for the next blow or feat. Discerning Sees what kind of monster each one in sight is, and sees clearly in the dark or blind. Foreseeing Has seen how the next moments could go. Each second look left makes her next Edge roll, shot or blow likelier to come off. Hidden Dead, though nobody would know it. It keeps its skills and its face, and kills for one purpose. The hardest of the afflicted to find and to stop. Hiding Monsters looking for someone to attack pass this hunter by, until one of them sees through it or she attacks. Illuminating Blazing with a light only the imbued and monsters can see. Every hunter on the map knows the monsters for what they are, and the monsters go for her. Imbued Woken by something no one can name. This person sees the monsters hiding among people for what they are, and has been given the means to do something about it. Insinuated Yes A hunter's question has dragged up something it lost. Its blows, shots and work are worse for four hours. Lent self Part of a hunter's self has been lent, or borrowed, for a while. Marked Yes A dying Judge showed everyone what this is and where to hit it. Every blow lands harder for the rest of the fight. Necromancer A living sorcerer who calls the dead out of the ground and holds them. Wherever one walks the dead get up, and when the necromancer dies they fall. Paid back Yes A hunter has cut it down to size: as frail as a person, or without one of its powers, while she's near. Radiant Wrapped in a white light that turns monsters' attacks aside, a tenth of them for each success. Rejuvenating Her body knits itself back together: bruises close in minutes and cuts in hours. Revenant Dead, and back for one person. It passes for living at a distance and mends its wounds by will alone. Once the one it came for is dead, or it is, it goes back to the grave. Shambler A corpse that got up. Slow, strong and hard to stop: it feels nothing and doesn't bleed, and only taking the head or destroying the body puts it down. Strapped down Yes Held to the autopsy table by the straps. Whoever lies here isn't crawling away. Surging Her Zeal runs through her body: stronger, quicker and tougher for four hours. Trailed A hunter has touched it and can follow its trail wherever it goes. Warding Monsters can't come within as many cells of her as she has Zeal, unless their will is stronger than hers. Winded Yes Gave away her own breath to heal someone. Slow and clumsy for the hour. Witnessing Sees what kind of monster each one in sight is. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Every event the storyteller can send, what it means and what to do about it. Most can be switched off or made rarer one by one in the mod settings. A cell asks for silver nitrate Event 20 A cell asks for flasks of silver nitrate from your storage. Pays goodwill and xp. A cell asks for stakes Event 15 A cell asks for stakes from your storage. Pays goodwill and xp. A cell asks to read the case files Event 15 A Hunter-Net cell asks to read your case files. Pays Hunter-Net goodwill and xp. A cell's captive to hold Event 30 A cell asks you to hold a captured monster for it for a while. Pays goodwill and xp. A hunter asks for a lesson Event 15 A hunter of a cell asks one of yours for a lesson in what they know of a monster kind. Pays Hunter-Net goodwill and xp. A hunter chased by a monster Event 20 A hunter of a cell runs for the colony with a monster behind them and asks to be let in. Saved, the cell owes you help, called in from the Hunter-Net page. Whatever tied them may come back. A hunter wanted by a cover-up Event 25 A hunter wanted by a cover-up asks you to hide them for a while. Kept safe, the cell owes you help. A hurt hunter asks for a doctor Event 20 A hurt hunter of a cell asks your doctor to patch them up. Pays goodwill and xp. A meeting to host: Creed summit Event 30 days A cell writes to offer you a Creed summit to host. At most once a year. A meeting to host: great hunt Event 30 days A cell writes to offer you a great hunt to host. At most once a year. A meeting to host: regional meet Event 30 days A cell writes to offer you a regional meet to host, once that meeting opens. At most once a year. A new imbued to foster Event 30 A cell asks you to take in a newly imbued hunter and teach them. Pays goodwill and xp. Cell under attack Event 10 20 days A Hunter-Net cell a caravan's reach away is holding out against the walking dead and calls for help, as a quest. Taken, the cell holds three days for you to arrive. First horror returns Event Once a season, the monster that made your hunters what they are comes back with more followers each time. Below half health it runs again unless you finish it. A monster let go on its word may come back the same way. Hunted stranger Event For a colony with no hunters: someone who was just imbued runs onto your land at night, the monster that woke them on their trail. Take them in and they join as a hunter, and the monster comes for them a few hours later as their first horror. This is the usual way a colony meets the hunters. Hunted stranger's pursuer Event The monster that followed the hunted stranger arrives, alone, after dark. It came for the one who got away and won't leave without them. Only sent by the hunted stranger's letter. Hunter-Net caravan Visitors Hunter-Net's own caravan, selling the arsenal and what works on monsters. Only once your standing with the net is 40 or more. Mentor's visit Event 5 15 days A veteran hunter visits a colony hunter with the Mentor Background, more often for more dots. They bring either a monster kind's weakness (your hunters hit it a quarter harder) or the lair of a monster you know. Messengers' errand Event 15 days About once a season the Messengers speak through every screen: a spot is marked on the home map. Send any hunter there before dusk, or let it fade. Most wanted Big threat 20 days One of the Most Wanted passes near the colony. A monster that has never crossed you walks through unless you harm it; one that has, or the walking dead, comes for the colony. Revenant visit Event 15 20 days A revenant or one of the hidden walks in among ordinary visitors of a friendly faction, back for one colonist. It prowls two nights and strikes on the third. The letter reads like any visitor's. Shambler raid Big threat 8 The dead dig out of the ground at the map's edge at night and come for the living. More often where no vampire or Garou draws other enemies. One raid in six has a necromancer walking behind it: kill them and the dead fall. The Avengers ask for a monster put down Event 20 The Avengers ask one of their Creed in the colony to put a monster down. Pays more the stronger that hunter's Edges. The Defenders ask for a place guarded Event 20 The Defenders ask one of their Creed in the colony to guard a place. Pays more the stronger that hunter's Edges. The Innocents ask for a monster spared Event 20 The Innocents ask one of their Creed in the colony to spare a monster. Pays more the stronger that hunter's Edges. The Judges ask for a ruling Event 20 The Judges ask one of their Creed in the colony for a ruling. Pays more the stronger that hunter's Edges. The Martyrs ask for a risk taken Event 20 The Martyrs ask one of their Creed in the colony to take a risk for others. Pays more the stronger that hunter's Edges. The Redeemers ask for a monster talked round Event 20 The Redeemers ask one of their Creed in the colony to talk a monster round. Pays more the stronger that hunter's Edges. The Visionaries ask what the Messengers want Event 20 The Visionaries ask one of their Creed in the colony to work out what the Messengers want. Pays more the stronger that hunter's Edges. A post with a rope and a hook. Bind a live animal or a corpse to it, and the next group of monsters on the map goes for the body before anything else. Ordinary raiders ignore it, and it doesn't call anything or bring a threat sooner.
Wounds no animal of this size could leave, on someone torn apart. A hunter or a Bystander can examine them for who did it.
2000 Everything a cell learned before it went quiet: cases, the things behind them, what worked and what got people killed. An imbued who reads it through hunts better for it.
150 The notebook of a hunter who didn't come back. Read through, it gives one clue on an open case: what kind of thing did it, or one person it wasn't. Then the rest is just the hunter's last days.
Where a body lay, the ground is clawed and churned, as if it got up and walked away. Something brought it back. A hunter or a Bystander can examine it.
Two small punctures on the throat of someone drained to death. A hunter or a Bystander can examine them for who did it.
400 Rope from a gallows that hanged a guilty man. Thrown over a monster, it holds it like a net. It holds two, then needs a week to get its grip back.
What someone keeps hidden among their things: a bottle of blood, coarse grey hair, a black ooze, grave dirt. A hunter or a Bystander can examine it.

10 Pages of what the table has shown: what each kind of monster is, what hurts it and how to hit it. The colony's blows follow the most complete copy on a home map. Keep a copy somewhere safe, because if every copy burns the colony forgets it all.

A cork board where the hunters pin what they need to see: newspaper clippings with string between them, one for every monster tracked down in a town and put down, and the notes other cells leave. Seeing it lifts the mood of everyone in the colony, more with each case solved. Look at it to read what's pinned there.
60 Something taken from a monster the hunters put down, kept to remember the case by.

60 A short length of hemp rope, frayed at one end and tied in a hangman's knot at the other. Study it at a case board or a research bench to find out what it is, or let a hunter with second sight look at it.
The Messengers want a hunter here before dusk. Nobody can say what for. Ignore it and it fades.
1 A piece cut from the monster that made a hunter. It doesn't rot, which is the worst thing about it. Study it on the autopsy table and the colony hits that monster harder.
500 A bone from a holy man's hand. Carried, it breaks a monster's hold on its bearer's mind once a day: a frenzy, a fear or a madness that no mood caused ends on the spot.
Blood from a wound, too dark or too thick to be a person's. A hunter or a Bystander can examine it.
A greasy black residue that smells of rot and chemicals, left where something used a power. A hunter or a Bystander can examine it.
An animal killed in the night, torn open and left where it fell. Nothing that lives here hunts like that. A hunter or a Bystander can examine it.
Bare footprints, walking slowly round and round someone's bed, where nobody should have been in the night. A hunter or a Bystander can examine them.
Footprints that end in the middle of open ground, as if whoever made them stepped out of the world. A hunter or a Bystander can examine them.
60 A pocket notebook swollen with damp, its pages stuck together. Study it at a case board or a research bench to find out what it is, or let a hunter with second sight look at it.

Someone saw something here they can't explain and couldn't keep quiet about it: a few lines dropped on a scrap of paper, a description that doesn't sound human. A hunter or a Bystander can examine it.
60 A finger bone, smooth from handling, wrapped in a strip of old cloth. Study it at a case board or a research bench to find out what it is, or let a hunter with second sight look at it.

Every mission a court, sept, cell or consilium can give, and every quest these mods offer. Mission What it asks Where the dead lie down Travel to where the walking dead go to ground and put down every one of them. The sleeper's house The cell at *asker* followed one of the undead home to *site*. It sleeps there through the day behind blacked-out windows, and the people it feeds on guard the door and call it family.- Kill or drive off everyone there The beast's den The cell at *asker* found a shapeshifter's den at *site*: bones in the yard, claw marks on the doorframes, and people inside who serve the same thing it does. The hunter-net posts on these always say the same thing: don't go in without silver.- Kill or drive off everyone there- Bring silver The marked hunter Hide a hunter from the cell at your colony for a while and keep them alive. What marked them will come looking. The stakeout Lend one of your hunters to the cell for some days to watch a house in its town. They come home when the days are up. The dead cell's notes Travel to a dead cell's safe house and put down everything there. The casebook inside is yours to keep. Newly woken Shelter someone newly imbued at your colony for a while and keep them alive. The dead will come for them. The grave that won't stay shut Travel to a grave where something the other cell couldn't finish waits, and put it down. Cleaning up after the hunt Lend one of your hunters to another cell for some days, to clean up after a hunt that went loud. A shared case Lend one of your hunters to another cell for some days, to work a case with them. The dead walk at *site* A cell is calling for help on hunter-net, the posts coming fast and badly spelled. The dead have come out of the ground around *site*, and the cell's hunters can't hold out alone.- Take the call and the cell will hold for three days while your caravan gets there- Put the dead down while some of the hunters still stand+ Silver from the cell, and its gratitude The hunt for *monster* The trail of *monster* leads to *site*. The other cells have passed on everything they have: photographs, a floor plan, a list of the missing. The lair is a caravan's trip away, and whatever lives there is waiting.- Clear it out+ Conviction for every hunter there when the last of them falls+ Whatever the lair holds Whispers from *town* *found*Nobody in *town* is saying what did it. Something in the crate Hold one of the walking dead as your prisoner until the cell comes for it. It must not die, escape or go free before then. Another pair of hands for *asker* Lend one of your hunters to the cell for some days to clear a nest. They come home when the job is done.
