Every other kind of thing this mod defines that has a name and a description: Merits, Backgrounds, gatherings, places, personalities and the rest.

Name What it is Close a case See one of the colony's cases through to the one behind it. Destroy a monster Kill two monsters with your own hands. Find a lair Get a lead to where a monster sleeps. Hold the line Go a whole season without a colonist dying. Learn the truth Learn three things about monsters: from a body, a book, a captive or a case. Mend the hurt Heal two people a monster has hurt. Redeem a monster Talk a captured monster into turning from what it is. Save someone Get someone away from a monster that has hurt them, or stand over them while they're down. Spare a monster Let a beaten monster live, or let one go on its word. Take the blow Stand between a monster and someone who is down. Three monsters Kill three monsters with your own hands. Unmask them Show two monsters for what they are, to yourself or to everyone.

Name What it is Arsenal The cell's armoury. Each season it sends a crate of hunter weapons worth 150 silver for each dot. Each dot also gives 3% better prices when trading with hunter-net. A starting hunter packs one hunter weapon for each dot.

Name What it is Avenger The monsters have to be destroyed, every one of them, and the Avenger means to do it. Of all the hunters they are the readiest to fight and the least willing to stop. Defender Someone has to stand between the monsters and the people they prey on. The Defender guards a home, a family or a whole colony, and fights to keep it safe. Innocent The Innocent sees the monsters as they are and isn't afraid of them. They ask questions where others would shoot, and trust that understanding can do more than a weapon. Judge Not every monster is the same, and not every one deserves the same end. The Judge weighs what a creature has done before deciding what to do about it, then acts without flinching. Martyr Whatever it costs, the Martyr pays it so that no one else has to. They take the blow meant for someone else and count their own pain as the price of saving others. Redeemer Something human may still be left inside a monster. The Redeemer looks for it, and tries to bring it back before deciding the creature is beyond saving. Visionary Why were they chosen, and what for? The Visionary wants to know what the monsters are, what the Imbuing means and where it all leads, and looks for the answers before anything else.

Name What it is Augur The hunter sees what's coming to this place, though the future doesn't always tell the truth. Balance The hunter weighs a monster and finds it wanting. For a time, whatever powers it has won't answer. Becalm A calm spreads out from the hunter. Fists slow, triggers wait, and rages burn out. Blaze The nearest light flares into something no monster can stand, and burns every one of them in reach. Bluster One shouted word, "No!" or "Stop!", and the blow goes wide. Brand The hunter's touch burns a mark into a monster that every hunter can see and no disguise hides. Burden Under the hunter's stare a monster grows too heavy to move. Burn Something like molten rock runs under the hunter's skin. Touching her burns, and so does her touch. Champion The hunter calls the monsters out, and they forget everyone but her. Cleave The hunter's weapon, or a blade of nothing in her empty hand, cuts like it was made for the monsters. Confront The hunter meets a monster's eyes and stands there, and hurting her becomes the hardest thing it has ever tried to do. Delve The hunter reads the recent past of the ground she stands on, and sees who walked there. Demand The hunter hurts herself to do what she couldn't, and the pain becomes strength. Discern The hunter sees what a monster is: the dead that don't breathe, the beast under the skin, the blood-drinker's pallor. Donate The hunter lends part of herself to someone else: her strength, her quickness, her wits, for as long as she can spare them. Expose For a moment everyone around the hunter sees the monsters as she does. Foresee A flash of how the next few moments could go, and the chance to choose the better one. Hide Monsters look straight past the hunter, as if she weren't worth the trouble, until she makes them notice her. Illuminate The hunter blazes with a light only the imbued and the monsters can see. Every hunter near her knows the monsters for what they are, and every monster wants the light put out. Insinuate One quiet question that reminds a monster of what it used to be. It falters, and sometimes it runs. Payback The hunter holds a monster's gaze and makes it pay: it's as frail as a person, or one of its powers is gone, for as long as she stays near. Pierce The hunter knows a lie when she hears one, and with a touch she sees someone's last brush with a monster, or a monster's past. Pinpoint The hunter looks at a monster and knows where it's weak. Radiate A white light wraps the hunter and those close to her, and the monsters' blows slide off it. Ravage The air shimmers with heat round one monster and it burns from the inside. The hunter pays for it in her own body. Rejuvenate The hunter's body knits itself back together far faster than it should, and her hands can close another's wounds. Respire The hunter breathes life into someone hurt, or draws it out of a monster. Restore The hunter pictures a body whole and it becomes so: deep wounds turn to bruises, and what was lost grows back. Smite Something that isn't quite lightning and isn't quite fire leaps from the hunter, with a crash and a stink of ammonia. Smolder Thick black smoke pours off the hunter, and anything shooting at her shoots blind. Surge The hunter's fury runs into her body: stronger, faster, harder to put down. Suspend The hunter shuts this place off from every other world. Whatever is here stays here and answers for itself. Trail One touch and the hunter can follow a monster anywhere: she sees the track it leaves, and no one else does. Ward A crackling edge round the hunter that monsters can't push through unless their will is stronger than hers. Witness The hunter sees the monsters for what they are, and glimpses the harm they've done.

Name What it is Creed summit Hunters of all seven Creeds argue at the colony about what the Messengers want, then vote on the net's next aim. Great hunt Cells from across the region gather at the colony against a known nest, and march out together from it. Regional meet Hunters of the nearby cells meet at the colony to share leads round a table, then plan a hunt together.

Name What it is Merciful Wants the innocent kept out of it, and the monsters given a chance to be something else. Shares its cases. Pays in medicine. Visionary Wants to know why the Messengers chose it. Shares its cases and asks for help with what it finds. Pays in books and notes. Wary Wants to stay alive and unknown. Asks only for help covering its tracks. Pays in silver. Zealous Wants every monster dead, whatever it costs. Hands off the ones it can't reach, and asks for its tracks covered. Pays in weapons.

Name What it is A Bystander This colonist missed the Imbuing by a little. They have no sight and no Edges, but they know monsters exist: they panic a little less, work 10% faster at research and tending, and can examine clues. See [[HTR_Guide_Being_Imbued#bystanders\ Bystanders]]. A clue Examining a clue is research work, for hunters and Bystanders only. It takes ten seconds and the clue is used up. The reading goes in the case window, and you piece it together. See [[HTR_Guide_Investigation_and_Lairs#examining\ Examining]]. A piece of the horror A piece of a first horror can go on the [[HTR_Guide_Hunter_Tools#the-autopsy-table\ autopsy table]]. See [[HTR_Guide_Hunter_Tools#the-first-horror\ The first horror]]. A shambler Slow, strong and hard to stop. It feels no pain and doesn't go down to wounds, and only the head or the whole body ends it. - Fire does half again as much. - Aim for the head. - Shamblers are slow with doors. See [[HTR_Guide_The_Walking_Dead#fighting-them\ Fighting them]]. A Virtue to raise At 10 Conviction this hunter can cash it in for a Virtue point, which leaves them at 3. Open the Imbued tab and press Choose a Virtue. Waiting keeps the Conviction. At 7 in any Virtue, and at each point after, the hunter gains a derangement. See [[HTR_Guide_Creeds_and_Virtues#virtues\ Virtues]]. An Edge to learn This hunter has Virtue to spare and an Edge it can buy. Open the Imbued tab and press Learn an Edge. Unspent points keep, and a new Edge is ready at once. See [[HTR_Guide_Edges#buying-edges\ Buying Edges]]. Hunter's notes What the autopsy table wrote down. See [[HTR_Guide_Hunter_Tools#the-notes\ The notes]]. Out of Conviction At 0 this hunter is an ordinary person to every monster. No second sight wakes, so keep them out of the fight. - Conviction comes back after each threat ends, up to the Creed's level. - Deeds raise it past that. See [[HTR_Guide_Being_Imbued#conviction\ Conviction]]. Righteous fury risk This hunter shares a map with a colonist they know is a monster, and their Creed can break into righteous fury against it. - Keep their mood up, or keep them apart. See [[HTR_Guide_Living_with_Monsters\ Living with monsters]]. Second sight is up For three hours every monster this hunter sees gets a mark, and each one seen this way is known from then on. Their mind is closed, and illusions show as false. Keep them where they can see the threat. See [[HTR_Guide_Being_Imbued#second-sight\ Second sight]]. Strapped down The table's straps stop a downed subject crawling off, and hold a prisoner down until someone carries them away. See [[HTR_Guide_Hunter_Tools#the-autopsy-table\ The autopsy table]]. The autopsy table Lay a subject on it: right-click a downed monster, a staked vampire, a prisoner or a corpse and pick Carry to the autopsy table. Nobody sleeps on the table. See [[HTR_Guide_Hunter_Tools#the-autopsy-table\ The autopsy table]]. The bait stake Right-click a live animal or a corpse and pick Bind to the bait stake. The next group of monsters on the map goes for the bait first. Ordinary raids ignore it, and it doesn't bring a raid sooner. Select the stake and press Release to untie the body. See [[HTR_Guide_Hunter_Tools#bait\ Bait]]. This corpse may rise On a haunted map, unburied corpses can get up as shamblers, a fifth of them each night hour. Bury it or burn it. Anything in a grave or a sarcophagus stays down. See [[HTR_Guide_The_Walking_Dead#where-they-come-from\ Where they come from]].

Name What it is Burned Was let down by someone it trusted once and hasn't forgotten. Its good opinion of anyone grows half as fast. Cold to anyone from a colony it has never talked to. Driven Hates one kind of monster above all and wants it hunted. Its fights pay a third more.

Name What it is Cell under attack A hunter cell holding out against the afflicted. Dead cell's safe house The safe house where a cell made its last stand. Whatever killed them still walks the rooms. Hunters' camp Where the hunters hold the one the colony handed over, until they are sure of what to do with it. Necromancer's house A house with the curtains drawn, and too many people inside who don't breathe. Open grave A burial ground where the earth doesn't stay put. The dead that walk come back to lie here. Revenant's old home The place the dead one lived before it died. It still goes back there. Vampire's haven Where one of the undead sleeps through the day, and the mortals it keeps stand guard. Werewolf's den A den where one of the shapeshifters lies up between hunts, among people who serve the same rot.

Name What it is Dissect Three rolls of an hour each, added up. Up to two points in the file and proof for a case. A corpse is used up. A living subject most likely dies, and lives through it only maimed. A subject that has given its points is passed over. Examine 15 minutes. Tells a monster from a person, and on two successes what kind. Half a point in the file. Nothing happens to the subject, though a monster not staked may wake. Each subject is examined once. Study a horror's piece 15 minutes, on a horror's piece lying on the table. On a success the colony hits that monster 10% harder, up to the ceiling, and the piece is used up. A failure leaves it to try again. Test for weakness 30 minutes. Pick the methods under "test with" in the bill's details: silver, fire (chemfuel) or holy water. The nearest item of a picked method not yet ruled out for the kind is used up and deals one wound of its damage. A method that does nothing special is ruled out; a hit on two successes, or ruling out all three, finds the kind's weakness and gives a point in the file.

Name What it is Fresh cell Three strangers were on the same road the night the thing came out of the dark. Each of them heard the voices, and each of them saw it for what it was. They don't know each other, and they don't know what they've become, but they know they can't go back. Note: three new hunters with one Edge each and almost nothing else. Hunting party Four hunters who have done this before. The other cells passed word of a revenant's old home a few days from here, and you came to finish it. Note: four experienced hunters with two or three Edges each and hunter weapons, and a lair on the world map from the start. Lone survivor The others are dead. You heard the voices while it happened, and when you looked again you could see what was eating them. You ran. It didn't stop following. Note: one new hunter, alone, and the afflicted arrive within days. A hard start. Plague doctors You came to treat the sickness. Then the dead got up out of the pits. Two of you saw them for what they were; your assistant only saw you put them down. The plague went one way and you went the other, and the dead are following.Note: two hunters and a mortal assistant, with herbs and quicklime. The walking dead come in a few days. Medieval arms and the old crafts; research is as normal. Witch-hunters You saw the thing in the miller's house for what it was, and so did two others. Nobody else believed you. Now the three of you travel with cold iron, holy water and a crossbow, and burn what needs burning.Note: three hunters with a crossbow each in their packs. Medieval arms and the old crafts; research is as normal.

Name What it is Contact Keeps up with Hunter-Net and the cell's people outside it, and brings in leads. Leader Picks the cell's next target and speaks for it. The cell votes for whoever it trusts most and who has done the most for it. Medic Patches up the cell's hurt and hides them until they can walk again. Muscle Goes through the door first when the cell raids a lair. Researcher Digs through records and rumours until the thing has a name and a weakness. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. The factions, the kinds of people and the creatures this mod adds.

Faction What it is Fresh cell Strangers who were Imbued on the same night and have stuck together since.The Imbued are ordinary people who heard the Messengers and woke up able to see the monsters hiding among them. Nobody told them why. They have no church, no order and no leaders, only each other and the hunter-net, where cells trade what they have learned. Each hunter follows one of the creeds, and the creeds don't always agree on what to do with what they find. Hunting party Veteran hunters who have done this before, come to finish a job other cells found.After a few hunts the Imbued learn what silver, fire and wood do and don't do, which creed to trust with a prisoner, and how little the people they protect want to know. Their names are on the hunter-net, and the monsters keep lists too. Lone survivor The only one who lived through the night the dead came.The Messengers spoke while the others were dying, and since then the survivor has seen the walking dead for what they are. Hunters alone don't last long. Somewhere on the hunter-net there are others who have heard the same voices, and the survivor will need them. Plague doctors Doctors who went where the sick were dying and saw what climbed out of the plague pits.When the dead get up, someone has to put them down and burn what's left. These hunters came to treat a sickness and found the corpses wouldn't stay buried. They carry herbs, quicklime and more spades than knives. Raiders People who move in silence and don't stop to talk. Nobody has traded with them and come back to say so. Settlers A loose network of people moving messages and goods between far-off posts. They trade what they pick up on the road and don't say who they work for. Witch-hunters Hunters who took up the old tools of the witch-finders.The Imbued see the monsters for what they are, all at once and without asking to. These three answered with what their grandparents' grandparents used: cold iron, holy water, salt, a crossbow and a fire. They have no church behind them and no one to tell them they're right.

Self 1 h 3 Conviction, Intelligence + Vision at 8, once a scene. The hunter carries a vision of what's coming here, for a season at most: before the next big threat strikes, a letter names it a few hours ahead. A botch gives a false vision.
24.9 cells 4 h Wits + Zeal against the monster's Stamina + 2. An hour a success: it can't spend blood, Rage or Gnosis, use its powers or mend, wherever it goes.

Self 15 s 1 Conviction, Manipulation + Mercy at 7. Everyone within 5 cells a point of Mercy, the hunter too, is slow to strike and to hurry for two turns a success, and rages and frenzies end. A frenzied monster may hold on to its frenzy.

Self 15 s 2 Conviction, Strength + Mercy at 8. The brightest light near her flares, and every monster within 5 cells a success takes its lethal dice in burns: daylight outdoors 10, a sun lamp 8, a campfire 6, a lamp 5, a torch or a flare gun in the hand 3, otherwise 1. Moonlight doesn't count.

Self 4 h For four hours, once every few seconds, a shouted word turns aside a melee blow on anyone the hunter can see: her Wits + Mercy at 6 against the attacker's Dexterity + Melee. It counts as the dodge.

Touch 15 s Zeal at 6, by touch, on a monster. A level of lethal burning a success, and a mark every hunter can see, even through a disguise: a day at one or two successes, a week at three or four, a season at five or six, a year at seven or eight, and for good beyond.
24.9 cells 15 s Stamina + Zeal against the monster's Stamina + 3. A turn a success it can barely move, for as long as she keeps it in sight.
Self 15 s 2 Conviction, Stamina + Zeal at 6. A turn a success, anyone she strikes by hand, or who strikes her, takes lethal dice in burns equal to her successes.

Self 15 s 1 Conviction, Appearance + Zeal at 6. A hostile monster who can see her turns to her and no one else, or three for a second point of Conviction, five for a third, spent as the monsters in sight need them. Each resists with Wits. Someone else hurting it frees it. Once a scene for each monster.

Self 4 h No roll. For four hours, the hunter's melee blows do two dice of extra lethal damage, or Strength + 2 with an empty hand. A real weapon holds for two turns of fighting; after that each turn takes a Zeal roll at 6, or the weapon wears.

24.9 cells 4 h 1 Conviction, Manipulation + Mercy at 5, at a monster. While she keeps it in sight, every turn it means to go for her costs it a point of Willpower for each success; with too little left, it can't.

Self 1 h Perception + Vision at 6, once a scene. A letter lists the monsters who passed within eight cells in the last fifteen days, one a success, newest first. Every clue within eight cells is read with her successes, along with what kind of creature left it.
Self 10 s No roll. The hunter takes a bruise that no armor stops, and adds her Mercy to her Strength for her next blow or feat of strength.

Self 1 h Perception + Zeal at 6. Forty minutes a success: the hunter sees what kind of monster each one in sight is, without spending Conviction, and sees clearly in the dark or blind. It gives no protection to her mind.

Touch 4 h 2 Conviction, by touch, on someone of her own side. Pick an Attribute; Mercy + that Attribute at 7 moves a dot of it from her to them a success, for two turns, an hour, five hours, a day or three days by successes. She always keeps one.

Self 1 h 2 Conviction, Zeal at 8, once a scene. Every monster near her shows its true face to everyone who can see it: 5 cells at one success, 15 at two or three, 40 at four or five, 65 at six or seven, the whole map beyond. Mortals who see a vampire or a Garou are witnesses to an open breach.
Self 1 day Intelligence + Vision at 7, once a day. Each success is a second look: her next Edge roll takes the better of two, and her next shot or blow is likelier to land.

Self 4 h Wits + Mercy at 6. For four hours, monsters looking for someone to attack pass the hunter by, unless one of them beats her successes with its Perception. She shows herself by attacking, and once one monster has seen her, they all have.

Self 1 h Perception + Mercy at 6. Forty minutes a success: every hunter on the map sees what kind each monster in sight is, without spending Conviction. The monsters see her as a bright light and go for her. Ends Hide.
24.9 cells 4 h Manipulation + Mercy at 6, at a monster, once a scene each. For four hours its blows, shots and work are a tenth worse a success. At four successes or more it runs.
Touch 10 s No roll. Rejuvenate's touch closes another's worst wound: 1 Conviction for a bruise, 2 for anything worse.

24.9 cells 4 h 5 Conviction, at a monster. Pick a human frailty (it can't mend by its own means and takes its wounds in full) or one of its powers to take away. Manipulation + Mercy against its Stamina + 4, or + 3 for a power. It lasts until the monster leaves her presence.

Touch 1 h No Conviction, Perception + Zeal at 7, by touch. A person: a letter with their last brush with a monster. A monster: who it has hurt, a week back a success. On a suspect it tells true from false: a monster's case gains her successes and its kind, and an innocent's is closed.

24.9 cells 1 h Perception + Vision at 6, at a monster, once a scene. A letter names one of its kind's weaknesses, and from then on the colony's hunters hit that kind a quarter harder. At three successes she also finds where its kind lairs, and the lair goes on the world map.
Self 15 s Stamina + Mercy at 6. A turn a success: monsters' attacks on her miss more, a tenth a success, and on one more person within Mercy cells for each success after the first.

24.9 cells 10 s Manipulation + Mercy at 7, at someone within Mercy cells. A monster takes a level of lethal burning a success, through any armor; a person is stunned with horror a turn a success. The hunter takes a bruise either way.

24.9 cells 10 s Stamina + Mercy at 6. On someone hurt: a wound closed a success, each paid with a point of Conviction while she has more than one, or else an hour short of breath. On a monster within Mercy cells: its Stamina against her successes, a level of lethal damage for each she has over, and a point of Conviction back for every two, up to her Creed's starting level.

Touch 1 h 3 Conviction, Stamina + Vision at 6, one harder for each level of lethal damage (at most 10), on herself or someone she touches, once a scene. Every lethal wound becomes a bruise of the same size, and lost parts grow back.

24.9 cells 10 s 1 Conviction, Dexterity + Zeal at 6, at anyone within Zeal cells. Lethal dice of her Strength plus each success after the first, through any armor. Machines within 6 cells of the strike are scrambled.
Self 15 s Manipulation + Zeal at 7. A cloud of thick black smoke round the hunter, bigger for each success. Shots into it or through it mostly miss.
Self 4 h 1 Conviction, no roll. For four hours her Zeal is spread a dot at a time over her Strength, Dexterity and Stamina, none above 6.

Self 1 h 2 Conviction, Charisma + Mercy at 8, once a scene. For the hour this map is sealed from every other world: nothing steps sideways into or out of the Penumbra, no spirit is called up, no shadow carries anyone across.
Touch 1 h Perception + Zeal at 6, by touch, on a monster. Six hours a success, her second sight marks where it is on the map, and when it leaves she's told.

Self 4 h Stamina + Zeal at 6. For four hours, monsters can't come within as many cells of the hunter as she has Zeal unless their Stamina beats her successes, one try each. People can shelter inside, and shots still pass.

Self 1 h Perception + Mercy at 6. Forty minutes a success: the hunter sees what kind of monster each one in sight is, without spending Conviction. Each success past the first shows one of their past meetings with a person, as evidence for the suspect list.

Every setting in Options, Mod settings, The Rim by Night, with what it does. Setting What it does Imbued among the wandering hunters About one in four of the travellers and order hunters is imbued, with two or three Edges, and sees through a vampire's mask. Off, they're all ordinary people, as in a game without Imbued. A hunted stranger comes A colony with no hunters gets a stranger running from a monster by night, some time between day 15 and day 40, and again every 30 to 60 days until one is taken in. Taken in, the stranger joins as a hunter, and a few hours later the monster comes after them as their first horror. Off, the stranger still turns up now and then as an ordinary event. Bait calls lone monsters A few nights after an animal or a corpse is bound to a bait stake, one monster comes for it: a shambler, or with Kindred or Garou loaded a young vampire (generation 10 to 13, or a shovelhead) or a fomor. With Garou, one in ten is a Black Spiral Dancer. It keeps away while anyone of the colony within 12 cells can see the stake, feeds there for a few hours, then leaves. Off, the stake only turns monster raids already on the map. Chance of the Imbuing How likely a colonist who sees a monster hurt someone is to wake as a hunter. The mod's chance is 2%. It is doubled for the brave, kind or tough and halved for a wimp. A near miss leaves a Bystander. Hunters before the Imbuing slows Once the colony has more hunters than this, the next one wakes at most once a season. Hunters hold True Faith Every new hunter wakes with full True Faith. Off, a hunter has only the Faith it held before. Fifth Edges from the hunter's own Creed A level 5 Edge can only come from the hunter's own Creed, with its primary Virtue at 10. Off, any Creed's, with the same Virtue. Elders hide from second sight An old vampire or a great Garou takes a Virtue roll to see for what it is. Off, second sight sees every monster. The walking dead Unburied corpses can rise on a haunted night. Off, the dead stay down. An exposed monster turns its town When a hunter names or exposes a monster in a town, its own kind there turn on the hunters, and in an ordinary town the others hiding there may too. Off, nobody takes it up. Exposure gain Scales how much the colony's Exposure rises for each outsider who leaves having seen a hunter's Edge at work. Exposure fading Scales how fast the colony's Exposure falls back each day as people forget. Case rewards The silver and goodwill a town pays for a solved case, against the mod's own. Edges camera shake How hard big Edges shake the camera: Smite landing, mostly. At 0% the camera stays still. Edges sky flashes Big Edges flash the sky in their colour, and storms tint it while they build. Off, the sky keeps its own light. Notes on the Hunters' Board How often a new note goes up on the Hunters' Board. At 100% it is one every one to three days. Most Wanted A handful of monsters Hunter-Net most wants dead roam the world map, one kind for each monster mod you have loaded and the walking dead's worst. They roam either way, but only a colony with an imbued is told of them, sees them on the map or is thanked for one. Turned off, they leave the world map; turned back on, a new list arrives in one letter. The tips the game shows the first times you meet something. Tip What it is Clues and suspects A monster hiding among your visitors or colonists leaves marks: fang marks, claw marks, blood trails, tracks that stop dead. Each fades in 15 days.Hunters and Bystanders examine clues as research work. Each reading adds evidence against whoever was near when it was left, most against the one who left it. With enough evidence, a hunter can name the suspect from the Suspects list on the Imbued tab. Name the wrong person and the colony pays for it. Conviction Conviction is the hunter's certainty that they're doing right. It pays for second sight and for the stronger Edges.It comes back after each threat ends, up to the Creed's level, and deeds raise it past that. At 0 a hunter is an ordinary person to every monster. At 10 they can cash it all in for a Virtue point. Creeds, Virtues and deeds Mercy, Vision and Zeal are the hunter's Virtues, and the Creed's own Virtue always leads.Each Creed has its deeds, such as rescuing, learning, unmasking or killing. Each deed gives a point of Conviction, once a day for each kind. Virtues rise only when a hunter at 10 Conviction cashes it in. Edges Edges are the powers the Messengers give. Each Creed has a path of five, and a level costs its number in points of its Virtue.A hunter's Edges sit on tiles above their buttons, one per path. Click a tile, pick an Edge, then pick the target. A greyed Edge says why it can't be used now. Hunters among monsters A hunter who learns a colonist is a monster knows it for good, and how they live with it depends on their Creed.Some talk, some watch, and an Avenger may break into righteous fury against the monster. Keep such hunters in good spirits, or apart from the monsters they know. Second sight When a hostile monster comes into view, a hunter spends a point of Conviction and sees clearly for three hours.Every monster they see gets a mark that says "not human", their mind is closed to Dominate, Presence and the Delirium, and every monster seen this way is known to them for good. The afflicted The dead don't always stay down. Shamblers dig out at the map edge at night, and revenants arrive as ordinary visitors, back for one colonist.While a map is haunted, its unburied dead can get up at night. Bury or burn them, and send a revenant on its way to stop it. The imbued One of your colonists has been imbued. The voices called the Messengers have woken them, and they now see monsters for what they are.A hunter is still human: no fast healing, no frenzy. What they have is second sight, Conviction, Edges and each other. The Imbued tab shows their Creed, Virtues and Conviction. The other cells Other cells of hunters are scattered across the world, and now they know about your colony.They trade the weapons that work, send word of the afflicted before they come, and ask for help when a cell is in trouble. Their requests show in the Quests tab. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. With Odyssey your colony can live in orbit. The World of Darkness stays on the ground: nobody from these mods comes up uninvited unless "The World of Darkness reaches orbit" is on in Core's settings. Help you call still comes, by drop pod, and leaves on Royalty's shuttle. Without Royalty it stays aboard until the ship lands. The colony is whichever home holds most of your free colonists, so visitors go where your people are. Cases stay on the ground, so hunters sit quiet in orbit unless the setting is on. A case's pay comes by drop pod.

Can I add it to a running game? Yes. Nobody is imbued until a colonist sees a monster hurt someone and the roll comes up. Can I take it out? Use Remove Imbued from this game first. Every hunter becomes an ordinary person again, the mod's things, factions and sites go, and the game is saved under a new name. Do I need Kindred or Garou? No. The afflicted are the mod's own monsters. With either or both loaded, hunters go after vampires and werewolves too. What about Anomaly? Imbued ignores it. Second sight doesn't mark Anomaly's creatures. Can a vampire or a Garou be imbued? No. One kind per pawn: no vampire, ghoul or Garou is ever imbued. Blood-feeders like sanguophages aren't either, unless "Blood-feeders can become hunters and mages" is on in Core's Rules settings. Can I get into a hostile town without attacking it? Yes. A caravan standing on any hostile town gets Sneak in beside Attack, at night only, whoever is in it. The caravan walks onto the town's map unseen, and the town's people and guns can't go for anyone they haven't found. A townsman with a clear view may notice something move, less often in the dark, and the town then searches round that spot. A searcher who comes close may find who is there. Attacking anyone gives the attacker away. My hunter can't see a monster. Check their Conviction: at 0 they're an ordinary person. A very old or powerful monster can also be too strong for their sight. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Throw the colony in with one cell and its imbued stop being a headcount. Each has a personality, means, a goal of its own and an opinion of you that moves with what you do. They hand you work, owe you debts, hunt beside you and, if they come to hate you, work against you.

The Hunter-Net page of the Hunters window names the nearest cell the colony knows, with Swear to this home. You need: - a colony imbued, - the cell met and Hunter-Net on speaking terms with the colony. One cell at a time. Its roster fills to 8 to 12 named imbued from its hunters, and the most seasoned leads. New pages appear on the Hunters window's rail: People, Council and, while a war runs, War. Leaving costs 20 goodwill with Hunter-Net. Loyal hunters drop to -5 regard, and the debts the cell owes you shrink a size. A cell that falls frees the colony with a letter.

Every cell the colony knows can owe it debts, trivial, minor, major or life, as Kindred courts do. A cell's mission pays one when it's done: trivial for an early colony, minor once raids come at a mid-game size, major for the hardest. Once you throw in with a cell, its hunters owe you debts for their own errands too. Spend them on the Debts page of the Hunters window. Ask lists what a cell does for a debt, and a bigger debt covers a smaller service: two plain hunter's weapons (trivial), a few of its hunters at the door or a lead that opens a case (minor), one of its better weapons (major), a season's training, 8 experience and a point of Conviction for every colony hunter (life). Ledger lists each debt with who owes it and why; Call in on a row picks what that debt pays for. Trained dogs bought from a cell are paid in debts too. Leaving a sworn cell shrinks its debts a size.

The People page lists every named imbued: role, cell (Creed for those in none) and regard, with a filter for friends, rivals and enemies. Click a hunter to see their personality, means, goal, friends and dislikes. You only see a hunter's personality and means once you've met them: talked to them in their town or finished a mission they gave. Regard event Change A mission done for them +2 A mission done for a friend of theirs +1 A step of their goal done +3 A gift from their row +1 per 500 silver, up to +3 a season Their mission refused or let lapse -1 (Proud -3) A mission done against them or a friend -3 Betraying their goal -10, for good Regard drifts a point toward 0 every season.

Personality How they pay and behave Greedy silver x0.7, trust x1.5 Cautious silver and trust x1.25, but the biggest debt they'll owe is a size smaller Loyal everything x1.25 while you never cross them or their friends; betrayal makes an enemy for good Conniving pays with a debt another hunter owes them Cowardly one more open mission, aimed at their rivals; pay x1.2 Proud trust x1.5, silver x0.8; refusals cost 3 regard Zealous only the hunt; those pay x1.5 Generous everything x1.3; now and then asks one back Vengeful bad blood never fades; an enemy at -5 Burned regard grows half as fast Driven asks for fights, and pays x1.3 for them

Every imbued of a cell sits on its council, so each starts with some means. A poor hunter offers one mission at a time and pays x0.6, a comfortable one two at x1.0, a rich one three at x1.4. Each hunter wants something, hidden until they count you a friend (regard +6) or you have a hold over them. A goal is three steps: two missions bent to it, then the prize. Keeping the prize is a betrayal. Goal What you get for it Collector a hunter's weapon Lore hunter a dead cell's casebook (experience for an imbued reader) Power seeker silver by its means, and its vote for a year Revenge a major debt and the enemy's goods Freedom its regard stays at +6 or more for good Childe a minor debt now, a new hunter on your side later Mercy each colony imbued learns, 8 experience Kingmaker the new Leader starts at regard +6 Homecoming another cell, met Buried secret a life debt

The hunters round a cell work in smaller cells of their own: two to four, each around its strongest hunter, the one leading the local hunt first. Each has a temperament that sets what it wants, what it pays in, which others it gets on with and which it feuds with. The Cells page of the cell's window shows them as cards: temperament, members, power out of 20 in ten cells, and a bar for what they think of you. While you're sworn there, that bar is the average regard of its members. Pick one to see its leader, members, allies and feuds, and Ask them for work: one of their own missions, once every five days, shown in the Quests tab to accept there. Done, the cell gains a point of power and 2 regard. A cell that thinks -5 of you or worse gives no work. When a rival comes within two power of the leader's cell and stays there for 30 days, it tries to take over the local hunt. The showdown comes 20 to 40 days later: the hunters round it pick a side. Each side's chance is its power against the other's; a deciding mission done for a side counts two. Back a side from the page: 6 standing if it wins, 6 lost if it doesn't, and the winners' regard moves the same way. Plotters who win take the lead, and nobody plots again for 60 days. Temperament Wants Missions Zealous every monster dead a monster off their hands, covering their tracks Merciful the innocent kept out of it a shared case, covering their tracks Visionary to know why they were chosen a shared case, a monster off their hands Wary to stay alive and unknown covering their tracks

Under Your seats on the Hunter-Net page, once Hunter-Net's goodwill is 25 or more, a colony imbued can take a role. A role held by a hunter makes that hunter your rival. The Leader is chosen by the cell's vote: the cell's average regard for the colony must be +4 or more, and the colony must have done more missions for it than anyone. Role Duty each season Leader vote and pick the next target Researcher one case or lore mission Contact chase one lead Muscle one raid Medic shelter one wounded hunter at the colony A duty kept adds 3 trust and a dot. Three missed in a row and the role is lost, with 10 trust, to the next in line. The hunter's own tab shows the role and when its duty is due, and an alert warns two days ahead.

Each season the cell votes on one or two motions: vetting new hunters, going after the monsters' home, hunting every monster or leaving the quiet ones, paying into the fund. A colony imbued with a role votes too.

Rivals slander the colony or stymie your next mission with their own people. Enemies send hired raiders. Capture one and question them in prisoner talk to learn who sent them, then Accuse that hunter.

With Kindred or Garou loaded, a war runs against the nearest court or sept the cell would hunt. Its score starts at 50: a season of incursions, two of raids on their havens and lairs while you hold your safehouse, armory, informant and lab, then the final assault at 70, the desperate defence at 30, or a truce. With Imbued alone there's no war. The skirmishes come a few weeks apart. A war mission you let lapse is fought without you: the cell's members against the enemy's, by their strength, and members can die in it. Hover over the stages, the score and the holdings on the War page for what each one needs.

The Backgrounds page on a hunter's tab buys rated Backgrounds with standing at the sworn cell: the new rating x 2, never experience. Dots from the Imbuing or the making menu count as bought. Leaving the cell, or the cell falling, halves every dot. Now and then a rival strikes at one of them, at most once a season: a letter gives six days (more with Contacts) to answer with a mission or a favour the rival owes, or the dot is lost. The "Rival strikes on Backgrounds" setting makes strikes rarer or more common, or turns them off. Background Each dot Allies a friend in a town, and armed mortals to call on any map with enemies on it; they never witness anything Contacts a person in a town, a day more to answer a strike, and a chance each season to strike back at a rival Fame more tavern guests and regulars Influence a caravan from the cell's town once a season Mentor more visits from an older hunter Resources 100 x dots squared silver a season Arsenal a crate of hunter weapons worth 150 silver a season, and 3% better prices with hunter-net

On the Hunting page of the Imbued settings: the sworn cell on or off, the war chance, enemy acts a season and how fast regard fades. The mod's own monsters. They come with or without Kindred and Garou. Kind What it is Shambler Slow, strong and hard to stop. Feels no pain and doesn't go down to wounds; only the head or the whole body ends it. Comes in groups, at night Revenant Someone back from the dead for one person. Passes for living at a distance and mends a wound for each point of Willpower. Once its target is dead, it falls for good Hidden Passes for living and keeps its skills. Kills for one purpose. The toughest of the three Necromancer A living sorcerer. Raises a corpse within 10 cells every 10 seconds, up to six at once. When the necromancer dies, those dead fall

- Shambler raids. The dead dig out of the ground at the map edge at night. In a colony with no vampire or Garou to draw other enemies they come half again as often. One raid in six has a necromancer walking behind it. - Revenant visits. A revenant or a hidden arrives alone as an ordinary visitor of a friendly faction, back for one colonist. Someone who has killed is likelier to be the one. It strikes at night. The map stays haunted while it's there. - The colony's own dead. On a haunted map, unburied corpses can get up as shamblers, a fifth of them each night hour. Anything in a grave or a sarcophagus stays down.

Fire does half again as much to them, and the head ends them fastest. Shamblers are slow with doors; revenants aren't. Ordinary people who see one of the afflicted for what it is get a mood shock, and family and friends of one who rose take it harder.

A revenant or a hidden that a colony hunter has seen, and that hasn't struck yet, can be talked down by its target, a Redeemer or an Innocent: about twenty minutes, then Social + Mercy at 7, two dice more for the one it came back for. A failure and it strikes at once. ← Imbued contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Any adult humanlike can Awaken, modded races included, but never a vampire, ghoul, werewolf or hunter. A blood-feeder like a sanguophage can only Awaken if "Blood-feeders can become hunters and mages" is on in Core's Rules settings. The chance comes from: - Omens: an eclipse, a psychic drone, toxic fallout, a flashstorm, a herd migration, an aurora, and several Anomaly events. Every colonist on the map rolls, and only the first one Awakens. - Near death: getting up after nearly bleeding out. - Seeing magic: an obvious spell cast in sight. - Extremes: a lost lover or bonded animal, a masterwork, a big research project, a catharsis. - Sleeping at a Hallow. - A mentor: a mage teaches a Sleeper an hour a day for 5 to 15 days, then the Sleeper rolls. Psychically sensitive colonists Awaken twice as often. The settings set the odds and a cap of one a season once the colony has three mages. The colonist falls into a trance of 6 to 12 hours and walks to a Watchtower in her dreams. When she wakes, a letter names her Path. About one Awakening in ten goes wrong and makes a Banisher, a mage who hates magic, her own included. A true mage's daily talk can turn a colonist Banisher, slowly.

Path What it is Acanthus Enchanters. Their souls reached Arcadia, the realm of fae and fortune, and signed the Watchtower of the Lunargent Thorn. They see the threads of luck and time, and are poorest at the plain push of Forces. Mastigos Warlocks. Their souls reached Pandemonium, the realm of demons and desire, and signed the Watchtower of the Iron Gauntlet. They master space and the mind, and struggle with the stubborn stuff of Matter. Moros Necromancers. Their souls reached Stygia, the realm of the dead and of treasure, and signed the Watchtower of the Lead Coin. They command matter and death, and are blind to the world of Spirit. Obrimos Theurgists. Their souls reached the Aether, the realm of angels and fire, and signed the Watchtower of the Golden Key. They wield raw Forces and the Prime stuff of magic itself, and shy from Death. Thyrsus Shamans. Their souls reached the Primal Wild, the realm of beasts and spirits, and signed the Watchtower of the Stone Book. They rule Life and Spirit, and find the Mind of others hard to reach.

Gnosis runs from 1 to 10. It sets the Mana cap, how much Mana she can spend at once, how many spells she can keep up, her Paradox dice, her ritual time and her Arcanum limits. It also helps her resist other kinds' mind powers. Raise it on the tab for 5 Experience.

Mana pays for spells outside her Ruling Arcana, Mage Armor, Pattern Restoration and Paradox removal. The Mana gizmo offers: - Oblation at a waking Hallow: an hour, a Mana a success. - Tass: draw Mana from a stack. - Scouring: lose a Physical dot for a day, or take a lethal wound, for 3 Mana. - Pattern Restoration: heal a wound for 3 Mana, 2 with Life 2.

Wisdom starts at 7. An Act of Hubris at or below her tier rolls Wisdom: obvious magic before outsiders, overriding a will, killing a helpless foe, Blood Sacrifice. A failure costs a dot and gives Megalomaniacal or Rampant. At 0 she goes Mad and leaves. A spell that cost Wisdom can be inured on the tab: it stops counting as Hubris but rolls two more Paradox dice.

Beats come from work, raids, quests and Aspirations. Arcane Beats come from Obsessions, Paradox and new sights. Five of either make an Experience. Spend them on the tab for Arcana, Gnosis, rotes and Merits. Beside the three short Aspirations, a colony mage works toward one long-term Aspiration at a time. A letter offers three: raise an Arcanum, learn a rote, tend a Hallow, scribe a grimoire, a season with no Paradox, grow wiser, uncover a Mystery, and one for her Path or Order (win a Duel Arcane for the Adamantine Arrow, rise in Status for the Silver Ladder, and so on). The Growth page and the Quests tab show how far along it is. Only what happens after it is taken counts, and it pays 2 to 4 Arcane Experience. There's no deadline. Drop one and another letter comes in five days. An Obsession pays nothing on the way: resolving it is two Arcane Beats and a Mana, and the same one can't come back for a season. Steps count only when they mean something: - Master an Arcanum: a cast at a foe, with enemies on the map, or on an ally who is down, under half health or bleeding out. - Study a Hallow: a different Hallow each time. Oblations count once a day. - Examine an Artifact: one she has never studied or looked at. - Speak with the dead: a different dead person each time, killed by violence or by something strange. - Becoming wiser: fifteen days with no Act of Hubris. One starts the count again. Newer Obsessions: cross into Twilight, bargain with a spirit (bind it or pay its chiminage), face the Abyss (be there when an Acamoth is driven out or a Gulmoth destroyed), unmask a Seer (solve a Seer case), win a Duel Arcane, scrutinize a monster with Focused Sight, witness an Awakening (or mentor one), make magic last (an Imbued Item, or a spell let go for good), and a brush with death against a supernatural foe. Each is offered only when it can happen. They serve the Exarchs and act only while the colony has a true mage. Their Pylons hide in the region's towns. They: - raid with sleeper thralls led by one Seer, a Disciple with her Ministry's Arcanum; - empty a waking Hallow and put it to sleep, and raid a few days later; - pay a hostile faction to bring a Seer along on its raids for a year; - bribe a trader to sell a cursed Imbued Item; - send a recruiter to a mage of low Wisdom, or an exile. Seer cases: a drained Hallow, a talkative prisoner or a Seer's body is a clue. Each one rules out towns until the Pylon is found. Then you can raid it, tell the Consilium, or sell the secret back.

Mages who hate magic, their own included. A Banisher leads raids on the colony and ambushes caravans with a true mage. With Imbued loaded, hunters sometimes ride along and turn on their own side when she falls. A colonist Banisher may betray the colony, step by step, unless talk or Mind or Fate spells set her back.

Released Paradox of 5 points or more can call something through. - Gulmoth walk the map. They take half damage from mundane weapons, and they grow on Paradox, Dissonance and frightened Sleepers. - Acamoth ride a colonist unseen. Bad nights first, then fights, then sabotage. Mind, Death or Fate sight finds them, and an exorcism drives them out.
Hostile mages arrive with Mage Armor and prepared spells up, fight with attack rotes, and always contain their Paradox. A Banisher counters spells better than any mage.

The Consilium's list of those it has declared enemies of every mage. Five names roam the world map, whether the colony has a mage or not. Only a colony with a mage is told of them. - Who is on it. Banisher killers with one to three Sleeper followers, Seer agents with their Ministry's sign and one to three thralls, and now and then a Gulmoth loose from the Abyss at its third rank. All of them shrug off half of every wound. - The mark. Each is a mark on the world map that moves every few days and shows only within 25 tiles of a home or a caravan. Read the Proscribed on the Awakened window's Overview opens the list. - Meeting one. Send a caravan to its mark to hunt it. It's found at its camp: Banishers in their fortified camp, Seer agents in a safehouse, a Gulmoth in the ruined Sanctum it broke into. It holds the camp a few hours before coming out at you. One within 12 tiles can come to the colony: a mage that has never crossed it walks through unless harmed, and a Gulmoth, or a mage who knows the colony, attacks. - The reward. The mage who kills one gains 2 Arcane Experience and 8 standing toward Status with the Consilium. The kill goes in the chronicle and can be the subject of art. - Setting. The Proscribed turns the list off. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Harmony, then The Rim by Night: Core, then Awakened. Kindred, Garou and Imbued are optional and can sit anywhere after Core.

There are three ways to get one: - Start one of the four scenarios below. Each starting mage opens the making window, the same frame every Rim by Night mod uses, where you pick her Path, Order, Virtue and Vice, her Arcana and rotes, her Merit dots, and her tool. - Wait for an Awakening. A colonist may Awaken after an omen, after nearly dying, after seeing magic, or after a great loss or a great work. See Being Awakened. - Take in the hunted stranger. With no mage in the colony, a stranger may turn up asking for shelter, chased by the Seers or by Banishers. Take her in and she Awakens, and her pursuers arrive within a day and a half.

1. Open the Awakened tab on your mage. It holds her Path, Arcana, Mana, Wisdom and spells. 2. Cast a rote from her power tile, or open the spell builder with "Cast a spell". 3. Keep an eye on Mana. Refill it at a Hallow, from tass, or by Scouring. 4. Keep magic out of strangers' sight. Obvious spells seen by outsiders add Paradox dice and can cost Wisdom. 5. Within a few weeks the nearest Consilium's Herald writes to you. See The Consilium.

Scenario What it is Apostates Three people saw the Watchtowers in the same season and woke up afterwards with their names written on stone they had never touched. Nobody came to explain it. There is no Consilium out here that knows them, no mentor and no Order. They have each other and the little they can do. Note: three new mages at Gnosis 1, with no Hallow and no friends among the Awakened. The lone Awakened One of you went to sleep ordinary and woke up able to see what the world is made of. The others still can't, and every spell cast in front of them pulls at the Abyss. Somewhere a Consilium has already noticed, and a letter is on its way. Note: one mage among sleepers. The Consilium writes within a few days. Hallow founders Two mages followed the pull of Mana for weeks and found it here: a Hallow, free and unclaimed, welling up out of the ground. They mean to build around it. The Seers of the Throne mean to take it, and they know where it is. Note: two mages and a Hallow of rating 2. The Seers come before the season is out. Consilium exiles Two mages broke the Lex Magica and were cast out. They took what they could carry from their old Sanctum and went far enough that nobody would follow them. The Consilium remembers them, and its next Herald won't be friendly. Note: two exiled mages with no Status and a Sanctum focus. The Pentacle starts out cold toward you. Hermetic scholars You copied grimoires by candlelight in your order's library for years. Then you and a fellow scholar took one tome you weren't meant to take and left by night, with an apprentice who wouldn't stay behind. Now you need a library of your own.Note: two mages and one apprentice, with a tome and a Sanctum focus. Medieval arms and the old crafts; research is as normal. Cunning folk People came to you for a cure, a charm or a lost cow found, and you usually helped. One night you saw what stands behind the world, and since then your charms work a little too well. The priest started asking questions, so you and your family moved on to a place with a Hallow and no neighbours.Note: one mage and two mortal family members, with a Hallow of rating 1. Medieval arms and the old crafts; research is as normal. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Awakened works on its own. With the other Rim by Night mods loaded, the kinds share a world.

Tame animals can learn more than guard and attack. The extra roles show on the vanilla Training tab, are taught by a handler over several lessons, and fade the same way when nobody keeps them up. Each needs guard (obedience) first. Role Who can learn it What it does Guard post body size 0.4 or more Holds a spot you pick with its Guard post button (or right-click, Guard this spot), and goes for any enemy within 8 cells of it Watch any Raises the alarm when it sees an enemy, day or night, and wakes everyone asleep. Once an hour Sniff out an animal with a nose Barks at anyone within 12 cells who hides what they are. A pawn hidden by a power shows for an hour; a guest or prisoner in disguise is known for good Track after sniff out Follows a trail you pick with its Track button: a fled prisoner, quarry marked for hunting, an enemy unseen. It stays close and sniffs them out Scouting a bird that really flies Circles a spot, shadows someone, or flies out over the land and comes back with what it saw Messenger a flier, or body size 0.3 or more Tends one of your town contacts, or asks an allied town for a trade caravan on the comms console's terms (15 goodwill, once every four days) Hunt a predator Once a day brings back one or two small animals from round here, about half of them still alive Fight beside after attack Defends its master without an order, and fights better at their side for an hour Spirit scout a familiar only Looks across to the spirit side for three hours, once a day, and comes back with what waits there Selected, a trained animal shows a line to its guard post or to the one it's tracking. The kennel (Misc tab) takes up to six of your animals: they learn half as fast again and forget at half the rate. Name a kennel master on it, and that colonist trains the kennel's animals before any other handling work. A mage's familiar learns twice as fast, forgets at half the rate, and can learn spirit scout, which looks into the Shadow and names the map's Hallows. Members of your sworn Consilium sell trained creatures fit to be familiars (cats, crows, cobras, monkeys, foxes). Ask for a trained animal is on each member's row, paid with the favours that member owes you: a trivial favour counts 1, a minor 2, a major 3 and a life debt 4. An animal costs 1, plus 1 a role, plus 1 for every 500 silver it's worth, and comes by drop pod.
A vampire shows as a dead Pattern to Prime and Death sight. A Kindred can Embrace a mage. She loses her magic and keeps her Wisdom as Humanity.
Spirit sight marks a Garou as half spirit. A Garou distrusts any mage with Spirit 3 or more, who could bind spirits.

Prime sight shows an Imbued's borrowed light. An Imbued colonist stays uneasy while a mage shares her map, until a mage tells the hunters what she is (a link on the Order page). Banishers sometimes bring Imbued hunters along.

Ordinary colonists are Sleepers. Obvious magic in their sight risks Paradox and Wisdom, but it can also start an Awakening. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. A Hallow is a spot where Mana wells up: a geyser, an ancient building, an old tree or a rock face. Some maps have one, and the same tile always does. Each day a waking Hallow fills up to its rating in Mana. Anything past that forms as tass beside it. Colonists who sleep there may Awaken. A colony mage can see a Hallow's ring and label. Oblation there gives Mana. Hallow Dance wakes a sleeping Hallow or damps a waking one, and Create Truth makes a new one for 5 Mana a dot.
Mana in matter: stone, ash, water or fruit, by the Hallow's resonance. Draw its Mana from the Mana gizmo, or eat the fruit.

Build a Sanctum focus in a room and assign up to five mages. The room's beauty sets the rating, from 1 to 5. In her own Sanctum, a mage keeps Gnosis + rating spells up, and outsiders outside the room don't see what's cast there.

The sight gizmo opens one Arcanum or more. Marks float over pawns nearby: the Awakened, the dead, spirits, the sick, the possessed. Focused Sight studies one pawn, corpse, item or place for an hour, and Scrutiny goes deeper for a Willpower. Sight slows work a little while it's open.
Every successful cast flares her Nimbus and puts her Path's Tilt on those around her. Cloak Nimbus hides it.
A grimoire holds rotes. A mage can learn from one, and Scribe Grimoire writes new ones. A Library Merit adds dice.

Ten rare books, one per Arcanum, each a few chapters long. A tome is where the lost attack rotes, the Ossuary rule and spreading Doom come from: no teacher, grimoire or Order hands them out. - Studying. Select the tome and press Chapters... to pick the reader and a chapter. The tome must lie in a Library (loose or on a shelf). A chapter takes one to three days of work, faster with a better Library and a quicker researcher, and the reader needs its Arcanum and Occult (and sometimes Gnosis). A finished chapter teaches its rotes for good. Progress is kept if the reader stops, but another reader or chapter starts over. - The price. Every chapter costs something, rolled when it's done: usually the tome's own price, sometimes another. It can be Paradox, an Act of Hubris, a bad mood (shaken, or obsessed with the book), the Abyss noticing (an Acamoth or a Gulmoth a few days later), a Seer Pylon learning where you are, a ghost following the reader, a spirit with a grudge, or a year of the reader's life. - Hidden chapters. Six tomes have one, and only half their copies hold it (about one tome in three). A mage who knows Supernal Vision or Pierce Deception finds it at once; anyone else rolls Intelligence + Occult once a day. - Where they come from. One ancient complex in five has one by a crate, one Seer or Banisher raid in ten carries one, the Consilium sells one at Status 4, and a cabal may ask for help taking one from a Banisher camp ("The tome hunt"). Awakened Mage: The Awakening (second edition) in RimWorld. A colonist whose soul reaches one of the Supernal Realms Awakens. From then on she can cast spells with the ten Arcana, and every spell risks Paradox. > In beta. Balance will change and bugs are likely. Keep a backup of any save you add the mod to.

- The Awakening, from omens, near death or a mentor, and the five Paths. - Gnosis, Mana, Wisdom and the ten Arcana, with close to every spell in the core book. - Rotes, Praxes and a spell builder for Potency, Duration, Scale, Range and Reach. - Paradox, Conditions, Abyssal Tilts, Dissonance and Acts of Hubris. - Hallows, tass, the Sanctum, Mage Sight and the Nimbus. - Grimoires, Imbued Items and twenty Artifacts. - The five Orders, Legacies, Merits, Obsessions and Aspirations. - The Consilium: Status, services, the Lex Magica, hearings and the Duel Arcane. - The Seers of the Throne, Banishers and the Abyss. - Cabals, NPC mages who fight with spells, and colonies shared with vampires, werewolves and hunters. A gate to the Underworld, cold and dark. Death magic is stronger near it, and every day a ghost climbs out.
Nothing. This piece of the world has been set aside, and there is no way into it.
A worktable marked with circles and the names of the Watchtowers. Standing in a Sanctum, it lets a mage with Prime 4 set a spell into an item, which anyone can use afterwards.
A doorway of grey mist. Whoever walks through it becomes a shade, and walking through again brings them back.
A faint picture of something solid that a spell has made insubstantial. Anything can pass through.
A message written in light only mages can see.
A hole in the Gauntlet. Whoever steps on it crosses into the Shadow, and its twin on the far side brings them back.
A fold in space. Whoever steps on it comes out of its twin, here or somewhere else entirely.

An altar, a desk of tools and a circle on the floor: the heart of a mage's Sanctum. The room it stands in becomes the Sanctum of the mages assigned to it, rated by how impressive and how closed off it is.
A shadow standing up like a person. From a distance it could be anyone.
Light a spell pours into this place, bright as a sun lamp.
Power a spell feeds into the conduit here. Nobody can see where it comes from.
Symbols drawn on the ground for a spell. While they last, so does the spell; scuff them out and it ends.
What each update changed, newest first, as the grimoire shows it.
A player's ideas from the Workshop, and a few of our own. Each spell's page now lists its other buttons and its Reach effects.

- Golems and Eidolons clean the home area when idle, and take a standing order: haul, clean, mine, build, guard or follow. - Albedo and Without a Trace can take a corpse's taint off clothes; Shaping can wash an area and cut chunks into blocks; Albedo can turn slag into steel; Celestial Fire can feed the caster Mana. - Birth Spirit can make a servitor over a room, which reports what it did every 30 days. - Create Life can make a homunculus for two kinds of work. Bind Spirit can raise a fire, earth, water or air elemental. Golem can stand a rock wall up as a stone giant. A Familiar can help round the house.

- Thunderbolt, Telekinetic Strike and Piercing Earth have new energies, and any aimed damage spell can take a shape: line, cone, burst, ring or chain. Thunderbolt chains by default. - Telekinetic Strike can throw people back and knock them down. Ex Nihilo can raise a wall from nothing.

- Ex Nihilo can finish blueprints, State Change can raise rock and mountain, Transubstantiation can change the ground or make ore, Shifting the Odds can give a lucky seam. - Pocket Dimension picks its look, can last with a name and an upkeep, and doors can lead to any lasting pocket.

- A spirit made to serve keeps a grudge; any mage or Garou can bargain with one for a day's service instead. - Cleanse the Body can flush a vampire's blood out of a ghoul; Supernal Dispellation can silence a vampire's, werewolf's or hunter's powers for a while. - Self-Repairing Machine mends a linked person's gear from far away.
- Biotech: rewrite a gene, fill the blood, fill or drain a mechanoid, take a mechanoid. Royalty: open or close a psylink. Odyssey: molten ground, no breath needed, teleport to orbit.
- The enchanting table is 2x1, and its buttons draw it at its own shape.

- The Consilium and the Orders send requests: Mysterium readers come to a Library worth it, guests ask to learn a rote, an Arcanum dot or an Attainment, and some ask to be rescued. - By the host's Consilium Status the colony can host a cabal summit at 2, a Lex Magica hearing in its Sanctum at 3, the Consilium's assembly, and more.

- Obsession steps pay nothing on the way; resolving one gives two Arcane Beats and a Mana. - Scrying reaches any spot on the map, unseen too. - Towns and sites have better rooms, with beds only where people sleep. - A glossary of mages' words, underlined wherever an Awakened page uses them. - See [[RBN_Changes_20261114 the grimoire's own changes]]. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Only Scouring it out, at the cost of a lethal wound, takes it away. Abyssal Backlash Yes Something vast in the Abyss has noticed this mage. The next Paradox they risk rolls as many more dice as the number shown, and then this ends. Scouring ends it too. Left to lapse, it lets the Abyss into their Pattern. Abyssal Imago Yes The Abyss blurs this mage's picture of what their spells should be. Every spell takes as much more Reach as the number shown, which can bring Paradox where there was none. It ends when they cast a spell that risks no Paradox, when it's Scoured out, or when it lapses, and then the Abyss is in their Pattern. Abyssal scream Yes A scream from somewhere that isn't anywhere. It's still ringing. Acamoth Yes Something from the Abyss is riding this person. It whispers in a language nobody taught them, keeps them up at night, and turns them against their friends. In time it will stop hiding.Exorcism, Banishment or Annihilate Spirit can drive it out. Accelerated growth Yes A spell makes this creature's years pass many times faster. Accelerated work Yes Time runs fast for this person's hands. They work many times as fast. Accelerating growth This mage holds a spell that makes the plants of a place grow many times faster. Acceleration This person moves through the world as a blur. Active Mage Sight Yes This mage has opened their Mage Sight and sees what their open Arcana cover. Ordinary work and aim suffer while it's open. Aegis A spell hardens what this person wears. Alchemist's immunity Yes No poison, gas or fallout can touch this person. Alchemist's touch A spell makes poisons and toxic air wash off this person. All-round sight A spell lets this person see in every direction at once. Hungry or hurt, the animal's instincts may take over for a while. Apocalypse Yes A spell has torn the blindfold from this person's eyes. They see magic everywhere and can't look away. Augmented charisma A spell makes this person shine. Augmented intelligence A spell quickens this mind. Augmented manipulation A spell puts the right words in this person's mouth. They can work magic by imposing that higher world's truths on this one, and every spell an outsider sees risks Paradox. Balanced tools A spell makes this person's weapons and tools sit just right in the hand. Bare Yes A Dispel Magic tore this person's defences open. The next spell cast on them meets no resistance. Befuddled charisma Yes A spell sours this person's charm. Befuddled intelligence Yes A spell slows this mind. Befuddled manipulation Yes A spell trips this person's tongue. Body control A spell gives this person conscious hold of hunger, sleep, breath and healing. Body of the Lie This thing came out of the Abyss and wore the world's lies as a body. Ordinary weapons only half hurt it; magic hurts it in full. Every breaking mind, every spell that frays and every Paradox let loose nearby feeds it, and it grows. Bone armour A spell has closed a dead body's bones round this person as armour. Bone thrall A spell keeps this body on its feet to fight. It's fast, feels nothing and does no work. Wounds that would kill it or bring it down end the spell. When the spell ends it falls apart. Boon Luck runs this person's way. Each charge turns a hit into a miss, makes a thing a step better, saves a surgery or skips a mental break. Bound A spell has made this being solid and seen, and it serves the one who cast it. Breaking into a sanctum Yes This intruder is inside a mage's guarded Sanctum. Its traps, guns and wards slow them and spoil their aim. Burning A bound fire elemental. What it strikes catches fire, and it warms the room it stands in. Capping the well This mage holds a spell that wards the Essence of a place against anyone else drawing it. Caught in an anomaly Yes A Paradox anomaly holds this mage: the world around them keeps slipping out of true, and they can't move or think through it. Carried to a bed, away from where it broke, it lets go. Caught in time Yes This person moves a beat behind the world. They can't dodge anything. Clear sight Yes Rain, snow and fog don't spoil this person's aim. Clear thoughts A spell holds this mind still. No break can start while it lasts, and no derangement surfaces. Cloaked nimbus A spell dims this person's aura. To Supernal sight they look like any Sleeper. Co-located This mage holds a spell that lays two places on top of each other. Cold snap This mage holds a spell that covers a place in ice. Cold snap This mage holds a spell that freezes a room. Commanded A spell makes this spirit serve the one who cast it. Commanded to sleep Yes A spell ordered this person to sleep. They wake when it ends or something hurts them. Constant presence Whatever happens to time, this person stays as they are. Contagious Yes This person carries a sickness made by magic, and passes it to anyone close. Controlled healing Yes A spell lets this person's body close even deep wounds quickly. It turns blows less well until it passes. Craftsman's insight Yes A spell showed this person how a thing is meant to be used. They build and work as if they'd done it for years. Creating a truth This mage holds a spell that made a Hallow out of nothing. When it ends, the Hallow goes too. Cursed venom A Consilium mage laid a curse in this animal's venom. Each bite that lands drains a point of Mana from a mage and slows a spirit for an hour. Cutting power This mage holds a spell that keeps a power net switched off. Dazzled Yes A spell focuses light into this person's eyes. Deafened Yes The noise of a spell drowns out every other sound. Deafened by thunder Yes A thunderclap from a spell left this person's ears ringing. They hear nothing for now. Deafening noise This mage holds a spell that fills a place with deafening noise. Deathly stillness Yes This person's body has gone still as a corpse's. They can't move. Deep heat ward Yes A spell keeps the heat and cold off this person further than most could bear. Deep psychic daze Yes A psychic blow left this mind barely working. Deepening shadows This mage holds a spell that fills a place with darkness. Degraded dexterity Yes A spell makes this body's nerves misfire. Degraded stamina Yes A spell makes this body tire and break easily. Degraded strength Yes A spell has wasted this body's muscles. Destiny's Trail Her Long Road reaches anywhere in the world, and anyone she has a sympathetic link to. Devil's whisper Yes A mage's Nimbus flared near this person: a cold voice in the back of the head. Silver-tongued, but on edge. Dimming This mage holds a spell that keeps all light out of a place. Displaying power This mage holds a spell that lays the magic of a place out in the air to see. Divine intervention Yes Fate pushes this person toward a goal or away from it, and hexes them when they go the wrong way. Doom Yes Bad luck is piling up on this person. Every event the storyteller can send, what it means and what to do about it. Most can be switched off or made rarer one by one in the mod settings. Event Kind From day Again after What happens A gathering to host: Arrow war council Event 30 days The Adamantine Arrow offers you a war council to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: cabal summit Event 30 days A Consilium writes to offer you a cabal summit to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: convocation Event 30 days The Consilium offers you a convocation to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Free Council vote Event 30 days The Free Council offers you a vote to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Guardians review Event 30 days The Guardians of the Veil offer you a review to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Ladder audience Event 30 days The Silver Ladder offers you an audience to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Lex Magica hearing Event 30 days A Consilium writes to offer you a Lex Magica hearing to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Mysterium symposium Event 30 days The Mysterium offers you a symposium to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: the Consilium's assembly Event 30 days A Consilium writes to offer you its assembly to host. At most once a year. A mage asks for a lesson Event 15 A mage asks one of yours for a lesson: a dot more of an Arcanum or the next Attainment of a Legacy. Pays Consilium standing. A mage caught in an anomaly Event 20 A Consilium mage lies senseless at the edge of your land inside a Paradox anomaly of their own making. Carry them to a bed and it lets go: Consilium standing for your highest mage, and they owe a service. A mage chased by Seers Event 20 A mage with Seers on their heels asks to be let in. Saved, they owe your mages a service. A mage in a long trance Event 20 A mage going into a long trance asks you to guard their body while their mind is away. Pays Consilium standing. A maimed mage asks for a doctor Event 25 A maimed mage asks your doctor to make them whole. Pays Consilium standing. A Sleepwalker's skill lent Event 25 A mage asks to borrow one of your Sleepwalkers for their skill for a while. They walk back in at the end. Abyssal incursion Big threat 30 Rarely, while you have a mage, the Abyss finds a thin place on its own: a Gulmoth walks in from the map's edge, or an Acamoth slips into a colonist and nobody notices. Most Abyssal entities come from released Paradox instead. An apostate begs shelter Event 30 An apostate, a mage outside the Consilium, begs shelter for a while. Kept safe, it repays you. An apprentice to foster Event 30 The Consilium asks you to foster an apprentice and teach them. Pays Consilium standing. An Imbued Item commission Event 25 A mage commissions an Imbued Item from your mages. Pays Consilium standing. An order for tass Event 15 A mage orders tass, Mana in solid form, from your storage. Pays Consilium standing. Banisher ambush Big threat 15 Banishers wait by the road for a caravan with a mage in it. A mage away from home is what they hunt best. Banisher raid Big threat 25 A Banisher, a mage who hates magic, raids with her followers. She strips your mages' spells and goes for their souls. Only while you keep a mage. Bribed trader Event 15 An ordinary-looking caravan the Seers have bribed, with a cursed Imbued Item among its goods. Nothing tells it apart until it goes off, unless a mage looks with Focused Mage Sight. Cabal call Event 10 days A cabal of the nearest friendly Consilium calls: it visits, asks for help, wants a share of a Hallow, sends a mage who asks to join, or asks a colony mage to sit with it. Hallow drained Event 20 The Seers drain one of your Hallows overnight and put it to sleep, then raid a few days later to take the place. Hallow Dance can wake it again. Hunted mage Event For a colony with no mage: someone who just Awakened comes running, with the Seers of the Throne or the Banishers on their trail. Take them in and they join as an apostate, and the hunters raid a day or two later. This is the usual way a colony meets the mages. Mysterium readers Event 15 Mysterium readers ask to study in your Library. Pays Consilium standing. Proscribed Big threat 20 days One of the Proscribed passes near the colony. A mage that has never crossed you walks through unless you harm it; one that has, or a Gulmoth, comes for the colony. Raiders bought Event 30 The Seers buy a hostile faction. For a year its raids bring a Seer along who keeps the raiders on a leash, and the first comes within days. Seer raid Big threat 20 A Seer of the Throne raids with her sleeper thralls, sent by the nearest Pylon's Ministry. Down the Seer and the thralls break and run. Only while you have a mage and none who serves the Seers. Seer recruiter Event 30 days A letter for an unhappy mage (Wisdom 5 or less, or cast out by the Consilium) from the Seers of the Throne, offering a Ministry's rotes, protection and silver to switch sides. Seers raid for grimoires Big threat 30 Once your Library is worth a reader's trip, a Seer of the Throne comes with her thralls for your grimoires. They make for the shelves and attack whatever holds a grimoire or an Artifact. Down the Seer and the thralls break. The Arrow asks for a guard Event 20 The Adamantine Arrow asks one of its mages in the colony to stand guard. Pays Order standing. A Hallow claimed Travel to a Hallow the Seers have taken and scour it, so a cabal can claim it. A Paradox in the making Lend one of your mages to a cabal for some days, to quiet a mage who works vulgar magic in front of Sleepers. The tome hunt Travel to the Banisher camp that holds a tome a cabal has tracked down, break it and take the book. An envoy of the Consilium Host one or two of the Consilium's mages at your colony for a day and a half and keep them all alive. Seers and Banishers may attack while they stay. Called to the Consilium Lend one of your mages to the Consilium for 4 days. They leave when you accept and come home when the working is done. Reclaiming the Hallow Travel to a Hallow the Seers of the Throne hold and clear out their thralls. The Consilium shares the tass the Hallow gives.
