Name What it is A quiet season Go a whole season without calling up a Paradox. Climb the Watchtower Buy a dot in one of your Path's two Ruling Arcana. Grow wiser Raise your Wisdom by a dot. Keep the Veil Go a whole season without calling up a Paradox. Learn a rote Learn a rote from a grimoire, a teacher or the Consilium. Raise an Arcanum Buy a dot in any Arcanum. Rise in Status Gain a dot of Status in your Order or the Consilium. Something new Learn a Praxis: a spell of your own making. Tend a Hallow Draw Mana from a Hallow with two Oblations. Two Mysteries Meet two Mysteries you haven't met before. Uncover a Mystery Meet a Mystery you haven't met before. Win a Duel Arcane Beat another mage in the Duel Arcane. Write it down Scribe one of your rotes into a grimoire.

Name What it is Retainer Sleepwalker servants: mortals who can watch magic without forgetting it. Each dot keeps one in a town near the colony, who does the mage a favour once a week as a pulled string does. A Sleepwalker never counts as a witness to vulgar magic.
Name What it is Pocket dimension A small world a mage made, with nothing in it they didn't bring.

Name What it is Adamantine Arrow war council Arrow mages plan their season at the colony, then test each other in duels of skill in a ring. Cabal summit Two cabals of the Consilium bring their quarrel over a Hallow to the colony, to settle it on neutral ground. Convocation Mages of several Consiliums meet at the colony, agree on a common war on a Seer Pylon, and set out from it. Free Council vote The Free Council votes at the colony on a new rule for the Consilium, and the colony's vote is counted. Guardians of the Veil review Guardians walk every room of the colony and rate how well it keeps the Mysteries from Sleepers. Lex Magica hearing The Consilium holds a hearing under the Lex Magica at the colony, with the host on the bench in its own Sanctum. Mysterium symposium Mysterium mages bring their finds to the colony's Library to compare them; the best find earns Status. Silver Ladder audience An elder of the Silver Ladder holds an audience at the colony, where its mage pleads a cause. The Consilium's assembly The Consilium meets at the colony: the officers report, a Duel Arcane is settled at the Hallow, and a vote is taken.

Name What it is Ambitious They want friends in the right places. They court the colony's mages, ask for rivals' Hallows, and remember who said no. Militant They hunt the Seers and the Abyss's servants, and they silence mages who are careless in front of Sleepers. Reckless They want Mana, and they want it now. A Hallow they're refused is a Hallow they'll send you to take. Reclusive They keep to themselves and are seldom heard from. Now and then they want an Artifact back. Scholarly They want books, quiet and good company to argue with. They ask you to find lost Artifacts.

Name What it is The Bearers of the Eternal Voice Mastigos persuaders who study the words that move crowds, and the ones that move them against their will. The Eleventh Question Moros investigators who believe every death, theft and lie leaves a trace in time for someone patient enough to read it. The Orphans of Proteus Thyrsus shapeshifters who hold that no body, human or beast, is the one they were born for. The Perfected Adepts Obrimos monks who train the body until it is fit to hold the Supernal. The Walkers in Mists Acanthus pathfinders who know every road through the wild and a few that aren't on any map.

Name What it is Adamant Hand Adamantine Arrow martial arts: a melee blow struck just before a spell counts as an Order tool. Between the Ticks She acts at the perfect moment: once an hour, a die more on a spell. Cabal Theme Her cabal has a shared look, motto or ritual that she wears as part of her magical persona. While she's in the colony's cabal it counts as a persona Yantra in her spells. Destiny Her thread stands out in the skein of Fate. A point a day a dot, spent by itself: an even chance to turn aside a mental break, a bad wound when she is already hurt, or a failed surgery she performs. Familiar A spirit, ghost or Goetia is bound to her for good. It follows her, and she can draw on its Essence as Mana. Two dots for a Rank 1 being, four for Rank 2. Fast Spells Her aimed spells move like bullets: no one can dodge them. High Speech She knows the High Speech of the Supernal, and can chant it as a Yantra in her spells without belonging to an Order. Lex Magica The laws of the Pentacle as symbols she wields: half her Status, rounded up, is a Yantra for spells that find out or command. Mana Sensitivity She feels Mana before she sees it: tass near her shows itself, once a day. Occultation She is hard to read: a die off Focused Mage Sight on her for each dot. Potent Nimbus Her Nimbus hits witnesses as if she had two more Gnosis a dot, and she adds her dots to flaring it on purpose. Retainer Sleepwalkers who work for her: mortals who can stand to watch magic without forgetting it. Each lives in a town near the colony and does her a favour once a week. Shadow Name A magical persona with its own name and symbols. It is a Yantra worth a die a dot in every spell. Techné Free Council practice: any machine-age thing she carries is an Order tool for her Order's spells.

Name What it is Adamantine Arrow Warrior-mages who hold that magic is conflict. They guard the Consilium and answer its calls to fight. Free Council The youngest Order, who look for magic in the made world: machines, cities, the work of Sleepers' hands. Guardians of the Veil The Order of secrets. They keep magic hidden from Sleepers and hunt down the mages who show it. Mysterium Scholars and keepers of lore. They hunt for Artifacts, grimoires and places of power, and keep them safe. Seers of the Throne Mages who serve the Exarchs, the tyrants who rule the Supernal from the far side of the Abyss. They hold the world's Sleepers in their sleep and pay well for the work. Silver Ladder Would-be rulers of the Awakened, who mean to lead mages and, one day, the world.

Name What it is Acanthus Enchanters. Their souls reached Arcadia, the realm of fae and fortune, and signed the Watchtower of the Lunargent Thorn. They see the threads of luck and time, and are poorest at the plain push of Forces. Mastigos Warlocks. Their souls reached Pandemonium, the realm of demons and desire, and signed the Watchtower of the Iron Gauntlet. They master space and the mind, and struggle with the stubborn stuff of Matter. Moros Necromancers. Their souls reached Stygia, the realm of the dead and of treasure, and signed the Watchtower of the Lead Coin. They command matter and death, and are blind to the world of Spirit. Obrimos Theurgists. Their souls reached the Aether, the realm of angels and fire, and signed the Watchtower of the Golden Key. They wield raw Forces and the Prime stuff of magic itself, and shy from Death. Thyrsus Shamans. Their souls reached the Primal Wild, the realm of beasts and spirits, and signed the Watchtower of the Stone Book. They rule Life and Spirit, and find the Mind of others hard to reach.

Name What it is Careless Doesn't mind who sees magic done. Its work is riskier, and it pays a third more for it. Mystery-hungry Wants to know everything. Asks for lore, and pays in what it knows: Arcane Experience for the mages who helped.

Name What it is Abyssal breach A shrine where something tore through from the Abyss. The air there is wrong, and what came through hasn't left. Banisher camp A camp of Banishers, mages who hate what they are and kill the others for it. Held Hallow A Hallow the Seers of the Throne found first. Their thralls guard it while the Seers drink its Mana. Seer Pylon A house near the town where the Pylon's Seers meet, guarded by their thralls.
Name What it is Cut out lodged thing Cut out what a spell shoved into this body, so the wounds can heal.

Name What it is Apostates Three people saw the Watchtowers in the same season and woke up afterwards with their names written on stone they had never touched. Nobody came to explain it. There is no Consilium out here that knows them, no mentor and no Order. They have each other and the little they can do. Note: three new mages at Gnosis 1, with no Hallow and no friends among the Awakened. Consilium exiles Two mages broke the Lex Magica and were cast out. They took what they could carry from their old Sanctum and went far enough that nobody would follow them. The Consilium remembers them, and its next Herald won't be friendly. Note: two exiled mages with no Status and a Sanctum focus. The Pentacle starts out cold toward you. Cunning folk People came to you for a cure, a charm or a lost cow found, and you usually helped. One night you saw what stands behind the world, and since then your charms work a little too well. The priest started asking questions, so you and your family moved on to a place with a Hallow and no neighbours.Note: one mage and two mortal family members, with a Hallow of rating 1. Medieval arms and the old crafts; research is as normal. Hallow founders Two mages followed the pull of Mana for weeks and found it here: a Hallow, free and unclaimed, welling up out of the ground. They mean to build around it. The Seers of the Throne mean to take it, and they know where it is. Note: two mages and a Hallow of rating 2. The Seers come before the season is out. Hermetic scholars You copied grimoires by candlelight in your order's library for years. Then you and a fellow scholar took one tome you weren't meant to take and left by night, with an apprentice who wouldn't stay behind. Now you need a library of your own.Note: two mages and one apprentice, with a tome and a Sanctum focus. Medieval arms and the old crafts; research is as normal. The lone Awakened One of you went to sleep ordinary and woke up able to see what the world is made of. The others still can't, and every spell cast in front of them pulls at the Abyss. Somewhere a Consilium has already noticed, and a letter is on its way. Note: one mage among sleepers. The Consilium writes within a few days.

Name What it is Councilor Sits on the Hierarch's council and votes on what the Consilium does. Herald Carries the Consilium's word and calls mages to its hearings. Hierarch Rules the Consilium and leads its council. Won only by the Consilium's election or a cabal's plot, never handed out. Interfector Deals with the Consilium's enemies: Banishers, Seers and mages who break the Lex Magica. Provost Keeps the Consilium's goods, its Tass and its debts. Sentinel Guards the Consilium's Hallows and its meetings.

Name What it is The Atlas of Unfolded Rooms An atlas of houses whose rooms don't fit inside them. Some of the maps are folded in ways paper can't be folded. The Banefather's Liturgy A liturgy for a church that worshipped the spirits of what people hate. The responses are written for a congregation that never sings back. The Book of the Seventh Storm The diary of an Adamantine Arrow who counted the storms she called and wrote the seventh down as a set of rotes. The pages smell of ozone. The Clockmaker's Heresy A clockmaker's notebook full of escapements that should not work. He wrote that time is a spring, and that a spring can be wound by hand. He died old at forty. The Gambler's Concordance A gambler's ledger of every bet he won and lost, and why. By the end it stops being about cards. The Lantern Scrolls Twelve scrolls in a lead tube, written by a Mysterium lamplighter who swore that Mana could be thrown like light. Half the scrolls are scorched at the edges. The Leaden Codex A book with lead covers too heavy to hold open on one hand. Its author believed every metal remembers being ore and can be made to hurt like it. The Mirror Psalter A book of psalms with a small mirror set into the cover. Each psalm is a way to make a mind sing someone else's words. The Ossuary of Saint Absalom Bound in vellum the colour of old teeth. The monks who kept it lived in a charnel house and wrote down what the bones taught them. Its last owner is said to still be reading it. The Red Herbal A healer's herbal with every plant drawn in red ink. Read in order it teaches mending; read the other way it teaches the opposite. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. The factions, the kinds of people and the creatures this mod adds.

Faction What it is Agents Well-dressed people with good papers and blank-faced followers. Whoever employs them pays on time and never signs anything. Apostates Mages who Awakened on their own and have joined no Order.Every Awakening is a journey to one of the five Watchtowers, where the mage writes their name and comes back able to rewrite the world. Most are found by a mentor and brought into one of the Pentacle Orders, which keep the knowledge of Atlantis. Apostates belong to none of them. They are free of the Orders' politics and their teaching both, and every Consilium watches them, some to recruit them, some to make sure they don't become a problem. Consilium exiles Mages cast out of their Consilium for breaking the Lex Magica.A Consilium is the government of the Awakened in a region: a Hierarch, the councillors of the Orders, and a Herald who carries its word to every mage it claims. Exile is the punishment one step short of death. The exiles took what they could from their old Sanctum and went far enough that nobody followed. A Consilium remembers its exiles, though, and its Herald will come. Cunning folk A village wise one who is more than they look, and the family who keep their secret.In the old villages people went to the cunning man or the wise woman for cures, charms and lost things found. Most of them knew herbs and nothing more. This one Awakened, saw the Supernal behind the world and can bend it a little. The family helps with the herbs and says nothing about the rest. Hallow founders Mages who found an unclaimed Hallow and mean to build their Sanctum around it.A Hallow is a place where Mana wells up out of the world, and Mana is what lets a mage cast past their limits, heal the Pattern and make what lasts. A cabal with a Hallow has power, and everyone who wants it knows where to look: rival cabals, the Consilium that claims the land, and the Seers of the Throne, who serve the Exarchs and take Hallows to keep them from anyone else. Hermetic scholars Mages of the old learning who left their order with a book.In the old orders, mages studied in towers and cloisters, copying grimoires by hand and teaching one apprentice at a time. Knowledge was hoarded, and the master's word was law. These scholars broke with their order over one tome and mean to found a library of their own around it. Lone Awakened A mage who has just Awakened among Sleepers.Sleepers are everyone who never Awakened. Their disbelief is a force of its own: magic cast in front of them can tear open a hole to the Abyss, and they forget what they saw anyway. A new mage has to learn this, and the rest of the Lex Magica, before a Consilium decides they are a danger to the Mysteries. Scholars A quiet circle of learned households that keep to their libraries and their own rules. They trade books and curios and say little about what they study. Zealots Grim people who travel light and ask about strange lights and people who talk to themselves. They say they're cleaning something up.

0 A thing from the Abyss, the nothing between the world and the Supernal. It has no body of its own, so it wears one made of every lie the world tells, and it looks wrong in ways the eye slides off. It hates everything real, and it feeds on fear and broken magic.
0 A small body a mage has grown out of nothing and set to work. There is nobody inside it: it hauls, cleans, builds, guards and fights as it's told, and when the spell ends it comes apart.

Every setting in Options, Mod settings, The Rim by Night, with what it does. Setting What it does Chance of an Awakening How likely a colonist is to Awaken at a qualifying moment: coming back from near death, an eclipse or psychic drone, losing a lover or bonded animal, a masterwork, a big research breakthrough, a mental break that ends in catharsis. The mod's chance is 2%, doubled for the psychically sensitive. Mages before the Awakening slows Once the colony has this many mages, the next one Awakens at most once a season. A mentor's lessons aren't held back by this. Paradox dice Dice added to or taken from every Paradox roll, once something has put a Paradox die in it. Acts of Hubris cost Wisdom When off, mages never roll to lose Wisdom, and so never become Megalomaniacal, Rampant or Mad. Keep snapshots for Corridors of Time While a colony mage with Time 3 knows Corridors of Time, the game saves itself to a hidden folder now and then, so the spell can turn the world back. Saving can stutter a big colony for a moment. When off, Corridors of Time has nothing to go back to. Hours between snapshots How often the hidden snapshot is taken, in game hours. Fewer hours means more moments to go back to and more saving. Chance of a ghost How likely someone who dies badly (murdered, executed, burned, starved or frozen) is to leave a ghost behind. The mod's chance is 5%. Quiet spirits on home maps A few harmless spirits live unseen on each colony map, for Spirit magic to find. When off, the only spirits are the ones a spell calls up or Garou brings. Walking on walls Transform Life's wall-crawling and Alter Direction let a pawn walk over walls and rock. This changes how those pawns find their way, so turn it off if another pathing mod (Pathfinding Framework, Vehicles) has trouble with it. When off, the spells still cast but nobody climbs. The Lex Magica The Consilium hears of colony mages' crimes and summons them to answer. Off, nobody is ever charged. Spell camera shake How hard big spells shake the camera: a thunderbolt, an earthquake, Paradox. At 0% the camera stays still. Spell sky flashes Big spells flash the sky in their colour, and storms and curses tint it while they last. Off, the sky keeps its own light. Mage looks A selected mage shows the lights of their spells, their Nimbus glow and the marks of lasting spells, and Hallows show their ring and motes. Another group's mage shows them only while one of yours has Mage Sight open. Off, none of these are drawn. Casts still show. Arcane Experience gained How much each Arcane Beat counts. At 50%, two Arcane Beats count as one; at 200%, one counts as two. Dramatic failures for Arcane Beats A drafted mage's failed cast becomes a dramatic failure, with its Paradox, for an Arcane Beat. The autocast never does this. Chance of a Hallow How likely a newly made map is to have a Hallow on it. The mod's chance is 12.5%, about one map in eight. Long-Term Nimbus Mages of Gnosis 6 and up now and then cause small strange happenings near them: breakdowns, weather, wandering animals, lucky finds or bad dreams, by Path. The Proscribed A handful of enemies of every mage roam the world map: Banisher killers, Seer agents and Gulmoth loose from the Abyss. They roam either way, but only a colony with a mage is told of them, sees them on the map or earns anything for one. Turned off, they leave the world map; turned back on, a new list arrives in one letter. Disbelief gain Scales how much the colony's Disbelief rises for each Sleeper who leaves having seen vulgar magic. Disbelief fading Scales how fast the colony's Disbelief falls back each day as Sleepers forget. Serendipity coincidences Serendipity with nothing to find makes a small coincidence instead, once in five days for each goal: a wanderer who asks to join, herbal medicine just outside, a forgotten stash. Off, it finds nothing. Counterspells A mage with Active Sight up who isn't busy casting counters an enemy's spell cast in sight, in a Clash of Wills. Colonists only do it when drafted. A hunted mage comes A colony with no mage gets a stranger who has just Awakened, with the Seers of the Throne or the Banishers on their trail, some time between day 15 and day 40, and again every 30 to 60 days until one is taken in. Taken in, the stranger joins as a mage and the hunters raid within a day or two. Off, the stranger still turns up now and then as an ordinary event. Awakening gives a psylink A colonist who Awakens, or starts the game Awakened, gets a first psylink level if they have none, for psycast mods. Further levels come from psytrainers as usual. Cantrips Every mage knows a cantrip for each Arcanum they have a dot in: a small aimed spell of one wound, with a range of Gnosis x10 cells. Cantrips are obvious and roll Paradox as usual. Off, they're hidden and can't be cast. Show spell areas When a lasting area spell's circle and name show on the ground. "When selected" shows it while its mage is selected or the mouse is over it, and always under Mage Sight of its Arcanum. A spell let go with a dot of Willpower shows only under Mage Sight. Mana from Hallows How much Mana and tass a Hallow makes each day, as a share of its rating. *The dark thickens until a lamp barely reaches across it.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: It goes so dark that everyone in it who isn't on the caster's side sees at half their sight. Shots into or out of it miss as they would through smoke - Vampires: A vampire inside doesn't burn by day - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Darkness as cover. Enemies in it see at half range and shots through it miss as if through smoke, while your people see normally. A vampire inside doesn't burn by day, which makes it a daytime shelter for Kindred allies. The Reach blinds everyone else in it.

*Ghost-stuff takes the shape the mage gives it.* - Target: A lump of ectoplasm in sight - Effect: It becomes a simple thing made of ectoplasm: a tool, a weapon, clothes or furniture - Lasts: The Duration, then the thing is gone - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Turns a lump of ectoplasm (made with the Ectoplasm spell) into a simple item: a tool, a weapon, clothes or furniture. It's gone when the spell ends, so it's for stopgaps, not stock.

*The body tells the mage how it died.* - Target: One corpse in sight - Effect: A letter: how long ago it died, and up to 1 causes of death (one per Potency). If whoever last fought them is still on the map, the letter points them out - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Corpse Mask on the body shows its false cause How to use it: Read a corpse: when it died and what killed it. If the killer is still on the map, the letter points them out. A body under Corpse Mask shows the false cause.

*A cantrip of Death. A breath of the grave's cold.* - Target: One target in range (Gnosis x10 cells), with an attack roll - Effect: The cold of the grave: one bashing wound and a small chill - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A cantrip, only with the Cantrips setting on: one wound from range, for a mage with a single dot of Death.

*Shadows gather into a shape that isn't there.* - Target: A spot in sight - Effect: A shadow shaped like a person stands there, and enemies nearby go to see who it is - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A decoy. A shadow shaped like a person stands at a spot, and nearby enemies go to check it out. Use it to pull raiders out of cover or into a trap.

*The mage reads the scars on a soul.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: A letter with 1 facts about their soul (one per Potency), from: Awakened or Sleeper, another kind of supernatural, a ghost's or spirit's Rank, whether the soul is whole or torn, whether a mage rides them, a Paradox Condition - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Reads a soul: mage or Sleeper, what other kind of supernatural, and whether the soul is whole, torn or ridden by another mage. A cheap check on a suspicious visitor.

*The mage sees the dead who linger, and they see the mage.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Ghosts around the caster show, with their Rank - Graves: Each body or grave within 24 cells teaches the caster 300 XP of the dead one's best skill, once per body - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Shows nearby ghosts and their Rank, and it's a training spell: each body or grave within 24 cells teaches the caster 300 XP of the dead person's best skill, once per body. Walk it past your graveyard.

*The body lies about how it died.* - Target: One corpse in sight - Effect: It seems to have died of something else, picked from a list, and it looks freshly dead: the rot starts over - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Forensic Gaze sees through it How to use it: Hides how someone died, and makes the corpse look fresh (the rot starts over). Cover up a killing, or keep a body fresh for a while. Forensic Gaze sees through it.

*Wood rots, iron rusts, cloth falls to threads.* - Target: One item, building or mechanoid in sight - Effect: It loses 10% of its hit points (10% per Potency) - Mechanoid: Its plating rusts instead: armour -10% (10% per Potency) for a day - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Its toughness, each dot takes 1 off the Potency How to use it: Rots an item or a building, or rusts a mechanoid's plating so your weapons hurt it more for a day. Tough materials resist.

*The mage draws ghost-stuff out of their own body.* - Target: The caster's feet - Effect: A lump of ectoplasm appears. Ectoplasmic Shaping can make things of it. Slime spreads round it and slows whoever walks through, like deep mud - Lasts: The Duration, then it's gone - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Makes a lump of ectoplasm at the caster's feet, for Ectoplasmic Shaping to turn into items. The slime around it slows anyone walking through like deep mud, which works as a quick trap in a doorway.

*The dead slide off the subject.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: A ghost's Numina and other mages' Death spells must win a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power) to affect them - Mood: The dead don't trouble them: no bad mood from corpses, and deaths weigh half as much - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Protection from ghosts and enemy Death magic, and the dead stop bothering the person: no bad mood from corpses, and deaths hurt their mood half as much. Good on a doctor, a grave digger or a butcher. The Reach also halves ghosts' blows.

*A ghost's own stuff becomes a blade or a coat of mail.* - Target: One ghost in sight - Effect: Armed and armoured with its own ephemera: melee damage x1.5, and +30% sharp and blunt armour - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: Arms and armours a ghost with its own ghost-stuff. Cast it on a ghost that fights for you. On an enemy ghost it makes things worse.

*The soul holds fast to its body.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Any spell that would tear out their soul must win a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power). Mental break threshold -5% - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Protects someone's soul from being torn out by Sever Soul, and makes them a little steadier against mental breaks.

*A bottle becomes a prison for a soul.* - Target: One loose soul in sight - Effect: It's held in place and can't drift home - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Holds a loose soul (one torn out by Sever Soul) in place so it can't drift home and return to its body.

*The light of magic around the subject goes out.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Hunters and other kinds' senses take them for a Sleeper - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Hides a supernatural from hunters and from other kinds' senses: they read as a plain Sleeper. Cast it before a hunter cell visits.

*Breath and heartbeat stop, and the subject passes for dead.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They pass for dead, and nobody attacks them until they attack. Nobody attacks them until they attack, and hunters' sight passes over them. Learned as a rote, it casts itself when the mage goes down, if she has the Mana, which can save her life.

*The mage's hands close on what the living can't hold.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They can strike ghosts and anyone in Twilight - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Lets a fighter hit ghosts and anyone in Twilight. Cast it on your melee fighter when a ghost attacks.

*Footprints, dirt and smears never happen.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They leave no dirt or tracks behind and nothing a hunter can trace. Harming or killing a faction's people costs no goodwill - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Leave no evidence: no dirt, no tracks, nothing a hunter can trace, and hurting or killing a faction's people costs no goodwill. Cast it before a raid on a settlement. Cleaning a dead man's clothes is Lift the Taint, a Matter spell.

*Worked from Shadow Crafting, Death Weaving. The bones of a corpse come out and close round the caster as armour, and the body is left a dry skeleton.* - Target: One corpse in sight - Effect: Its bones close round the caster as armour: +12% sharp and blunt armour. The corpse is left a skeleton - Lasts: The Duration, then the bones fall away - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Armour from a corpse in sight, +12% sharp and blunt a Potency, for the Duration. The corpse is left a skeleton, so it can't be raised or cast on again. Comes with Shadow Crafting's rote.

*Worked from Quicken Corpse, Death Weaving. The dead get up to fight, fast and tireless, and fall apart when the fight is over.* - Target: One corpse in sight - Effect: It rises at once to fight for the colony: fast, tireless, feels no pain, does no work - Lasts: The Duration, then it falls apart - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: The fighter's Quicken Corpse: the body rises fast and sure-handed, does no work, and falls apart quietly when the spell ends. Comes with Quicken Corpse's rote.

*Frost spreads over the ground in a breath.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: The ground is slick with ice: everyone in it who isn't on the caster's side moves at 60% speed - Frostbite: Those on the ice may get frostbite on their fingers and toes, a 4% chance (4% per Potency) every few seconds - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Ices the ground: enemies on it move at 60% speed and may get frostbite. Your own side isn't slowed. Good across a raid's approach.

*The mage tears at a ghost's Corpus.* - Target: One ghost in sight, with an attack roll, in Twilight or not - Effect: 8 blunt damage (8 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss, and a miss lands within a few cells on whoever is there How to use it: An attack that hits ghosts, whether they're manifested or hiding in Twilight. It rolls to hit.

*The mage feeds on a life as it leaks away.* - Target: One person with an open wound, by touch - Effect: The caster takes 1 Mana from them (one per Potency), and each Mana tears the wound wider - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher) How to use it: Takes Mana from someone who's bleeding, and makes the wound worse with each point. Cruel and an Act of Hubris, but it works on a downed enemy when you're out of Mana.

*A doorway the living can walk through into Twilight.* - Target: A spot in sight - Effect: A gate stands there. Whoever walks through takes Twilight form: no harm reaches them, and they can't harm or work. Walking through again brings them back - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A gate into Twilight. Walking through makes you safe from all harm (but unable to fight or work); walking through again brings you back. Use it as a panic room in a fight.

*The mage calls, and the dead come.* - Target: The caster - Effect: The nearest ghost on the map comes and stays near the caster. With none, the newest dead raise one - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Calls the nearest ghost on the map. If there are none, the most recently dead raise one. Follow it with Revenant or a familiar spell to make it useful.

*Worked from Rotting Flesh, Death Perfecting. Hands of shadow rise from the ground to tear and hold. A lost rote from the Ossuary.* - Target: One target in range, with an attack roll - Effect: Claws of shadow rise under them: 1 cut wounds (one per Potency), and they're held fast for 1 seconds - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Cut wounds and a hold of a second a Potency, so the next aimed spell can't be dodged. A lost rote, taught only by the Ossuary.

*Worked from Shadow Crafting, Death Weaving. Shadow worked into a weapon's edge leaves the cold of the grave in each wound.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Each hit leaves a grave cold: the wounded heal 10% slower for a day. Their weapon glows and every swing and shot leaves a trail - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Every wound the wielder deals heals slower for a day, up to half as fast at Potency 5. Comes with Shadow Crafting's rote.

*The dead get up and go to work.* - Target: One corpse in sight - Effect: It rises and joins the colony: slow, needs no food or sleep, and hauls, mines, cleans, cuts plants and builds. An animal corpse follows the caster - Lasts: The Duration, then it falls apart - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Raises a corpse as a slow worker: no food, no sleep, hauls, mines, cleans, cuts plants and builds. An animal corpse follows the caster instead. It falls apart when the spell ends. It's an Act of Hubris and your colonists may not like it.

*The mage feeds a ghost strength.* - Target: One ghost in sight - Effect: It heals 2 wounds (2 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Heals a ghost: your summoned or revenant ally after a fight.

*Flesh sloughs and sickens.* - Target: One person in sight, with an attack roll - Effect: 8 blunt damage as spreading rot (8 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss, and a miss lands within a few cells on whoever is there - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A Death attack as spreading rot. It rolls to hit. The Reach makes the target stink, which puts people off them.

*The mage tears a sleeper's soul out of them.* - Target: One Sleeper in sight, or the body of one not yet buried (the soul stays in it until then) - Effect: Their soul comes out: Soulless, then Enervated after a week, then a Thrall after a month. One already Soulless goes straight to Enervated - The soul: It lies at their feet and drifts home in a day unless jarred - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Resolve, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll for any mage) How to use it: Tears out a Sleeper's soul. Without it they slowly fall apart: Soulless, then Enervated after a week, then a Thrall after a month. The soul lies at their feet and drifts back in a day unless you hold it with Soul Jar. It's an Act of Hubris for every mage, whatever their Wisdom. The Reaches skip straight to the later stages.

*Shadow hardens into a thing that can be held.* - Target: A spot in sight - Effect: A tool, weapon, clothes or furniture of solid shadow appears there - Lasts: The Duration, then it's gone - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Makes a simple item of solid shadow: a tool, weapon, clothes or furniture. No ectoplasm needed, unlike Ectoplasmic Shaping. It's gone when the spell ends.

*Worked from Withering, Death Unraveling. A dead body made a bomb of its own bones. A lost rote from the Ossuary.* - Target: One corpse in sight - Effect: It bursts in a spray of bone: 1 piercing wounds (one per Potency) to every enemy within a few cells. The corpse is used up - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Turns a corpse into a bone bomb that hits every enemy round it. A lost rote, taught only by the Ossuary.

*Strength drains out of a limb.* Enervation - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Their manipulation drops to 30%: they can barely use their arms - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Stamina, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist Enervation: Legs - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Their moving drops to 30%: they can barely walk - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Stamina, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: Cripples without wounding. Arms: they can barely use their hands, so shooting and fighting suffer. Legs: they can barely walk, which is great for catching someone who runs. The Reach immobilizes them.

*The mage unmakes a ghost's hold on the world.* - Target: One ghost in sight. With Mind 4 or Spirit 4, Goetia and spirits too - Effect: A manifested ghost fades back into Twilight. One already in Twilight is laid to rest - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Gets rid of a ghost: a manifested one fades back into Twilight, one already there is laid to rest for good. With Mind 4 or Spirit 4 it works on Goetia and spirits too.

*Worked from Withering, Death Unraveling. The target's life withers, and the caster drinks what's left. A lost rote from the Ossuary.* - Target: One target in range, with an attack roll - Effect: The flesh withers: 1 lethal wounds (one per Potency), and half of what it deals heals the caster's worst wounds. Needs Life 2 as well as Death - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Half the harm it does heals the caster. Needs Life 2. A lost rote, taught only by the Ossuary.

*The mage gives a ghost a body to fight with.* - Target: One ghost in sight. With Mind 4 or Spirit 4, Goetia and spirits too - Effect: It manifests, solid and seen, and fights for the caster - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Gives a ghost a solid body and has it fight for you. Pair it with Ghost Summons. With Mind 4 or Spirit 4 it works on Goetia and spirits too.

*The mage becomes a shadow on the wall.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Twilight form: no physical harm reaches them and they pass through doors, but they can't harm, work or carry. Spells still work - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Death's version of Twilit Body: no physical harm reaches them and they walk through doors, but they can't hit, work or carry. Spells still work, so a mage can cast safely in a fight.

*Flesh dries and dies.* - Target: One person in sight, with an attack roll - Effect: 8 damage as withering (8 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss, and a miss lands within a few cells on whoever is there - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Death's big attack. It rolls to hit. The Reach makes the wounds aggravated, which heal very slowly.

*A thing becomes a ghost's tie to the world.* - Target: One item or building in sight - Effect: It becomes a ghost's anchor, and the nearest ghost moves its haunting there. The ghost guards it, going for the caster's enemies within 5 cells - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Gives a ghost a new anchor, and the nearest ghost moves its haunting there. The ghost guards it and attacks your enemies within 5 cells: a ghostly guard for a gate or a vault.

*A well opens down toward the Underworld.* - Target: A spot in sight - Effect: A gate to the Underworld opens. Death spells cast near it roll 2 more dice - Ghosts: One climbs out each day, some of them angry - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Opens a gate to the Underworld. Death spells near it get 2 more dice, but a ghost climbs out every day, and some are angry. Strong for a Death mage, risky for the colony.

*The mage shapes a ghost from someone's echo.* - Target: One person or corpse in sight - Effect: A Rank 1 ghost, an echo of them, appears and serves the caster - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Makes a ghost from a person's or a corpse's echo: a Rank 1 servant (Rank 2 with the Reach).

*The mage turns back the clock on wounds and wear.* - Target: One person or item in sight - Effect: On a person, a lost part or scar from the last 1 months grows back (a month per Potency). An item is mended whole - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Regrows a lost limb or removes a scar from the last few months (a month per Potency), or mends an item completely. A strong healing spell for old injuries.

*The world forgets the subject was ever there.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Nobody attacks them until they attack, and others forget what they thought of them - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Nobody attacks the person until they attack first, and others forget what they thought of them. Use it to walk someone out of a fight, or to reset a feud.

*Even a mage's soul can be torn loose.* - Target: One mage or other supernatural in sight - Effect: As Sever Soul: their soul comes out, and they go Soulless, then Enervated, then a Thrall - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Resolve, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll for any mage) How to use it: Sever Soul for mages and other supernaturals. Their soul comes out and they decline the same way: Soulless, Enervated, then a Thrall. It's an Act of Hubris for every mage.

*The mage sees the threads of fate that run from a person: who they are bound to, what binds them.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: A letter lists their 1 strongest ties to other people (one per Potency) and every spell on them - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Someone under Fabricate Fortune shows nothing How to use it: A cheap way to learn who matters to a stranger before you deal with them, and to spot lasting spells another mage put on one of your people. Each Potency shows one more link.

*A cantrip of Fate. A small jinx that trips its target.* - Target: One target in range (Gnosis x10 cells), with an attack roll - Effect: A stumble: one bashing wound and a stack of Doom - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A cantrip, only with the Cantrips setting on: one wound from range, for a mage with a single dot of Fate.

*The mage ties a knot in someone's fate and feels it pull when the moment comes.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Pick an event: they're hurt, go down, leave the map, are captured, eat, sleep or break an oath. A letter tells you when it happens, wherever they are - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: A tripwire on one person. Use it on a prisoner you released ("leave the map" tells you when they're gone) or on an enemy leader ("go down" tells you when they fall in a fight you can't see). The letter comes wherever they are, even off the map.

*Small chances line up in the subject's favour, and nothing quite gets in the way.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Luck bends their way in a fight. They feel 15% less pain (15% per Potency), with melee hit +2 and aim +1. A point is about one skill level - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Cast it on your best fighter just before a raid. Its primary factor is Duration, so your Fate dots go into making it last; more Potency costs dice.

*A small turn of luck, one way or the other, before the day is out.* Reading the Outmost Eddies: Good - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Some time before the spell ends, a small piece of good luck: a few coins turn up, or they get a good feeling. They also get one boon charge - Lasts: Until it happens, at most the Duration - Resisted by: Composure, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist Reading the Outmost Eddies: Bad - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Some time before the spell ends, a small piece of bad luck: they drop their weapon, their food goes bad or they get a bad feeling. They also get one hex charge - Lasts: Until it happens, at most the Duration - Resisted by: Composure, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: A small nudge, not a weapon. Good luck is a pleasant surprise for a colonist; bad luck can make an enemy drop their weapon at the wrong moment. Either way the person also carries one boon or hex charge (see Exceptional Luck). The "within the hour" Reach makes it happen soon instead of some time before the spell ends.

*The mage names what they need, and the world shows a corner of where to find it.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Name a goal: a recruit, a cure, something hidden on the map, or the strongest enemy's weakness. A letter says where to look - Nothing to find: Chance sends a small gift: a wanderer who asks to join, 1 herbal medicine, 50 silver, or word of who leads the likeliest raiders - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: The small gift comes at most once every 5 days for each goal How to use it: Ask it for what you're stuck on: a doctor when nobody can treat a disease, a recruit with a skill you lack, or how to beat the enemy that keeps winning. When there's nothing out there to find, you still get a small gift. Each goal can only give that small gift once every 5 days.

*Fortune bends around someone, for them or against them.* Exceptional Luck: Boon - Target: One person in sight - Effect: 1 boon charges (one per Potency). Each charge does one of these when it comes up: a hit on them misses, a thing they make is one quality step better, a surgery they get doesn't fail, or a mental break is skipped - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Composure, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist Exceptional Luck: Hex - Target: One person in sight - Effect: 1 hex charges (one per Potency). Each charge does one of these when it comes up: a hit on them does double damage, or a thing they make is one quality step worse - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Composure, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: Boon is a spare life for a colonist: each charge turns one hit into a miss, or saves a surgery that would have gone wrong. Hex is the reverse on an enemy. Charges sit until they're used or the spell ends, so cast it before the fight, not during.

*A false fate laid over the true one.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Other mages' Fate sight reads nothing on them, and spell triggers set on them don't go off - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Protection against other mages, not against bullets. Cast it on someone a rival mage is likely to spy on or curse with a trigger.

*The subject goes in blind and somehow does fine.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Every skill they're able to use counts as at least 4, and their first talk with someone new gets +1 dice - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Turns anyone into a passable everything: a cook who can't doctor can patch a wound, a shooter can plant crops. It doesn't lower skills that are already above 4. Good on a new recruit, or on whoever has to talk to a stranger.

*The right code, the right combination, the first time.* - Target: One building in sight - Effect: Opens or unlocks the building, or else improves the caster's prices - Hackable: Hacked at once - Casket or crate: Opens, if something is inside - Comms console: Call anyone you pick, with +2 goodwill for a faction (2 per Potency). It needs power - Anything else: The caster trades at 2% better prices for a day - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Skips the hacking job at ancient complexes. It also opens a cryptosleep casket from across the room, so whatever is inside wakes up next to it, not next to you. The console has to have power. With nothing to open, aim it at any building before a trader arrives to get the price bonus.

*The mage leans on chance until what they want walks through the door.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Pick what comes within a day: a wanderer who wants to join, a trade caravan, a few farm animals, a crashed pod of goods, better prices for a day, or fighters from the friendliest faction for the next attack that day - Lucky seam: Or, for a day, plain rock mined on this map gives ore 5% of the time (5% per Potency) - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Order up what the colony is short of. Out of food: farm animals. Short of hands: a wanderer. Need to sell: a caravan. Expecting a raid: allies. The lucky seam is good on a map with plenty of plain rock to mine. With the "within the hour" Reach it comes the same hour.

*A sign against ill fortune.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Another mage's Fate spell on them works only if that mage wins a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power). Melee dodge +5 besides - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Mostly a shield against enemy mages who use Fate. The dodge bonus is a small extra for anyone who has to fight hand to hand.

*Worked from Monkey's Paw, Fate Weaving. A weapon marked to bring bad luck to whoever it strikes.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Each hit lays a stack of Doom on the target: -5% aim and dodge a stack, and at three something goes wrong for them. Their weapon glows and every swing and shot leaves a trail - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Every hit lays a stack of Doom. At three, the target's gun jams or they trip, and the stacks clear. Comes with Monkey's Paw's rote.

*Every scratch the subject takes goes deeper than it should.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: The next 1 times they're hurt (one per Potency), each wound is 1 wounds worse - Lasts: Until the hits are used, at most the Duration - Resisted by: Composure, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: Cast it on the toughest enemy before your shooters open up. At Potency 3 the next 3 hits each count as 3 wounds. It ends early once the hits are used up.

*A blessing or a curse laid on a thing.* Monkey's Paw: Bless - Target: One item in sight - Effect: It's 1 quality steps better (one per Potency), up to legendary - Lasts: The Duration Monkey's Paw: Curse - Target: One item in sight - Effect: It's 1 quality steps worse (one per Potency), down to awful - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Bless a weapon or armour before a fight, or a piece of art before you sell it to a trader. Curse an enemy's gear you can see. The item goes back to its real quality when the spell ends.

*Two fates tied in one knot.* - Target: One person by touch, and the caster - Effect: Every wound either of them takes, the other takes too - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Dangerous both ways: any wound on either of you lands on the other too. Cast it on an enemy you want to stop, then let a tough ally take the hits, or take the "one-way" Reach so only the caster's wounds pass across and the enemy's don't come back to you.

*For a little while, the subject cannot do anything badly.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Their next 1 key moments (one per Potency) go as well as they can: a thing they make comes out at a master's quality, and a surgery they do can't fail - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Costs 1 Mana How to use it: Save it for the moment that matters: crafting a weapon from rare materials, or surgery on someone you can't afford to lose. Each key moment uses one charge. It costs 1 Mana on top of the cast.

*Fate witnesses a promise. Keeping it brings luck; breaking it brings the curse that was named.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They swear an oath. A prisoner swears never to attack the colony and is set free. A guest swears their faction keeps the peace (a vampire swears to pay the boons it owes). A colonist vows not to drink, take drugs, fight or leave - Kept to the end: They get a boon - Broken: A hex and a letter. A faction that breaks the peace loses goodwill with everyone - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: The best use is on prisoners you don't want to keep or kill: they swear never to attack you and walk free. A guest's oath ties their whole faction to the peace. A colonist's vow helps fight an addiction. Keep the Duration long: the boon only comes if the oath holds to the end.

*Every curse has a way out. The mage finds it.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Pick a curse on them of strength 1 or less: a hex, a Paradox Condition, another mage's spell or another kind's curse. Doing a task lifts it - Task: Silver for a small curse, a journey of 10 tiles for a middling one, 25 tiles for a great one - Lasts: Until the task is done How to use it: A cure for curses you can't dispel. It doesn't lift the curse at once: it gives the person a task, and the curse lifts when the task is done. The stronger the curse, the harder the task.

*Unlikely things happen, all at once, to the wrong people.* - Target: Up to 1 enemies (one per Potency) in an area in sight, the Scale - Effect: Pick what goes wrong for them: their guns jam, a seizure, visions, a stumble, or every fire there goes out - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A crowd stopper for a raid. Jammed guns stop a firing line; putting out every fire saves a burning base. Mind the Paradox: anyone who isn't Awakened and sees it makes it riskier.

*Fate pushes someone toward a goal, or away from it.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Goad or ban one of these: drinking, drugs, fighting or leaving home - Goaded: Hexed each day they don't do it - Banned: Hexed each time they do it - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Resolve, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: An Act of Hubris: a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher How to use it: Steer someone's habits. Ban drugs on an addict, ban fighting on a hothead, or goad a lazy colonist to fight. Casting it on a person is an Act of Hubris for a wise mage, so expect a Wisdom roll.

*A knot in fate cut through.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Pick a Fate working on them: a boon or hex, an oath, a trigger, Shared Fate or an Atonement. It ends if its strength is 1 or less - Lasts: Instant How to use it: The answer to other mages' Fate magic on your people, and a way out of your own oaths. Only works if the working's strength is no more than this spell's Potency.

*The mage pulls a string, and something happens to someone, soon.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Pick an event for them: a wanderer joins, a caravan comes, animals wander in, goods fall from the sky, a quest is offered, no raid comes for 1 days (a day per Potency), a prisoner gives in, an accident, an illness, or a lucky seam in the rock for a day - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Shifting the Odds for someone else, with harm on the list. Give a colonist a quest or a quiet stretch with no raids, or give an enemy an accident or an illness. "A prisoner gives in" is a fast way to recruit.

*The mage writes a destiny.* - Target: The caster - Effect: For each Potency (1), choose one: take up a new Obsession, draw her Aspirations anew, raise or lower a Merit by a dot, or gain a dot of Destiny with its Doom (enemies come within days) - Lasts: A Merit dot for the Duration, the rest for good How to use it: Rewrites the mage herself. Changed Obsessions and Aspirations last for good. A Merit dot only lasts as long as the spell. A dot of Destiny is powerful but brings its Doom: enemies come for her within days, so be ready.

*Small miracles, ready to hand.* - Target: The caster - Effect: 1 miracles (one per Potency), each used from a button on the caster: an enemy trips, a downed friend stops bleeding, or a friend on their feet gets a boon - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Saved-up help for a fight. Cast it before a raid, then use the buttons when you need them: trip the enemy who's about to reach your shooters, or stop a downed friend from bleeding out.

*The whole world turns its back on someone.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Their social impact drops 10% (10% per Potency) and everyone thinks less of them. Whoever tends them gets a hex, and whoever harms them gets a boon - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: An Act of Hubris: a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher How to use it: Social exile. Use it on a rival faction's speaker before talks go badly for you, or on a prisoner nobody should get attached to. Be careful with your own people: anyone who looks after them gets hexed. It's an Act of Hubris.

*A plague out of an old story.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: Pick a plague: locusts eat the crops, frogs or blood rain down, an eclipse, or the wild animals there stampede off the map and trample anyone in the way. Sleepers there are shaken - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A biblical plague on an area. Locusts on an enemy's fields, a stampede to clear wild animals, an eclipse for vampire friends. It's an Act of Hubris and obvious magic, so cast it where few outsiders can see.
