*The mage reads the threads that tie a person to everyone and everything they care about.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: A letter with their 1 strongest links (one per Potency), and which of those people and things are on this map - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Shows who and what a person is tied to (family, lovers, bonded animals, treasured things) and which of those are on this map. It's the first step for the other link spells: Borrow Threads, Veil Sympathy, Cut Threads.

*The distance under someone's feet shrinks, or stretches.* Ground-Eater: Hasten - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They move 10% faster (10% per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Stamina, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die Ground-Eater: Slow - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They move 10% slower (10% per Potency), down to half speed - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Stamina, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Hasten gets a friend somewhere fast: to a downed ally, or away from a fight. Slow keeps a chaser off them. It's obvious, so use it out of outsiders' sight.

*Everyone around the subject seems a long way off.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They feel cut off: social impact -10% (10% per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Composure, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: Weakens someone's social pull. Cast it on a rival faction's negotiator, or on a prisoner warden from another side.

*The mage always knows which way to turn to face someone.* - Target: One person on the map who isn't on the caster's side - Effect: The caster knows where they are, with a button that finds them - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Cloak Nimbus or Supernal Veil on them needs a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power) How to use it: Track one outsider anywhere on the map: a raider who fled into the hills, a hidden monster, a guest you don't trust. The button jumps the camera to them.

*A cantrip of Space. A little fold in space that catches like a hook.* - Target: One target in range (Gnosis x10 cells), with an attack roll - Effect: A fold in the air snags the flesh: one cut wound - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A cantrip, only with the Cantrips setting on: one wound from range, for a mage with a single dot of Space.

*The mage sees all around themselves at once.* - Target: The caster - Effect: They see all around: sight +5% (5% per Potency). Cover protects the people they shoot at 10% less (10% per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: A shooter's buff. Enemies behind cover are easier to hit, and the mage sees further. Duration is the primary factor, so it can last a whole fight cheaply.

*The mage takes one of someone's links and ties it to themselves.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Pick one of their links: it's the caster's instead - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: The link's strength How to use it: Take over someone's tie to a person or thing for a while: their bonded animal answers to the mage, or their link to a loved one becomes the mage's. Strong links resist.

*A door is only a line, and the mage steps over it.* - Target: A door, fence or fire in sight, a gap beside the caster, or someone bound - Effect: The caster gets past a barrier, or someone bound gets free - Door, fence or fire: The caster steps through to the far side, locked or not, and fire won't catch them for an hour - Gap: The caster steps through a gap a wall's corner shuts off - Someone bound: They slip their cuffs or a silver net - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: The mage's way past locked doors, fences and walls of fire, and a way out of cuffs. It also lets the mage slip through a gap that a wall's corner shuts off. Stepping through fire is safe for an hour afterwards.

*The subject is sure the wrong way is the right one.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They walk off toward the far edge of the map - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Resolve, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: Sends one enemy wandering off toward the far edge of the map. Good for splitting up a raid, or getting rid of a lone threat without a fight.

*A window opens on a far place.* - Target: A spot anywhere on the map - Effect: The fog lifts 4 cells around it (4 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Lifts the fog anywhere on the map, to scout a cave or see what's waiting in a ruin. With the first Reach the mage can cast sensory spells on people near that spot. With the second Reach it looks at another map: one the colony is on, or a nearby settlement.

*A door nobody else can see.* - Target: One door in sight - Effect: It opens only for its owners, and raiders go around it - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Turns a door into one only your people use. Raiders path around it, which lets you funnel them toward your defences. The Key Reach lets you choose who else it opens for.

*One of someone's links goes quiet.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Pick one of their links: no spell can read it - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: The link's strength How to use it: Hides one of a person's links so no spell can read or follow it. Use it to protect a colonist's family from an enemy mage who'd use them to reach the colonist.

*Space around the subject folds shut against other mages.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Another mage's Space spell on them works only if that mage wins a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power), and the caster hears when one is tried. A caravan they travel with moves 10% faster - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: A shield against enemy Space magic (teleporting your people away, scrying on them), and it tells the caster when someone tries. The faster caravans are a handy extra for a trade trip.

*A dome of space nobody can cross.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: Nobody crosses its edge: whoever is inside stays in, whoever is outside stays out - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A wall nobody can cross, in either direction. Trap raiders inside it, or shut them out of your base while you regroup. Your own people can't cross it either.

*Two places sit on top of each other, and the mage steps between them.* - Target: The caster and a spot in sight - Effect: The caster can step between where they stood and that spot, as often as they like - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A personal shortcut. The mage can step between two spots as often as they like for the Duration. A pair anyone can use is Portal Pair.

*Everything the subject does with the things and people they love goes right.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Social impact +15% and work speed +10% - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: A small, long, flat buff with no Potency in it: more social impact and faster work. Cast it with a long Duration on a trader or a busy crafter.

*Worked from Co-Location, Space Fraying. A pair of portals anyone can walk through.* - Target: The caster and a spot in sight - Effect: A stable pair of portals joins where the caster stands and that spot, and anyone can walk through them - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A pair of portals anyone can walk through for the Duration: a quick road from the base to the fields, or an escape route.

*Worked from Warp, Space Fraying. Space torn along a line. A lost rote from the Unfolded Rooms.* - Target: One target in range, with an attack roll - Effect: Space twists along a line: 1 cut wounds (one per Potency) to everyone on it - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing: no one inside dodges it - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Cut wounds along a line. A lost rote, taught only by the Unfolded Rooms.

*Space twists inside someone's body.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: 8 blunt damage (8 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A plain damage spell that can't miss and needs no roll to hit. The Reach aims it at an arm or a leg, to cripple instead of kill.

*The mage pulls someone's links tighter.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: 1 of their weaker links (one per Potency) grow a step stronger - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Composure if they're unwilling, each dot takes 1 off the Potency How to use it: Strengthens a person's weaker ties. Use it on a couple who keep fighting, or a colonist barely tied to the colony. An unwilling person resists.

*In this place, away means away from the mage.* - Target: The caster's enemies in an area in sight, the Scale - Effect: They stagger out toward its edge - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Pushes enemies out of an area: they stagger toward its edge. Its Reaches change it a lot: enemies fall to the south edge, a corridor they can't walk north in, or shots at your people bend away. Curving Shots and Wall Walking are spells of their own.

*Something is shoved into the space where someone stands.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: 8 crushing damage (8 per Potency), as something is shoved into the space where they stand - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Heavy damage that can't miss. The second Reach leaves the object inside the body: no healing until surgery takes it out, which is cruel and very effective.

*Worked from Alter Direction, Space Patterning. The caster's shots bend round cover.* - Target: The caster's enemies in an area in sight, the Scale - Effect: The caster's shots go round cover, and the enemies there stagger out toward its edge - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: The caster's shots go round cover for the Duration, and enemies in the area are pushed out of it too.

*The mage cuts a link for good.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Pick one of their links and cut it: a spouse, lover or fiancé becomes an ex, a bonded animal is just an animal - Lasts: For good - Resisted by: The link's strength - Watch out: Cutting a strong link to a person is an Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher) How to use it: Ends a tie for good: a spouse becomes an ex, a bonded animal just an animal. Use it to free a colonist from a bad relationship, or to break an enemy's bond with their war animal. Cutting a strong tie to a person is an Act of Hubris.

*A room is bigger on the inside, or much smaller.* Secret Room: Grow - Target: One room in sight. The Scale (the Scale) must cover it - Effect: Every cell holds 1 more stacks (one per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Magic for a chore (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Enlightened). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die Secret Room: Shrink - Target: One room in sight. The Scale (the Scale) must cover it - Effect: It crushes everyone inside for 8 damage (8 per Potency), throws them out, and lets nobody in - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Magic for a chore (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Enlightened). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Grow makes a storeroom hold more: each cell takes extra stacks. Shrink crushes everyone in a room, throws them out, and keeps it shut. The Scale has to be big enough to cover the room. Using it for storage is magic for a chore.

*Worked from Teleportation, Space Patterning. Two people trade places in a blink.* - Target: One person in sight, and another person in sight - Effect: They trade places - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Stamina if they're unwilling, each dot takes 1 off the Potency - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Two people in sight trade places: swap a downed friend with an enemy, or a guard with a prisoner.

*Someone is here, and then they're there.* Teleportation - Target: One person in sight, and a spot in sight - Effect: They go to the spot - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Stamina if they're unwilling, each dot takes 1 off the Potency - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die Teleportation: To orbit - Target: One person in sight (needs Space 5) - Effect: They go to a space map the colony is at (a gravship or a platform), inside where there's air if there is any. From orbit, they go back to a home map - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Stamina, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Move anyone in sight to a spot in sight: pull a downed friend to safety, drop an enemy into a killbox, or send a doctor straight to a patient. Unwilling targets resist. The Reach leaves a portal pair open for a while. "To orbit" needs Space 5. Trading two people's places is Swap Places.

*Worked from Alter Direction, Space Patterning. Up is wherever the caster puts a foot, walls included.* - Target: The caster's enemies in an area in sight, the Scale - Effect: The caster walks on walls as on the floor, and the enemies there stagger out toward its edge - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: The caster walks on walls as on the floor: over a base's walls, onto a roof, past a killbox.

*Two people who never met are tied together.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They and the caster share a medium link - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: On anyone not on the caster's side, an Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher) How to use it: Makes a link to someone the mage never met. That link makes other spells on them easier to aim from far away. On an outsider it's an Act of Hubris. The Reach makes the link permanent.

*Nothing ties the subject to anything.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They have no links at all, and no spell can make or move one. No vampire's blood bond can take hold of them or grow stronger - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Total protection from link magic, and from a vampire's blood bond. Cast it on a colonist a vampire is trying to bind.

*The mage makes a little world of their own.* - Target: The caster - Effect: A small map of its own, sized by the Scale (the Scale): indoors or outdoors, rock or built walls, as you pick. The caster steps in and out with whoever stands beside them. When it ends, everything inside comes back out - Indefinite: It gets a name and stays on the colony's list. A later cast can open it again, and a door can lead to it - Lasts: The Duration. An Indefinite one takes a Mana a week from the caster or a Hallow, and closes after a week unpaid - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A small private map. Pick indoor or outdoor, rock or built walls; the Scale sets its size. The caster steps in and out with whoever stands next to them. Cast it Indefinite to keep it: it gets a name, a later cast can open it again, and a door can lead to it. An Indefinite pocket needs a Mana a week from the caster or a Hallow. The Reaches add a doorway building, a Key, time passing inside, farmland with daylight, or a set temperature.

*A piece of the world is cut out and set aside.* - Target: Everyone and everything loose in an area in sight, the Scale - Effect: They go to a pocket map, then come back to where each one was when it ends - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Cuts a whole area out of the world and sets it aside. Everyone and everything loose in it goes to a pocket map and comes back when the spell ends. Use it to lift a raid off your base, or to hide your people. It's an Act of Hubris.

*The spirit of a thing wakes and does one thing that fits it.* - Target: One animal, person or door in sight - Effect: An animal bites or bolts, a person drops their weapon, or a door swings open or shut - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Composure for a person or animal, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A one-dot trick with several uses: make an enemy drop their gun, make a war animal turn on its handler or run, or slam a door in a raider's face from across the room.

*The mage sees the spirits that share the world.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Spirits around the caster show. With Death 1, ghosts too; with Mind 1, Goetia - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Lets the mage see spirits that are hiding in Twilight. With Death 1 it shows ghosts, with Mind 1 Goetia. Cast it first when something invisible is hurting your people.

*A machine's spirit sulks.* - Target: One machine or mechanoid in sight - Effect: It breaks down or switches itself off - Powered building: It shorts out as well, starting a fire or blowing its batteries - Mechanoid: It turns on its own side, berserk for 10 seconds (10 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Breaks a machine or a mechanoid. On a building that's on a live power net it also shorts out, which can start a fire or blow batteries, so don't aim it at your own grid. A mechanoid goes berserk and attacks its own side for a while.

*The thing a spirit hates fills the place.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: Spirits of Rank 5 or less flee it and won't come in. A fomor in it burns every few seconds it stays, since a bane rides inside them - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Keeps spirits out of an area: ones of Rank 5 or less flee and won't come in. Fomori (Wyrm-possessed people) burn while they stand in it. A good ward for a bedroom or a hospital.

*The mage reads a spirit's nature.* - Target: One spirit in sight - Effect: A letter with 1 facts about it (one per Potency), from: its kind and Rank, what it wants, its mood, its Charm - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency How to use it: Learn about a spirit before you deal with it: what it wants (for a bargain), its mood, and what its Charm (power) does. Strong spirits resist.

*A cantrip of Spirit. A small spirit's bite, called up for a moment.* - Target: One target in range (Gnosis x10 cells), with an attack roll - Effect: A nip of spirit teeth: one bashing wound, and it hits spirits - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A cantrip, only with the Cantrips setting on: one wound from range, for a mage with a single dot of Spirit.

*The mage seals a source of Essence.* - Target: The caster's area - Effect: Anyone else who draws Essence there must win a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power). The caster draws 1 more Mana there - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Claims a place's Essence for the caster: others must win a Clash of Wills to draw there, and the caster draws 1 more Mana. Cast it on your Hallow or ley node.

*Essence flows from a place into the mage, or from the mage into a spirit.* Channel Essence - Target: The caster, at a Resonant place (a ley node, a Locus, an Avernian Gate) - Effect: They draw 1 Mana (one per Potency) - Lasts: Instant Channel Essence: Give - Target: A spirit or another mage, by touch - Effect: 1 Mana (one per Potency) goes from the caster into them. A spirit heals with it - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Mana on the go: at a ley node, a Locus or an Avernian Gate, draw Mana straight away. The Give version pours Mana into another mage, or heals a spirit ally.

*The mage gives a spirit orders.* - Target: One spirit in sight - Effect: It serves the caster - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency - Watch out: A spirit forced to serve keeps a grudge: when the spell ends it may fight, curse the caster or leave. A bargain (right-click it) leaves none How to use it: Makes a spirit work for the mage. A spirit forced to serve holds a grudge and may fight or curse the caster when the spell ends. Right-click the spirit to strike a bargain instead: it serves just the same, with no grudge.

*Spirits' powers slide off the subject.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Other mages' Spirit spells must win a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power) to affect them. Spirits' blows do them half harm - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Protection from spirits: enemy Spirit spells need a Clash of Wills, and spirits' blows do half harm. With the Reach, it covers more of a spirit's attacks.

*The mage's hands can close on a spirit.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They can strike spirits in Twilight. With Death 2, ghosts too; with Mind 2, Goetia - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Lets a fighter hit spirits in Twilight. With Death 2 it also hits ghosts; with Mind 2, Goetia. Cast it on your melee fighter when an invisible spirit attacks.

*The mage thins a place so spirits can be seen there.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: Spirits there show to everyone - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Exorcist's Eye for everyone: spirits in the area show to all, so all your people can see and shoot them.

*Spirits don't notice the subject.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Spirits pass them by, banes included - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Spirits ignore the person, banes included. Good for walking through a place full of hostile spirits, or the Umbra.

*A beaten spirit sleeps longer.* - Target: One beaten-down spirit in sight - Effect: It sleeps 1 days longer (a day per Potency) before it fades - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency How to use it: A beaten spirit normally sleeps a while and then fades. This keeps it asleep for longer, which gives you time to turn it into a fetish or a familiar.

*Worked from Gossamer Touch, Spirit Ruling. Hands that bite into anything the spirits have touched. A lost rote from the Banefather's Liturgy.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Their blows on anyone spirit-touched (Garou, Fera, fomori, spirits) do 1 more wounds (one per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Extra wounds on Garou, Fera, fomori and spirits. A lost rote, taught only by the Banefather's Liturgy.

*The mage feeds a spirit strength.* - Target: One spirit in sight - Effect: It heals 2 wounds (2 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Heals a spirit ally, a familiar or a bound spirit in a fight.

*The mage wears a place's spiritual nature away.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: Other mages' Spirit spells on places there end: opened spots, Loci, Places of Power, capped wells. It also cleans 6 polluted cells (6 per Potency, Biotech) and lifts any Wyrm taint (Garou) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: A Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power) for each other mage's spell there. Spells from the caster's own side end without one How to use it: Cleans an area: it ends other mages' Spirit spells on places there, cleans pollution (with Biotech) and lifts Wyrm taint (with Garou). Your own side's spells end without a contest; another mage's need a Clash of Wills each.

*A torrent of raw Essence slams into the target.* - Target: One target in sight, with an attack roll, spirits in Twilight included - Effect: 8 blunt damage (8 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss, and a miss lands within a few cells on whoever is there - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A Spirit attack that also hits spirits hiding in Twilight. It rolls to hit like a gun. The Reach makes the target easier prey for spirits for a day.

*The wall between the worlds thickens.* Place of Power - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: The Gauntlet there rises by 1 (one per Potency). Hostile spirits and banes are driven out and can't walk in - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die Place of Power: Lower - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: The Gauntlet there falls by 1 (one per Potency). A mage standing in it casts Spirit spells with a die more - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Raising the Gauntlet drives hostile spirits and banes out and keeps them out: a good ward for your base. Lowering it makes Spirit spells easier there and makes it easier to cross into the Penumbra.

*The mage opens a hole between the worlds.* - Target: A spot in sight - Effect: An Iris opens: anyone who steps on it crosses into the Penumbra, and its twin on the far side brings them back - Without Garou: The caster steps into a small pocket of the Shadow instead, with a spirit or two in it - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Opens a door to the spirit world: step on the Iris to cross into the Penumbra, and its twin brings you back. Without the Garou mod, it leads to a small pocket of the Shadow with a spirit or two. The Key Reach limits who can use it.

*A sleeping spirit wakes.* - Target: One beaten-down spirit in sight - Effect: It wakes, with 2 wounds healed (2 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency How to use it: Wakes a beaten spirit and heals it a little. Use it on your own familiar or bound spirit after a fight.

*The mage calls, and a spirit comes.* - Target: The caster - Effect: The nearest spirit on the map comes and stays near the caster. With none, the caster calls one of a kind they pick - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Calls a spirit to the mage. The nearest spirit on the map comes; if there are none, pick the kind you want. Follow it with Command Spirit, Bind Spirit or Familiar.

*The mage strips a spirit's hold on the world.* - Target: One spirit in sight. With Death 4 or Mind 4, ghosts and Goetia too - Effect: A manifested spirit fades back into Twilight. One already in Twilight is sent away for good - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Gets rid of a spirit. A manifested one is pushed back into Twilight; one already in Twilight is sent away for good. With Death 4 or Mind 4 it works on ghosts and Goetia too.

*The mage gives a spirit a body and holds it there.* Bind Spirit - Target: One spirit in sight. With Death 4 or Mind 4, ghosts and Goetia too - Effect: It manifests, solid and seen, and serves the caster - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: A spirit forced to serve keeps a grudge: when the spell ends it may fight, curse the caster or leave. A bargain (right-click it) leaves none. Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die Bind Elemental - Target: A spot in sight with its element close by: a fire, stone or a rock wall, water, or open sky (needs Spirit 4, and Forces 3 or Matter 3) - Effect: An elemental of that element rises and serves the caster, its Rank the Potency up to 3 - Fire: Burns what it strikes and warms a room - Earth: Slow, hard to hurt, and mines - Water: Puts out fires and knocks down what it strikes - Air: Fast, throws back what it strikes, and clears gas - Lasts: The Duration, then it's gone - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Gives a spirit a solid body and makes it fight for you. It holds a grudge if forced; right-click it for a bargain instead. The elemental version needs Spirit 4 plus Forces 3 or Matter 3, and something of its element nearby: fire burns and warms, earth is tough and mines, water puts out fires, air is fast and clears gas.

*A sleeping spirit is bound into a vessel.* - Target: One beaten-down spirit in sight - Effect: It becomes a fetish holding 11 Essence (10 plus the Potency). A mage who uses it draws Mana from it - Lasts: For good - Watch out: Magic for a chore (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Enlightened) How to use it: Turns a beaten spirit into a fetish: a lasting store of Essence that a mage can draw Mana from. Beat a spirit down first (Slumber keeps it asleep longer). It's magic for a chore.

*A small spirit bonds to the mage.* - Target: One spirit in sight. With Death 4 or Mind 4, a ghost or a Goetia - Effect: It becomes the caster's familiar and follows them. The caster can draw its Essence as Mana (5 a Rank, a point back a day) - For good: Cast to last for good, it's the Familiar Merit - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Bonds a spirit (or, with Death 4 or Mind 4, a ghost or Goetia) to the mage as a familiar. It follows them and is a Mana battery: 5 Mana per Rank, a point back each day. Cast it for good and it becomes the Familiar Merit. The Reach makes it clean and haul when idle.

*A howling mass of spirits tears at the target.* - Target: One target in sight, with an attack roll, spirits in Twilight included - Effect: 8 damage (8 per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss, and a miss lands within a few cells on whoever is there - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Spirit's big attack. It rolls to hit and hits spirits in Twilight too. Its Reaches add aggravated wounds, burn the target's fuel, or leave them open to spirits for a day.

*A spirit becomes something else.* - Target: One spirit in sight - Effect: It becomes another kind of spirit, picked from a list, whole again - Lasts: For good - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency How to use it: Turns a spirit into another kind, fully healed. Make a dangerous spirit into a harmless one, or a weak one into a kind with a better Charm.

*The mage steps halfway out of the world.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Twilight form: no physical harm reaches them and they pass through doors, but they can't harm, work or carry. Spells still work - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: The person steps into Twilight: no physical harm can touch them and they walk through doors, but they can't hit, work or carry anything. They can still cast spells, so it's a safe way for a mage to cast in a fight.

*The mage carries someone across the Gauntlet.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They cross into the Penumbra, or back out. A spirit brought out stays in Twilight - Without Garou: They cross into a small pocket of the Shadow instead, with a spirit or two in it - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: The Gauntlet, each point takes 1 off the Potency - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Sends one person across into the Penumbra, or brings them back. A spirit you pull out stays in Twilight. Without the Garou mod it leads to a small pocket of the Shadow.

*The mage unmakes a spirit for good.* - Target: One spirit in sight - Effect: It's destroyed and never comes back - Lasts: For good - Resisted by: Its Rank, each dot takes 1 off the Potency - Watch out: Unmaking one that meant no harm is an Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Destroys a spirit for good. Use it on a bane or a spirit that keeps coming back. Destroying one that meant no harm is an Act of Hubris.

*A new spirit wakes out of quiet Essence.* - Target: A spot in sight - Effect: A Rank 1 spirit of a kind the caster picks appears, grateful and asking nothing - Servitor: Or a made spirit in Twilight over the room at the spot (or the Scale's area outdoors) with one task: sweeping, keeping watch, keeping the room warm or cool, tending plants, mending things or giving light - Indefinite: Cast Indefinite (Advanced Duration, slider at the end), it lasts for good. It shows under Spirit sight as a small light, and a servitor sends a letter on what it did every 30 days - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Makes a new spirit. Pick a Rank 1 spirit of any kind, or a servitor with one job over a room: sweeping, keeping watch, keeping it warm or cool, tending plants, mending things or giving light. To keep a servitor for good, cast it Indefinite (Advanced Duration, slider at the end). It sends a report every 30 days.

*A place becomes a well of spirit.* - Target: An area in sight, the Scale - Effect: It becomes a Locus: the Gauntlet there is 1, it counts as a Resonant place for Channel Essence, and spirits in it heal - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Makes an area into a Locus: the Gauntlet is thin, spirits heal there, and it counts for Channel Essence. Make one at home and your mages can draw Mana there every day.

*Essence wells up out of nothing.* - Target: A mage or spirit, by touch - Effect: 1 Mana (one per Potency) for a mage, or that much healing for a spirit, made from nothing - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Mana from nothing, anywhere. Top up a mage in a fight, or heal a spirit.

*The mage makes a home in the Shadow.* - Target: A spot in sight - Effect: A small world of the caster's own opens in the Shadow, with a door at the spot that leads in - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: It needs no Garou. Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A private realm in the Shadow with a door at the spot. It works without the Garou mod. The Reaches add an Iris back to the map and a Key for it.

*The mage looks a little way down the likeliest road.* - Target: The week ahead, and one person in sight - Effect: A letter with 1 answers (one per Potency): is a raid coming, is a trader coming, and will the person join, die or break - Afterwards: For a week, the caster feels the next raid a few hours before it comes - Lasts: Instant How to use it: A cheap early warning. Ask about the coming week, and the caster also senses the next raid a few hours ahead for a week. Aim it at a visitor you're thinking of recruiting to learn whether they'll join, or at a sick colonist to learn whether they'll die.

*Everything happens on time for someone, or nothing does.* Green Light - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They move and work 10% faster (10% per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration Red Light - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They move and work 10% slower (10% per Potency), down to half speed - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Green Light speeds up a builder, a hauler or someone running from danger. Red Light slows an enemy (down to half speed at most). Both work on anyone in sight with no roll to resist.

*Will this turn out well? The mage feels the answer.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They show green if they'll be good for the caster, red if not: a hidden enemy, a carrier of a deadly illness, a cruel nature or a grudge - Lasts: Instant How to use it: A quick yes or no on a stranger before you let them in. Red means trouble of some kind (a hidden enemy, a deadly illness, a cruel streak or a grudge) without saying which.

*The mage sees the right moment coming and is ready for it.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Melee hit +2, aim +1 and social impact +5% (5% per Potency). A point is about one skill level - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: A self buff for a mage who fights or negotiates. Duration is the primary factor, so it lasts a long time for little effort.

*The mage looks back down the road something has come.* - Target: One person, corpse or item in sight - Effect: A letter with 3 lines (3 per Potency) of what happened to it lately: fights, talks and tales - Case clues: Clues and signs of monsters passing where it lies are read with 1 successes - Lasts: Instant How to use it: The detective's spell. Read a corpse to learn who killed it, or an item to learn where it's been. Cast it where a monster walked to find case clues; each Potency is one success on the clue roll.

*A cantrip of Time. A second stolen from the target.* - Target: One target in range (Gnosis x10 cells), with an attack roll - Effect: A skipped second: one bashing wound, and -10% speed for a second - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A cantrip, only with the Cantrips setting on: one wound from range, for a mage with a single dot of Time.

*The mage sees two ways a moment could go, and picks.* - Target: One person in sight - On a friend: The next thing they make is rolled twice and the better result kept, or their next surgery can't fail - On anyone else: A hex charge - Lasts: Until used, at most the Duration - Resisted by: Resolve if they aren't the caster's own, each dot takes 1 off the Potency How to use it: On a friend, it's a safety net for one craft or one surgery. On anyone else, it lays a hex charge. It waits until it's used.

*Whatever happens to time, the subject stays as they are.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: If Corridors of Time turns the world back, they keep the skills they had. Stuns on them last half as long - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Mostly a partner for Corridors of Time: whoever has it keeps the skills they learned when the world is turned back. Halving stuns is useful in a fight against stunning weapons.

*Spells held in a moment that hasn't come yet.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Their next 1 spells (one per Potency, 1 Mana each) don't go off yet. They all go off when it ends, or when it's let go from its button - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Store spells now, fire them all at once later. Cast Hung Spell, then cast your next spells (each costs 1 Mana more); they wait instead of going off. Let them go from the button, or they go off when the spell ends. Waiting on the ground for an enemy is Spell Trap.

*The subject's past and future close like a book.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: Another mage's Time spell on them works only if that mage wins a Clash of Wills (a contest of the two casters' power) - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Protection against enemy mages who use Time on your people. Does nothing against mundane harm.

*Worked from Hung Spell, Time Ruling. Held spells wait on the ground until an enemy steps there.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Their next 1 spells (one per Potency, 1 Mana each) wait where the first was aimed, and go off when an enemy steps there; the others land on that enemy - Needs: Fate 2 as well - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Hung Spell with its spells waiting on the spot the first one was aimed at; they go off on the first enemy who steps there. Needs Fate 2 as well.

*The subject acts first, or last.* Tipping the Hourglass: First - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They stop waiting: any aim or cooldown holding them ends, and they act now - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Resolve, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist Tipping the Hourglass: Last - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They lose 1 seconds (a second per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Resolve, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist How to use it: First lets a friend shoot right now instead of aiming, or skip a cooldown. Last makes an enemy lose a few seconds, often enough to get away or land the first blow.

*Time stops for the subject's ills.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: No bleeding; illnesses and poisons freeze where they are and no new ones take hold; no mental breaks. No healing either - Lasts: The Duration How to use it: Stops someone getting worse while you find a doctor or a cure. They don't bleed, their illness doesn't advance and they can't break, but they don't heal either, so end it once they're being treated. The Reaches give back a Willpower or a Mana.

*The subject moves through the world as a blur.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They move 50% faster (50% per Potency), aim and attack 20% quicker (20% per Potency), and get melee dodge +5 (5 points per Potency; the Nimble trait gives 15) - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Costs 1 Mana. Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Turns a fighter into a blur: faster on foot, faster to shoot and hard to hit in melee. It's obvious, so cast it where outsiders can't see. For work, cast Tireless Work.

*The subject crawls through a thicker kind of time.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They move at half to a sixth their speed, aim and attack 20% slower (20% per Potency), and melee dodge -5 (5 points per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Stamina, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: Costs 1 Mana. Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: The strongest slow in the game. At high Potency the target barely moves. Good for pinning down a melee enemy while your shooters work. Take the "no dodging" Reach against a dodgy fighter.

*Worked from Acceleration, Time Perfecting. Time between blows taken away. A lost rote from the Clockmaker's Heresy.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: 1 of their melee blows (one per Potency) come with no pause between them - Lasts: The Duration, or until the blows are spent How to use it: A Potency of melee blows with no pause between them. A lost rote, taught only by the Clockmaker's Heresy.

*Worked from Weight of Years, Time Perfecting. Years laid on what an enemy carries. A lost rote from the Clockmaker's Heresy.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Years pass for what they carry: their weapon and armour lose 10% of their condition (10% per Potency), and the weapon comes apart in their hands: a wound for every 2 Potency - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Wears down a target's weapon and armour without a wound. A lost rote, taught only by the Clockmaker's Heresy.

*A few seconds of the subject's life run backward.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They go back 3 seconds (3 per Potency): back where they stood, with their cooldowns and stance as they were. Spells cast on them since are gone. Wounds stay - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Undoes the last few seconds for one person. Use it to pull a friend back from where they stepped into danger, or to strip the spells an enemy mage just put on someone. Wounds aren't undone. The Reach turns the whole world back an hour or more, to a Corridors of Time snapshot.

*The subject's earlier self, called up to stand in its place.* - Target: One person or item in sight - Effect: It becomes its earlier self. A person loses the wounds and ills of the last hour to the last week; an item stands whole - Lasts: The Duration, then the present comes back, with whatever happened meanwhile - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Temporary healing. A badly hurt friend becomes their unhurt earlier self, fit to fight; when the spell ends the wounds come back, plus anything they took meanwhile. On an item, it stands whole again for the Duration. Have a doctor ready for when it ends.

*Worked from Acceleration, Time Perfecting. Hands move many times as fast at their work.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: They work many times as fast, move 50% faster (50% per Potency), aim and attack 20% quicker (20% per Potency), and get melee dodge +5 (5 points per Potency) - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Costs 1 Mana. Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Someone works many times as fast for the Duration: a builder finishes a wall in moments. A chore spell, and obvious.

*Years fall on something all at once.* - Target: One item or living body in sight - Effect: An item loses 10% of its hit points (10% per Potency); a body takes 1 aching wounds (one per Potency) - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: The undead are immune. Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Ages a thing or a body in an instant. Good for knocking down a wall or a door, or wearing down a living enemy. The undead don't age, so it does nothing to vampires and ghosts.

*The mage sees what the enemy will do before they do it.* - Target: The caster - Effect: Every enemy near them shows its next target (red) and where it's headed (orange). The caster gets melee dodge +2.5 and aim +1. A point is about one skill level - Lasts: The Duration - Watch out: Costs 1 Mana How to use it: A battle sense. You see who every nearby enemy will attack next and where they're going, so you can pull the target back or set an ambush. It costs 1 Mana.

*The mage reads the road ahead in full.* - Target: The week ahead, and one person in sight - Effect: A letter with 1 detailed answers (one per Potency): the day, faction and size of a coming raid, when a trader comes, a prisoner's resistance, or what's killing someone - Afterwards: For a week, the caster feels the next raid a few hours before it comes, and her next talk with the person gets +1 dice - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Divination in full detail: the day, faction and size of the next raid, so you can prepare for exactly that. It also gives dice for the next talk with the person you aimed it at.

*Parts of the body age in an instant while others go young.* - Target: One target in range, with an attack roll - Effect: 8 crushing damage (8 per Potency), as parts of the body age and others go young - Lasts: Instant - Resisted by: Nothing, but it can miss, and a miss lands within a few cells on whoever is there - Watch out: The undead are immune. Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A Time attack spell. It rolls to hit like a gun, so a miss can hit someone near the target, friend or foe. The "aggravated" Reach makes the wounds much harder to heal. It does nothing to the undead.

*The subject has always been someone else.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: Pick another past (backstory) for them, with the work it rules out - Vampire or werewolf: They lose their strongest power instead (a Discipline's top dot, a Gift). Its rank Withstands the spell - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Resolve, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Changes who someone has been. Give a colonist a past that suits the work you need, or give an enemy one that rules out fighting. On a vampire or werewolf it strips their strongest power instead. It's an Act of Hubris.

*The subject skips forward in time and is simply gone.* - Target: One person in sight - Effect: They vanish from time, then come back where they stood - Lasts: The Duration - Resisted by: Stamina, each dot takes 1 off the Potency. The caster's own people don't resist - Watch out: Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Takes one enemy out of the fight for the Duration. They come back exactly where they stood, so be ready when they do.

*Hours of work done in a moment.* - Target: One person in sight, while they work - Effect: 4 hours of their job (4 per Potency) are done at once, on a bill, a building or research - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Magic for a chore (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Enlightened). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: Finishes a job in a moment: a long build, a research project, a big crafting bill. The person has to be working on it when you cast. It's magic for a chore, which costs an Enlightened mage a Wisdom roll.

*The mage sends someone back down the road, knowing what lies ahead.* - Target: The world, through one person touched - Effect: The world goes back to a snapshot from up to 1 days ago (a day per Potency), and that person keeps a letter of what they saw - Lasts: Instant - Watch out: Snapshots are only kept while a colony mage with Time 3 knows this spell (see the settings). An Act of Hubris (a Wisdom roll if the caster's Wisdom is Understanding or higher). Obvious: each outsider who sees it adds a Paradox die How to use it: A save-scum in the story. The world goes back to a snapshot from a few days ago, and the person you touched keeps a letter of what happened, so you can avoid it this time. Snapshots are only taken while a colony mage with Time 3 knows this spell, so learn it before you need it. It's an Act of Hubris.

*The world stops for one person, and they get hours to themselves.* - Target: One person, by touch - Effect: The world stops for them for 2 hours for each step of Duration. They come out having researched or studied a skill for that long, and just as tired - Lasts: Instant How to use it: Time to study, for free. The person steps out of time and comes back having researched or trained a skill for hours, while no time passed for anyone else. Options, Mod settings, The Rim by Night, then Awakened on the rail down the left, which every Rim by Night mod shares. - Awakening: the odds of an Awakening, the mage cap before the season limit, the hunted stranger, and the Proscribed. With Royalty, Awakening gives a psylink (off by default) gives a colonist who Awakens a first psylink level, for psycast mods. - Paradox: a dice offset, and Wisdom loss on or off. - Time: game snapshots for the Time rewinds, and how often they're taken. - Beings: ghost odds and spirits in Twilight. - Places: Hallow odds, Hallow Mana and the long-term Nimbus. - Growth: dramatic failures for Arcane Beats, and how much each Arcane Beat counts (25% to 200%). - Looks: camera shake, sky flashes, and when a lasting spell's circle shows on the ground: always, when its mage is selected or the mouse is on it (and under Mage Sight of its Arcanum), or under Mage Sight only. - Consilium: the Lex Magica on or off. - Event chances: each event on or off, and how often.

With Odyssey your colony can live in orbit. The World of Darkness stays on the ground: nobody from these mods comes up uninvited unless "The World of Darkness reaches orbit" is on in Core's settings. Help you call still comes, by drop pod, and leaves on Royalty's shuttle. Without Royalty it stays aboard until the ship lands. The colony is whichever home holds most of your free colonists, so visitors go where your people are. No Hallow forms on an orbit home or an asteroid. A sympathetic spell between orbit and the ground costs one more Reach. There are no Sleepers up there to witness magic, and Banishers only come up with the setting on.

Is it safe on my main save? It's in beta, so bugs are likely. Keep a backup of any save you add it to. Can I add it to a running game? Yes. Colonists start rolling for the Awakening from then on. How do I take it out? Use "Remove Awakened from this game" in the mod settings, save, then disable the mod. Do I need the other Rim by Night mods? Only Core. Kindred, Garou and Imbued add the other kinds. Do I need to know the tabletop game? No. The grimoire explains the rules in game. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Some spells are worked from another one in the book: Flight from Levitation, Wash Clean from Shaping, and the rest. Each says so at the top of its description. Knowing the first spell's rote, or its Praxis, teaches the ones worked from it. - Rotes are spells she knows by heart. They add the mudra, her best rote Skill, to the pool. - Praxes are spells she has mastered. Three successes count as exceptional. - Improvised spells are anything her Arcana reach. Outside her Ruling Arcana they cost a Mana. Spells sit on one power tile per Arcanum. Click one to cast it with its preset, or right-click it to open the builder. The Spells page of the Awakened tab shows each Arcanum's spells as icons, as the Kindred tab shows Disciplines: click one to take it off the bar or put it back. Faint icons are rotes in her Order's library she hasn't learned. An Order's library, the Consilium's rote and grimoire, and Scribe Grimoire open one spell list with a search box, a chip for each Arcanum and dot rating, and "Can pick only".

"Cast a spell" opens the builder. Pick a spell, then set: - Potency, Duration and Scale. Each step past the free ones takes 2 dice off the pool. - Range: touch, or sensory to reach anyone she can see. - Casting Time: instant, or a ritual that takes longer and gets more help. - Reach: Advanced factors and the spell's own Reach effects. Reach past her free Reach rolls Paradox. - Yantras: High Speech, concentration, runes and a sacrament for more dice. A line that does nothing on the picked spell (Potency on a spell that never reads it, Duration on an instant one, Scale on a spell cast on herself) is left out, and its row stays empty so the window keeps its shape. The pool is Gnosis + Arcanum + Yantras. At -6 or worse, the spell can't be cast. The tab's Willpower habit says when the mage spends Willpower on her own. Never spend; To resist (the default), a point adds two to Resolve or Composure against a hostile spell or power as it lands; Spend freely, which also puts a point into each casting for three more dice. Letting a spell go and Scrutiny ask for Willpower as before, whatever the habit says.
A ritual takes from 3 hours at Gnosis 1 down to a minute at Gnosis 9. Other mages can stand in and add their successes. Sleepers add a die.

Some spells ask something once they land: which works a homunculus does, which animal to become, who to call. A window opens and the game pauses. Click an option to tick it and click it again to untick it, then press Done. If that pick leads to another question, it appears as the next step. Call off gives the Mana back.

A lasting spell counts against her Spell Control (her Gnosis, plus her Sanctum's rating while she's inside it). The tab lists each one with End, Let go (1 Willpower) and Let go safely (a Willpower dot).

Reach past free rolls Paradox dice by Gnosis. More dice come from outsiders watching, inured spells, the Abyss in her Pattern and earlier rolls this hour. The tab sets a policy: contain, release, or contain only when 5 or more dice come up. - Containing rolls Wisdom. Each cancelled success is a bashing wound, and the rest becomes Backlash or Imago. - Releasing spends the Reach on an Abyssal Tilt on the map, a new subject, or a warped spell. - A Condition left to lapse adds the Abyss to her Pattern. The Scour button ends it at the price of a lethal cut.

How hard the Lie presses back on your mages, from 0 to 100, shown on the Awakened tab's Overview. A Sleeper from outside the colony who saw a vulgar spell adds 4 once they get away from the map, twice that for a trader, and 10 at most for one caravan. The witness already added a Paradox die to the spell they saw; the score never adds that die again. It falls by about a third of a point a day, slower once it's high. Level Score What happens Quiet under 20 Nothing Whispers 20 A letter Disbelief 40 Vulgar spells roll one more Paradox die Notice 60 The Consilium's Sentinel asks who keeps casting where Sleepers can see Hunted 80 Two more Paradox dice, and the Seers of the Throne raid within three days When the Sentinel asks (or once 12 points are laid on one mage), name the mage and half of it is cleaned up, take the blame as a colony, or refuse. Standing with the Consilium moves 5 up, 5 down, or 15 down (a Status dot).
An obvious lasting spell seen by outsiders can be worn down by their disbelief, one factor at a time, until it ends.
With 2 dots in an Arcanum, she can put up Mage Armor for 1 Mana and an hour: armor and dodge by her dots.

Thunderbolt, Telekinetic Strike and Piercing Earth each have more than one energy, picked on the builder as a button of its own. Thunderbolt throws a Lightning Bolt, a Fire Bolt (it can set them alight), a Frost Bolt (it chills toward hypothermia), a Radiation Bolt (no wound, but toxic buildup) or a Thunderclap (a stun, a small bruise and deafness). Telekinetic Strike is a Force Blow, an Air Blade or a Force Spike. Piercing Earth is Crushing Earth, Stone Spikes, or a Sand Blast that blinds for a few seconds. The builder's search finds a button by its name, so typing "fire" finds Thunderbolt. Any aimed damage spell also takes a shape on the builder. A bolt hits one target, or one more for each step of Scale. A line runs from the mage through the target, 12 to 24 cells long by Scale, and a wall stops it. A cone fans out 8 to 16 cells deep. A burst hits everyone round the target, out to the Scale's radius. A ring hits everyone 4 to 10 cells round the mage, who is spared. A chain hits the target and jumps to the nearest person within 8 cells, once for each subject the Scale allows, so 16 subjects is 16 jumps. Advanced Scale makes every shape bigger still. No one inside a line, cone, burst or ring can dodge it, and only a chain's jumps can miss. Friends are hit as well, unless the mage pays a Reach to spare her side.

On the Awakened tab's Conduct page, Attacks with sets what the mage fights with: - Weapons: her gun or blade. Autocast still casts what its own setting allows. - Magic: the hardest-hitting aimed attack rote that can reach the enemy, with its saved setup from Cast a Spell. Her weapon takes over only when no rote can go (out of range or sight, no Mana or Spell Control to spare). - Smart (the default): a rote when it hits harder than her weapon. She keeps to the weapon while her Mana is under a quarter, and won't cast an Obvious rote with Sleepers watching or one that would go past her Spell Control. Drafted, a right-click on an enemy casts the rote, as a right-click fires a gun. Undrafted, she casts it wherever she would shoot, whatever the autocast setting. The cast is the power button's own, so rolls, Paradox and witnesses work as they always do.

Six touch spells put a glyph on a fighter's weapon for the spell's Duration. The weapon glows in the Arcanum's colour, and every swing and shot leaves a trail. Each comes with the rote of the spell it was worked from, and each costs one Reach. Glyph Worked from What it does Force Wave Kinetic Blow (Forces) A melee blow carries on as a blade of force: the first enemy within Potency x2 cells behind the target takes it at half Long Reach Kinetic Blow (Forces, and Space 2) Melee blows land from up to Potency cells off Supernal Rounds Ephemeral Enchantment (Prime) +10% armour piercing a Potency on shots, and they hit beings in Twilight Grave Edge Shadow Crafting (Death) Each wound heals 10% a Potency slower for a day Doom Mark Monkey's Paw (Fate) Each hit lays a stack of Doom Keen Edge Alter Integrity (Matter) +10% damage a Potency on every blow and shot The glyph sits on the wielder, so it follows them to the next weapon they pick up.

Eighteen attack spells are lost rotes: they don't show in Cast a Spell until a tome teaches them, and no teacher or grimoire hands them out. Each is worked from a spell in the book, and each names its tome in its description. Shadow Sculpting has a Reach effect, "the shadow fights" (2 Reaches): instead of a figure that draws enemies, the caster's shadow stands up in Twilight and fights for the Duration, going for her enemies within 12 cells. It's weak, but its blows reach the living, and only harm that touches Twilight can hurt it. It fades when the spell ends.

- Bone Armour (from Shadow Crafting): a corpse's bones close round the caster as armour for the Duration, and the body is left a skeleton. - Bone Thrall (from Quicken Corpse): a corpse rises at once as a fast fighter that does no work, and falls apart when the spell ends. - Bottle Mana (from Channel Mana): the caster pours up to Potency of their own Mana into a stone chunk beside them, and it becomes that many hallow stones.

With the Cantrips setting on (off by default), every mage knows a cantrip for each Arcanum they have a dot in: a small aimed spell of one wound, with a range of Gnosis x10 cells. They're obvious, so Paradox rolls as usual. With the setting off they're hidden and can't be cast. A hex, Grave Misfortune, Pariah and Doom Mark each lay a stack of Doom: -5 aim and dodge a stack, for a day. The third stack goes off at once. A gun jams, or the target trips and falls, and the stacks clear.

A spell checks what's already on its target. A word over the target says when one fires. Matter can make and change the ground for good. - Build from Nothing builds every blueprint and frame of the colony's in its area at once, if the material is one the Potency reaches. It costs 1 Mana more for each step of Scale. - Raise Stone puts natural rock of the map's own stone on the empty ground in its area. A +2 Reach puts overhead mountain over it too, which can cave in and draw infestations. - Reshape the Ground turns natural ground into soil, rich soil (Life 2 as well), sand, gravel, rough stone, marsh or shallow water. Floors and bridges are left alone, and nothing built turns to water. - Vein of Ore turns a rock wall into a vein: compacted steel at Potency 1, silver and jade at 3, gold and plasteel at 4, uranium at 5. - Shifting the Odds can give a lucky seam: for a day, plain rock mined on the map gives ore 5% of the time a Potency. A Reach names the ore. - With Odyssey, State Change's Molten ground (Forces 3 as well) turns the area to lava for the Duration. When it ends, the old ground comes back.

Pocket Dimension asks how its world looks: indoors (a roof and still air) or outdoors (open sky and soil), then natural (rock walls and rough ground) or built (smooth walls and floor). With Life 2 the ground is rich soil, and an indoor pocket gets spell lights bright enough for crops. With Forces 2 you pick its temperature: cold, cool, mild or hot. An Indefinite pocket gets a name and goes on the colony's list. A later Pocket Dimension can open one of those instead of making a new one, and a pocket's door on the map has a Leads to button to pick which pocket it opens on. Its Key still decides who passes. Each lasting pocket takes a Mana a week, from its maker first and then a Hallow on her map. After six days unpaid a letter warns that it closes the next day. When it closes, everything inside comes out beside its maker, or in the middle of the map if she has left.

- Ex Nihilo's A wall from nothing puts up a line of plain stone walls across the way from the mage to the spot, 3 cells and 2 more a step of Scale, for the Duration. - Thunderbolt starts as a chain, jumping from the target to the next person near. Pick Bolt on the builder to hit one. - Telekinetic Strike's "throws them back" Reach sends whoever it hits a cell a Potency and knocks them down for a few seconds. - Familiar's "it helps round the house" Reach has the familiar clean and haul a little when it's idle. - Self-Repairing Machine cast along a sympathetic link at a person mends a piece of their gear, wherever they are, even with a caravan. - Golem's Stone giant (Matter 4) stands a natural rock wall up as a golem with an earth elemental's body. It mines when it has no order, and goes back to rock when the spell ends. - A servitor sends a letter every 30 days on what it did: messes swept, enemies warned of, things mended.

No spell makes anyone a vampire, a werewolf or a hunter. Two come close the other way. - Cleanse the Body's Flush the blood (Life 4 and Death 2, with Kindred) washes a vampire's blood out of a ghoul. The ghouling ends and the years it held back catch up at once. A blood bond stays, since it's in the mind. - Supernal Dispellation's Silence a nature (Prime 5) stops a vampire's, werewolf's or hunter's powers for an hour a Potency: no gifts, no blood spent, no healing the way they should. The caster has to win a Clash of Wills against the subject's Resolve plus three.

These show only with their DLC. - Biotech: Transform Life's Rewrite the blood (Life 5) adds a gene the colony knows from a genepack or one of its people, or takes a xenogene away. It goes back when the spell ends, unless the Duration is Indefinite. A Reach works on germline genes instead. Knit's "fill the blood" Reach takes away blood loss and fills hemogen. Create Energy's Current gives the mechanoids in its area a fifth of their energy a Potency, and Eradicate Energy's Drain a mechanoid takes it away. Remote Control's Mechanoid makes one fight for the caster for an hour a Potency, with no mechlink. A mechanitor's mech is held unless the caster wins a Clash of Wills. - Royalty: Psychic Genesis can open a psylink a level, or with Prime 3 close one a level. It stays, and it's an Act of Hubris. - Odyssey: Environmental Shield at Potency 5 keeps out vacuum entirely. Body Control's "no breath needed" Reach does too. Teleportation's To orbit (Space 5) sends someone to a gravship or platform where the colony is, inside where there's air, or from orbit back home.

A golem, an Eidolon or a quickened corpse has no mind of its own. Its Order button gives it one standing order: haul, clean, mine, build, guard a spot, or follow its maker. With no order, a golem or an Eidolon works as a trained animal and cleans the home area when it's idle. A quickened person keeps its own work and only takes Guard or Follow. Building leaves anything with a quality to the colonists. Create Life's Homunculus (Life 5) makes a small pale body with nobody inside. It works like a golem: one standing order (haul, clean, mine, build, guard or follow), no food, sleep or mood, and it isn't one of your colonists. A faint green shimmer rises off it. With Mind 5 it's a real person instead, for two kinds of work you pick, from cleaning, hauling, growing, cutting plants, cooking, crafting, mining and construction, at 3 skill a Potency and nothing else. Bind Spirit's An elemental (Spirit 4, and Forces 3 or Matter 3) raises one from its element near the spot: a fire, stone, water or open sky. Its Rank is the Potency, up to 3. Fire sets alight what it strikes and warms a room. Earth is slow, hard to hurt and mines. Water puts out fires and knocks down what it strikes. Air is fast, throws back what it strikes and blows gas away. A spirit made to serve by Command Spirit or Bind Spirit keeps a grudge. When the spell ends it may turn and fight, curse the caster with a bad mood, or slip away. With Spirit 1 a mage can right-click a spirit and bargain with it instead: a day's service for Mana, its offering, or the bane it wants gone. A bargain leaves no grudge. Birth Spirit can make a servitor instead of a spirit: a small made spirit in Twilight over a room, with one task. A sweeper clears filth, a warden sends a letter when an enemy walks in, a hearth keeps the room at 21°C, a gardener makes plants grow a fifth faster, a mender gives damaged things back some hit points each day, and a lamp lights the room. Only Spirit sight sees it, as a small light over its spot. Cast Indefinite (Advanced Duration, slid to the end), it lasts for good.

Some spells take care of the dull work round the colony. Each one is a chore, so a mage whose Wisdom is Enlightened rolls Wisdom after it. - Shaping can wash an area clean of filth, or cut its stone chunks into blocks. - Nigredo and Albedo can take a corpse's taint off clothes, or turn a slag chunk into steel. - Without a Trace can hide that a corpse ever wore what the subject has on. - Celestial Fire can bring the fuel it burns (blood, Gnosis, Conviction or Mana) to the caster as Mana, up to her Gnosis. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. The Pentacle mages of the region keep to themselves. A few days after your colony's first true mage, the nearest Consilium's Herald writes, and from then on its towns show on the world map. Each Consilium has 7 to 11 named mages, led by a Hierarch.

An apostate whose Consilium knows her can ask to join an Order from the Order page. A trial errand follows, and members get a duty about every 45 days. Each Order brings its rote Skills, its own rotes and High Speech. Order What it is Adamantine Arrow Warrior-mages who hold that magic is conflict. They guard the Consilium and answer its calls to fight. Free Council The youngest Order, who look for magic in the made world: machines, cities, the work of Sleepers' hands. Guardians of the Veil The Order of secrets. They keep magic hidden from Sleepers and hunt down the mages who show it. Mysterium Scholars and keepers of lore. They hunt for Artifacts, grimoires and places of power, and keep them safe. Silver Ladder Would-be rulers of the Awakened, who mean to lead mages and, one day, the world. Seers of the Throne Mages who serve the Exarchs, the tyrants who rule the Supernal from the far side of the Abyss. They hold the world's Sleepers in their sleep and pay well for the work.

Deeds add standing, 10 points to a dot of Status. Crimes and refused summons take it away. Titles follow Status, from Herald at 2 up to Councilor. When a Hierarch's seat comes free, the Consilium elects a new one.

A mage with the Retainer Background (see the sworn Consilium), or with Status 2 or more in her Order or the Consilium, has a Sleepwalker working for her from a town near the colony: one for each dot of whichever is higher. They show on the Contacts page of the Awakened tab. They need no looking after, and go when the dots do. Once a week each can be asked for one favour: - Goodwill: they put in a good word, and the town's faction thinks better of the colony. - Seer word: if the Seers keep a Pylon in a town near theirs, its place comes to light, with the letter to raid it, tell the Consilium or sell the silence.

Standing buys things from the Consilium's mages: tass, rotes, grimoires, teaching, healing and more. "Ask the Consilium..." on the Order page opens a window with a tab for each price; a greyed Ask button says what's missing. The giver depends on the service. At Status 1 or more a mage can go into debt. The Order page shows both Statuses as dots, with the standing toward the next one, her office, the Hierarch and any debt.

A Consilium hears crimes by colony mages it knows: killing a mage, Blood Sacrifice of a person, obvious magic before Sleepers, and more. The summons offers four answers: - Attend the hearing. The Provost comes for about a day. Talk your way through it in the talk window. Friendly cabals speak for you, and feuding ones against you. - Pay a fine in standing. - Refuse, and lose Status. - Duel the Consilium's champion in a Duel Arcane. Sentences run from cleared, through penance and lost Status, up to exile and death. An exiled mage has no Status and no Consilium. A summons, a trial errand, a duty and a Seer case each show in the Quests tab with what's left to do and the time left.

The nearest Consilium you know sends requests through the storyteller, like any vanilla quest: - Host an envoy. One or two of its mages stay for a day and a half. Seers or Banishers come for them. - Lend a mage for four days. - Take back a Hallow the Seers' thralls are holding. Pays tass and silver. - Recover an Artifact Banishers stole from the Mysterium. Pays the Artifact, one not yet found in your world. - Break a Banisher camp near the Consilium. Done, every colony mage that Consilium knows gains 3 standing, as for a duty; let lapse, they lose half that.

Besides missions, the Consilium and your mages' Orders write with smaller requests. Each answers with Accept or Refuse; a refusal is noticed. Every one has its own switch and frequency in the settings. - Mysterium readers. Once your grimoires are worth it (a rote's dots each, an Artifact 5), a Mysterium mage asks to read in your best library for 2 to 6 nights. Refused, your Mysterium mages lose Order standing and the others Consilium standing. A big Library also draws Seer raids. - Teaching. A guest asks to learn a rote, an Arcanum dot or an Attainment from one of your mages, one lesson a night (right-click the guest). - Rescues. A mage chased by Seers (the Seers follow), a mage caught in a Paradox anomaly at the map's edge (carry it to a bed), an apostate under sentence (hiding one is a crime the Consilium may find out). A rescued mage owes a service, paid as standing. A mage freed from a Paradox anomaly also leaves the Consilia owing the colony help: the Fighters on call row on the Overview page counts it, and Call in brings a few of their mages to fight. - Favours. Watch a mage in a long trance, foster an apprentice for a season, send tass or a good-quality item to imbue, host two quarrelling cabals for a night, have a doctor restore a maimed mage, lend a skilled Sleepwalker for a season. - Order requests. At Order Status 2, 3 and 4 each Order asks its own: tass, a catalogue and a relic hunt for the Mysterium; sparring, a guard post and a Banisher hunt for the Arrow; a witness questioned, a watcher housed and a Hallow held for the Guardians; backing, a case argued and an envoy for the Ladder; parts, a technique and a mage lent for the Free Council. They pay Order standing, more at higher Status. A guest hurt or killed in your care costs every colony mage standing.

News of the Consilia reaching the colony (Sleepers Awakening, Paradoxes, duels arcane, Seer attacks, Hallows found and gone dry) is on the Chronicle page under Rim by Night, at the top of the list down the window's left side, and the colony's own mages (Awakenings, duels arcane and Paradoxes lived through) are on its Our story page. Both hold every mod's lines; click Awakened on a page's left for only the mages' lines. Click a line to find the Consilium or the mage. The Overview page has an "Ask to host" link for the highest gathering the colony can host now (greyed with the reason when none is), and the Consilium or an Order writes when one opens. Each is hosted once a year at most. The preparation window lists what's needed; the Seers may strike on one night, and the host's skill rolls decide each night. Host's Status Gathering Nights Needs Consilium 2 Cabal summit: two cabals settle a Hallow quarrel 1 Consilium 3 Lex Magica hearing, the host on the bench 1 the host's Sanctum Consilium 4 The assembly: reports, a Duel Arcane, a vote 3 a Hallow, free beds Consilium 5 Convocation: a war on the nearest Seer Pylon 3 a Hallow, free beds Order 2 Mysterium symposium, Arrow war council and duels, Guardians' secrecy review, Ladder audience, Free Council vote 1 or 2 a library for the symposium Every gathering needs meals for each guest and night. A good showing pays the host Consilium standing (Order standing at an Order's event), more for a high score. If the convocation backs the war, the Pylon is found and a raid site appears beside its town. Titles still follow Status as before.

Two colony mages can form a cabal from the Order page, and you name it when the first one joins. Cabalmates share their Sanctums, think better of each other, and can take the Cabal Theme Merit. The Consilium's own cabals visit, ask for help or for a share of your Hallow, send a mage who wants to join, and take sides at hearings by how much they like you. The Consilium's cabals are also on the Cabals page of its window, as cards with temperament, power out of 20 and what they think of you. Ask them for work gives one of their missions once every five days: an Artifact back from Banishers (scholarly, reclusive), a rival's Hallow taken from the Seers (ambitious, militant, reckless), or a mage to lend for quieting a careless one (ambitious, militant). Done, the cabal gains a point of power and 2 regard. When a cabal comes within two power of the Hierarch (who stands at 10 above the cabals) and stays there for 30 days, it calls a vote on the seat. The Consilium sits 20 to 40 days later; each side's chance is its power, a deciding mission done for it counting two. Back a side from the page: 6 standing if it wins, 6 lost if it doesn't. A cabal that wins makes its leader Hierarch.
Each side has Doors equal to their Willpower. Attacks open Doors and Defenses close them. The winner leaves Triumphant, and the loser loses Willpower for each Door opened.

A tavern counter (Furniture tab) works for a mage colony too. Its Guests button lets in the named mages of the nearest Consilium you know, by Path, besides townsfolk. A counter standing on a Hallow is a cafe: each party of mages leaves a point of Mana in the Hallow, up to what it holds. Mage Sight shows a mage what any other guest is. ← Awakened contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material.
