Swear the colony to one Consilium and its mages stop being names on a roster. Each has a personality, means, a goal of its own and an opinion of you that moves with what you do. They hand you work, owe you pledges, fight beside you and, if they come to hate you, work against you.

On the Overview page of the Awakened window, use Swear to this home. You need: - a colony mage with Status 1 or more at that Consilium, - the Pentacle at peace with the colony. One Consilium at a time. Its roster fills to 8 to 12 named mages with new apprentices. New pages appear on the Awakened window's rail: People, Council and, while a war runs, War. Leaving costs your mages a dot of Status there. Loyal mages drop to -5 regard, and the pledges the Consilium owes you shrink a size. A Consilium that falls frees the colony with a letter.

Every Consilium the colony knows can owe it pledges, trivial, minor, major or life, as Kindred courts do. A Consilium's mission pays one when it's done: trivial for an early colony, minor once raids come at a mid-game size, major for the hardest. Once sworn, its mages owe you pledges for their own errands too. Spend them on the Pledges page of the Awakened window. Ask lists what a Consilium does for a pledge, and a bigger pledge covers a smaller service: tass (trivial), Sentinels at the door or a lesson worth 1 Arcane Experience to every colony mage (minor), an Artifact (major), the Athenaeum opened, 4 Arcane Experience each (life). The services priced in standing stay on Ask the Consilium. Ledger lists each pledge with who owes it and why; Call in on a row picks what that pledge pays for. Animals bought from a Consilium are paid in pledges too. Leaving shrinks its pledges a size.

The People page lists every named mage: title, cabal (Path and order for those in none) and regard, with a filter for friends, rivals and enemies. Click a mage to see their personality, means, goal, friends and dislikes. You only see a mage's personality and means once you've met them: talked to them in their town, finished a mission they gave, or looked at them with Mage Sight. Regard event Change A mission done for them +2 A mission done for their cabal or a friend +1 A step of their goal done +3 A gift from their row +1 per 500 silver, up to +3 a season Their mission refused or let lapse -1 (Proud -3) A mission done against them or a friend -3 Betraying their goal -10, for good Regard drifts a point toward 0 every season.

Personality How they pay and behave Greedy silver x0.7, standing x1.5 Cautious silver and standing x1.25, but the biggest pledge they'll owe is a size smaller Loyal everything x1.25 while you never cross them or their friends; betrayal makes an enemy for good Conniving pays with a pledge another mage owes them Cowardly one more open mission, aimed at their rivals; pay x1.2 Proud standing x1.5, silver x0.8; refusals cost 3 regard Zealous only the fight against the Seers; those pay x1.5 Generous everything x1.3; now and then asks one back Vengeful bad blood never fades; an enemy at -5 Mystery-hungry asks for lore, and pays in Arcane Experience: one per 250 silver of the job to each colony mage there Careless riskier work, paying x1.3 A cabal's first mage has the personality of its temperament: Scholarly Mystery-hungry, Ambitious Proud, Reclusive Cautious, Militant Zealous, Reckless Careless. Cabalmates are friends.

Means come from the mage's title, wealth and the pledges owed to them: a poor one offers one mission at a time and pays x0.6, a comfortable one two at x1.0, a rich one three at x1.4. Each mage wants something, hidden until they count you a friend (regard +6) or you have a hold over them. A goal is three steps: two missions bent to it, then the prize. Keeping the prize is a betrayal. Goal What you get for it Collector a daimonomikon Lore hunter an Atlantean tablet or a Seer's ledger, both grimoires Power seeker silver by its means, and its vote for a year Revenge a major pledge and the enemy's goods Freedom its regard stays at +6 or more for good Childe a minor pledge now, its apprentice on your side later A cure for Paradox scars each colony mage learns, 3 Arcane Experience Kingmaker the new Hierarch starts at regard +6 Homecoming another Consilium, met Buried secret a life pledge

Under Your seats on the Overview page, a colony mage can take the title her Status there earns. A title held by a mage makes that mage your rival. The Hierarch's seat is still won by election, as before. Title Status Duty each season Herald 2 one hearing or message Sentinel 3 one guard mission Provost 3 one goods or trade errand Interfector 3 one mission against a Banisher or Seer Councilor 4 vote in the council A duty kept adds standing and a dot. Three missed in a row and the title is lost, with a dot of Status, to the next in line. The mage's own tab shows the title and when its duty is due, and an alert warns two days ahead.

Each season the Hierarch and Councilors vote on one or two motions: bringing Awakenings before the Consilium, moving against the Seers, hunting Banishers, the Hierarch's due. A colony Councilor votes too.
Rivals slander the colony or stymie your next mission with their own people. Enemies send hired raiders. Capture one and question them in prisoner talk to learn who sent them, then Accuse that mage.

A war runs against the Seers of the Throne's nearest settlement. Its score starts at 50: a season of incursions, two of raids on their Hallow, sanctum and archive while you hold your own, then the final assault at 70, the desperate defence at 30, or a truce. The skirmishes come a few weeks apart. A war mission you let lapse is fought without you: the Consilium's members against the enemy's, by their strength, and members can die in it. Hover over the stages, the score and the holdings on the War page for what each one needs.

The Backgrounds page on a mage's tab buys rated Backgrounds with standing at the sworn Consilium: the new rating x 2, never experience. Leaving the Consilium, or the Consilium falling, halves every dot. Now and then a rival strikes at one of them, at most once a season: a letter gives six days (more with Contacts) to answer with a mission or a favour the rival owes, or the dot is lost. The "Rival strikes on Backgrounds" setting makes strikes rarer or more common, or turns them off. Background Each dot Allies armed mortals to call on any map with enemies on it; they never witness anything Contacts a day more to answer a strike, and a chance each season to strike back at a rival Fame more tavern guests and regulars Influence a caravan from the Consilium's faction once a season Mentor a Consilium mage of high enough rank (a member 1 to the leader 5) teaches Resources 100 x dots squared silver a season Retainer a Sleepwalker in a town near the colony who does a favour once a week, and never witnesses vulgar magic Retainer used to be a Merit. A mage who had it keeps the same dots, now as the Background.

Under the Consilium heading of the Awakened settings: the sworn Consilium on or off, the war chance, enemy acts a season and how fast regard fades. The werespiders: children of Queen Ananasa. An Ananasi has no Rage and feels little. It runs on blood, bites with venom in every form, spins webs, and has a swarm form that crawls under doors and survives being killed. Silver doesn't hurt it. Other shifters think it evil, and the Wyrm-serving Hatar give them reason to.

- Blood. A pool of 10 pays for Gifts, shifts and healing. The "Spend blood" button quickens it, mends its worst wound (five points for an aggravated one) or purges a disease. - Feeding. Blood comes back only by drinking. Right-click someone who can't resist: downed, asleep, a prisoner or a colony animal. It never drains a victim past a dangerous blood loss. - Venom. Lilian and Pithus bites are aggravated and can leave a venom that kills if no one tends it. - Webs. Pithus spins web walls and throws snares that hold a pawn until it tears free. - The swarm. As a Crawlerling it takes little from bullets and arrows, a lot from fire and blasts, passes any door, and is the only form that can step sideways. Killed by anything but fire or a blast, it scatters and reforms days later at its Sylie, weak for a while and maybe with some skills lost. - The Sylie. The Rite of Spinning makes one. In its room the Ananasi regains Gnosis. - Cold. It breaks less often than a mortal and heals at a human's pace. - Fighting. Lilian, and away at 30% health.
Breed What it is Homid Born human, then changed slowly over days in the Metamorphosis. Arachnid Hatched from an egg sac, a spider that became a person.

Aspect What it is Tenere Servants of the Weaver as she was: order, pattern and control. Hatar Servants of the Wyrm as it was, the Destroyer: the Unweavers. Kumoti Servants of the Wyld as it should be: change and growth.
Group What it is Myrmidon The Queen's warriors. Viskr Judges and mystics. Wyrsta Questioners, who test the other Ananasi.

The wereravens: Gaia's eyes and tattletales. A Corax is fragile, fast and curious, and can't keep a secret to itself. It flies in two of its three forms, gold burns it, and it drinks the eyes of the dead to learn how they died. Corax have no packs, no auspices and no real tribes; every one of them belongs to Raven and to the sun.

- Flight. Crinos and Corvid can fly (a jump of 25 cells, 15 for a homid) and peck out an eye. A caravan with a raven in it travels faster. - Light bones. A Corax dodges well but takes more from blunt blows. - Secrets. A Corax learns secrets about people and factions. It can tell them to a colonist, whisper them to Raven, sell them to the subject's faction or its enemies, or hold one over a trader for a better price. Each one is Wisdom. The Secrets page on its tab lists them. - Raven's laws. Holding a secret past a week costs Wisdom. Three days in a bad mood cost Honor. A season without flying costs Glory. - Shiny things. A drafted Corax near silver, gold or jade rolls Willpower or pockets it, and carries its finds to its bedroom. - Drinking eyes. Right-click a fresh corpse in a flying form. The left eye names the killer, the right gives a secret and some of the dead's best skill. One eye a body, unless the Corax has the Double Draught Merit. - The uPhone. A fetish that calls any faction you know by radio. - Fighting. A Corax fights from range or from the air, takes the Crinos when cornered, and flies off at half health.

Breed What it is Homid Born human, with thin black hair, black eyes and a ring finger longer than the middle one. Slower to take to the air than a raven-born Corax. Corvid Born a raven, and still a raven at heart: a fast flier, poor with tools, books and medicine.

Group What it is No group Most Corax answer to Raven alone and belong to no group. Chasers Gangs of young Corax who hunt the uncanny together. They break up within a year or two. Leshy Paranoid forest tricksters. Three in four of them were born ravens. Hermetic Order of Swift Light The breed's business arm: couriers and sellers of secrets. Gulls of Battle Seekers of old stories and new corpses. They follow the fighting. Murder's Daughters Women only. They pick fights to catch the Morrigan's eye, take the birdman's shape to do it, and stay in a fight longer than other Corax. Tulugaq The tricksters' tricksters, close to the Nuwisha. The Morrigan Always exactly three women, with eagles. They turn up before every great battle. The Sun-Lost Corax who left the sun for the deep spirit world.

Claw and beak wounds are aggravated. Mortals who see it suffer a lesser Delirium. Corvid -1 +1 -3 +4 A raven with a four-foot wingspan. It talks only with other Corax, and carries almost nothing.

Fera works with every mod in the series. This page covers how the breeds get on with the others, and what the Embrace does to each.

Each breed has its own feelings toward Garou, each Garou tribe, vampires, hunters, mages and mortals. They come from the book and run through Core's kind opinions, so the opinion slider in Core's settings scales them too. Anyone who feels something about the Garou feels the same about a Fera, unless they have a lean of their own. - The Garou Nation loses a little goodwill each day while the colony keeps a Garou alongside a Ratkin, Mokolé or Ananasi colonist. - The Corax, Ananasi, Gurahl and Gumagan Mokolé dislike mages who bind spirits, as Garou do.

Hunters who come for a colony of Fera arm for the Fera they find: gold for a Corax, often gold for a Mokolé, plain steel for a Nuwisha or an Ananasi. With any Garou on the map they bring silver, as before.
A vampire can drink from a Fera, with one exception: Ananasi blood is rejected, and the vampire throws it up. An Ananasi that drinks a vampire takes vitae, a blood point at a time, with no bond.

Breed What happens Corax Rises as an Abomination, and burns to ash at the first sunrise, roof or not Ratkin Rises, then rots over fifteen days, losing pieces, and dies Ananasi Refuses the Embrace Gurahl Rises as Garou do Mokolé Rises in a frenzy that won't end, and burns at the first sunrise Kitsune Never rises. Its body burns in a burst of fire Nuwisha Never rises While a risen Fera lives, its breed's faction thinks worse of the colony. The Abominations setting in Fera's settings turns all of this off; a Fera then rises as a Garou does.
Hunters see a Fera as a monster, as they see a Garou. Fera kills leave claw marks for a case, like Garou ones.

Mage Sight reads a Fera as half spirit, like a Garou. Death sight sees an Ananasi as alive. ← Fera contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. The werebears: Gaia's healers, nearly wiped out in the War of Rage and only lately awake again. A Gurahl is huge, patient and slow to anger. When it does get angry it pours Rage into its own body. It sleeps heavy in winter, can hibernate for a season, and its oldest Gift brings a dead shapeshifter back.

- Rage on the body. Spend Rage for a moment of Strength or Stamina, or for an hour of bear's vigour that cuts the damage it takes. - Adamant Will. Hard to bend its mind, while it keeps its duty. - Auspices in order. Every Gurahl starts as Arcas and lives the five auspices in turn. Each step opens with a milestone: a kill, a lover or a peaceful season, then ranks 3 and 4. The Gifts of every auspice it has lived stay open. - Winter. Drowsy on a winter map: it tires sooner and fights a little slower. - Hibernation. Fifteen days of sleep, half inside its Glade. Sleeping it through heals everything, aggravated wounds too. A wound wakes it early with nothing healed. - Duty. A season away from home fails its duty. It loses Willpower each day, then sinks into Bhernocht, the Gurahl's Harano. Coming home ends it. - The Umbral Glade. A Background: a claimed stretch of land. A Gurahl steps sideways only from inside it, and regains Gnosis sleeping there. - Gaia's Breath. Brings back a dead Garou or Fera, never kin, for a permanent Gnosis and Willpower. It gets harder each hour after the death, and a botch brings the body back as a fomor. - Fighting. Crinos, and it stays until 20% health.
Breed What it is Homid Born human, often tall and strong. Ursine Born a bear, and slow to learn the ways of people.

Group What it is Forest Walkers Black bears and spirit bears: the most numerous tribe, fond of powwows and respectful of elders. Ice Stalkers Polar bears who live in family groups, playful artists of bone and ice. Mountain Guardians Grizzlies: solitary, competitive, given to ritual combat. River Keepers Bears of every kind, givers of gifts and hosts of gatherings.

Aspect What it is Arcas The first auspice: the First Change, the Gallivant and a head full of questions. Uzmati The warrior, travelling alone after the first real battle. Kojubat The rememberer, learning lore and starting a lifework. Kieh The mystic, given to reflection, rites and mentoring. Rishi The judge, who keeps the peace.

The werefoxes: tricksters, sorcerers and holy warriors bound by the Laws of Heaven, and the youngest Changing Breed. Kitsune don't regenerate, cause no Delirium and frenzy only as foxes, so they keep out of fights and win with magic, illusion and the odd killing. Silver hurts them no more than any blade.

- Paths. A new Kitsune has no Path. It chooses one at the Rite of the Crossroads, held by a Kitsune of rank 2 or more. With no elder around it can choose by itself once it has the Renown. Choosing gives rank 1, the Path's Rage and a first Gift. - Long life. Ageing halves with each rank past the first. - No Delirium. Mortals who see a Kitsune in its war form know what they saw, and the Veil suffers. - Healing. As a human, unless Enduring Warrior lends it regeneration for an hour. - Fighting. It stays back in human form and casts. An Eji fights as a fox. It runs at 40% health.

Breed What it is Kojin Born human, and aware of being different long before the First Change. Roko Born a fox and often raised by wild foxes. Shinju Born of two Kitsune, with no deformity and no curse: a full Kitsune in every way.

Aspect What it is Kataribe The path of clay: poets, builders and loremasters. Gukutsushi The path of fog: dreamweavers, tricksters and healers. Doshi The path of lightning: sorcerers who use evil against evil, living alone in old temples. Eji The path of lava: holy warriors of swift, neat executions. No Path A young Kitsune who has not yet chosen a Path at the Rite of the Crossroads.

The weresaurians: Gaia's memory, last of the dragons, children of the sun. A Mokolé remembers what its line has seen back to the age of the dinosaur kings. It has a human form, a crocodile or lizard form of its varna, and the Archid, a dragon shaped by its own memory. Gold and silver both burn it.

- The sun. Its auspice comes from the sun at the First Change: eclipse, night, cloud, noon, dawn or dusk. A seasonal stream takes it from the season instead. It gains Gnosis only by meditating in daylight under open sky; cloud halves it, the wallow adds half again. - Varna. Each Mokolé is born to a varna that sets its Rage and its reptile form. Alligators and Gila monsters are slow on land, monitors quick. - The Archid. Each permanent Gnosis point buys a characteristic for the war form, kept for good: armoured scales, wings, fire breath, poison sacs and more. Some can be taken up to three times. The Mokolé page on its tab has the builder. - Mnesis. A trance of a few hours lends a skill for a day, at 10 plus the Background's dots. - The Innocents. In the Penumbra, the stillborn may whisper, haunt its dreams or steal a memory that spoils the next Mnesis. - Stepping sideways needs Walking Between Worlds, except for a Gumagan. - Fighting. Archid, and away at a quarter health.
Breed What it is Homid Born human, often in warm lands. Suchid Hatched from a reptile egg, a crocodile or lizard that became a person.

Group What it is Mokolé-mbembe The Stream of the Fighters, the largest: alligators, crocodiles and a few caimans. Gumagan The Stream of the Forerunners, with the deepest memories. Saltwater crocodiles and monitors. Makara The Stream of the Folk, diplomats to the other Fera. Gharials and muggers. Zhong Lung The Stream of the Philosophers, part of the Beast Courts with the Kitsune.

Aspect What it is Rising Sun, Striking Changed between dawn and noon: quick to strike first. Noonday Sun, Unshading Changed within an hour of noon: the bane of creatures of darkness. Setting Sun, Warding Changed between noon and sunset: defenders of others. Shrouded Sun, Concealing Changed under a hidden sun: hunters who go unseen. Midnight Sun, Shining Changed at night: humour and courage when all seems lost. Decorated Sun, Gathering Changed under a haloed sun, the rarest of all: at their best working with others. Solar Eclipse, Crowning Changed in an eclipse. All Mokolé defer to them, and they must serve the greater good. Vasanta A Makara changed in spring: warriors and travellers. Grisma A Makara changed in summer: judges and police. Zarad A Makara changed in autumn: mystics. Hemanta A Makara changed in winter: tricksters. Tung Chun A Zhong Lung of spring and the east wind, blue-green. Nam Hsai A Zhong Lung of summer and the south wind, yellow. Sai Chau A Zhong Lung of autumn and the west wind, white. Pei Tung A Zhong Lung of winter and the north wind, black.

The werecoyotes: Coyote's children, who teach the proud, the foolish and the Wyrm through tricks that are often deadly. They have no Rage and never frenzy, silver doesn't hurt them, and they regenerate like Garou. Each follows one face of Coyote.

- No Rage. The Gift of Rage gives it 5 Rage for an hour. While it lasts it can frenzy and silver burns. - Faces of Coyote. Pick one with the "Face of Coyote" button. The first is free; after that it can change once a season for experience. Each face gives something: stealth, toughness, research, trade, plants and more. Ptah opens the Rite of Dansing. Raven's face turns away from a Nuwisha who carries too much silver. - Pranks. Right-click a person and choose "Play a prank": a tripwire, swapped food, a stolen garment, a false alarm, a rigged blast, a falling weight, or setting two people on each other. Most wait hours for the right moment. Each target once a season. - Renown from pranks. The Wyrm and the proud are worth the most. Hurting an innocent costs Humor, and being seen by the target's side costs Cunning. - Sing Back the Dead. A rank 5 rite on a fresh corpse. Coyote's odds show first. If Coyote says no, singing on kills the singer. - Sendeh's cries. Laughter that sours moods, and a predator's cry that scares off wild animals. - Fighting. At range in human form, Manabozho against a lone foe close by, coyote form to run.
Breed What it is Homid Born human. The First Change came as a revelation, not a horror. Latrani Born a coyote, and far more common than wolf-born Garou.

The wererats: Gaia's cullers, the most numerous Changing Breed and the least sane. A Ratkin is small, quick and angry at everything human. It lives in tunnels, can't catch a disease, and calls its kind with a scream only they hear. Ratkin fight from cover and run when it goes badly.

- Plague-proof. No vanilla plague, infection or parasite takes hold. - Tunnels. In the dark under a thick roof a Ratkin moves faster. Its Crinos digs fast. - Rat-holes. Build them, and a Ratkin in Crinos or rat form can go in one and come out of another, unseen and untouchable on the way. - Keening. At half health or downed, a Ratkin keens. The colony gets a letter and friendly Ratkin nearby come running. - Litters. Once a day a Ratkin colonist makes up to ten tamed rats its kin. A wild rat comes when it calls. - The Birthing Plague. A rite on an adult kin that might make a new Ratkin, and might kill. The odds show before it starts. A survivor wanders in a birthing madness for days, shorter with Ratkin colonists nearby. - Aspects. Each aspect plays differently: a Blade Slave frenzies easily and starts with a dagger, a Twitcher's Rage jumps about, a Knife Skulker grows angry at injustice. - Fighting. Crinos, with friends, then away at 40% health.

Breed What it is Homid A human kin who lived through the Birthing Plague. At the bottom of the nest. Metis Born of two Ratkin, deformed and sterile. The nest keeps them as guards and wardens. Rodens Born a rat and raised in the walls. Rodens sit at the top of the nest, as courtiers and Rat Kings.

Aspect What it is Tunnel Runner Messengers and scouts who blend into any crowd and never stay long. Shadow Seer Mystics who hear the spirits and sometimes care more for the spirit world than this one. Knife Skulker Spies and assassins with a sense of justice. A Skulker never lets a target see the blow that kills it. Blade Slave The warriors, tough and thirsty for blood, each carrying a pain-dagger. Engineer A freak aspect: tinkerers who can make any machine run for a while out of junk. Plague Lord A freak aspect: healers who serve a spirit of disease, and spread what it asks. Munchmausen A freak aspect: liars so good that everyone believes them, themselves included. Twitcher A freak aspect: paranoid and forgettable, with a Rage that runs away with them.

At the start, each Fera in the scenario opens a making menu, on the same frame as Garou's. The kind is fixed by the scenario. You pick the group, breed, aspect and varna where the breed has them, and a Merit and a Flaw (more with Core's Merits at making setting, each extra Merit with a Flaw of its own). The beginning Gifts come by the breed's own rule.
A Fera's inspect tab has Garou's pages plus one for its kind, named after it: the Corax's secrets, the Mokolé's Archid builder and so on.

The Fera button on the bottom bar shows once the colony has a Fera: - Overview: the colony's Fera, the breeds you've met and how they feel about you. - Homes: every known home of every breed you've met. - A page per breed you've met: what they are, their goodwill, your colonists of that breed and their homes.
- An Archid point is waiting to be spent. - An Ananasi is low on blood. - A drowsy Gurahl isn't in bed. Garou's Gift-ready and Veil alerts count Fera too.

With Odyssey your colony can live in orbit. The World of Darkness stays on the ground: nobody from these mods comes up uninvited unless "The World of Darkness reaches orbit" is on in Core's settings. Help you call still comes, by drop pod, and leaves on Royalty's shuttle. Without Royalty it stays aboard until the ship lands. The colony is whichever home holds most of your free colonists, so visitors go where your people are. Keep Fera in their breed form in vacuum. Any form that can't wear clothes pulls the vacsuit off, and a frenzy forces the shift. Outside the ship that kills. No rat holes can be dug in orbit, and a Corax can't fly where there's no air. A kin animal brought aboard needs air like any animal. Far from Gaia, caerns and stepping sideways work as they do for Garou.

Every Fera is built on Garou's rules, so most of Being Garou holds for them too. This page covers what's the same for all seven breeds and what each changes.

- Rage works as Garou's for the Corax, Ratkin, Gurahl, Mokolé and Kitsune. The Ananasi and the Nuwisha have none. - Gnosis works as Garou's, except for the Mokolé, who gain it only from sunlight. - Blood is the Ananasi's pool: 10 points, refilled only by feeding. It pays for what Rage pays for in the others. - Willpower works as Garou's.

Each breed has its own forms on Garou's five slots: a human form, a near-man form, a war form, an in-between form and an animal form. Not every breed has all five, and some forms open only with a Gift (the Ratkin's Ratman and Rat Thing, the Ananasi's Araneid, the Mokolé's Reptoid). Each breed's page lists its forms and what they add to the Attributes. Shifting, the form bar and gear by body work as Garou's. Shifting is a Veil act unless the new form brings the Delirium with it.
The Corax, Ratkin, Gurahl, Mokolé and Nuwisha regenerate as Garou do. The Ananasi heal by spending blood. The Kitsune heal like humans unless a Gift helps.

Breed Burned by Corax Gold Mokolé Gold and silver Ratkin, Gurahl Silver Kitsune Silver hurts them like any blade, no worse Ananasi, Nuwisha Nothing A bane wound is aggravated and doesn't regenerate, as silver is for a Garou. Hunters who know what they're after bring gold for a Corax.
Breeds with Rage frenzy as Garou do, each in its own way. The Kitsune frenzy only as foxes. The Ananasi and the Nuwisha never frenzy, unless a Nuwisha takes the Gift of Rage.

Each breed has its own three Renown tracks and its own rank names, and earns them by its own deeds: secrets for the Corax, pranks for the Nuwisha, milestones for the Gurahl. Experience works as Garou's.

Each breed has human kin, and most have animal kin too. Tamed animals of the right kind become a Fera's kin: rats for the Ratkin, bears for the Gurahl. Ratkin and Ananasi kin never have a First Change.

Shifters of different breeds can form one pack with the Rite of the Joined Circle, Garou among them. It works like Garou's Rite of the Totem. With a Nuwisha in the circle, the totem has to be a trickster. Rite What it does Rite of the Joined Circle Shifters of different breeds, Garou among them, sing of Gaia's need for renewal in a space decked out to please a spirit, and bind themselves to it as one pack. Their Totem dots together must reach the totem's cost. A Nuwisha in the circle means a trickster totem.

Merit What it is Double Draught Can drink both of a dead body's eyes, not only one. Background What it is Umbral Glade A stretch of land where the Gauntlet is thin and Bear's children rest. Inside it a Gurahl steps sideways freely, regains Gnosis while it sleeps, and hibernates in half the time. Each dot makes it bigger: 36 cells at one dot up to 5000 at five. Mnesis The memories of every ancestor of its line. Each dot reaches further back, from a century to the time of the Dinosaur Kings, and lends a stronger ancestor's skill to a Mnesis quest. Wallow A home by the water where the Mokolé and their kin gather. On its home map it draws half again as much Gnosis from the sun, and a Mnesis trance takes half the time. ← Fera contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. The Changing Breeds have been in hiding since the War of Rage. Each breed has its own faction. They're all there from the start of the game, hidden, with homes on the world map. Like every faction in the series, each one rolls its own name.

Breed Where they live Ratkin Nests, often under or near towns Gurahl Small homes of one werebear and a kin or two Mokolé Wallows by the water Kitsune The Beast Courts Corax, Ananasi, Nuwisha No homes of their own: they travel, or keep to themselves Homes grow, fall and get founded through Core's living world, and show in the Chronicle like everyone else's. A few ordinary towns hide an Ananasi, and some hide Ratkin kin or other kin.

A breed's faction stays hidden until the colony has one of that breed. Three to eight days later it comes out of hiding: its goodwill resets to what it feels toward a colony with one of its own, and its nearest home writes to you. Travelling breeds send word by a passing stranger. Once a faction is known, its visitors, caravans and raids come like any other faction's.

Each breed starts with its own goodwill toward a colony, better if the colony has one of its kind, worse if the colony keeps Garou. Most of them have not forgiven the War of Rage. The Ratkin dislike everyone, and the Kitsune and Mokolé get on with each other.

While the colony has no Fera, a stranger may turn up: someone in the middle of their First Change, running from whatever is after them. They join at rank 0 or 1. Their pursuers arrive a few hours later: fomori, a Garou hunting pack, or plain raiders.

A breed's faction that likes you (goodwill 40 or more) may send one of its own to join, at most once a year for each breed. A known home can also find you a Fera of a group, aspect and rank you ask for, paid in goodwill.

The old war still smoulders. Garou septs strike the breeds' homes, the Ratkin and Mokolé most often, the Kitsune least. Ratkin nests strike back at the septs. When a fight the colony knows of happens, its Garou and that breed's Fera feel old wounds: a worse mood for a few days and a worse opinion of each other. ← Fera contents · The Rim by Night This is not official World of Darkness material. Big clothes, tools and weapons still work, and mortals find it hard to look at. Awe People listen when it speaks. Backbite Striking from behind. Bad medicine Yes A sickness no doctor can find. Everything is a little harder for a month. Bad Medicine Bag The bones of a small creature dead of disease, with a Rat-spirit in them. Woken and slipped to someone within reach, it brings a month of a sickness no doctor finds. Bad Mnesis Yes An Innocent has twisted one of its memories. The next Mnesis quest will turn on it. Bargain Knows something a trader would rather keep quiet, and trades the better for it. Bear's vigour Rage turned into sheer toughness: it shrugs off part of every wound for an hour. Beautiful lie told Told today's lie that everyone believes. Befriend Strangers warm to it from the first word. Behemoth Twice the bulk: it shrugs off more of every wound and hits harder, more each time it is taken. Beneath notice Part of the background. Nobody sees it while it keeps still, and thieves overlook whatever lies near it. Binocular vision Eyes set forward like a hunter's: it sees better. Birthing Pains Yes The price of a fox child. It comes as labour ends, with no wound and no cure. Bjornen A cave bear, bigger than any bear alive. No hands and no speech. Black widow Its venom makes every hurt worse for a day. Blade slave Tough as old leather. Bladed tail A tail edged with blades that lashes for aggravated wounds. Blessed blade A spirit in its weapon: its blows wound as a Garou's claws do. Blisters Yes Ugly blisters all over the face. Nobody wants to look at them, or listen. Blood of Illusion Its blood makes those who drink it see things. Blood of Pain Its blood sickens whoever drinks it. Blood pump The heart pumps blood at a rate no body should bear: faster on its feet and in a fight. Blood-sick Yes Sick on a werespider's blood: wracked and barely able to act. Borrowed Gift A Gift borrowed from the mynah-spirits, for a few hours. Bound by the Great Web Yes Held fast to the world of flesh. It can't step sideways. Breath of Ananasa Holding its breath: smoke, gas and bad air can't reach it. Breed's curse Yes The Embrace took, but the blood of the Changing Breed fights it. Each breed ends its own way: the Corax and Mokole burn at the first sunrise, and the Ratkin rot to bones. The breed's own people count this one a creature of the Wyrm while it lives. Burning Blood Its blood burns whoever wounds it. Cajoled Talked round by a bear's kind words. Cajoling Has someone feeling generous: deals go its way. Can't see weapons Yes Weapons have vanished from its sight. It drops what it holds and can't find another. Carapace Skin hardened into chitin. Carrion clothes It seems dead to anyone who looks, until it acts. Chi Sense Feels Yin and Yang move: a die more on Gifts that read or change the land around it. Chung Kuel Coyote as bringer of bad luck to those who deserve it. Its followers hunt unseen and lie well. Clear mind Willpower turned to thought until sunrise: it studies and talks better. Cloak of shadows Hidden in the shadows until it strikes. Cocooned Yes Spun into an Ananasi's cocoon by the Master's Needs. Each day it fights the venom's hold on its will, and each day it loses owes the spider a service. When the venom is gone it breaks out. Cooling Yes Something is changing. Feelings come dull and distant, the skin bristles, and there are lumps beneath it that move. Corax A wereraven, one of Raven's children. The sun and the sky run in the blood, and so does the urge to tell what it knows. Hollow bones make it quick to dodge, but blows land harder. Corvid A raven with a four-foot wingspan. It talks only with other Corax, and carries almost nothing. Coyote's Intuition Knows what people least want to talk about. Coyote's mark Coyote's mark: spirits keep away. Crawlerling Hundreds of spiders of the Ananasi's mass, moving as one. It crawls under doors, bullets and arrows mostly miss it, and fire and blasts tear through it. It can't fight, carry or wear anything. Killed in this form by anything but fire or a blast, it scatters and reforms days later. Crinos The birdman: feathers, a beak and claws, with wings for arms. Clumsy on foot, it can't hold a weapon or wear anything. Claw and beak wounds are aggravated. Mortals who see it suffer a lesser Delirium. Crinos Fifteen feet of bear-man, over a ton, with nine-inch claws that dig through stone. It speaks in single words. Mortals who see it suffer a lesser Delirium. Crinos A humanoid rat with beady eyes, a pointed muzzle, clawed hands and a long naked tail. It keeps a blade in hand but sheds clothes and guns. Its bite is aggravated. Mortals who see it suffer a lesser Delirium. Curious Can't leave a new machine alone. Learns fast, and wanders off to poke at things mid-job. Curse of Tiresias Yes Turned into the other sex by a trickster's blow, for a while. Danger sense Feels trouble coming before it arrives. Darksight Sees as well in pitch dark as in daylight. Death bear delayed A werebear has asked the Death Bear to wait: it can't die of its wounds for now, though it stays down. Deep lung Lungs that hold a breath for an hour: toxic gas and smoke hardly touch it. Deep pockets Room for more than seems possible. Deeper Lungs Holds its breath for hours: toxic gas and smoke hardly touch it. Delusions of grandeur Certain of a glorious triumph to come, and telling everyone about it. Diagnose Sees at a glance what ails someone. Disappearing act Gone to every sense, as long as it doesn't move. Dragon drill Drilled into a workforce: uses the best skill any of its group has. Earworm Yes A tune that won't stop. Careful work goes slowly. Enduring warrior Its wounds close as a Garou's do. Engineer Clever hands that can make any machine run. Epidemic contagion The sicknesses this Ratkin gives spread from victim to victim. Exile from fairyland Knows for a fact it was born in fairyland and cast out, and misses it. Eye drunk A Corax drank this eye and saw what it saw. Eyes of the eagle An eagle's sight: nothing hides in the dark, smoke or fog. Fable: calm A Kitsune's tale keeps it calm: it breaks less easily. Face of Mangi The Death Bear's face: grim and deadly. It hits harder and surer. Face of Ursa Major The mother bear's face: patient and healing. Its tending heals better and it keeps calm. Face of Ursa Minor The young bear's face: curious and quick to learn. It learns faster and dodges better. False memory Yes It remembered how an ancestor did things, and remembered it wrong. Everything goes slowly for a day. False spoor It smells exactly as someone else. Fan-shadow-robe Wears a face that isn't its own, for a while. Fire breath It breathes fire, once a day. Flight of separation One raven among many. Striking gives it away for a few seconds. Fool's luck Bad luck can't touch it: no botches, only plain failures. Fox-blinded Yes A Kitsune has taken its sight for a day. Friend and foe Trusted by another people as one of their own, until it strikes or shifts. Gaia's Breath tried A werebear has already tried to breathe life back into this one. Gauntlet rent The Gauntlet is torn open here. For an hour this werebear may step into the spirit world from anywhere. Gentle Soul Free of the Curse: its Rage doesn't frighten people. Ghost danse Dancing in both worlds at once: most blows pass through it. Gift of rage Borrowed Rage, as a Garou has. It can frenzy, and silver burns. Gold burn Yes A wound from gold. On a Corax or a Mokolé the flesh around it sears, and it won't regenerate. Groom Always looks well kept. Gurahl A werebear, one of Bear's children. Healing comes to its hands as easily as fury. Hand fangs Venom fangs in the palms. Happy thoughts Calm and silly. No Rage, no frenzy. Hatchling Yes Fresh from the egg sac and ravenous. It can't leave the swarm until it has eaten for three days; then an elder takes it into the Umbra to learn the Laws. Hazer tag A patsy wears this Ratkin's trail. No hunter or nemesis can pick it out. Heart-strings played A chain of odd chances is on its way to bring it true love. Hibernating Asleep for the season. It needs no food, and when it wakes every wound and sickness will be gone. A wound or the Gift Waken will wake it early. Hollow bones Light bones make it quicker on its feet. Horn A great horn to gore with, for aggravated wounds. Hot ichor Rage boiling in the blood: it hits harder and moves faster. Hummingbird dart Feathers that fly like darts. Hydraulic strength Blood forced into the muscles: a point of Strength for each blood point spent. Image of the Great Mother Four legs, four arms, eight eyes: the shape of the Queen herself. Everyone who sees it reels. A week in the swarm follows. Imaginary friend Talks to a friend nobody else can see. The friend is very supportive. Imperial authority People listen to it as to their better, and animals bow to it. Improvisation Anything in hand is a deadly weapon. Inflict pain Each blow racks the victim with pain. Juko A fox the size of a wolf, built for long travel. It speaks only Kitsune-go. King in exile The rightful ruler of a distant, powerful country, travelling incognito. Kishijoten Coyote as healer. Its followers shrug off a little more harm and tend wounds well, and they always stop for the hurt. Kitsune A werefox. Its tails count its years of wisdom, and its illusions hide most of them. Kleptomania Pockets anything small that might come in handy, unless it wins a Willpower roll every few hours. Kokopelli Coyote as the flute player. Its followers have stamina for anything, and never strike in anger. Koto A fox's head on a furred body, with clawed hands and a tail. A blade still fits the hand. It brings no Delirium: mortals who see it remember. Its bite is aggravated. Kyubi An ordinary red fox, with a little grey. It hides well and passes for an animal. Latrani An ordinary coyote. Outsiders see only an animal. Lesions Each blow raises sores that keep the victim from running. Lesions Yes Weeping sores that make running agony. Lifted mood A werespider's touch has lifted this one's spirits. Lilian A horror of woman and giant spider: extra limbs, chitin and eight eyes, half again the Homid's size. The spare arms carry more. Clothes fall away. Mortals who see it suffer the full Delirium. Lingering pain Yes Pain that won't fade, however the wounds heal. Loki Coyote as the warrior trickster. Its followers are stronger and harder to put down, fight as Garou do, and accept every challenge. Long running The road runs short under it. Long teeth Longer fangs: its bite does more harm. Longer legs Yes Long spider legs on the war form: it runs faster. Lured Yes Drawn by pitiful moans toward their source, until something hurts it. Man-Spider Form Knows the Araneid form. Manabozho Almost eight feet of scrawny coyote-man, easily taken for a Garou's Crinos. It talks in a deep, gravelly voice. Mortals who see it suffer a lesser Delirium. Mangi's strong arms Rage in the arms: every blow lands half again as hard. Mantis blades Blades from the forearms. Fine work comes hard. Many eyes Eyes all over the body. Nothing takes it from behind. Marionette Yes It moves as a Kitsune mimes and can use no powers. Masked by the bear Hidden from its enemies by a werebear's Gift, until it attacks. Mnesis trance Deep in the memories of its line, helpless and unaware of anything around it until it comes back. Mokolé A werelizard, one of the dragon breed. The memories of its line run in the blood. Moon dance Unseen for the night, until it attacks. More arms Yes A second pair of arms on the war form: it carries twice as much. Mountain Guardian Grizzlies who test each other in ritual combat from cubhood. They fight a little surer. Munchmausen A liar everyone believes. Necrosis Yes The flesh around a werespider's bite is dying, and the rot spreads. Nest mother's rage A mother's fury at harm done to its young: stronger for an hour. New face Wears a face that isn't its own, for a while. Numbed by spider blood Yes Splashed with a werespider's blood, and the limbs have gone heavy. The feeling comes back an hour at a time. Nuwisha A werecoyote. Coyote laughs in the blood, and nothing has made it stop. Oghma Coyote as Oghma, who chooses the worthy and is never chosen. Each season he gives back five Willpower. His followers never strike another in anger. One land Leads its companions as if the world were one land again. Out of luck Yes Luck has run out: nothing it tries comes off. Paper body Folded from paper: one wound tears it. Past the tomorrow wall Has glimpsed what comes next: the next great threat is foreseen. Patience of Ananasa Perfectly still, and unseen until it strikes. Perfect sentai (Doshi) One of each Path in its sentai: a die more on its rolls. Perfect sentai (Eji) One of each Path in its sentai: it hits harder. Perfect sentai (Gukutsushi) One of each Path in its sentai: steadier hands and a better word. Perfect sentai (Kataribe) One of each Path in its sentai: its making and its words go further. Pithus A giant spider the size of a car, five hundred pounds and more. No hands and no speech. Mortals who see it suffer the full Delirium. Plague fever Yes Burning up with Rat's plague. Some never come out of it. Plague lord Knows sickness from the inside, and so knows how to treat it. Plenipotentiary The fox ring's protection: no foe picks it out while it doesn't attack. Plenipotentiary A ring with a stylised fox. Woken, it keeps the wearer from attack for a while, as long as the wearer starts nothing. Poison sacs Venom in its jaws, for one poisoned bite a day. Portable Door Chalk with an Epiphling in it. A door drawn on the wall beside the carrier lets it through to the other side, or now and then somewhere else entirely. Possession trance The Kitsune has left this body to ride another. Powwow lessons Elders at the powwow showed this werebear how their Gifts go. For a season its Gifts cost half the experience. Pranked Something waits for this one. Predator's roar A roar that sends anyone close running, friend or foe, unless they stand their ground. Proprieties of conduct Yes The rules of the gathering were announced. Tempers keep for a day. Ptah Coyote as keeper of the stars. Only Ptah's followers may learn the Umbral Danse. Pull of the Chosen Land Always knows the quickest way. Puppeteer's Secret Everyone assumes it belongs. Quick on land A monitor runs as fast as a human. Quickened Blood driven through the limbs: faster on its feet and in a fight. Racked with pain Yes Pain that a Ratkin put there. Rage in the arms Rage poured into the muscles: Strength +1 a point. Rage in the hide Rage poured into the body: Stamina +1 a point. Rage of the mother bear Twice as fast on its feet and with its claws. Rat Thing A lumbering rat the size of a big dog, fast and strong, with no hands and no speech. Its bite tears. Rat Thing Knows the Rat Thing form. Rat's teeth The thrown weapon in hand never runs out. Ratkin A wererat, one of Rat's children. It survived the Birthing Plague, and no sickness takes it now. It sees in the dark for a little Gnosis and screams for its kind when it's hurt, in a voice only Ratkin hear. Ratkin battery Fizzing with junk-brewed strength. Ratman Mostly human, with beady eyes, a long nose, gnarled hands and sharp front teeth. Clothes, guns and tools still work, the claws cut, and it moves quietly. Mortals see an ugly stranger, nothing worse. Ratman Knows the Ratman form. Rattle-trap A bone rattle bound with a spirit of sleep. While its bearer sleeps, foes who come near may fall asleep too. Rattled asleep Yes A bone rattle shook somewhere, and sleep came down like snow. Raven Coyote as Raven. Its followers think quickly and talk well. Razor-webbed Yes Wrapped in cutting spider silk. Every struggle opens another wound. Recapitulated Yes Pushed back down the tree of life: no powers answer it in this shape. Recluse Its venom rots the flesh around the bite for a day. Recluse rot Yes The flesh around a spider bite is dying, and the dead patch spreads for a day. Reforming Yes Pulled back together from a scattered swarm, and still weak from it. Refreshed A werebear's touch: no pain, and wounds don't slow it. Reptoid Hairless, lightly scaled, with small sharp claws. Clothes, tools and weapons still work, and at a distance or under heavy clothes it passes for human, though close up people find it unsettling. Reptoid Form Knows the Reptoid form. Resplendent crest A crest of splendid colour that makes even a dragon handsome. Rodens A rat, from a big one to the size of a housecat, with thumbs on its front paws. It talks only with Ratkin and rats. Salaryman Just another face in a crowd. Sambuhenge Pointed ears, slanted eyes, a longer nose, whiskers and one tail: comical, and hard to take seriously. Anything a human can do, it can. Scampering Running, and very hard to hit. Attacking ends it and empties Rage and Gnosis. Scorpion tail A stinging tail that carries its venom. Seal of Inari: call for help A ghostly plea only Kitsune see. They want to help its bearer. Seal of Inari: death mark A ghostly death mark only Kitsune see. They hate its bearer. Seal of Inari: warning A ghostly warning only Kitsune see. They are wary of its bearer. Secret Question Always has the right answer when asked who it is. Sendeh A red wolf, bigger than a coyote. It can't speak, but it mimics any sound it has heard. Shadow seer The spirits speak to this one, and it speaks back. Shadow Walk Walks through the Gauntlet anywhere. Sheep's clothing Looks, smells and moves like another shifter. Their own people take it for one of them until it strikes or shifts. Sheltered by the earth The land hides it, until it attacks. Short-legged A heavy reptile on land: half a human's running speed. Silenced Yes An eerie silence: it can't speak. Silent running Leaves no trace. Silver sigil Guards take its paper badge for the real thing. Sleep of the ages Yes A sleep nothing short of a touch can break. Sliver tooth Each bite leaves splinters in the wound. Softened air The bear has softened the air around: heat and cold bite less. Sorcerous bite Teeth of jade: its blows wound deep. Spent by the Great Mother Yes Wearing the Queen's shape costs a week as a swarm. It can't change until the week is out. Spider swarm A swarm of spiders at its call, biting any foe that comes near. Spider venom Yes Werespider venom burning in the flesh. It never heals by itself; a doctor has to draw it out, a little with each tending. Spirit egg A Corax's spirit egg, grown in this body. Spirit-struck Yes Disconnected: the spirit world matters more than this one for now. Works at half speed. Spirits of laughter Laughing spirits in the air: hard to stay angry. Standard issue sunglasses A shadow spirit in the shades hides the wearer when woken. Still Blood Its blood numbs whoever it splashes. Stolen stars Yes Helios has taken this one's light. They can hardly see. Stop hitting yourself The next blow that lands goes back to whoever struck it. Submerged Yes Lying low in the water, only the eyes showing. Suchid The reptile of its varna. It talks only in the Dragon's Tongue. Sun enfleshed Burns in silent sun-fire: its blows burn. Sun's guard Raven's sunlight: no fire or heat can touch this one. Survival Needs no food today. Swallow's return Homeward bound, and fast. Swollen tongue Yes The tongue fills the mouth. No words come out. Sworn to the Beast Courts It keeps the nine Mandates as well as the Laws of Heaven, and the courts favour it. Tall Twice the height: it sees further, more each time it is taken. Tarantula Its venom itches and burns. Tarantula itch Yes A maddening itch around a spider bite. Terrible claws Claws like sickles: its claws do more harm. The dagger's curse Yes A Pain-Dagger in the wrong hands. It cuts its holder until they drop it. Thick chitin Yes Thick chitin plates on the war form: blades and blows glance off. Thin Gauntlet The Gauntlet is thin here. Stepping sideways is easier. Ti Malice Coyote as the merciless dealer. Its followers drive hard bargains and lie with a straight face. Tick Body A body that holds more blood. Tiny coyote Shrunk to the size of a mouse. It slips under any door. Tooth splinters Yes Splinters of a rat's tooth in a wound. Trickster's skin Wears someone else's looks, voice and scent. Their own people take it for one of them until it strikes or shifts. Tsitsu A few inches taller and a little more muscle. Two tongues Holding two conversations at once: its words carry twice the weight. Understanding the Tapestry Sees how the world's threads cross: quicker at research, and harder to fool. UPhone A Chimerling in the phone puts a call through from anywhere. Urban camouflage Just another face, until it attacks. Ursa's blessing: body Blessed in body: stronger blows, a steadier aim and a quicker step. Ursa's blessing: heart Blessed in heart: easier to like, to trust and to bargain with. Ursa's blessing: mind Blessed in mind: quicker to learn and to work things out. Ursus A bear of its tribe's kind. It talks only with bears and the Gurahl. Venom in the eyes Yes Spat venom in both eyes: blind for now. Walking Between Worlds Steps sideways anywhere, as the Garou do. Walking like a man Leaves the prints it chooses. It hunts unheard, and its war form strikes no Delirium. Webbed Yes Wrapped in spider silk nearly as strong as steel. It struggles to break free. Weeping eyes Yes Eyes swollen shut by a Ratkin's spit. Widow venom Yes Black widow venom: every hurt feels worse. Wings Wings big enough to carry it: it flies as a Corax does. Winter drowsy Yes Winter weighs on a werebear: it tires sooner and moves a little slower in a fight. Woke ready The rattle woke this werebear with its blood already up. Wolf spider No worse venom, but a harder bite. Wyrmling Kinship The Wyrm's creatures take it for one of their own. Xochipilli Coyote as the flower prince. Every event the storyteller can send, what it means and what to do about it. Most can be switched off or made rarer one by one in the mod settings. Event Kind From day Again after What happens A gathering to host: Council of Autumn Event 30 days The Gurahl offer you the Council of Autumn to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: powwow Event 30 days The Gurahl offer you a powwow to host. At most once a year. A gathering to host: Regalia Event 30 days The Gurahl offer you a Regalia to host. At most once a year. Changing one Event For a colony with no Fera: a stranger in the middle of a First Change stumbles to your land, feverish, with something on their trail. Take them in and they join as a Fera of their breed; the pursuers arrive a few hours later. This is the usual way a colony meets the Changing Breeds. Corax news Event 15 days A Corax drops in, talking fast, and leaves the colony with news it didn't know. Nuwisha visitor Event 20 days A lone Nuwisha wanders in, all grins, with news from the road and a prank or two in mind. A quarter as often as the other breeds' visits. Ratkin sabotage Threat 20 days Ratkin sneak in and sabotage the colony's machines and works. Sept demands Gaia's Breath Event 120 days A Garou sept learns your werebear knows Gaia's Breath and wants it taught to its Theurges. Teaching costs the Gurahl 5 Honor and breaks its oath to guard the secrets; refusing angers the sept. Swift Light courier Event 30 days A rare caravan of the Hermetic Order of Swift Light. It sells uPhones and news on paper, and buys your Corax's secrets while it's here.
